Product Edit Studio · audit of 12 September 2026

# The studio has no listing in it, and the parts that try to remove one are broken

Thirty agents read the studio, the lifecycle backend and the design system, and returned 180 findings; 163 survived adversarial verification. The short answer to your question: the capability is half built, entirely unreachable from the studio, and the half that exists fails in ways that report success. Then a critic read the whole roster and called it 163 sightings of one absence.

Amazon is sent the ASIN where the API needs the seller SKU, so the offer is never removed. Shopify unpublish sends a malformed body, so the product is never drafted. eBay UK throws before it sends. All three then mark the job green. And the whole-product delete destroys its own queue rows inside the same transaction, so no channel call was ever going to run.

### The design critic8a principal designer asked whether the findings add up to a coherent picture

> The roster is empirically excellent and structurally blind. Its 165 findings are, as far as I sampled them, correctly located and correctly cited — and they are 165 sightings of ONE absence, graded as 165 missing verbs. Nobody wrote the sentence the Owner's request actually implies: **the studio has no listing in it.** Its object model is (rows = variants) × (columns = attributes), re-projected by an ambient coordinate; a `ChannelListing` appears in the UI only as `row.listing`, a *field of a variant row*, rendered inside a per-row drawer pane (drawer/panes/ListingsPane.tsx:34-36, whose own header at :12-16 states the constraint: "ONE listing, not a map... the studio sheet is loaded FOR one scope"). Set claim, /usr/bin/grep over the studio tree: `channelListings` occurs exactly once, in a comment (lastMarket.ts:7); positive control, 169 files match "listing". Every studio read is coordinate-scoped by construction (`/studio/sheet`, `/studio/destination`, `/readiness?market=&channel=` — product-studio.routes.ts:387,125,421). You cannot put a verb on an object the page does not render.

#### There is no Listings surface — the listing exists only as a field of a variant row, so lifecycle has nowhere to attach
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
The page's whole object model is variants × attributes, re-projected by scope. A ChannelListing is surfaced once, as `row.listing` inside a per-row record pane (drawer/panes/ListingsPane.tsx:34-36), explicitly singular by design (:12-16: "ONE listing, not a map… the studio sheet is loaded FOR one scope"), and read-only by decision (:5-9). Set claim (/usr/bin/grep, studio tree): `channelListings` appears only in a comment at lastMarket.ts:7; control, 169 files match "listing". Consequence: the Owner is not asking for a button, he is asking for a noun. Delist/relist/archive/close/reopen/alias are all verbs on a ChannelListing (schema.prisma:1509, keyed product × channel × marketplace × connectionId × aliasKey, :1783-1784) and the studio renders no such row anywhere — so all 165 roster findings correctly report an absent verb and none can say where it would go. Design: the channel half of the studio needs a Listings page — one row per real coordinate (channel · market · account · alias), each carrying external id, listing state, offer state, last confirmed, and its own verbs. That is the object the schema, the queue, the recovery service and the Owner's sentence all already agree exists. The server can nearly feed it today: `/products/:id/sync-queue` takes channel/marketplace as OPTIONAL filters (product-studio.routes.ts:872-890) and the only consumer pins both (ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:152).

#### The coordinate is ambient, per-browser and frequently absent from the URL — the worst possible targeting model for irreversible external verbs
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
The target of every future lifecycle verb would be "whatever the bar currently says", and the bar is resolved from browser-local state, not from the document. `market` falls back to `readLastMarket()` localStorage and then to a channel-count tiebreak (lastMarket.ts:20-27; scopes.ts:174-183; contracts.tsx:648-651); `scope` silently degrades to master when the market is not served (contracts.tsx:653-660); `account` defaults to the primary (contracts.tsx:664); when the operator is already on their remembered market, `?market=` is never written into the URL at all. The roster treats this as a link-sharing nit. It is not: it means an "End this listing" control would be a verb with an implicit, unstated, per-user argument. Design rule to adopt before any lifecycle verb ships: a channel-reaching verb never inherits the scope bar. It takes its target(s) explicitly, restates them in the confirm in operator words (channel · market · account · alias · external id), and refuses to run if the coordinate it was constructed with no longer matches the one on screen — the same class of guard `validateImpact` already applies to a typed confirm with no phrase (registry.ts:264-273).

#### The page has one meter and it measures readiness — there is no state axis for what is live right now, so lifecycle has nothing to act on or report to
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
Everything the studio displays about a channel is pre-publish completeness: `ScopeBarReadiness {pct, state}` (ScopeBar.tsx:26-40) over the vocabulary ready|missing|errors|live|unlisted. There is no orthogonal readout for post-publish presence: external id, since when, under which account, offer open/closed (`offerClosedAt`, schema.prisma:1591-1594, read by nothing in the studio), last confirmed by the channel, suppressed, ended. The roster reports the symptoms — "Live has three definitions", "offerClosedAt never read", "no as-of", "closed market reads selling" — but not the cause: a single meter is being asked to carry two orthogonal facts, and the code already shows the slot is oversubscribed, because transient SAVE state overwrites readiness in the same pill (StudioBar.tsx:18-19). Design: two independent readouts per coordinate — Completeness (can I publish; the existing readiness) and Presence (what is live; new, sourced from the listing row, always stamped with an as-of). They must never merge into one word, and the lifecycle verbs read from Presence, not Readiness. Without this, a delist verb has no before-state to show and no after-state to confirm against.

#### Autosave direct manipulation is the wrong interaction model for external irreversible acts — and the right model (a staged queue) already exists in the backend with a read-only window onto it
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
D8 removed Save/Discard; every content edit is a fire-and-forget cell write with no undo (the DS has no undo pattern and Toast carries no action slot). That is defensible for cells. It is indefensible for acts that reach Amazon. Bolting a modal-confirmed verb into an autosave surface inherits the operator's learned reflex ("I change things here and they just happen") and applies it to an EndFixedPriceItem. Meanwhile the system's own channel-reaching layer is already a plan: OutboundSyncQueue, with PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/CANCELLED states, which the studio reads but cannot act on (channel-ops/ErrorsSyncTab.tsx, ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:152). The missing layer is a **stage → review → apply** band for channel-reaching intent: compose "end IT, keep DE", see the per-coordinate consequences enumerated (registry.ts's ActionImpact shape already supports itemised consequences), apply as one authorised act, then watch the queue rows drain in the same panel. This also answers the open question nobody could settle ("which confirmation surface is canonical for a delete raised outside a grid?"): none of the three. A lifecycle act should not be a modal at all.

#### Reversibility and reach are not in the action vocabulary — so every lane states them in prose, and prose is exactly where every lie in the roster lives
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
`GridAction` carries one severity bit, `danger?: boolean` (registry.ts:169-171), and ConfirmLevel is none|confirm|type-to-confirm. Nothing in the type system distinguishes REACH (does this touch a local row or a live marketplace?) from REVERSIBILITY (undoable / recoverable-with-loss / permanent). Because the type cannot say it, each lane writes a sentence — and the roster's most dangerous findings are all mis-written sentences: "Unpublish (recommended) — keeps the listing record so you can republish later" over a hard SP-API delete; "the record is kept, so <ItemID> is not lost" over a local-only flag; "HARD DELETE IS NEVER PERFORMED" above a deleteMany. Fixing them one at a time guarantees the next one. Design: extend ActionImpact with `reach: 'local' | 'channel'` and `reversal: { how: string } | null`, have the confirmation renderer DERIVE the reversibility sentence rather than accept one, and make an unstated reversal on a `reach: 'channel'` verb a refusal — the exact shape validateImpact already uses to refuse a typed confirm with no phrase (registry.ts:264-273). Then the DS, not the lane, owns the promise.

#### CH.1's "one flat ⋯, never a button" was written for a page with no destructive verbs and will actively degrade lifecycle when it lands
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
The toolbar contract is explicit: a scope's own verbs are ITEMS of the one ⋯ overflow, they never add a button, and `trailing` is "Transient STATUS only… Never a control" (SheetToolbar.tsx:15-30, 100-108). The prop that carries them is `overflow?: readonly MenuItemDef[]` (:104) — a flat list with no grouping and no severity. The DS registry meanwhile promises destructive verbs are "grouped apart and rendered with danger tone by every adapter" (registry.ts:169-171) and both adapters drop the flag. So the ruling and the DS contradict each other, and the ruling wins at the call site. Landing lifecycle under it produces exactly the shape the Owner would reject: "End listing on Amazon · IT" as an unstyled row between "Cell details" and "Formula history". This is not a token bug to file against the Menu; it is a ruling that needs amending on the record, with the reason stated: lifecycle verbs are not scope verbs, because they do not act on the sheet — they act on a listing. Note the same rule already forced two lanes to smuggle real controls into `trailing` (MasterSheet.tsx:1777, ChannelSheet.tsx:2124) — the contract is being violated because it has no legitimate slot for a verb that is not a column filter.

#### The scope model is single-valued, so the plural intents that dominate lifecycle work cannot even be STATED — only decomposed into N visits with no aggregate and no atomicity
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
`coordinate` is one triple (contracts.tsx:955-958); market is one code with GLOBAL excluded from the default pool (scopes.ts:174-177); readiness is fetched per single market (contracts.tsx:378-383). But almost every real lifecycle intent is plural: "off everywhere except DE", "off eBay entirely, keep Amazon", "take the whole family down for the season and back in November", "this account's listings only". The studio can express none of them. An operator must visit each coordinate, with no view of the set, no consistency check across it, and no single authorised act — which is precisely how the roster's cross-market defects (broadcast that never sends, per-market close invisible elsewhere, one market removed while a sibling keeps selling) become invisible to the person doing the work. Related and unnoticed: the channel sheets count a multi-row selection and mount no selection bar at all, so even the intra-coordinate plural case has no home. Design: the channel half of the studio should open on a markets × channels matrix for THIS product, with multi-select and one verb rail — the aggregate view is the natural place for both the state axis (item 3) and the staged plan (item 5).

#### The IA already reserved the slot for a listing object, and the DS already shipped the affordance — both are wired to a spreadsheet instead
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
Two pieces of the right design are already in the tree, unused. (a) The navigation drawer builds a per-channel group whose sole universal item is `Listing information` → `tab: 'sheet'` (StudioSubheader.tsx:33-52) — the group is the correct place for a Listing page and it currently contains a grid. (b) `StudioTabHost` already resolves a destination OBJECT and gates every channel tab on `destination.status === 'ready'` plus a selected account (StudioTabHost.tsx:69-77) — the page knows which listing it is standing on and never shows it. (c) The DS `ScopeBar` ships an `onAdd` affordance documented for exactly "adding a listing alias, connecting a channel" (ScopeBar.tsx:79, 269-270); set claim, /usr/bin/grep over the studio tree: zero occurrences of `onAdd` — the studio never passes it, which is why "put this on a new channel × market" has to leave the page to the legacy wizard (PublishMenu.tsx:17-19), itself a D9 violation. The cheapest coherent first move is therefore not new chrome: promote the destination the frame already resolves into a visible object at the top of each channel group, hang state and lifecycle on it, and pass `onAdd` for the create direction.

#### The two global auth/tenancy preHandlers were never opened — and the destructive lifecycle routes carry no in-file guard at all
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
Every permission finding in the roster (products.delete unused, API-key coarse family, 'default-user' actor) was derived from route bodies and permission NAMES in the manifest. Nobody read the hooks that actually decide. `apps/api/src/index.ts:633-634` registers `workspaceHook` then `rbacHook` globally; `apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts` contains ZERO occurrences of preHandler/requirePermission/authenticate (counted with /usr/bin/grep -c), and its `POST /api/amazon/flat-file/remove` (`:1806-1819`) loops caller-supplied `{productId, marketplace}` pairs straight into `removeAmazonListing`. That service's queries carry no workspaceId (`apps/api/src/services/amazon/amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:52-64`: `channelListing.deleteMany({ where: { productId: { in: ids }, channel: 'AMAZON', marketplace } })`), and the eBay twin is identical (`ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:644-647`). The bulk-hard-delete eligibility query is the same shape (`products-catalog.routes.ts:1803-1806`), and `workspaceId` appears exactly ONCE in that entire route file (line 2326). Whether an unmapped destructive route defaults to allow or deny, and whether workspaceHook row-scopes anything or merely sets context, is the single discriminator that decides if this is safe or is the worst finding in the audit. MEMORY already flags 'field security BUILT, ROW scoping open'. It is unmeasured. Note also `apps/api/src/lib/database-context.ts` (72 lines) is an AsyncLocalStorage transaction context with no workspace injection — so scoping is manual per query, and these queries do not do it.

#### The restore / recover family — the only existing 'put it back' — was cited once in passing and never audited as a surface
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why

#### Per-market economics — price, listed quantity, business policies, replication — audited only for lifecycle side effects, never for whether the studio can do them
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
When an operator wants a product 'off' one market, the first thing they reach for is not a delist verb: it is the price and the quantity. The roster knows this (one finding calls zeroing quantity 'the documented storewide incident') but never audits the levers themselves. #### Product recall / safety stop-sale: the recall track exists and cannot stop a single listing — and there is no "stop selling everywhere, keep everything" verb at all
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
A recall (or a supplier safety notice, or a hazmat re-classification) is the one lifecycle event where every hour counts and nothing may be destroyed: orders, lots, serials and listing identity must all survive for the traceability file. Nexus already models the recall — `LotRecall` (schema.prisma:9456, status OPEN/CLOSED, reason, openedBy) plus `computeDefectRecallSignals` (returns-defect-recall.service.ts:1-45) which clusters DAMAGED/UNUSABLE returns into "recall candidates" and lists the lots to open a recall against. But `openRecall` (lot.service.ts:321-346) has exactly one downstream effect, stated in its own doc comment at :315-320 and confirmed at stock-level.service.ts:248: "subsequent FEFO consume picks skip this lot". Nothing reads an open recall when computing published quantity, nothing enqueues a pause, nothing writes ChannelListing. /usr/bin/grep for recall|lotNumber|ReturnItem across the whole `_studio/` tree returns one hit and it is the word "recalled" in a comment (lastMarket.ts:11) — the studio has no recall surface, no hold, no banner. So the operator's only channel-wide off switch is `POST /products/bulk-hard-delete` (products-catalog.routes.ts:1772), which requires the product to already be in the bin (`deletedAt: {not: null}`, :1801), is irreversible, and — per the roster's own confirmed defect — cascade-deletes its delist queue rows before they fire. The studio cannot handle this today and could not be made to without a new non-destructive "suspend on all coordinates" verb; every ingredient (offerActive, syncPaused, SCT.6 close, Shopify draft) exists but nothing composes them.

▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
"Same product, new SKU, keep the ASIN and its reviews" is a weekly move (barcode change, supplier switch, FNSKU re-label, a SKU scheme migration). Product.sku IS the seller SKU sent to Amazon — amazon-live-images.service.ts:13 states "Resolve sellerSku — for now this is Product.sku" — and ListingReconciliation is keyed on `externalSku` (schema.prisma:14994, unique [workspaceId, channel, marketplace, externalSku]). Meanwhile the two real mechanisms are both outside it: Amazon `SAME_ASIN_NEW_SKU` / `DELETE_RELIST_SAME` (recovery.service.ts:44-49), reachable only from /products/[id]/recover, and eBay `relabelListingToPoolSkus` (ebay-variation-relabel.service.ts, route ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:3162, UI only at EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:4146). #### Selling privileges suspended on a marketplace, or a market you have exited: SP-API participation status is measured and stored, and the studio's market model throws it away
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
"Amazon suspended our selling privileges on FR", "we deregistered for VAT in PL and stopped selling there", "eBay closed that site" — in all three the market must read as unsellable while the listings still exist. Nexus measures this: `Marketplace.isParticipating`, `participationStatus` ('PARTICIPATING' | 'SUSPENDED' | 'NOT_PARTICIPATING' | 'ACCESS_DENIED' | 'UNKNOWN') and `participationCheckedAt` (schema.prisma:1971-1976), with the schema comment stating the rule outright: "A sync should run only when isActive && isParticipating". Other surfaces honour it — the FBA inbound modal labels a market "(not participating)" (fulfillment/inbound/v2/NewPlanModal.tsx:227) and the mapping catalogue projects it (pim/mapping/editor-catalogue.service.ts:43). The studio does not: `MarketplaceLite` carries only id/channel/code/name/language/languages/accounts/connected (types.ts:78-89) and `deriveScopeOptions` filters solely on `connected` (scopes.ts:108-125). A SUSPENDED or ACCESS_DENIED market therefore renders as an ordinary chip, is selectable, is writable, and its listings report readiness as if publishable — the studio will tell an operator a suspended market is "Ready 94%". The remedy is cheap (project two fields the API already has) but the roster never mentions participation at all; it only covers the operator-controlled `isActive` deactivation.

#### Reopening a market after a season replays last season's price verbatim — no margin, floor or promo-window revalidation on the one reversible relist path in the codebase
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
Everyone on this sweep, correctly, named SCT.6 close/reopen as "the only truly reversible per-market path" and asked for the studio to reach it. Nobody read the reopen. `reopenMarketOffers` takes the stored `offerCloseSnapshot.purchasableOffer` and pushes it back with `patchPurchasableOffer({ op: 'replace', value: offerValue })` (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:246-270) — verbatim, with no pass through the pricing engine, no `minPrice`/`minMargin` check (Product carries both, master-field-gate.ts:29-31), and no inspection of the date windows embedded in an Amazon `purchasable_offer` (discounted_price entries carry their own start/end). A jacket closed in March at a clearance price and reopened in October republishes the clearance price — after a cost increase, potentially below cost — and any embedded promo window comes back with it. The row is then immediately flipped to `followMasterQuantity: true` and a QUANTITY_UPDATE is enqueued (:276-299), so stock flows to that price at once. The other arm is just as operator-hostile: if the snapshot is unusable the result is `FAILED` with "no usable close snapshot — reopen needs a manual price set" (:257-259) — a market that can be closed but never reopened from the same surface. If the studio is going to expose close/reopen (and it should), it must show the snapshot's price and date windows at reopen time and re-run the price guard.

#### The fulfilment dimension of a listing is invisible: "withdraw the merchant offer, keep FBA" (or the reverse when units strand) cannot be expressed anywhere in the studio
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
On Amazon a coordinate routinely carries two offers — FBA and FBM — with their own SKU, price, quantity and on/off state, and the normal operator move during a stockout, a courier failure, a peak-season handling-time risk or an FBA strand is to withdraw ONE of them, not the listing. The studio has no offer dimension at all: /usr/bin/grep over `_studio/` finds `fulfillmentMethod` nowhere and `fulfillmentChannel` only as a label map (sheet/referenceLabels.ts:51). Its one off-switch writes `ChannelListing.offerActive`, which is listing-wide, and the reversible Amazon path refuses FBA rows outright (`SKIPPED_FBA`, amazon-market-offer.service.ts). So the sheet's single row per coordinate is a lie about Amazon's actual structure, and two paths silently destroy the finer state — catalog.routes.ts:1075 and :1110 `tx.offer.deleteMany`. Before any delist verb lands, the studio has to decide whether its unit of removal is the listing or the offer.

#### Supplier discontinues mid-season: there is no end-of-life state, no sell-through-then-end, and at zero stock the studio cannot say whether the eBay listing is still up
▸ Why it matters and where to look

##### Why
The commonest lifecycle event in apparel is not a delete: the supplier drops the line, you sell the remaining units, then the listing must end and never be recreated. Nexus has no vocabulary for it. `Product.status` is `DRAFT, ACTIVE, INACTIVE` only (schema.prisma:129-130) — /usr/bin/grep for DISCONTINUED across apps/api/src, apps/web/src and the schema returns exactly one hit, and it is a comment inside the Amazon delist adapter (channel-delist.service.ts:152). There is no "do not relist" flag, so every resurrection path (flat-file import, reconciliation, the workbook round trip) has nothing to refuse — which is why the roster's "a removed Amazon listing comes straight back in the flat file" is a symptom, not the disease. And the end-state at zero stock is genuinely unknown to the product: the repo deliberately stops sending `OutOfStockControl` — "deprecated by eBay — incident #25; the account-level out-of-stock preference governs keep-alive" (ebay-trading-xml.vitest.test.ts:30-31) — so whether an eBay listing survives a stockout is configured in Seller Hub, outside Nexus, per account. The studio shows one "Available" roll-up and cannot tell the operator whether the eBay listing is still live at qty 0 (keep-alive on) or was auto-ended by eBay with its ItemID retired (keep-alive off). A discontinuation plan needs a state, a scheduled end, and that fact rendered; none of the three exists.

#### The Amazon delist adapter sends the ASIN where SP-API requires the seller SKU — the only backend a studio "remove from this market" button could call deletes the wrong key

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the GALE jacket live on Amazon IT (ASIN B0C1234567, seller SKU GALE-JACKET-M-BLK) and Amazon DE. They want it off IT only. Whatever verb the studio eventually offers has exactly one backend: dispatchChannelDelist. Today the only way to reach it is to bin the whole product and hard-delete with channelAction 'delete' — and on that path Amazon is handed the string 'B0C1234567' as the SKU to delete.

##### What happens today
channel-delist.service.ts:139-141 comments "externalListingId for Amazon is typically the SKU (since the Listings Items endpoint is keyed by SKU, not ASIN)" and assigns `const sku = job.externalListingId!`, then calls amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem({sellerId, sku, marketplaceId}) at :162, which builds DELETE /listings/2021-08-01/items/{sellerId}/{sku} (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1160). The comment asserts a property the column has never had. Every Amazon writer of externalListingId writes an ASIN — amazon.routes.ts:1263,1270,1451,1458; amazon/flat-file-pull.service.ts:267; amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3469; listing-wizard/submission.service.ts:1482,1486; listing-reconciliation.service.ts:375,390,520,533; inbound-sync.service.ts:69,81 — and schema.prisma:1542-1545 documents the column as "Amazon: Parent ASIN (non-buyable) or child ASIN (buyable)". I ran /usr/bin/grep over all 129 non-test externalListingId assignment sites in apps/api/src: zero write a SKU on the Amazon path. The other caller of the same client method gets it right — recovery.service.ts:320 passes `preview.before.sku`. Consequence: the delist either 404s (silent no-op reported as a retryable failure while the local ChannelListing row is already gone by FK cascade) or, for the common seller practice of using the ASIN as the SKU, deletes a real but unintended listing. On the amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts path the local row is deleted first (:59-63) and the dispatch result is swallowed by `catch { }` at :82, so nobody ever learns which happened.

##### Proposed fix
Fix before any studio affordance is wired, or the new button ships the defect. (1) Change ChannelDelistJob to carry an explicit `sellerSku` field resolved from Product.sku / ChannelListing.sku at enqueue time, never inferred from externalListingId — the 'explicit flag beats inference' rule. products-catalog.routes.ts:1849-1866 already selects the listing row; add `product: { select: { sku: true } }` and stamp it onto the queue row's payload. (2) Make delistAmazon refuse fail-closed when `sellerSku` is absent rather than falling back to externalListingId, and assert the value does not match /^B0[A-Z0-9]{8}$/ (an ASIN shape) before calling. (3) Delete the stale comment at :139-140. (4) Remove the bare `catch {}` at amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:82 and reorder so the SP-API call happens BEFORE the local deleteMany — a local row destroyed while the channel listing survives is the one outcome no reconcile job can repair.

CONFIRMED, and the finding understates reachability. Every cited line says what the finding claims.

VERIFIED CORE DEFECT
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:138-141 — the comment "externalListingId for Amazon is typically the SKU (since the Listings Items endpoint is keyed by SKU, not ASIN)" is present verbatim, followed by `const sku = job.externalListingId!`. It is contradicted 100 lines above it in the SAME file: the module docblock at channel-delist.service.ts:34 documents the field as "externalListingId (ASIN | eBay ItemID | Shopify product gid/number)".
- channel-delist.service.ts:161-166 passes that value as `sku` to `amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem`.
- apps/api/src/clients/amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1159-1165 builds `DELETE /listings/2021-08-01/items/${sellerId}/${sku}` — the value goes straight into the SKU path segment.
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1541-1545 — "Amazon: Parent ASIN (non-buyable) or child ASIN (buyable)" directly above `externalListingId String?`.
- I re-ran the set claim with /usr/bin/grep (not the ugrep shell function): 228 `externalListingId:` sites under apps/api/src; the only two that mention `sku` on the same line (apps/api/src/routes/sync-control.routes.ts:411, apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file-pull.service.ts:190) are Prisma `select:` clauses, not assignments — and both select `product.sku` SEPARATELY from `externalListingId`, i.e. the rest of the codebase already treats them as different values. Positive control: 20 sites mention `asin`. I opened the cited Amazon writers and all write an ASIN: amazon.routes.ts:1255-1275 (`externalListingId: asin`), amazon.routes.ts:1445-1462 (`product.amazonAsin!`), amazon/flat-file-pull.service.ts:267 (`asin`), amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3464-3469 (`asin ? { externalListingId: asin } : {}`), listing-wizard/submission.service.ts:1482,1486 (`asin`).
- Contrast confirmed: listings/recovery.service.ts:318-322 passes `sku: preview.before.sku`. /usr/bin/grep shows exactly two non-test callers of `deleteListingsItem` — recovery.service.ts:318 (correct) and channel-delist.service.ts:162 (wrong).
- ChannelListing has NO `sku` column: /usr/bin/grep -i over the full model body (schema.prisma:1509-1888, 380 lines, positive control on "price" hit at :1552-1554) returns nothing for sku/seller. So the delist adapter has no per-row SKU to read even if it wanted one.

WHY THE FINDING IS UNDERSTATED (mis-stated, not refuted)
The scenario says "whatever verb the studio eventually offers… today the only way to reach it is to bin the whole product". That is false, and the truth is worse: a market-scoped Amazon removal already SHIPS. apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1801-1819 exposes `POST /api/amazon/flat-file/remove` → `removeAmazonListing` (apps/api/src/services/amazon/amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:32-86), which deletes the local ChannelListing rows in a transaction at :59-65 and THEN dispatches the delist at :71-80 with `externalListingId: l.externalListingId` as the Amazon SKU. It is wired to a live operator button: apps/web/src/app/products/amazon-flat-file/AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1883-1899 (`removeFromAmazon`), which toasts "Removed N listings from Amazon {marketplace} — product and stock kept." So the defect is exercisable today from a shipped UI, not only prospectively from a future studio button. bullmq-sync.worker.ts:142-151 is the second live entry point, passing the queue row's externalListingId through unchanged.

AMPLIFIER I FOUND WHILE VERIFYING (not in the finding)
`deleteListingsItem` is the one SP-API write method that BYPASSES the publish gate. amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1143 reads `process.env.AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE` directly, while :519, :669, :792 and :884 all call `getAmazonPublishMode()` (amazon-publish-gate.service.ts:45-53), which folds in the `NEXUS_ENABLE_AMAZON_PUBLISH` master flag and default-safes any unrecognised value to dry-run. The delete does neither: the master kill-switch does not gate it, and any mode string other than 'dry-run'/'dryrun' (including 'sandbox' or a typo) sends a real HTTP DELETE. So the failure mode is unprotected by the flag every other Amazon write sits behind.

ERROR-SWALLOWING, precisely: the bare `catch { }` at amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:82 eats thrown exceptions, and separately line 81 reads only `r.success` — a returned `{ success: false, error }` is dropped on the floor because `RemoveAmazonResult.error` is never assigned from it. The route returns `delisted: false` with no error, and the client at AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1894 filters only on `r.error`, so a channel-side failure renders as a green success toast. The finding's consequence ("nobody ever learns which happened") is correct; the mechanism is two defects, not one.

MINOR INACCURACIES (do not change the verdict): the "129 non-test assignment sites" count is not reproducible with my method (I get 228 `externalListingId:` occurrences including selects) — the conclusion holds regardless, since I re-derived it independently; and the proposed fix's "ChannelListing.sku" does not exist.
Directionally right, three corrections. (1) Step 1 says resolve the SKU "from Product.sku / ChannelListing.sku" — ChannelListing has no sku column (verified over the whole model, schema.prisma:1509-1888), so Product.sku (or the flat-file row's SKU) is the only source; say so explicitly or the implementer will chase a field that does not exist. (2) The entry point to patch is not only products-catalog.routes.ts:1849-1866: the live path today is amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:53-56, whose `select: { externalListingId: true }` must become `select: { externalListingId: true, product: { select: { sku: true } } }`, plus bullmq-sync.worker.ts:142-151 which forwards the queue row. Patching only the products-catalog enqueue leaves the shipped button broken. (3) The ASIN-shape assertion `/^B0[A-Z0-9]{8}$/` is too narrow to be a safety net (pre-B0 ASINs and 10-char ISBN-style ASINs slip through) and too broad to be safe (a seller SKU legitimately equal to the ASIN would be rejected). Prefer fail-closed on a missing explicit sellerSku, and drop the regex — or make it a warn-and-log, not a hard gate. Missing from the fix: deleteListingsItem should route through getAmazonPublishMode() like every other write method in that client (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1143 vs :519/:669/:792/:884), so the master publish flag gates the delete and an unrecognised mode default-safes instead of going live. Step 4 (reorder SP-API call before the local deleteMany, remove the bare catch) is correct and is the highest-value item; also fix line 81, which discards a returned `{success:false,error}` even when nothing throws — the client at AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1894 filters only on `error`, so a channel failure currently renders as a success toast.

[critical]verifiedALLux defect

#### The studio's only per-market off-switch tells the operator "Buyers stop seeing this offer" — it is refused on every live listing, and when it does run it reaches no channel at all

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the jacket live on eBay IT and eBay DE with heavy cross-border shipping costs on DE. They open the studio on scope eBay · DE, select the SKU rows and use the row menu's "Pause 4 offers on eBay · DE". The confirmation reads: "Buyers stop seeing this offer on this channel and market. The listing itself is not ended and its reviews and identifiers are untouched." They confirm and consider DE closed.

##### What happens today
Two separate failures. (a) On every live row the verb refuses: preflight sets `unavailable` (channelActions.ts:249-251, "Refused for now: N of these are live listings, and wave-1 verbs do not send to a channel. Preview only.") and `run` refuses again at :259-261. So for the exact rows the operator cares about, nothing happens. (b) On the rows where it is NOT refused, the promised consequence is still false. PATCH /api/products/:id/offer-availability (marketplaces.routes.ts:295-325) does one prisma.channelListing.upsert writing `offerActive` and nothing else — no marketplace call, no OutboundSyncQueue row. I traced every consumer of `offerActive` on a push path in apps/api/src: exactly two. amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3415-3419 injects `skip_offer` into the collapsed attributes, which takes effect only the NEXT time somebody runs an Amazon flat-file publish; and outbound-sync.service.ts:646-655, which is explicitly opt-in — "OPT-IN (default OFF): only when NEXUS_RESPECT_OFFER_ACTIVE=1 do we skip pushing to a suppressed offer" — and the variable is set in no env file in the repo (/usr/bin/grep over apps/api/.env* and ./.env*, rc=1). For eBay and Shopify there is no consumer at all: `offerActive` never becomes an EndFixedPriceItem, a quantity-zero revise, or a status:DRAFT. The jacket keeps selling on eBay DE. The same endpoint is used with the same false premise outside the studio (products/_components/GridView.tsx:977, edit/tabs/MasterDataTab.tsx:1174), and the /fulfillment Control Tower states it honestly — "This suppresses outbound pushes for DE. No quantity updates will be sent until re-activated" (ControlTowerClient.tsx:673-676) — which is what the studio's copy should have said.

##### Proposed fix
Two moves, both small. (1) Honesty now: rewrite the preflight consequence to state what the write actually does — "Outbound pushes for this channel and market stop. The offer stays as the channel last received it until a publish carries the change." Keep the sideEffects line about the auto-created DRAFT row. This is a one-string edit inside the existing ActionImpact and needs no new component. (2) Capability: the verb an operator reads as 'pause' must be the SCT.6 offer close, not a local flag — see SC-DR-3. Rename the flag verb to "Stop pushing to this market" (it is a sync-pause, and the studio should also surface `syncPaused`, which currently has ZERO references in the whole _studio tree) and give the real pause its own action id `listing-pause` in channelActions.ts, gated `danger: false`, level 'confirm', consequences itemised from the server's preflight rather than composed client-side.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts:228-231
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts:249-251
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts:258-261
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts:265-276

- apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3413-3419
- apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:645-655
- apps/web/src/app/fulfillment/stock/control-tower/ControlTowerClient.tsx:658-676

##### Verifier
The cited code says what the finding says it says, but the finding's headline scenario is impossible and two of its supporting claims are wrong. What survives is still a real defect, so refuted=false with corrections.

CONFIRMED BY MY OWN READING
- channelActions.ts:228-231 — the pause consequence is verbatim "Buyers stop seeing this offer on this channel and market. The listing itself is not ended and its reviews and identifiers are untouched."
- channelActions.ts:249-251 (`unavailable`) and :258-261 (`run` refusal) exist as quoted; `liveAliasKeys` (:120-121) keys off `externalListingId`, so any row with a channel id is refused.
- marketplaces.routes.ts:295-325 — the endpoint does one `channelListing.upsert` writing only `offerActive`, auto-creating a DRAFT row. No OutboundSyncQueue write on the pause branch.
- outbound-sync.service.ts:645-655 — the offerActive skip is gated on `NEXUS_RESPECT_OFFER_ACTIVE === '1'`. I re-ran the env check with /usr/bin/grep over apps/api/.env, apps/api/.env.example, .env, .env.naf-a2-backup: rc=1, the variable is set nowhere (only worktree copies and an SDD report mention it).
- amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3413-3419 — `skip_offer` injection, effective only on the next flat-file publish.
- ControlTowerClient.tsx:658-676 — the wording is as quoted.
- Capability search (all /usr/bin/grep, so these are sound set claims): channelActions.ts has exactly three verbs — `open-record` (:381), `offer-toggle` (:163), `broadcast-to-listings` (:309) — wired at :404 and consumed by ChannelSheet.tsx:863; no delist/end/relist/withdraw verb anywhere under _studio; `syncPaused` = 0 hits in all of apps/web/src (schema.prisma:1650 defines it); `offerClosedAt` = 0 hits in apps/web/src while nine API files use it (sync-control.routes.ts, outbound-sync.service.ts, listing-activation-sync.service.ts, …). So the real per-market offer-close concept genuinely has no web surface, and the studio genuinely has no delist/relist.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG
1. The scenario cannot happen. runAction.ts:74-75 returns `{kind:'refused'}` on `impact.unavailable` BEFORE the confirm dialog is ever shown (rule 4, ahead of rule 5's `ask` at :78). So with live eBay DE rows selected the operator never sees the "Buyers stop seeing this offer" sentence at all — they get the refusal. And on the only path where the dialog does render (no live channel id), ActionConfirm.tsx:123-131 renders the sideEffects block "This also happens", which carries channelActions.ts:238 "No live channel id on these rows — the change stays local until they are published." The two halves the finding stacks are mutually exclusive: (a) prevents (b). Nobody's jacket keeps selling because of the studio verb.
2. "when it does run it reaches no channel at all" is false for half the verb. marketplaces.routes.ts:326-328 calls `syncActivatedListings(activatedIds)` for rows turned active, and listing-activation-sync.service.ts:24-80+ enqueues a QUANTITY_UPDATE. Activate reaches the channel; only Pause is inert.
3. "exactly two consumers of offerActive on a push path" is not a sound set claim. /usr/bin/grep -rn offerActive over apps/api/src returns 62 non-test hits across 17 files; besides the two named, content-auto-publish.service.ts:105-113 filters `offerActive: true` before enqueuing content FULL_SYNC, and listing-automation/evaluator.ts:119-126 excludes paused listings from automation. None of them end or hide a live listing, so the substance holds, but the enumeration does not.
4. GridView.tsx:973-978 is mischaracterised. It posts `{ offerActive: false }` with no `markets` array; marketplaces.routes.ts:298-300 rejects that with 400 "markets array is required". That surface's "close listing" is simply broken, not a working write under a false premise. (MasterDataTab.tsx:1090/1130/1155/1179 and BulkActionBar.tsx:1410 do send `markets` and are ungated by any live-row refusal — that is where a live listing can actually be flagged with no channel effect, outside the studio.)

WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHY IT IS STILL A FINDING
The studio's only per-market off-switch writes a DB flag that produces no channel effect on the pause direction, and it describes that flag to the operator as a buyer-visible consequence — on the one path where the dialog renders. Separately and more importantly for the owner's brief, there is no per-market delist/relist in the studio at all, and the server-side `offerClosedAt` close has zero web callers. That is a genuine capability gap, shown missing with /usr/bin/grep, not assumed.
Fix (1) is correctly scoped — a one-string edit inside the existing ActionImpact — but the proposed replacement is itself false. "Outbound pushes for this channel and market stop" is not what the flag does: outbound-sync.service.ts:646 only honours offerActive when NEXUS_RESPECT_OFFER_ACTIVE=1, and that variable is set in no env file, so ordinary quantity/price pushes continue. What actually changes is narrower: the next Amazon flat-file publish injects skip_offer (flat-file.service.ts:3414-3419), content auto-publish skips the row (content-auto-publish.service.ts:110), and listing automation stops evaluating it (evaluator.ts:119-126). The honest sentence has to say the flag is recorded and only those paths read it. For the same reason the ControlTower string the finding holds up as the model ("No quantity updates will be sent until re-activated", ControlTowerClient.tsx:675) is also wrong today, so it should not be copied. Fix (2) inherits the same overclaim: "Stop pushing to this market" is not true while the env gate is off. Also, surfacing `syncPaused` is a new feature (zero references in all of apps/web/src, plus a wire/type/column change), not part of a rename, and should not ride along inside a copy fix. Finally, the fix leaves the higher-value half untouched: the ungated callers at MasterDataTab.tsx:1090/1130/1155/1179 and BulkActionBar.tsx:1410 can set the flag on live listings with no wave-1 refusal, and GridView.tsx:973 sends a body the route 400s.

#### The exact reversible per-market capability the Owner asked for is already built (SCT.6 close/reopen) — the studio has no path to it and cannot even see it, so a closed market renders as "live · ACTIVE · selling"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator closes the jacket's Amazon IT offer for the season from /fulfillment/stock/sync-control (CLOSE_OFFER). Amazon IT now shows no buyable offer; DE is untouched; the ASIN, the reviews and the shared EU quantity survive; the verbatim purchasable_offer is stored for a one-click reopen next season. They then open the studio on scope Amazon · IT to check.

##### What happens today
The studio reports the market as fully live. `LISTING_SELECT` (studio-sheet.service.ts:458-463) selects listingStatus, isPublished, offerActive, externalListingId — and NOT offerClosedAt. closeMarketOffers writes only offerClosedAt / offerClosedBy / offerCloseReason / offerCloseSnapshot (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:178-195) and deliberately leaves listingStatus, isPublished and offerActive alone. So readiness computes `listing.externalListingId && listing.isPublished → 'live'` (studio-sheet.service.ts:1447-1450), the drawer's ListingsPane prints Status = ACTIVE (ListingsPane.tsx:103), "Pushed to channel: yes" (:113) and "Offer: selling" (:127), and the sheet's readiness chip says live. /usr/bin/grep for `offerClosedAt` across all of apps/web/src returns nothing (rc=1; positive control: `offerActive` matches in 10+ web files including drawer/types.ts and ListingsPane.tsx), so no web surface anywhere can render the closed state. Reaching the capability is equally impossible from the studio: my sweep of the whole _studio tree for sync-control|CLOSE_OFFER|REOPEN_OFFER|listing-recovery returned rc=1 against a positive control of 41 files containing fetch(. The only exposure is POST /api/stock/sync-control/actions (sync-control.routes.ts). Secondary scoping hole: closeMarketOffers' loadRow (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:66-75) is a findFirst on {productId, channel:'AMAZON', marketplace} with no channelConnectionId and no aliasKey, so on a coordinate with two accounts or two aliases it closes whichever row Prisma returns first.

##### Proposed fix
Display first, then reach. (1) Add `offerClosedAt`, `offerClosedBy`, `offerCloseReason` to LISTING_SELECT (studio-sheet.service.ts:458-463) and to the SheetListing wire type (:285-287); add a `paused` state to SheetReadiness ahead of the 'live' branch at :1447. ListingsPane already has the vocabulary — render it as a DS `Pill tone="warning"` via the existing readinessMeta() so the chip, the pane and the sheet cannot disagree, and add a `Closed since <date> by <actor>` KeyValue row beside the existing Offer row. (2) Expose the verb as two GridActions in channelActions.ts — `listing-pause` / `listing-resume`, scope SELECTION — routed through a new coordinate-scoped studio route POST /api/products/:id/studio/presence?channel=&market=&accountId=&aliasKey= with body { expectedVersion, verb }, mirroring the optimistic-concurrency contract writeProjectionInclusion already enforces (family-projection.service.ts:1595-1600). The handler delegates to closeMarketOffers/reopenMarketOffers after adding channelConnectionId + aliasKey to its loadRow filter. They surface as items of the sheet's ONE ⋯ overflow (CH.1: scope verbs are items, never buttons) and on the row menu, inheriting registry.ts's COLLECT→PREFLIGHT→CONFIRM→RUN and useActionConfirm's itemised consequences. The preflight must carry the service's own SKIPPED_FBA refusal per row rather than a generic count.

#### The studio's only per-variant channel removal is a local-only flag, and its copy — "the record is kept, so <ItemID> is not lost" — reads as a takedown while the variation stays buyable

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A jacket family is live on eBay IT as one multi-variation ItemID 257584954808 covering Colore × Taglia. Size XXS sells out permanently. The operator opens the studio on scope eBay · IT, goes to Variants, and unticks XXS in the Included column. The row greys out, the Excluded chip goes to 1, and the state line says "Excluded from this listing. The record is kept, so 257584954808 is not lost."

##### What happens today
XXS is still on sale on eBay. writeProjectionInclusion (family-projection.service.ts:1630-1667) runs one Serializable transaction that bumps the parent's version and calls setVariationExcluded, which is a raw UPDATE setting `variationExcluded = true, isPublished = false` on the child ChannelListing (family-projection.service.ts:415-424). Nothing else. The route handler states it outright: "Include / exclude. A LOCAL-RECORD write: it calls no marketplace and enqueues no sync row" (product-studio.routes.ts:226-228). Removing a live eBay variation needs ReviseFixedPriceItem with Delete=true (implemented at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:169-203, unreachable from the studio — /usr/bin/grep for flat-file/delete over _studio returns rc=1 against a 41-file fetch( control). The misleading half is the copy: the excluded branch (family-projection.service.ts:546-551) explains only that the local record survives; the adjacent 'listed' branch at :566-570 already knows how to state a channel fact honestly ("Live on this channel, with publishing turned off for this listing"), so the vocabulary exists and simply was not applied here. A sold-out variation left buyable is a defect-rate and cancellation event on eBay, and on Amazon the same exclusion leaves a child ASIN live under the parent.

##### Proposed fix
(1) Copy, today: when the excluded child carries an externalId OR its parent listing does, the reason must lead with the channel fact — "Excluded here. 257584954808 still offers this variation on eBay until the listing is revised." One string in family-projection.service.ts:546-551, alongside the existing 'listed' phrasing. Render it as a DS `Banner tone="warning"` above the grid when `counts.excluded > 0 && page.listing.externalId` — ChannelProjection.tsx:360-367 already mounts a Banner in that slot for write errors. (2) Capability: extend the same POST /studio/presence route from SC-DR-3 with `scope: 'variant', childIds: string[]`, so "Remove from this listing" is a real verb — eBay ReviseFixedPriceItem Delete=true with the qty-0 fallback already written at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:169-203, Amazon a child-ASIN offer close. Register it as a `danger: true` GridAction on the projection grid with ConfirmLevel 'type-to-confirm' and the phrase set to the child's real SKU (ActionConfirm's rule: never the word DELETE). Note that menuAdapters.tsx:75-91 drops GridAction.danger, so the item needs the selection-bar rendering path or a DS-GAPS entry for MenuItemDef tone.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens the studio on a jacket family, selects the discontinued child GALE-JACKET-XXS-BLK on the master sheet and chooses "Delete child…". The confirmation refuses: "This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record." They look for the resolving verb. It does not exist on any studio surface.

familyActions.ts:454 raises the refusal from the preflight, correctly keyed on liveness by externalListingId rather than status — listingRisk.ts:41-49 records that PES.3 found 20 non-ACTIVE eBay rows carrying real ItemIDs — and the server repeats it at product-relationship.service.ts:123-128. The studio then offers nothing that clears the condition. I swept the whole _studio tree with /usr/bin/grep for sync-control|listing-recovery|/recover|flat-file/remove|flat-file/delete|bulk-hard-delete|CLOSE_OFFER|REOPEN_OFFER|publish-amazon|delist|unpublish|relist: rc=1, against a positive control of 41 files containing fetch( and only two DELETE calls in the entire tree (useCellFormulas.ts:213, a formula; familyOps.ts:131, this very child delete). The header offers only PublishMenu, which is a link out to /products/:id/list-wizard on master and a tab switch on a channel (PublishMenu.tsx:13-19). The channel ⋯ offers three read-only items (ChannelSheet.tsx:2002-2035). The channel row verbs are three, two of which refuse every live row (channelActions.ts:404). So the operator's only exit is to leave the studio, soft-delete the whole product from /products, open the bin, and hard-delete with channelAction — which takes down every market on every channel, is documented as bulk-only and whole-product (products-catalog.routes.ts:1849-1856 has no channel or marketplace filter), skips every DRAFT row so wizard-created listings never get delisted (:1851), and on Amazon 'unpublish' silently performs a hard SP-API delete (channel-delist.service.ts:150-162).

##### Proposed fix
ONE capability closes this and every variant above. STATE MODEL — one `presence` per coordinate (product × channel × market × account × alias), with `variationExcluded` as a per-child modifier: ABSENT → DRAFT → LIVE ⇄ PAUSED (identity kept, fully reversible) → ENDED (identity kept, snapshot captured) → PURGED (identity released). Five verbs, each defined per channel: pause = Amazon patchPurchasableOffer delete (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:165-172) / eBay ReviseFixedPriceItem qty 0 / Shopify status DRAFT; resume = replay offerCloseSnapshot; end = captureSnapshot FIRST (listing-snapshot.service.ts:117, which today has exactly one caller) then set listingStatus ENDED keeping externalListingId — never the ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1960 behaviour of nulling the ItemID; relist = replay the snapshot (Amazon: surface the client's own ~30-day same-SKU cooldown warning from amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1121-1123; eBay: SellSimilarItem); purge = release the identity. API — POST /api/products/:id/studio/presence?channel=&market=&accountId=&aliasKey= with { expectedVersion, verb, scope: 'listing'|'variant', childIds?, schedule?: { at } }, sitting beside the projection routes and reusing their version-conflict contract (family-projection.service.ts:1595-1600). GET on the same path returns the current presence + what each verb would do, so the preflight is the server's answer rather than a client guess. UI — register the five as GridActions in channelActions.ts (SELECTION scope, plus a contextOf('listing') for the whole coordinate), so they inherit the registry's COLLECT→PREFLIGHT→CONFIRM→RUN order and useActionConfirm's itemised-consequences rendering; end/purge carry danger:true and ConfirmLevel 'type-to-confirm' with the real SKU as the phrase. They appear as items of the sheet's ONE ⋯ overflow and on the row menu (CH.1: scope verbs are items, never buttons), identical on both scopes. Because menuAdapters.tsx:75-91 drops GridAction.danger, file a DS-GAPS entry for a `tone` field on MenuItemDef or render the danger items through the BulkActionBar selection path. Finally, once 'end' exists, familyActions.ts:454's refusal should name it — "Remove it from eBay · IT first" with the verb one click away — instead of describing a task with no tool.

[critical]verifiedALLdata integrity risk

#### The "delete it from the channel too" option silently does nothing: the delist queue rows are destroyed by FK cascade inside the same transaction that creates them

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has finished with a jacket that is live as ASIN B0ABC on Amazon DE and ItemID 256789012345 on eBay IT. They soft-delete it from /products, open the bin, tick it, and choose Permanently delete with the channel action set to "Delete on channel" (or the default "Unpublish"). The modal says the listings will be taken down. The product disappears from Nexus. The jacket stays for sale on Amazon DE and eBay IT — forever, and now with no local record that it exists.

##### What happens today
POST /products/bulk-hard-delete builds the delist jobs INSIDE the transaction: `tx.outboundSyncQueue.createManyAndReturn` with `productId: l.productId` and `channelListingId: l.id` (products-catalog.routes.ts:1880-1898). Twenty lines later the same transaction runs `tx.product.deleteMany` (:1973). OutboundSyncQueue carries BOTH FKs as `onDelete: Cascade` — `productId` (schema.prisma:6822-6823) and `channelListingId` (schema.prisma:6825-6826) — and the live SQL agrees (migrations/20260502_phase31b_channellisting_marketplace/migration.sql:233-239, both `ON DELETE CASCADE`). So at COMMIT every delist row it just created is deleted: directly by the Product FK, and again by the ChannelListing FK when ChannelListing cascades from Product (schema.prisma:1515). `fireOutboundJobs(delistFireEntries, …)` then runs post-commit (:2001-2003) against ids that no longer exist; the worker's first act is `prisma.outboundSyncQueue.findUnique({ where: { id: queueId } })` and on miss it logs 'Queue record not found' and throws (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:105-111) — before the delist branch at :141 is ever reached. The route's own comment asserts the opposite premise in so many words: "by then the local Product + ChannelListing are gone, but the queue rows still carry productId + externalListingId + channel so the adapters can finish the channel-side work" (:1845-1850). The worker repeats the same false premise at :134-140. The only operator-visible signal is `channelCascadeEnqueued: N` in the response — a count of rows that no longer exist.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, and the first is not optional. (1) BREAK THE FK for delist rows: the delist job must not be a child of the thing it is deleting. Either create the delist rows with `productId: null, channelListingId: null` and carry `{ productId, channelListingId, channel, marketplace, externalListingId, externalParentId }` in `payload` (the worker's delist branch already reads `queueRecord.externalListingId` and `queueRecord.payload` and needs nothing else, bullmq-sync.worker.ts:142-150), or move both FK columns to `onDelete: SetNull` for this model. Nullable `productId`/`channelListingId` is already the schema's shape (schema.prisma:6822,6825), so option one is a route change with no migration. (2) VERIFY THE CLAIM BEFORE IT IS MADE: the response should report `channelCascadeDispatched` read back AFTER the commit (`outboundSyncQueue.count({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })`), not the pre-commit create count, and the UI must refuse to say "listings will be removed from the channel" on a zero. Give the delist rows a `holdUntil` of +5 minutes (the field exists, schema.prisma:6857-6859, and the grace window is what makes an Undo possible) and render the receipt with the DS `ToastProvider` — `message` is a `ReactNode` (components/Toast.tsx:10,15) so an "Undo delist" button can ride inside it with a longer `duration`, which is exactly the case that field's comment was written for.

#### Both the hard-delete preflight and the delist cascade key liveness on listingStatus, which the studio's own code documents as the wrong test — live ASINs and ItemIDs are orphaned with no warning

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator lists a jacket to Amazon IT through the listing wizard; it succeeds and the child SKUs get real ASINs. Months later the product is retired: soft-delete, bin, Permanently delete. The confirmation modal's preflight panel shows no channel listings at all, so the channel-action radio auto-selects "Local-only" (the deliberate "safer" default). The operator agrees. A row outside those two statuses is invisible to both — no warning, no delist. The studio already knows this is wrong and says so at length: listingRisk.ts:9-17 records that "PES.3 found a family where **all 20 non-ACTIVE eBay rows still carried a real ItemID**" and that "A confirm keyed on status would have described 20 live listings as safe to destroy"; `isLiveOnChannel` is `externalListingId !== ''` and nothing else (listingRisk.ts:46-48). Every listing the wizard ever created is therefore excluded from both the warning and the takedown. Worse, the preflight's emptiness drives the default: `setChannelAction(data.channelListings.length === 0 ? 'none' : 'unpublish')` (BulkActionBar.tsx:1114-1116) — so the surface that failed to look is the surface that decides not to act.

##### Proposed fix
Promote `listingRisk.ts`'s rule to the one definition and consume it on both sides. Move `isLiveOnChannel`/`classifyListings` into packages/shared and have the preflight and the cascade select on `externalListingId: { not: null, notIn: [''] }` with NO status clause — status becomes reported context, never the test, exactly as that file's header prescribes. The preflight response should then group by `(channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey)` and name the external id per row, so the confirmation itemises "Amazon IT — DRAFT, B0ABC123" instead of counting. Render it with the DS destructive contract rather than the current hand-rolled panel: `ActionImpact.findings` already has exactly the `{ rowId, label, severity }` shape for this (grid/actions/registry.ts:79-120) and `useActionConfirm` itemises consequences instead of counting them. Add a server-side assertion that refuses the purge when a live external id exists and `channelAction === 'none'` — a silent orphan must not be reachable by a default.
