Wizard writes no status — submission.service.ts:1472-1485 `create: { …, externalListingId: asin, platformProductId: asin }` with no `listingStatus`; the parent upsert at :1422-1441 likewise. /usr/bin/grep "listingStatus" across apps/api/src/services/listing-wizard/ hits only tests and product-presets.ts. Schema default is `listingStatus String @default("DRAFT")` at schema.prisma:1616 (cited 1615, off by one) inside `model ChannelListing` (starts :1509), which cascades on Product delete (:1516 `onDelete: Cascade`).
5. Emptiness drives the default — BulkActionBar.tsx:1114-1116 `setChannelAction(data.channelListings.length === 0 ? 'none' : 'unpublish')`; and the modal only renders the listings warning when `hasListings` (:1143, :1215), as counts grouped by channel (:1134-1141), never external ids — hand-rolled Tailwind panel, no DS destructive pattern.
6. The purge really orphans: :1970 `tx.product.deleteMany`, no server-side guard anywhere in the handler refusing `channelAction: 'none'` when a live external id exists; body default is `channelAction ?? 'none'` (:1786).

Refutation attempts that FAILED to kill it:
- Another surface that catches these rows? Only one consumer of the preflight exists (/usr/bin/grep "hard-delete-preflight" → BulkActionBar.tsx:1104 and the route itself). No alternative preflight, no second warning path.
- Is the DRAFT-with-external-id state hypothetical? No — it is manufactured by a running cron: ebay-status-reconcile.job.ts:50-54 maps eBay `UNPUBLISHED` and every unknown status to `'DRAFT'`, and :219-236 updates only `listingStatus`, keeping `externalListingId` (it even logs the retained ItemID). So the 20 eBay rows are a reproducible class, independent of the wizard.
- Does something later flip wizard rows to ACTIVE? The Amazon linkers at amazon.routes.ts:1256-1274 and :1442-1462 set `listingStatus: 'ACTIVE'` only in the `create` branch — an existing DRAFT row is updated without touching status. listing-reconciliation.service.ts:503-537 does set ACTIVE but is an operator-confirmed reconciliation flow on the primary (aliasKey '') row, not an automatic sweep of wizard-created child rows.

Mis-statement to correct: "Every listing the wizard ever created is therefore excluded from both" overreaches — wizard rows land on DRAFT and stay there unless republished through a surface that does write ACTIVE (marketplaces.routes.ts:1085/1107, amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3458, ebay-variation-push.service.ts:2046). The defect does not depend on that clause: the eBay reconcile cron alone guarantees a steady supply of live-ItemID/non-ACTIVE rows.
The direction is right — one definition (`isLiveOnChannel`) promoted to shared and consumed by both the preflight and the cascade, with status demoted to reported context — and the DS/itemisation point is well founded (the panel at BulkActionBar.tsx:1130-1230 is hand-rolled Tailwind and reports counts, never ids). Three corrections:
1. `externalListingId: { not: null, notIn: [''] }` does not reproduce the rule: listingRisk.ts:37 trims, so a whitespace-only id ('   ') is local per the studio rule but live per that Prisma clause. Either normalise on write or post-filter with the shared predicate after a `{ not: null }` select — do not let a second, subtly different definition appear on the server, which is the exact drift the finding is about.
2. Grouping by `(channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey)` requires the preflight's `select` (:1685-1691) to add `channelConnectionId` and `aliasKey`; it currently selects neither, and the response mapper (:1733-1738) collapses `marketplace ?? region`, which would merge two distinct accounts' rows under one label.
3. The proposed server-side refusal (`channelAction === 'none'` + live external id → reject) is the right rail but must not break the cron: purge-soft-deleted-products.job and any back-compat caller rely on the `channelAction ?? 'none'` default at :1786. Make the refusal explicit-opt-out (a `confirmedOrphan: true` flag the modal sets only after showing the itemised ids), or the first deploy will start failing the scheduled purge.
Also note the cascade drops ETSY unconditionally (:1871-1874, SUPPORTED list) — even a corrected filter leaves Etsy rows orphaned silently; the confirmation should say so rather than count them as handled.

[critical]verifiedALLmissing capability

#### There is no permanent-removal verb of any kind in the studio: two DELETE calls exist in the whole tree, neither of them removes a listing from a channel or a market

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket live on Amazon IT and Amazon DE. IT is being retired permanently — wrong compliance category, it must not come back and must not sit there as a suppressed offer. They are already in the studio on the Amazon · IT channel scope, looking at the listing. They want "remove this listing from IT, keep DE". Nothing on the screen does it, and nothing on the screen tells them where it is done.

##### What happens today
Nothing, on every surface I opened. `/usr/bin/grep -rn "method: 'DELETE'"` over the whole `_studio/` tree returns exactly two hits: `useCellFormulas.ts:213` (delete a cell formula) and `familyOps.ts:131` (the generic `del()` helper, used only by `deleteVariant`, :157-158). Positive control: 41 files in that tree contain `fetch(`. On a channel scope the header's PublishMenu returns `null` outright when the sheet tab is open (PublishMenu.tsx:12) and otherwise only switches tab (:13-15). The channel sheet's ⋯ overflow is Cell details, one "Check Information" per alias, and "+ Add listing alias" (ChannelSheet.tsx:2002-2026) — no archive, no end, no delete. `channelActions` declares three verbs total — open-record, offer-toggle, broadcast (channelActions.ts:403-406) — and the two that write refuse every live alias ("wave-1 channel verbs are preview-only", :249-251, :267-269). The one archive endpoint that exists, `DELETE /products/:id/aliases/:aliasId` (product-studio.routes.ts:990-1000), is deliberately not wired, and the client file says why: "Archiving (`DELETE`) is deliberately NOT wired here" (useChannelSheet.ts:438-439) — and it would only archive the local mirror anyway (listing-alias.service.ts:193-197), making no marketplace call. The Owner's dead end is literal: the studio's only hard delete, `delete-variant`, refuses with "This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record." (familyActions.ts:454, echoing the server guard at product-relationship.service.ts:128-129) while offering no verb anywhere in the studio to resolve it. A parent cannot be deleted at all — `delete-variant` disables on `row.isParent` with "a parent is removed by demoting it" (familyActions.ts:427) and `demoteProduct` deletes nothing (product-relationship.service.ts:114-121).

##### Proposed fix
Add ONE channel-scope verb family to `channelActions.ts`, registered exactly like the existing three so it inherits the DS COLLECT→PREFLIGHT→CONFIRM→RUN order (registry.ts:203-215) and appears in the sheet ⋯, the row menu and the selection bar with no extra wiring. Three levels, worded by consequence rather than by verb: (a) "Close this market's offer" — reversible, already fully built server-side as `closeMarketOffers`/`reopenMarketOffers` with a verbatim `offerCloseSnapshot` replay, reachable only from /fulfillment today; (b) "End the listing on this market" — the existing `dispatchChannelDelist('unpublish')`; (c) "Remove permanently" — `dispatchChannelDelist('delete')`. Back it with a studio-scoped route `POST /api/products/:id/listings/:channel/:marketplace/delist` taking `{ action: 'close'|'end'|'remove', accountId, aliasId, expectedVersion }` — `accountId`/`aliasId` are load-bearing: the existing removal services filter only `(productId, channel, marketplace)` and would wipe every account and alias on the coordinate. Preflight returns an `ActionImpact` whose `confirmPhrase` is the row's real SKU (registry.ts:117: "A SKU, never 'DELETE'") for level (c) and `level: 'confirm'` for (a). The refusal on `delete-variant` then stops being a dead end: its `unavailable` string can name the verb that resolves it, because one will exist on the same registry. The wave-1 preview-only refusal must be lifted for this family or the verb ships inert.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/useCellFormulas.ts:213
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/familyOps.ts:131
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/familyOps.ts:157-158
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/PublishMenu.tsx:12-19
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/ChannelSheet.tsx:2002-2026
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts:403-406
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts:249-251
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/useChannelSheet.ts:438-439
- apps/api/src/routes/product-studio.routes.ts:985-1000
- apps/api/src/services/pim/listing-alias.service.ts:193-197
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/familyActions.ts:427
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/familyActions.ts:454
- apps/api/src/services/pim/product-relationship.service.ts:114-129

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find any removal verb anywhere in the studio tree.

CONFIRMED BY MY OWN READS:
- I re-ran the set claim with /usr/bin/grep (not the ugrep shell function): `/usr/bin/grep -rn "method: *'DELETE'" apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/` returns exactly two hits — useCellFormulas.ts:214 (deletes a cell FORMULA via /api/pim/formulas/product/...) and familyOps.ts:131 (the generic `del()` helper). Positive control in the same run: 41 files in that tree contain `fetch(`. `del()` has exactly one caller, `deleteVariant` → `DELETE /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children/:childId` (familyOps.ts:157-158) — a local child record, not a channel/market listing.
- PublishMenu.tsx:12 is verbatim `if (scope !== MASTER_SCOPE && tab === 'sheet') return null`; :13-15 only calls `setTab('sheet')`; :17-18 links to the list-wizard on master scope. No removal.
- channelActions.ts:403-406 registers exactly three verbs: `openRecordAction`, `offerToggle`, `broadcastToListings`. The wave-1 refusals are real: the preflight `unavailable` "…wave-1 verbs do not send to a channel. Preview only." (~:248-251) and the run guard "Refused: this would change a live listing, and wave-1 channel verbs are preview-only." (~:261) — and offerToggle's write is only `PATCH /api/products/:id/offer-availability`, not a delist.
- ChannelSheet.tsx:2008-2033 (the `overflowItems` useMemo) contains only per-alias "Check Information"/"Review synchronization" and "+ Add listing alias". No archive/end/delete item.
- useChannelSheet.ts:442-443 comment verbatim: "Archiving (`DELETE`) is deliberately NOT wired here". The server route product-studio.routes.ts:990-1000 exists and calls `archiveAlias`, and listing-alias.service.ts:193-197 only flips `ProductListingAlias.status` to 'ARCHIVED' — no marketplace call.
- familyActions.ts:427 disables delete on a parent ("a parent is removed by demoting it"); :454 refuses with "This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record." — the identical string is the server guard at product-relationship.service.ts:128-129. demoteProduct (product-relationship.service.ts:109-121) deletes nothing; it clears parentId/isParent.
- The drawer cannot invent a verb: RecordActions.tsx:34-58 renders only `actionsFor(actions, ROW, …)` from the lane-declared list, so the drawer surface inherits the same three channel verbs.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
- No delist-shaped control anywhere in _studio: `/usr/bin/grep -rniE "delist|unpublish|withdraw|retire|archive|takedown|end listing|close.*offer"` over the tree returns only image-archive downloads, restore-plan wording, and prose comments.
- No writable listing-status escape hatch in the channel sheet: `listingStatus` appears only as a read field (types.ts:383, :475) and a display in AliasBandCell.tsx:132.
- No pointer out: the only `href`s in StudioHeader/StudioSubheader/StudioBar/navigation are "/products" (StudioHeader.tsx:52) and the parent's studio (:75).

WHERE THE FINDING OVERREACHES (why I corrected the title/severity): removal is NOT missing from the application, only from the studio, and the finding never says so. apps/web/src/app/products/ebay-flat-file/EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:2031,2091-2106,4065 drives real `delete-product`/`delete-family` intents whose server side (apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:33,212,278-280,384-414 via apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:3795-3796) soft-deletes the product and calls `dispatchChannelDelist`; the Amazon flat-file editor carries a `record_action = delete` path armed by typing DELETE (apps/web/src/app/products/amazon-flat-file/ImportWizardModal.tsx:355-400, guarded server-side at apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:805-807); and Amazon per-market offer close exists at apps/api/src/routes/sync-control.routes.ts:818-819 (`closeMarketOffers`/`reopenMarketOffers`). So the defect is a studio gap plus a discoverability gap, not an app-wide absence — the sentence "The Owner's dead end is literal" is true only within the studio.

FIX CRITIQUE: sound in shape, but see fixCritique — one of its named building blocks is the one thing I could not confirm is safely reusable at market scope.
The registry-integration half is right and cheap: `channelActions()` returns a plain array (channelActions.ts:403-406) and the drawer/row-menu/selection-bar all read it through `actionsFor` (drawer/RecordActions.tsx:53), so a fourth verb genuinely does appear on every surface with no extra wiring, and the wave-1 blanket refusal does have to be lifted for the family or the verb ships inert (channelActions.ts ~:249, ~:261).

Three problems the proposal understates:
1. It presents `closeMarketOffers` as "reversible, already fully built" for level (a). On Amazon EU that is contradicted by the app's own operator copy: sync-control-shared.ts:139 states Amazon keeps ONE quantity per SKU across IT/DE/FR/ES and that a partial-market action applies to every EU market, telling operators to close the offer in Seller Central for a single market. A "Close this market's offer" button in the IT scope must be proven not to touch DE before it ships, or it does exactly the thing the Owner's scenario forbids. I did not open amazon-market-offer.service.ts, so treat this as the first thing to measure, not as a defect claim.
2. Level (c) "Remove permanently" is mapped to `dispatchChannelDelist('delete')`, but the only proven consumer of that service is the BullMQ worker (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:18,142) driven from the eBay flat-file delete service. Whether an Amazon 'delete' arm exists and what it does was not established by the finding and I did not verify it; a level that cannot be shown to reach Amazon must not be offered on an Amazon scope.
3. The `accountId`/`aliasId` warning is the strongest part of the proposal and should be a hard precondition, not a parameter note — `channelActions` already degrades every non-open-record verb to disabled when `deps.accountSpecific` is set (channelActions.ts:405), which is evidence the account dimension is unsolved on this surface today.

Also worth adding to the fix: the `delete-variant` refusal string is duplicated client- and server-side (familyActions.ts:454 and product-relationship.service.ts:128-129), so naming the new verb in it means editing both, or the server copy keeps printing the dead end.

[critical]verifiedEBAYdata integrity risk

#### A permanent removal captures nothing: the marketplace id is nulled, the snapshot/override/offer history cascades away, and the one field designed to remember the old listing has zero code behind it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A seasonal jacket comes off eBay IT in October with the intention of relisting it next spring. The listing is ended through the eBay flat-file surface. In March the operator opens the studio to put it back and wants the old ItemID — for the watcher count, the sales history, the "sell similar" that preserves ranking. It is gone, and nothing in the system ever wrote it down.

##### What happens today
The eBay end path sets `{ listingStatus: 'ENDED', offerActive: false, externalListingId: null }` (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1958-1961 for the parent, :1980-1983 for a variation) and the operator-facing message says it plainly: "ItemID retired — a future publish creates a new one" (:1963). The ItemID is written to no snapshot, no audit row, no recovery event on that path. `EbayListingIndex.relistedFromItemId` exists for precisely this (schema.prisma:14107) and has ZERO code references — `/usr/bin/grep -rn "relistedFromItemId" apps/api/src apps/web/src packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma` returns only the schema line itself; positive control: 69 `endedAt` hits across apps/api/src, and EbayListingIndex is referenced by 5+ services. Two second-order effects follow. First, nulling `externalListingId` makes the row pass `assertCanDeleteRelationshipProduct` (product-relationship.service.ts:123-129, which tests exactly `externalListingId` OR `isPublished`), so the studio's `delete-variant` will now hard-delete it — and the cascade takes `ChannelListingSnapshot` (schema.prisma:1888), `ChannelListingOverride` (:1994), `Offer` (:2285), `ChannelListingImage` (:2412) and every `OutboundSyncQueue` row with it. Second, on the whole-product purge the images are not cascaded but explicitly destroyed: `tx.productImage.deleteMany` (products-catalog.routes.ts:1947), alongside marketplaceSyncs (:1950), listings (:1952) and stockLogs (:1954). The only thing that survives a purge is the AuditLog row, written before the cascade (:1906) and holding `{ sku, name, deletedAt }` — no channel, no marketplace, no ASIN, no ItemID. `captureSnapshot` is called on none of these paths.

##### Proposed fix
Make capture a precondition of every removal, not a separate manual endpoint. Before any path writes `externalListingId: null`, hard-deletes a ChannelListing, or purges a Product, write one `ChannelListingSnapshot` via the existing `captureSnapshot` (pim/listing-snapshot.service.ts:117) plus one AuditLog row per COORDINATE — `{ channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey, externalListingId, externalParentId, listingStatus, offerCloseSnapshot }` — since AuditLog has no FK to Product and is the only thing that survives (proved by :1906 already relying on that). Stop nulling `externalListingId` on end: the row is already discriminated by `listingStatus: 'ENDED'`, and keeping the id is what makes a relist, a shared-ItemID guard and the studio's own `isLiveOnChannel` test work. Then wire `EbayListingIndex.relistedFromItemId` to the relist path, or delete the column — a schema-dark field is a promise the UI cannot keep. Surface the result in the studio as a "Previous listings" group in the record drawer's ListingsPane using the DS `SummaryTable`/`KeyValue` components, so "what was here before" is answerable on the coordinate where the operator is standing.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1957-1963
- apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1980-1985
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:14107
- apps/api/src/services/pim/product-relationship.service.ts:123-129
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1888
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1994
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:2285
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:2412
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1906-1930
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1947-1954

##### Verifier
The core defect is real and I confirmed every cited line myself, but three of the finding's supporting claims are over-stated and one is wrong, so it must be re-scoped.

CONFIRMED FROM CODE I OPENED:
1. eBay end path nulls the ItemID with zero capture. apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1960 (parent) and :1983 (variation) both write `{ listingStatus: 'ENDED', offerActive: false, externalListingId: null }`; the operator message at :1963 is verbatim "listing ended on this market (ItemID retired — a future publish creates a new one)". The route is live: it is inside `POST /ebay/flat-file/push` declared at :1493. `/usr/bin/grep -n "auditLog|captureSnapshot|channelListingSnapshot" apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts` returns nothing — no audit row, no snapshot on that file at all. The author's own comment at :1841-1844 states it: "'end' → ... the ItemID is lost and a later publish mints a new one".
2. `relistedFromItemId` is schema-dark. packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:14108 (finding said 14107, off by one). `/usr/bin/grep -rn --exclude-dir=node_modules` over apps/api/src, apps/web/src, packages returns exactly two hits: the schema line and the DDL at packages/database/prisma/migrations/20260703_e2_ebay_ads_data_layer/migration.sql:155. No reader, no writer. Positive control in the same run: 69 `endedAt` hits in apps/api/src. The finding's own grep missed the migration hit but the conclusion holds.
3. captureSnapshot is on none of these paths. Its only production caller is apps/api/src/routes/product-studio.routes.ts:918 (a manual endpoint); the service is apps/api/src/services/pim/listing-snapshot.service.ts:119, and `SNAPSHOT_FIELDS` (:70-83) plus `captureState` (:92-98) deliberately EXCLUDE externalListingId — so even a manual snapshot taken before an end would not preserve the ItemID.
4. The purge claims are accurate. products-catalog.routes.ts:1905-1935 writes the AuditLog `before: { sku, name, deletedAt }` with `metadata: { source, channelAction }` — no channel, marketplace, ASIN or ItemID — before the cascade; :1947-1962 explicitly deleteMany productImage / marketplaceSync / listing / stockLog / fbaShipmentItem / listingWizard, then `tx.product.deleteMany` at :1969. And worse than the finding says: the delist rows enqueued at :1878-1897 DO carry externalListingId, but OutboundSyncQueue.productId is `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:6823-6824), so they are destroyed by the same transaction that created them — `fireOutboundJobs(delistFireEntries)` at :2003 fires post-commit against row ids that no longer exist.
5. Cascade lines check out (±2): ChannelListingSnapshot schema.prisma:1894 onDelete: Cascade; ChannelListingOverride :1998; Offer :2285; ChannelListingImage :2412.
6. No relist / prior-listing surface exists in the studio. `/usr/bin/grep -rn "relist|Relist|previous listing"` over apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio returns only unrelated hits (image "Previous", pagination "Previous listings" in import/ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:184, a test string). The drawer's ListingsPane has no previous-listing group.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG OR OVER-STATED (why it is re-titled and downgraded):
A. Second-order effect #1 is wrong as stated. `assertCanDeleteRelationshipProduct` (product-relationship.service.ts:123-129) tests `externalListingId != null OR isPublished == true`, and ChannelListing.isPublished defaults to TRUE (schema.prisma:1630). The eBay end path never touches isPublished — `/usr/bin/grep -n isPublished apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts` returns ZERO hits. So nulling externalListingId does NOT by itself open the hard delete (catalog.routes.ts:1837 → `tx.product.delete` at :1838); it only does for rows born `isPublished: false` (family-projection.service.ts:1644, catalog-transfer.service.ts:177, images/product-media.service.ts:74). Conditional, not automatic. Contrast the Amazon recovery path, which does both: listings/recovery.service.ts:337-350 sets `isPublished: false` AND deliberately preserves the ASIN for DELETE_RELIST_SAME.
B. "Nothing in the system ever wrote it down" is false. The ItemID minted at publish is persisted in durable push history: ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:2736 pushes `{ status: 'PUSHED', message: 'Listed', itemId }` into perRowResults, written to EbayPushJob.perSkuResults at :2827/:2836 (schema.prisma:8779, documented "inspectable forever"), readable via GET /ebay/flat-file/pushes at :2878. Independently, EbayListingIndex retains the itemId row and only stamps `endedAt` when the listing vanishes (marketing/ebay-listing-index.service.ts:255) — the id survives there too. Neither is product-coordinate-scoped nor surfaced in the studio, which is the real gap; but the record is not absent.
C. The scenario itself already has a correct path the auditor did not look for. The same Action column offers 'deactivate' — "live offer quantity set to 0 (ItemID kept)" (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1841, branch at :1874-1888, result message "deactivated — quantity 0 on the live offer (ItemID kept)"). The October-jacket-relisted-in-spring case is served today by deactivate, not end. That does not excuse `end` discarding the id silently, but it removes the "operator has no way to keep the ItemID" premise.

Net: a genuine, citable gap — no removal path captures the coordinate identity, the field designed to remember it is dead, and nothing in the studio can answer "what was here before" — but not the unrecoverable data loss the title asserts. Downgraded critical → high.
The fix is directionally right but two parts need correcting before anyone implements it. (1) "Stop nulling externalListingId on end" cannot be done in isolation: the row is NOT already discriminated safely, because isPublished defaults true (schema.prisma:1630) and the end path never clears it — keep the id AND set isPublished:false in the same write, mirroring recovery.service.ts:337-350, or the delete guard and every `isPublished: true` reader (sync-control.routes.ts:636, :713) will treat an ended listing as live. (2) captureSnapshot as proposed would not capture the ItemID at all: SNAPSHOT_FIELDS (listing-snapshot.service.ts:70-83) and captureState (:92-98) deliberately exclude externalListingId, with a comment explaining why a restore must never write it back. Capturing identity needs a separate field on the snapshot row (or the AuditLog row), not a call to the existing capture. (3) The AuditLog-per-coordinate idea is sound and cheap — products-catalog.routes.ts:1905 already proves the pattern survives the cascade. (4) A "Previous listings" group in ListingsPane should read from something product-linked; EbayPushJob.perSkuResults is a global time-ordered log with no productId, so it is not a usable backing store without an index — EbayListingIndex.productIds is the better source, and wiring relistedFromItemId there is coherent with how that table is already maintained (ebay-listing-index.service.ts:255).

[high]verifiedALLdesign inconsistency

#### The only permanent-delete UI in the product area is legacy Tailwind, sits on a different page from the studio, and violates the DS's own type-to-confirm rule by asking the operator to type "DELETE"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The operator finishes editing a jacket in the studio, decides it should be permanently gone, and has to leave the studio entirely: back to /products, find the row, soft-delete it, switch to the bin filter, re-find it, select it, and only then reach a permanent-delete dialog that looks nothing like the studio they just left — a rose-bordered Tailwind modal asking them to type the word DELETE.

##### What happens today
`POST /products/bulk-hard-delete` has exactly one caller in apps/web: `products/_components/BulkActionBar.tsx:337` (the other `bulk-hard-delete` hits are the orders and fulfillment routes, which are different endpoints). Its `HardDeleteConfirmModal` (:1077) is hand-rolled legacy Tailwind throughout — `className="flex items-start gap-2 rounded border p-2 cursor-pointer"` with `border-rose-300 bg-rose-50 dark:border-rose-700` on the radio cards (:1288, :1303), `bg-amber-50 dark:bg-amber-950/40` warning panels (:1252, :1268), raw `<input type="radio">` (:1289) instead of the DS `RadioCard`, and a raw `<input type="text">` with `focus:ring-rose-500` (:1345) — and the confirm button carries `className="bg-rose-600 hover:bg-rose-700 …"` overriding whatever the DS Button would have done (:1355). The typed phrase is the literal string `DELETE`: `const armed = typed.trim().toUpperCase() === 'DELETE'` (:1127). The DS's destructive contract says the opposite in a comment written for exactly this case: "For `type-to-confirm`: exactly what must be typed. A SKU, never \"DELETE\"." (grid/actions/registry.ts:117). The DS pattern this modal should be is fully built and already used in the studio — `ActionImpact` with `consequences`/`sideEffects`/`findings` separated (registry.ts:79-120), `validateImpact` refusing a typed confirm with no phrase rather than downgrading it (:264-273), `useActionConfirm` rendering it (grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx:18) — and `familyActions.ts`'s delete-variant preflight (familyActions.ts:466-486) is a model of it.

##### Proposed fix
Rebuild the confirmation as a `GridAction` preflight so there is one destructive pattern in the product area rather than two. `preflight()` calls `/products/hard-delete-preflight` and returns `{ level: 'type-to-confirm', confirmPhrase: row.sku, title, consequences, sideEffects, findings: [per-coordinate live-listing rows] }`; `useActionConfirm` renders it and `validateImpact` guards it. The three-way channel action becomes a DS `RadioCard` group (primitives/index.ts) inside the impact body instead of three bespoke bordered labels, with a `Tone`-driven `Banner` for the open-orders / FBA / bundle warnings instead of hand-mixed amber and rose. The typed phrase becomes the product's real SKU — the phrase the DS demands and the one an operator cannot muscle-memory through on a multi-select. Then give the studio a single-product entry point to the same verb (see PD-3), so leaving the page becomes a choice rather than a requirement.

[medium]verifiedALLux defect

#### "Delete child…" renders identically to "Open record" in both of the studio's menus — both DS menu adapters drop GridAction.danger, contradicting the registry's own promise

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator right-clicks a variation row on the master sheet to open its record. The context menu lists Open record, Unlink…, Reparent…, Delete child… — four plain identical entries in one column. They are one mis-click away from the verb that hard-deletes a product row and cascades its channel listings, with no colour, no icon and no grouping to slow the hand down.

##### What happens today
`GridAction` declares `danger?: boolean` with the comment "Destructive verbs are grouped apart and rendered with danger tone by every adapter" (registry.ts:183-184). Neither adapter does either. `actionMenuItems` builds `{ id, label, title, disabled, onSelect }` and never reads `action.danger` (menuAdapters.tsx:75-90); `actionContextMenu` builds `{ name, tooltip, disabled, action }` and never reads it either (:150-168) — `/usr/bin/grep -n "danger" menuAdapters.tsx` returns nothing (rc=1), against a control of two hits for the same pattern in registry.ts. There is nowhere for it to go: `MenuItemDef` has `id, label, icon, disabled, onSelect, href, target, title, description, separator` and no tone or danger field (components/Menu.tsx:8-50), and there is no danger rule among the 20 `.nds-menu` declarations in the DS stylesheet (styles/components.css:693-781, 962, 2265, 2668-2670). Neither adapter emits a separator before destructive entries either, so "grouped apart" is unimplemented as well. Both of the studio's menus route through these adapters — MasterSheet.tsx:484 (`actionMenuItems`, the row ⋯) and :494 (`actionContextMenu`, right-click) — and `offered()` deliberately includes SELECTION-scope verbs in both (menuAdapters.tsx:55-58), which is exactly how `delete-variant` (scope SELECTION, `danger: true`, familyActions.ts:420-424) gets there. The bounding fact, which makes this a menu defect rather than a system-wide one: `FamilySelectionBar` DOES honour it — `variant={action.danger ? 'danger' : 'secondary'}` (FamilySelectionBar.tsx:54) — so the same verb is red on the bulk bar and neutral in the menu, two answers to one question. The toolbar ⋯ is unaffected: `useFamilyVerbs` filters to `FAMILY_SCOPE` only (FamilyBar.tsx:44, 86), so delete-variant does not appear there.

##### Proposed fix
Close the gap in the DS, not in the lane, or the next grid reopens it. Add `tone?: Tone` to `MenuItemDef` (components/Menu.tsx:8-50) — the vocabulary already exists at primitives/tone.ts and every other DS surface speaks it — with one `.nds-menu button[data-tone="danger"]` rule in styles/components.css using the tier-3 `--nds-danger` / `--nds-danger-soft` roles (never a raw ramp, per GOVERNANCE.md), contrast-checked at AA against `--nds-surface`. Then have both adapters pass `tone: action.danger ? 'danger' : undefined` and emit a `separator: true` before the first danger entry so "grouped apart" becomes true as well; AG's side takes `cssClasses` for the same effect. Add a DS-level ratchet (scripts/ds-conformance-guard.mjs is the natural host) asserting that every `GridAction` field the registry documents as rendered is in fact read by every adapter — this defect is a doc promising behaviour no code implements, which is a class this repo has been bitten by repeatedly.

- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/FamilySelectionBar.tsx:54
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/FamilyBar.tsx:44-96

##### Verifier
The mechanical core is confirmed line by line. registry.ts:183 declares `danger?: boolean` with the comment "Destructive verbs are grouped apart and rendered with danger tone by every adapter". Neither adapter honours it: actionMenuItems returns `{ id, label, title, disabled, onSelect }` (menuAdapters.tsx:75-90) and actionContextMenu returns `{ name, tooltip, disabled, action }` (menuAdapters.tsx:150-168); `/usr/bin/grep -n danger apps/web/src/design-system/grid/actions/menuAdapters.tsx` returns nothing, rc=1, against 2+ hits for the same pattern in registry.ts as a positive control. There is nowhere to put it: MenuItemDef carries id/label/icon/disabled/onSelect/href/target/title/description/separator and no tone or danger field (components/Menu.tsx:8-50), and `/usr/bin/grep -n nds-menu` over styles/components.css lists 20 declarations (693-781, 958-962, 2265, 2668-2670) with no danger rule among them. Neither adapter emits a separator before a destructive entry (the only 'separator' in actionContextMenu is the rule above AG's kept clipboard items, menuAdapters.tsx:171-172). Both studio menus do route through these adapters (MasterSheet.tsx:483-501, actionMenuItems and actionContextMenu), `offered()` does include SELECTION verbs (menuAdapters.tsx:55-58), delete-variant is `scope: SELECTION, danger: true` (familyActions.ts:420-424), FamilySelectionBar.tsx:54 does read `variant={action.danger ? 'danger' : 'secondary'}`, and useFamilyVerbs filters to FAMILY_SCOPE only (FamilyBar.tsx:44, 86-96) so the toolbar ⋯ is indeed unaffected. Severity corrected to low because the finding's own scenario overstates the exposure: 'Delete child…' is not a one-mis-click destructive verb — it carries a preflight that hard-refuses any row with a live or published listing (familyActions.ts:448) and otherwise returns level 'confirm' with itemised consequences and side effects (familyActions.ts:452-475), rendered by ActionConfirm; a mis-click opens a dialog, it does not delete. What remains is a real but cosmetic DS-contract gap (documented behaviour no adapter implements) plus one verb rendered two ways across two surfaces.
The DS-side fix is right and correctly placed in the engine rather than the lane. Two cautions: the AG side does not accept a `tone`, so `cssClasses` there means the danger styling is defined twice and can drift — the same two-builders trap the repo has been bitten by; and the proposed ds-conformance ratchet ("every GridAction field the registry documents as rendered is read by every adapter") cannot be derived from a doc comment — it would have to be a hand-maintained list of field names, which is itself a set claim that goes stale.

#### A multi-language market (Amazon BE: nl + fr) has no content-language control on Amazon/eBay scopes — the second language is unreachable, and the studio actively wipes a pinned one

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator sells the GALE-JACKET on Amazon Belgium, which serves Dutch and French. They open the studio, pick the Amazon chip and market BE, and want to write the French title and bullets for the Belgian listing — the Dutch ones are already there. They then also try the deep link a colleague sent them, .../studio?scope=AMAZON&market=BE&locale=fr.

##### What happens today
There is no control. StudioBar.tsx:36 renders the Content language Listbox on a channel scope only when the scope is SHOPIFY or ETSY; the master-scope Listbox (StudioBar.tsx:29-31) is the only other one, and a /usr/bin/grep over the whole _studio tree finds exactly two setLocale render sites (StudioBar.tsx:31 and :36). Meanwhile contracts.tsx:670-673 computes options.locales for AMAZON/EBAY from the ordered Marketplace.languages ([nl, fr] for AMAZON/BE — schema.prisma:1948-1950, docs/audits/2026-09-12-language-axis/step2/belgium-paths.md rows for scopes.ts:192 and contracts.tsx:670) and then never renders them, and contracts.tsx:675 can emit the banner 'Choose a supported content language for this destination: nl, fr' with no control on screen to choose with. The colleague's ?locale=fr link survives only until the operator touches the market switcher: contracts.tsx:931 forces the locale back to nextLocale = languages[0] = 'nl' for AMAZON/EBAY, directly contradicting its own comment two lines above ('Only re-default the locale when the operator had not pinned one'), and contracts.tsx:904 drops the locale entirely when the scope changes to Amazon/eBay. Worse, the write coordinate carries no language at all (contracts.tsx:954-956 — { channel, marketplace, accountId }), so text typed into the BE channel sheet is stored as a language-less legacy pin, which content-resolver.ts:174-176 honours ONLY when the requested language equals listing.languages[0] — i.e. it is silently Dutch, and invisible to a French read of the same market. The catalog export drawer, by contrast, does offer Belgium's fr (ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:195 over a server-built locale set), so a workbook can carry copy the sheet can neither show nor edit.

##### Proposed fix
Render the existing DS Listbox for every scope whose coordinate has more than one language — delete the ['SHOPIFY','ETSY'] condition at StudioBar.tsx:36 and gate on options.locales.length > 1 instead (the options are already computed at contracts.tsx:672; nothing new is needed on the wire). Show it inside the ScopeBar `right` slot, next to the market Listbox, so the coordinate reads 'Amazon · BE · Dutch'. Fix contracts.tsx:931 to honour a pinned localeParam for AMAZON/EBAY exactly as its comment claims, re-defaulting only when the pinned language is not in the new market's languages. Then make the write language-addressed: add `locale` to StudioCoordinate (contracts.tsx:954-956) and carry it as the `address.requested` the resolver already models (content-resolver.ts:8-11), so a BE pin is stored as {language: 'fr', coordinate} rather than as the language-less legacy pin content-resolver.ts:174-176 can only read back as Dutch. Until that write lands, the language Listbox for a second language must be shown disabled with a DS disabledReason naming why (ScopeBar's disabledReason contract, patterns/ScopeBar.tsx:45-52) rather than absent.

##### Evidence

- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/StudioBar.tsx:36

##### Verifier
The core defect is CONFIRMED from code I opened, but two load-bearing parts of the finding are mis-stated, which lowers severity and invalidates the proposed fix.

CONFIRMED
1. No content-language control on AMAZON/EBAY. StudioBar.tsx:36 gates the Listbox on `['SHOPIFY','ETSY'].includes(scope)`; StudioBar.tsx:29-31 is the only other one (master scope). `/usr/bin/grep -rn "setLocale"` over the whole `_studio` tree returns render sites only at StudioBar.tsx:31 and :36 (plus the definition at contracts.tsx:942 and its context plumbing at :156, :971, :974). `/usr/bin/grep` for `URL_KEYS.locale` shows the only deliberate writers are contracts.tsx:904/931/942 — no overflow menu, modal, or other tab writes it. STUDIO_TABS (types.ts:66) has no translations tab.
2. The options are computed and then never rendered: contracts.tsx:670 reads `Marketplace.languages` for the (scope, market) row; :671-673 builds `options.locales` for AMAZON/EBAY from it; :674-675 can emit "Choose a supported content language for this destination: …" with nothing on screen to choose with (server twin: information-locale.ts:11-12 accepts ANY of the market's languages for an Amazon/eBay read, so the second language is a real, reachable read coordinate).
3. The locale is dropped/reset exactly as claimed: contracts.tsx:904 clears `locale` when switching to AMAZON/EBAY; contracts.tsx:931 forces `nextLocale` (= defaultLocaleFor → languages[0], scopes.ts:192-195) for AMAZON/EBAY, contradicting its own comment at :930.
4. The read axis is genuinely locale-aware end to end, so the missing control is a real capability gap and not a no-op: studio-sheet.service.ts:922 normalizes `input.locale`, :1306-1308 and :1428-1429 emit requestedLocale/effectiveLocale/needsTranslation; product-studio.routes.ts:405/451 forwards `q.locale`.
5. content-resolver.ts:174-176 says what the finding says: a legacy (language-less) pin is honoured ONLY when `requested === normalizeLanguage(listing.languages[0])`.

MIS-STATED #1 — the write mechanism and therefore the fix. "The write coordinate carries no language at all (contracts.tsx:954-956)" is wrong about the wire. `StudioCoordinate` (contracts.tsx:954-956) is not what addresses the write: ChannelScopeTab.tsx:66 passes the studio `locale` straight into ChannelSheet, useChannelSheet.ts:74 puts it on the read URL, and useChannelSheet.ts:309 puts `locale` inside `marketplaceContexts` on the bulk PATCH; the API accepts and validates it (bulk-edit.service.ts:56, :67, :202) and uses it for the column set (bulk-edit.service.ts:481) and the formula coordinate (:2647). The real reason a French pin cannot be stored is one layer deeper: ChannelListing's unique keys carry no language (schema.prisma:275-276 — workspaceId, productId, channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey), the model has no `translations` relation (so `content-read.ts:22`'s `translations: listing.translations` is never populated for a channel row and the resolver's `pin` tier is unreachable), and the write lands on the language-less columns/bag via the upsert at bulk-edit.service.ts:1771-1800. So the finding's own proposed fix ("add `locale` to StudioCoordinate and carry it as `address.requested`") targets a client field that is already being sent and would change nothing about storage.

MIS-STATED #2 — the data premise. The finding asserts AMAZON/BE has languages [nl, fr] today and cites schema.prisma:1948-1950 plus docs/audits/2026-09-12-language-axis/README.md. That README is a production measurement and says the opposite at lines 49-55: "All rows have a scalar `language`; the `languages` array column is absent", with AMAZON | BE | nl. The [nl, fr] value exists only in an unapplied migration in the working tree (packages/database/prisma/migrations/20260912_lx2_marketplace_languages/migration.sql: `CASE WHEN "code" = 'BE' THEN ARRAY['nl','fr']`), and flattenGrouped (scopes.ts:101) falls back to `[language]` when the array is absent. So today every market is single-language, `options.locales.length === 1` everywhere on Amazon/eBay, and both the "second language unreachable" and "actively wipes a pinned one" harms are LATENT (the :931 reset is a no-op at one language). They become live the moment LX.2 lands — which makes this a real gap to close before that migration, not a live operator-facing defect.

Also note the proposed gate `options.locales.length > 1` would render nothing at all in production today, i.e. the fix as written is unverifiable until LX.2 is applied.
Half of the fix is right, half is aimed at the wrong layer. Right: delete the ['SHOPIFY','ETSY'] condition at StudioBar.tsx:36 and render the DS Listbox from the already-computed options.locales (contracts.tsx:671-673), and make contracts.tsx:931 honour a pinned localeParam that is still in the new market's languages, as its own comment at :930 already claims. Wrong: "add `locale` to StudioCoordinate (contracts.tsx:954-956) and carry it as address.requested" — the client already sends the locale on both the read (useChannelSheet.ts:74) and the write (useChannelSheet.ts:309 marketplaceContexts), and the API already validates it (bulk-edit.service.ts:202). The storage is what lacks the axis: ChannelListing is keyed without a language (schema.prisma:275-276), has no translations relation to hold a per-language pin, and bulk-edit's channel upsert (bulk-edit.service.ts:1771-1800) writes the language-less columns/override bag regardless of the locale sent. Any fix must add channel-level per-language pin storage (the shape content-resolver.ts:8-11 and :168-176 already models) or the language picker will let an operator type French copy that silently reads back as Dutch. Sequencing also matters: the gate `options.locales.length > 1` is inert until migrations/20260912_lx2_marketplace_languages is applied, so ship the control with a positive control on a genuinely multi-language row, not on today's single-language data.

[critical]verifiedALLdata integrity risk

#### Removing a product from one market hard-deletes the coordinate row, destroying all per-market content and its own snapshots — a later restore starts from an empty DRAFT

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator takes the jacket off Amazon IT for the winter, keeping DE. Months of Italian-specific work sit on that coordinate: the Italian bullet array, the IT-only material/colour overrides, the Amazon item specifics. Next season they want IT back exactly as it was.

##### What happens today
The removal paths hard-delete the ChannelListing row for (productId, channel, marketplace): amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:58-63 and ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:642-645, both inside a transaction, with no snapshot taken first. That row IS the per-market content store — overrideData (schema.prisma:1596-1604), titleOverride / descriptionOverride / bulletPointsOverride (schema.prisma:1664-1668), platformAttributes, variationTheme/variationMapping (schema.prisma:1607-1612) — and every child cascades with it: ChannelListingOverride, the per-field audit trail (schema.prisma:1994-2001), and ChannelListingSnapshot (schema.prisma:1888), whose own doc comment three lines later says the coordinate is denormalised 'so snapshots stay queryable and readable after a listing row is replaced' — the Cascade makes that false. Production carries 512 non-empty bulletPointsOverride rows (docs/audits/2026-09-12-language-axis/README.md baseline), so this is live content, not theory. What survives is only the language tier, ProductTranslation (schema.prisma:13491-13519), which is keyed (productId, language) with no market dimension. Restoring the market re-creates the row through channel-value-write.ts:9-17 as listingStatus 'DRAFT', isPublished false, overrideData '{}' — shared text comes back, every IT-specific value does not. I searched the studio tree for any restore of a coordinate: drawer/panes/RestoreMode.tsx:13-17 states in its own header that it restores the MASTER record's scalar fields and is a different mechanism from listing restore, and RestoreMode.tsx:133 says it makes no marketplace call.

##### Proposed fix
Make per-market removal non-destructive by construction. (1) Never DELETE the coordinate row for a market removal: set { listingStatus: 'ENDED', isPublished: false, offerActive: false } — the shape flat-file/import/apply.ts already produces and the only relistable one — so overrides, snapshots and history survive. (2) Change ChannelListingSnapshot.channelListingId to onDelete: SetNull (it already denormalises channel/marketplace/aliasKey for exactly this, schema.prisma:1896-1899) and capture one snapshot inside the removal transaction, so even a genuine purge leaves a restore point. (3) Surface it in the studio at the coordinate the operator is standing on: a 'Remove from this market…' item in the channel sheet's single ⋯ overflow, run through the DS grid action registry (design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts) with danger + ConfirmLevel 'type-to-confirm' on the real SKU, and a preflight that itemises exactly what is kept (Italian bullets, IT overrides, ASIN) versus ended. API: POST /api/products/:id/listings/:channel/:marketplace/end and .../relist, both taking { accountId, aliasKey }, with relist replaying the snapshot the end captured.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The operator is standing in the studio on Amazon · IT with the jacket open. They want IT off and DE kept, and IT back next season. They look at the scope bar, the sheet toolbar's ⋯, the row menu and the drawer for anything that ends this market.

##### What happens today
Nothing exists in the studio. /usr/bin/grep -rInE 'sync-control|CLOSE_OFFER|REOPEN_OFFER|flat-file/remove|remove-channel-listing|bulk-hard-delete|delist|relist' over apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/ returns ONE hit, a string inside variants/channel/projection.vitest.test.ts:462 (positive control: 201 files in that tree match 'market'). The channel sheet declares exactly three verbs — open-record, offer-toggle, broadcast-to-listings (channelActions.ts:403-404) — and two of the three refuse any live listing outright ('wave-1 channel verbs are preview-only', channelActions.ts:250, :260). The correct instrument exists and is not here: closeMarketOffers writes offerClosedAt + a verbatim offerCloseSnapshot and cancels racing pushes (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:177-198), reopen replays it — and its operator copy on the fulfillment page literally describes this scenario: 'This is the RIGHT tool for "stop selling in DE/FR/ES while IT keeps selling" — unlike quantity, it truly is per-market' (apps/web/src/app/fulfillment/stock/sync-control/sync-control-shared.ts:147). The workaround an operator will reach for in the sheet — set this market's quantity to 0 — is the incident the codebase already paid for: 'pushing 0 "to DE" zeroes IT, FR and ES in the same instant. 302 market-scoped Zero & Pins therefore blanked the entire IT storefront' (amazon-eu-quantity-guard.ts:5-13; the shared set includes IT/DE/FR/ES/NL/BE/PL/SE/IE at :24-32). That guard runs only at the sync-control action layer and at the outbound push layer on a column-shaped payload.quantity (outbound-sync.service.ts:995-1020); the studio shows no EU-shared warning anywhere — the only mention in the studio tree is a source comment (ChannelSheet.tsx:2087).

##### Proposed fix
Put the reversible per-market verb on the coordinate the scope bar already selects. Add 'Stop selling in this market' / 'Resume selling in this market' as items of the channel sheet's one ⋯ overflow (CH.1 rule: scope verbs are items, never buttons) backed by the existing sync-control actions — POST /api/products/:id/markets/:marketplace/offer { action: 'CLOSE'|'REOPEN', accountId, reason } delegating to closeMarketOffers/reopenMarketOffers so the offerCloseSnapshot replay is reused unchanged. Build it as a GridAction (design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts) with danger, ConfirmLevel 'confirm', and a preflight() whose ActionImpact itemises the sync-control sentence verbatim: reviews and the ASIN untouched, other markets untouched, shared EU quantity untouched, FBA rows refused. Where the channel has no close primitive (eBay/Shopify), the action must be `disabled` with a DS disabledReason naming the end/relist consequence rather than absent. Separately, the Amazon quantity cell must carry an inline EU-shared warning sourced from AMAZON_EU_SHARED_MARKETS rather than a source comment.

#### A market whose Amazon offer is closed still reads 'live' and 'Offer: selling' in the studio — the studio has no vocabulary for a closed market

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A colleague closed the jacket's Amazon IT offer last week from Sync Control (the reversible, correct way). Today another operator opens the studio on Amazon · IT to check whether IT is selling, and to decide whether to push a price change there.

##### What happens today
The studio shows IT as live and selling. closeMarketOffers writes only offerClosedAt / offerClosedBy / offerCloseReason / offerCloseSnapshot (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:177-194) — it deliberately does not touch listingStatus, isPublished or offerActive — while the sheet's liveness rule is `listing.externalListingId && listing.isPublished` (sheet-rows.service.ts:268), both still true, so the row reads state 'live'. The drawer's Listings pane reads offerActive and prints the literal word 'selling' (drawer/panes/ListingsPane.tsx:125-131). offerClosedAt reaches no studio surface at all: /usr/bin/grep for 'offerClosed' over apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/ returns 0 (positive control: 'offerActive' matches 11 lines in the same tree), and it is absent from the pim sheet services (positive control: 'offerActive' is present in sheet-rows.service.ts and studio-sheet.service.ts). The concept is known server-side — prepare-dispatch.ts:15 refuses a mapping publish when `listing.syncPaused || listing.offerClosedAt` — so the studio is the only place that cannot see it. The market Listbox itself carries no state either: it is a plain DS Listbox of code+label (StudioBar.tsx:34-35) over markets derived from the Marketplace table (scopes.ts:128-134), not from this product's listings, so no market option can say live / ended / closed / unlisted.

##### Proposed fix
Add a 'closed' member to the one readiness vocabulary (design-system/grid/renderers/readiness.ts, which ScopeBar and the sheet both already read — patterns/ScopeBar.tsx:15) and set it whenever offerClosedAt is non-null: project offerClosedAt/offerClosedBy/offerCloseReason through studio-sheet.service.ts and sheet-rows.service.ts, make liveness `externalListingId && isPublished && !offerClosedAt`, and have ListingsPane print 'closed on <date> by <actor> — reopen restores the saved offer' instead of 'selling'. Give the market switcher the same state: replace the plain Listbox at StudioBar.tsx:34-35 with the DS Listbox's option-with-meta rendering (or the ScopeBar readiness chip vocabulary) so each market option shows its own state, sourced from the readiness call that already runs per market (contracts.tsx:378-383). A closed market must never be silently editable-and-publishable-looking.

- apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-rows.service.ts:268
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/drawer/panes/ListingsPane.tsx:125-131
- /usr/bin/grep 'offerClosed' over _studio/ = 0 hits (positive control 'offerActive' = 11 hits)
- /usr/bin/grep 'offerClosedAt' over apps/api/src/services/pim/ = 0 hits (positive control: 'offerActive' matches sheet-rows.service.ts and studio-sheet.service.ts)

- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/scopes.ts:128-134

WHAT I CONFIRMED
1. The close writes nothing the studio reads. apps/api/src/services/amazon-market-offer.service.ts:177-194 — the `prisma.channelListing.update` after a successful `patchPurchasableOffer({op:'delete'})` sets ONLY `offerClosedAt`, `offerClosedBy`, `offerCloseReason`, `offerCloseSnapshot`, then cancels PENDING queue rows (:195-198). `listingStatus`, `isPublished`, `externalListingId`, `offerActive` are untouched. 'errors' : listing && listing.externalListingId && listing.isPublished ? 'live' : ...`). So the row reads 'live'.

'selling' : 'paused'`, and the value is the raw column: studio-sheet.service.ts:1380 `offerActive: listingRow.offerActive !== false` (select at :468). Close never flips it, so it prints 'selling'. The DS row vocabulary is a closed union of five with no 'closed' member: apps/web/src/design-system/grid/renderers/readiness.ts:31 `'ready' | 'missing' | 'errors' | 'live' | 'unlisted'` (labels at :52-56).

Only the channel ScopeBar gets readiness (StudioBar.tsx:15-27).

- Capability elsewhere in the studio: `/usr/bin/grep -rni "reopen|close offer|offer clos|closed market|delist|withdraw"` over the whole _studio/ tree returns only unrelated hits (drawer reopen prose, `'recordClosed'` scroll-stash token, AliasBandCell 'withdrawn'). channel-ops/ contains only ErrorsSyncTab/Console/syncQueue. No tab, drawer pane, overflow or modal in the studio shows or sets closed state.
- Dead code: it is live and operator-reachable. sync-control.routes.ts:31,811-819 wires CLOSE_OFFER/REOPEN_OFFER to closeMarketOffers/reopenMarketOffers; registered at apps/api/src/index.ts:842. The UI exists: apps/web/src/app/fulfillment/stock/sync-control/SyncControlClient.tsx:603-604 and SyncProductsGrid.tsx:69-70 offer 'Close offer'/'Reopen offer', and that surface has a FULL vocabulary the studio lacks — sync-control-shared.ts:9 `Mode = ... | 'CLOSED'`, :81 tone 'warning', :92 label 'Closed', :104 the operator explanation. So the concept is a shipped, named UI state one page away; the studio is the blind surface.
- "Never runs" / harmless: the consequence is real. A price push from a closed coordinate is accepted and dies later — outbound-sync.service.ts:902-906 returns SKIPPED `"Market offer is CLOSED (Sync Control) — no pushes until Reopen"`, and prepare-dispatch.ts:15 throws at DISPATCH time inside the worker (its only caller is outbound-sync.service.ts:609), not at publish time in the studio. So there is no synchronous warning in the studio at all.

MIS-STATEMENTS WORTH CORRECTING (finding stands, two details are wrong)
a) "no studio surface at all" needs one caveat: after a push is attempted, the studio's own Errors & Sync tab renders queue failures (channel-ops/syncQueue.ts:93 `errorMessage`, :196+ cause derivation), so the SKIPPED "Market offer is CLOSED" message can appear there after the fact. That is post-hoc, not a state read, and it does not save the operator's "is IT selling?" decision — but "publishable-looking with a silent write" overstates it: the write fails loudly in the queue, it just fails late.
b) The fix instruction names only sheet-rows.service.ts:268 for liveness. The studio's rows come from studio-sheet.service.ts:1451, which restates the same rule. Patching only the cited line would change nothing in the studio.
Directionally right, three corrections before anyone implements it.

1. Patch BOTH row builders or nothing changes. The fix names apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-rows.service.ts:268, but the studio sheet computes its own state at apps/api/src/services/pim/studio-sheet.service.ts:1448-1457 with the rule restated verbatim. `offerClosedAt` is also absent from the studio's ChannelListing select (studio-sheet.service.ts:464-468) and from the `SheetListing` shape built at :1372-1389, so this is a producer+consumer change that must land together: select the column, widen SheetListing and its web-side mirror, then the state rule in both builders.

2. Adding a member to `RowReadinessState` (readiness.ts:31) is a DS-wide union change, not a local one. Every consumer of `ROW_META` (:52-56), `readyPillTone` (:99) and drawer/readinessMeta.ts must handle it, and the file's own doc at :19-23 warns that row and scope vocabularies are deliberately non-mappable — so decide explicitly what a closed market does to the SCOPE chip (ScopeBar) rather than letting a default fall through to 'absent'.

3. Scope it to Amazon and to closure, not to "not selling". CLOSE_OFFER/REOPEN_OFFER are Amazon-only by design — sync-control.routes.ts:812-815 marks non-AMAZON targets `unchanged` — so a 'closed' pill must not imply eBay/Etsy support. And reuse the wording already agreed with operators at sync-control-shared.ts:104 ("this market's offer is closed; SKU, content, ASIN, reviews and every other market are untouched; Reopen restores it") instead of inventing a second phrasing; two surfaces describing the same state differently is the exact failure readiness.ts:19-23 was written to prevent.

4. The market Listbox part is the weakest piece as written. `options.markets` comes from the Marketplace table (scopes.ts:110-134) and knows nothing about this product, and `useScopeReadiness` is keyed by scope (channel), not by market — StudioBar.tsx:15-27 only scores channel ids. Giving each market option its own state needs a new per-market readiness read, not a rendering change to the Listbox; cost it as such or drop it from this fix and ship the row/drawer truth first.

##### What happens today
Removal has no account or alias dimension at all. handleRemoveChannelListing deletes with `where: { productId: { in: productIds }, channel: 'EBAY', marketplace }` (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:642-645) and the Amazon twin with `{ productId: { in: ids }, channel: 'AMAZON', marketplace }` (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:58-62) — neither names channelConnectionId nor aliasKey. Those two columns are precisely what makes a coordinate unique: both @@unique keys are [workspaceId, productId, channel(Market), marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey] (schema.prisma:1783-1784), and the schema's own note explains aliasKey exists as a NOT-NULL discriminator so an alias row can be targeted at all (schema.prisma:1750-1769). The studio meanwhile models the coordinate WITH the account: it selects one (StudioBar.tsx:33, contracts.tsx:663-667, accountScope.ts:6-15) and resolves a destination per account+listing. So a removal issued for the coordinate the operator can see destroys Account A's IT listing and every alias's IT listing in the same statement, each with its own overrides and identifiers, and both services then best-effort delist only the externalListingIds they happened to read first. The schema comment concedes the constraint is only currently harmless because 977/977 rows carry a connection and one row per coordinate (schema.prisma:1765-1768) — a measurement from 2026-09-01, not an invariant.

##### Proposed fix
Make the coordinate mandatory in the removal contract: every end/remove service takes { productId, channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey } and refuses (rather than widens) when the caller omits them — the same fail-closed shape amazon-market-offer.service.ts already uses for FBA rows. The studio's verb passes the coordinate it already holds (contracts.tsx:954-956 plus aliasKey from the selected listing). In the UI, the DS confirmation must itemise the exact rows: use the grid action registry's preflight()/ActionImpact (design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts:167-198) to list every coordinate that will be ended — 'eBay · IT · Account B · Primary listing' — with consequences itemised, never counted, per the ActionConfirm contract; a removal whose impact names more coordinates than the operator selected is the thing the confirmation exists to catch.

- apps/api/src/services/amazon/amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:56-63
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1783-1784
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1750-1769
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/StudioBar.tsx:33
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:663-667
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/accountScope.ts:6-15

##### Verifier
Every cited line was opened and the code-level defect is real, but the finding's narrative is mis-attributed to the studio.

CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE:
1. eBay removal widens: apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:645-647 — `tx.channelListing.deleteMany({ where: { productId: { in: productIds }, channel: 'EBAY', marketplace } })` (finding cited 642-645; the actual deleteMany is 645-647 — a ~3-line drift, not a misquote). The pre-read that feeds the delist uses the same widened where at :636-639.
2. Amazon twin widens identically: apps/api/src/services/amazon/amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:60-62, pre-read at :52-55. Its target type is literally `{ productId: string; marketplace: string }` (:9) — no account, no alias.
3. Neither service names the discriminators. Set claim established with /usr/bin/grep, not the shell function: `/usr/bin/grep -n 'channelConnectionId'` and `'aliasKey'` over both service files return ZERO matches.
4. The route contracts are equally blind: apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1806-1819 accepts `targets: Array<{ productId, marketplace }>` and validates only those two fields; the eBay `DeleteTarget` (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:55-70) carries productId/sku/marketplace/itemId/parentSku/intent and nothing else.
5. The schema does make those two columns the uniqueness discriminators: packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1783-1784 — both @@unique keys are [workspaceId, productId, channelMarket|channel+marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey]. The aliasKey rationale block (1750-1769) and the "977/977 rows carry a connection (measured 2026-09-01)" concession (1765-1768) read exactly as quoted.
6. The studio does model the coordinate with the account: StudioBar.tsx:34 renders the account Listbox when accounts.length > 1; contracts.tsx:663-667 resolves accounts/requestedAccount/destination/accountId; accountScope.ts:6-15 is primaryStudioAccount as quoted.

ATTEMPTED REFUTATIONS, and what they found:
- Another path to removal that IS coordinate-scoped? The only alias-aware removal is DELETE /products/:id/aliases/:aliasId (product-studio.routes.ts:990-999), which ARCHIVES the alias record (listing-alias.service.ts:194-197), deletes no ChannelListing and delists nothing — a different capability, not a refutation.
- Dead or superseded code? No. `removeAmazonListing` is live at amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1816, called from AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1886; `remove-channel-listing` is dispatched at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:282 and driven from EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:713/2010.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG: the scenario has the operator "standing in the studio on eBay · IT · Account B" issue this removal. No such verb exists. The channel sheet's registry offers only offer-toggle, broadcast-to-listings and open-record (channelActions.ts:163, :309, :381); the family registry offers attach/unlink/reparent/promote/add-child/delete-child/demote (familyActions.ts:122-496), and delete-child is itself blocked while any listing exists (:454); StudioHeader/StudioSubheader/StudioBar/PublishMenu contain no remove/delist/end verb (/usr/bin/grep for remove|delete|end|archive|retire|withdraw over those four files returns one unrelated comment). The widening is therefore issued from the two flat-file editors, which are account-blind by construction (the eBay side resolves `tryResolveConnection({ channel: 'EBAY', primary: true })`, ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1532), not from the studio coordinate.

REACHABILITY (why not critical): the widening only destroys extra rows when a coordinate holds more than one row — a second account in the same market, or an alias row. Alias rows are creatable via POST /products/:id/aliases (product-studio.routes.ts:961-963, writing aliasKey = alias.id at listing-alias.service.ts:148), but the studio's own "+ Add listing alias" is rendered and permanently disabled (ChannelProjection.tsx:395-413), and the schema's own measurement says one row per coordinate as of 2026-09-01. A confirmed latent contract defect with no demonstrated live-data exposure today: high, not critical.
The server half is right and should be kept: make { productId, channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey } mandatory in both removal services and both routes and fail closed rather than widen — the deleteMany at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:646 and amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:61 are the two statements to narrow, and DeleteTarget (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:55-70) plus the /amazon/flat-file/remove body (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1806) are the two contracts that must carry the extra fields. The fix omits one thing it must include: the pre-read that feeds the best-effort delist (ebay:636-639, amazon:52-55) uses the SAME widened where, so narrowing only the delete leaves the delist ending listings the delete no longer removed — strictly worse than today.

The UI half rests on a premise I could not confirm: "the studio's verb passes the coordinate it already holds (contracts.tsx:954-956)". contracts.tsx:954-956 is the `coordinate` memo inside the scope value, not a removal verb, and there is no removal verb anywhere in the studio (channelActions.ts:163/309/381; familyActions.ts:122-496; nothing in the four chrome files). This is not a matter of threading an extra parameter through an existing verb — the verb has to be built, which is a larger and separate piece of work, and is arguably the owner's actual complaint. The registry mechanics the fix leans on do exist (GridAction.preflight + ActionImpact, registry.ts:186-190), so an itemising ActionConfirm is achievable once a verb exists. The claim that "amazon-market-offer.service.ts already uses this fail-closed shape for FBA rows" is uncited and I did not verify it; treat it as a lead, not a precedent.

[medium]verifiedALLcorrectness risk

#### The remembered market is one global key and is restored without checking the scope serves it, so a deep link to a channel lands the operator on Shared product behind a banner

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Yesterday the operator worked on Amazon · BE, so 'BE' is remembered. Today a colleague sends them /products/<id>/edit/studio?scope=EBAY (no market in the link) to look at the jacket's eBay listing. eBay serves DE/ES/FR/IT/UK — not BE.

##### What happens today
They land on Shared product with a banner instead of eBay. The first-visit effect fires whenever the URL carries no market (contracts.tsx:886-894) and its only guard is that the remembered code exists somewhere in the global market list — `options.markets.some(m => m.code === remembered)` — with no check that the ACTIVE scope serves it. It pushes market=BE; the scope memo then falls back to master because the channel does not serve the market (contracts.tsx:654-661); scopeError is set to 'This channel is unavailable in the selected market. Choose an available scope.' (contracts.tsx:676) and StudioTabHost.tsx:68 returns that Banner INSTEAD of the tab. The memory is also a single browser-wide key, 'nexus:studio:market' (lastMarket.ts:18), so one market is remembered for all channels even though the channels serve disjoint market sets. The mirror case is silent rather than loud: clicking a channel chip whose markets exclude the current market relocates the market to that channel's first market alphabetically (contracts.tsx:903-905) without saying so and without updating the remembered value (setScope never calls writeLastMarket, unlike setMarket at contracts.tsx:925) — so the operator moves from Amazon · BE to eBay · DE with no notice, and the two defaults now disagree.

##### Proposed fix
Two surgical changes in the files that already own these rules. (1) In the restore effect (contracts.tsx:886-894) add the serving check that already exists as a pure helper: skip the restore when scope !== MASTER_SCOPE && !channelServesMarket(scope, remembered, options) (scopes.ts:199-205) — a remembered default must never override an explicit ?scope=. (2) Key the memory per channel in lastMarket.ts ('nexus:studio:market:<scope>' with the current key as the master/global fallback) and call writeLastMarket from setScope's relocation branch so the two defaults cannot diverge. For the silent relocation itself, keep the market Listbox as the one place the market is named, and announce the change the DS way: after setScope relocates, surface a DS Toast (design-system/components/Toast.tsx, tone neutral) reading 'eBay does not sell in BE — showing eBay · DE', rather than moving the coordinate underneath the operator without a word.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:886-894
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:654-661
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:676
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/StudioTabHost.tsx:68
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:903-905
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:925
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/lastMarket.ts:18
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/scopes.ts:199-205

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding says it says, and I could not find a path that defeats the mechanism.

CITATIONS VERIFIED VERBATIM
- contracts.tsx:888-894 — the restore effect is exactly `if (marketParam) return; const remembered = readLastMarket(); if (!remembered || remembered === market) return; if (!options.markets.some((m) => m.code === remembered)) return; push({ [URL_KEYS.market]: remembered })`. Its only guard is membership in the market list; there is no reference to `scope`, `scopeParam` or `channelServesMarket` anywhere in the effect or its deps.
- contracts.tsx:671-673 — `options` is `{ ...baseOptions, locales: ... }`; only `locales` is ever overridden, so `options.markets` in the effect IS the global market list, not a scope-filtered one. The auditor's premise holds. (Stronger than stated: deriveScopeOptions at scopes.ts:110-113 seeds `marketChannels` for a row BEFORE the `connected === false` continue, so `options.markets` can even contain a market with zero connected channels.)
- contracts.tsx:654-661 — the scope memo returns MASTER_SCOPE when `market && !channelServesMarket(scopeParam, market, baseOptions)`, and it depends on `market`, so the pushed market re-runs it.
- contracts.tsx:676 — `scopeError = scopeParam && scopeParam !== scope ? 'This channel is unavailable in the selected market. Choose an available scope.' : ...` — exactly the quoted string, and the exact condition that the demoted scope produces.
- StudioTabHost.tsx:68 — `if (scopeError) return <Banner tone="neutral" title="Choose an available scope">{scopeError}</Banner>` is the FIRST statement after the hooks, so it returns instead of the tab.
- contracts.tsx:905-906 — setScope's market key is `next !== MASTER_SCOPE && market && !channelServesMarket(next, market, options) ? options.channels.find(c => c.id === next)?.markets[0] : market ?? undefined`, and `markets` is `.sort()`ed at scopes.ts:132 — so "that channel's first market alphabetically" is right.
- contracts.tsx:924 vs 897-915 — `writeLastMarket(code)` sits inside setMarket only; setScope's relocation branch does not call it.
- lastMarket.ts:18 — `const KEY = 'nexus:studio:market'`, one global key, no scope segment.

SET CLAIM RE-ESTABLISHED WITH /usr/bin/grep (the broken shell function was not used): `/usr/bin/grep -rn "writeLastMarket|readLastMarket|nexus:studio:market" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' apps packages` returns exactly six hits — the three definitions in lastMarket.ts, the import at contracts.tsx:40, the read at 890 and the single write at 924. There is no second writer, so the memory genuinely cannot be updated by a scope change.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED
- "The market Listbox must already be scope-filtered, so a remembered market always serves the scope." StudioBar.tsx:33 does filter (`options.markets.filter(m => m.channels.includes(scope))`) — but that filter is what MAKES the divergence: in master scope StudioBar.tsx:29-30 renders no market control at all, so the memory can only ever be written from inside a channel scope, i.e. it always stores a market served by the channel the operator was on THEN, and nothing re-checks it against the channel they arrive on NEXT.
- "The push is swallowed by a guard." push (contracts.tsx:850-858) only returns early when `!canChangeEditor()`, i.e. an open editor guard (634); on first mount there is none.
- "The chip is disabled so the mirror case can't happen." ScopeBar disables only on `item.disabled` (ScopeBar.tsx:45, 97, 166), and StudioBar.tsx:26 never passes `disabled` — it only omits `readiness`. So the eBay chip is fully clickable while market=BE and the silent relocation at 905-906 is reachable by in-app clicks alone, despite scopes.ts:198 asserting "A chip outside its markets is disabled, not hidden."
- "The disjointness is hypothetical." The codebase asserts it itself: contracts.tsx:919 ("eBay is not in every market") and scopes.ts:164 ("PL is served by one channel and DE by two") — a remembered PL plus `?scope=EBAY` is a concrete instance.
- "Some test pins this as intended." No studio test touches it: the nine *.vitest.test.ts files in _studio/ contain no reference to lastMarket (checked with /usr/bin/grep).

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING (why the severity is medium, not higher)
1. Reachability of the banner half is narrower than the scenario implies. The only in-app studio deep-link builder, apps/web/src/app/_shared/product-workspace-href.ts:3, ALWAYS sets `market` alongside `scope`, so it never trips the effect; /products/next/columns.tsx:162 and listing-readiness/page.tsx:93 carry neither param. A scope-without-market URL comes from a hand-trimmed or hand-shared link — real, but not produced by the product.
2. Recovery is one click, not a dead end: the ScopeBar still renders above the Banner (StudioFrame.tsx:45-49 puts StudioTabHost below the subheader), and clicking the eBay chip runs setScope's relocation and clears the error. Also, the relocation is not invisible in state — the market Listbox visibly changes to DE — it is merely unannounced.

Neither correction touches the mechanism, and the memory-divergence half (a single global key that setScope never updates) is confirmed as a set claim.
