#### There is no way to end ONE listing of a multi-listing coordinate — the only removal paths delete every alias on the market and end every ItemID

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator sells the GALE jacket on eBay IT through three competing listings: the primary (ItemID 1953…), alias ② "Summer photos" and alias ③ "Outlet price". The outlet listing is cannibalising the others, so they want ③ ended on eBay and its record kept, with ① and ② untouched.

##### What happens today
Nothing in the studio can do it, and the one path that exists outside the studio does far more than asked. The channel sheet's single ⋯ overflow contains only Cell details, one "Check Information ①/②/③" per alias, + Add listing alias, Formula history and Apply formula (ChannelSheet.tsx:2002-2035); the per-alias 'Check Information' explicitly "sends nothing to the provider" (AliasPublishControl.tsx:34). The row/selection verb set is three: open-record, offer-toggle, broadcast — and the last two refuse any live alias as "wave-1 channel verbs are preview-only" (channelActions.ts:262-266, 348-353, 403). The band row itself is declared to have no verbs (AliasBandCell.tsx:59-62). The only implemented per-market removals are alias-blind: ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:641-645 runs channelListing.deleteMany({productId in ids, channel:'EBAY', marketplace}) — no aliasKey, no channelConnectionId — after collecting EVERY row's externalListingId at :634-637 for a best-effort delist loop, so "remove from eBay IT" ends ①②③ and hard-deletes all three local rows (losing each ItemID, overrideData and flatFileSnapshot). amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:53-64 is the same shape for Amazon. /usr/bin/grep over the five lifecycle files returns 0 hits for aliasKey|aliasId against a control of 2-17 hits for channelListing in the same files.

##### Proposed fix
Add an `end-listing` GridAction to channelActions.ts, scope ROW, available only on a band row whose alias carries an externalListingId, danger: true. Its preflight returns ActionImpact{ level: 'type-to-confirm', confirmPhrase: <the alias's real ItemID/ASIN> } — the registry's rule that the phrase is the real identifier, never "DELETE" (grid/actions/registry.ts:69,183) — with consequences itemised per alias so the confirmation names exactly which listing ends and which stay live; render via useActionConfirm (ActionConfirm.tsx), as MasterSheet/ChannelSheet already do. Note the DS gap: actionMenuItems drops GridAction.danger (menuAdapters.tsx:75-91), so the ⋯ entry must be worded to carry the weight until Menu grows a tone. API: POST /api/products/:id/listings/aliases/:aliasId/end { mode: 'unpublish'|'delete', accountId, expectedVersion } which (a) captures a ChannelListingSnapshot first, (b) enqueues OutboundSyncQueue{ syncType:'UNPUBLISH_LISTING', channelListingId } for the rows of that aliasKey only, (c) sets listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false and KEEPS externalListingId. Independently, add aliasKey + channelConnectionId to the where clauses of the two flat-file deleteMany calls so a coordinate-wide removal can never be mistaken for a per-listing one.

#### Archive is the only alias-removal API: it is unwired, unreversible, and leaves the eBay listing live and selling while hiding it from the sheet

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator decides alias ② of the GALE jacket on eBay IT is a mistake and asks support to "delete that listing from Nexus". Support calls the alias DELETE route. The eBay listing keeps selling; Nexus stops showing it; nobody can bring it back.

##### What happens today
DELETE /products/:id/aliases/:aliasId calls archiveAlias, which flips ProductListingAlias.status to 'ARCHIVED' and touches no ChannelListing row (listing-alias.service.ts:194-197; route product-studio.routes.ts:990-999). The studio sheet then drops the group entirely — the alias query filters status:'ACTIVE' (studio-sheet.service.ts:980-981) while the ChannelListing query at :985 still loads the rows, and the projection loop only walks the ACTIVE groups (:1073-1078), so the rows exist, keep externalListingId / isPublished / offerActive, and simply have no band. There is no un-archive: the only writers of ProductListingAlias.status are create (default ACTIVE) and archiveAlias's 'ARCHIVED' (/usr/bin/grep over apps/api/src: productListingAlias.update appears only at :187 label/position and :197 status), and updateAlias runs through mutateAlias with includeArchived=false (:187, :168-182, :55), so an archived alias cannot even be renamed back into view. The studio deliberately does not call it (useChannelSheet.ts:439-441: "Archiving (DELETE) is deliberately NOT wired here") — so today the exposure is API-only, but the route is live and named DELETE.

##### Proposed fix
Three changes. (1) archiveAlias must refuse while the alias's rows carry externalListingId or isPublished — the same liveness test listingRisk.ts already uses and the same shape as assertCanDeleteRelationshipProduct — with the message naming the end-listing verb from ALIAS-1 as the way through, so an operator is never told to resolve something the product offers no control for. (2) Add restoreAlias (status back to 'ACTIVE', reached by PATCH /aliases/:aliasId {status}) and let validateAliasWriteTargets admit archived aliases for that one call, so archive is reversible by construction. #### No alias can ever become the primary listing, and every relist/publish/recovery path is primary-only or alias-blind — recovery nulls the siblings' ASINs

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The primary Amazon IT listing for the GALE jacket is suppressed and the operator runs Recover → NEW_ASIN_SAME_SKU on it. Alias ② (a second live offer on the same coordinate) is meant to be untouched and, since the primary is gone, ought to become the product's main listing.

##### What happens today
The primary is a synthetic group the server invents — { id: null, label: 'Primary', position: 0 } — always rendered whether or not a listing exists behind it (studio-sheet.service.ts:1073-1076). No alias can take that slot: updateAlias rejects any position below 1 (listing-alias.service.ts:186), and position carries a unique constraint per coordinate (schema.prisma:1858) while the only writer is a single unconditional update (:187-190), so even swapping ① and ② collides with P2002 — there is no two-phase rotation anywhere. Meanwhile the relist side is primary-only or blind: the wizard's ASIN write-back hardcodes aliasKey:'' (submission.service.ts:1429-1430, 1472-1473), and recovery.service.ts:334-349 runs channelListing.updateMany({ productId, channel:'AMAZON', marketplace }) with no aliasKey and no channelConnectionId — so recovering the PRIMARY stamps listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false on every alias row of that coordinate and, for the NEW_ASIN_* actions, sets externalListingId: null on all of them, erasing alias ②'s live ASIN with nothing capturing it first.

##### Proposed fix
First make the blind writes safe: every updateMany/upsert in recovery.service.ts, submission.service.ts and the flat-file paths must carry aliasKey and channelConnectionId in its where, so a verb aimed at the primary can never reach a sibling listing (the same discipline channel-value-write already keeps). Then add promotion: POST /api/products/:id/aliases/:aliasId/promote, running a transactional rotation (park the target at a negative/temporary position, shift the rest, land it at the primary coordinate) because the position unique index makes a naive swap fail; surface it as a band-row GridAction "Make this the primary listing" with preflight level 'confirm' and consequences that name which ItemID becomes primary and which is demoted, rendered by useActionConfirm. Until promotion exists, the synthetic Primary band must not be drawn as a listing when no row backs it — render it through the existing readiness vocabulary as 'unlisted' rather than as a listing whose status is missing.

[high]verifiedALLdata integrity risk

#### Channel discovery can never create an alias: every reconciled listing is written onto aliasKey '' and the recon table is keyed by SKU, so a second live listing is merged away or overwrites the first

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator runs reconciliation on eBay IT (or Amazon IT) and it discovers two live listings that both map to the GALE jacket. They confirm both rows expecting Nexus to record both listings — that is precisely what the alias table was built for.

##### What happens today
Confirming a reconciliation row upserts a ChannelListing keyed with aliasKey hardcoded to '' — the primary — with the comment "'' = the product's PRIMARY listing, which is what every writer here addresses" (listing-reconciliation.service.ts:503-512). So the second confirmation lands on the SAME row as the first: on Amazon (where row.parentAsin is set) the update branch rewrites externalListingId/externalParentId to the new parent ASIN (:530-534), replacing the first listing's identity with no snapshot and no record that two listings exist; on eBay (parentAsin null) the update only stamps listingStatus:'ACTIVE', so the second offerId is dropped on the floor entirely. Upstream, discovery itself cannot hold two listings for one SKU: the eBay sweep upserts on channel_marketplace_externalSku (:806-812) so a second offer for the same SKU overwrites the first row's externalListingId. The connection is also fixed to the primary account (reconConn, :495), so a listing found on a second account is written onto the primary account's row.

##### Proposed fix
Make discovery alias-aware end to end. (1) Widen the ListingReconciliation unique key to (channel, marketplace, externalSku, externalListingId) so two live listings for one SKU are two rows, not one overwrite. (2) In confirmReconRow, resolve the target before writing: if the coordinate already holds a row with a DIFFERENT non-null externalListingId, create a ProductListingAlias (reusing createAlias, label defaulted from the channel title) and write onto that aliasKey instead of ''; never rewrite a non-null externalListingId in place. (3) Surface it where the operator works: a DS Banner tone="warning" on the channel scope reading "2 live listings found on eBay IT for this product" with the ⋯ item from ALIAS-4 as the action, so a discovered duplicate becomes an alias by an explicit operator decision rather than silently by last-write-wins.

- apps/api/src/services/listing-reconciliation.service.ts:530

2. The eBay half is understated, not overstated: because the update branch writes no externalListingId when parentAsin is null (:531-535), even a SINGLE discovered eBay offer is never recorded whenever a ChannelListing already exists at that coordinate — the row is merely stamped ACTIVE. A second, independent defect in the same five lines.
3. The account claim needs splitting: writing onto the primary account's row (:496) is real for both channels, but on eBay a second account's listing is never even discovered — runEbayReconciliation resolves `tryResolveConnection({ channel: 'EBAY', primary: true })` at :771, under the code's own unresolved marker `🔴 MAP.7: reconciliation is per account; sweep listActiveConnections`.

Severity high stands: an operator-triggered, registered, UI-reachable path silently repoints a live listing's external identity with no snapshot and no conflict, and every subsequent outbound push then targets the surviving ASIN — local mis-pointing that converts into real channel-side writes against the wrong listing.
Step (1) — widening the ListingReconciliation unique key to include externalListingId — is aimed at the wrong arm. Two live listings for one product already produce two recon rows because they carry different seller SKUs (schema.prisma:15019 keys on externalSku; both sweeps upsert on it at :365 and :807); the same-SKU collision the fix targets is largely theoretical on both channels. It is also not free: `confirmedSkus` at :787-791 dedupes by externalSku, so multiplying rows per SKU changes the skip semantics of every subsequent run. Drop it, or justify it on its own.

Step (2) is the right target but incomplete on the branch that matters. "Never rewrite a non-null externalListingId in place" fixes the Amazon arm and leaves the eBay arm exactly as broken: with parentAsin null the update writes only `listingStatus: 'ACTIVE'` (:531-535), so a discovered offerId is ALREADY discarded on the first confirmation whenever a row exists — no second listing needed. The rule must be paired with "if externalListingId is null, write it".

Step (2) also over-automates against the owner's framing. Auto-creating an alias inside confirmReconRow makes the machine decide that two listings exist — the same last-write-wins reflex in better clothes. setReconRowStatus already accepts 'CONFLICT' (:613+): the safe shape is to refuse the confirm, park the row as CONFLICT with a note naming both external IDs, and let the alias come from the explicit ⋯ action. Note too that createAlias is a family-level operation on the ROOT product (listing-alias.service.ts:105-113 resolves `seed.parentId ?? seed.id` and creates one row per family member), throws AliasCreationBlockedError when legacy indexes are present (:99), and opens its own relationshipTransaction — all of which would nest inside the caller's `prisma.$transaction` at :502.

Step (3) puts the banner in the wrong room. The operator doing this is on /reconciliation, and that page has zero alias vocabulary today (0 hits for "alias" across ReconciliationClient.tsx / ReconciliationLoader.tsx / page.tsx; positive control "confirm"=5). A DS Banner on the studio channel scope talks to someone who is not there; the conflict must surface on the recon row itself, with the studio banner secondary.

Missing from the fix entirely: the multi-account arm. runEbayReconciliation sweeps only the primary connection (:771, under the code's own `🔴 MAP.7` marker) and confirm resolves primaryConnectionIds (:496). Fixing the write while the sweep still sees one account leaves the second-account case unexercised — the arm that would have failed is the one never run.

[high]refutedEBAYcorrectness risk

#### eBay status reconcile stamps one SKU-level status onto every listing row of that SKU, so the alias band reports an ended listing as live (and a live one as removed)

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The GALE jacket has three eBay IT listings. A colleague ends alias ③ directly in Seller Hub. Overnight the reconcile job runs; next morning the operator opens the eBay IT scope to decide which listing to end next, and reads each band's status pill.

##### What happens today
The job loads every non-terminal eBay ChannelListing, groups them by PRODUCT SKU, and calls /sell/inventory/v1/offer?sku=… once per SKU (ebay-status-reconcile.job.ts:114-150). It then takes data.offers[0] — without matching offerId or ItemID to any row — derives one desiredStatus, and writes it to EVERY listing id in that SKU's bucket (:201-235). /usr/bin/grep finds 0 hits for aliasKey|aliasId in the file against a control of 2 for channelListing, and the only mention of marketplace is a comment at :133, so the stamp is alias-blind and market-blind. The studio reads exactly that field: the alias group's listingStatus comes from its head row (studio-sheet.service.ts:1523) and the band renders it as the listing's status in the pill tooltip — "Listing {status}" alongside the ItemID (AliasBandCell.tsx:66-71,132,180). So an alias whose listing was ended still reads ACTIVE, and if the SKU's offer is gone from the Inventory API all three read REMOVED/DRAFT while two are still selling.

##### Proposed fix
Reconcile per ROW, not per SKU: fetch the SKU's offers once, then match each returned offer to the ChannelListing whose externalListingId equals its offerId/listingId, stamp that row only, and mark a row whose identity appears in no returned offer as ENDED on its own evidence (rows with a Trading-API ItemID that the Inventory offer endpoint cannot see must be left alone rather than defaulted). Until that lands, the band must not present a SKU-wide value as per-listing truth: attach the DS ProvenanceMark the band already uses for inherited images to the status in bandTitle, worded "status last checked for this SKU, not for this listing", so the honest-UI rule holds and no operator ends the wrong ItemID on the strength of a pill.

[critical]verifiedALLcorrectness risk

#### Unticking a live variant says "Excluded" but the size stays on sale — the write never leaves the database

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has GALE-JACKET live on eBay·IT as one multi-variation listing with 20 sizes. Nero·XXS has been discontinued. They open the studio, go to Variants on the eBay·IT scope (or to the master Variants grid and find the `eBay · IT` column), and untick Nero·XXS. The cell goes muted, the Listing column reads `Excluded`, and hovering shows "Excluded from this listing. The record is kept, so 256789012345 is not lost." They move on believing the size is off sale. Buyers can still buy Nero·XXS on eBay.

##### What happens today
The tick is wired straight to a local-record write with no confirm, no preflight and no danger tone: `projectionColumns.tsx:307-313` calls `onIncludedChange` on toggle, which is `state.setIncluded` (`ChannelProjection.tsx:198`), and the master grid does the same through `columns.tsx:152-154` → `FamilyVariants.tsx:384-399`. Server-side `writeProjectionInclusion` is explicit that it "calls no marketplace, enqueues no `SyncQueue` row and touches no publish path" (`family-projection.service.ts:1558-1574`); the whole effect is `UPDATE "ChannelListing" SET "variationExcluded" = true, "isPublished" = false` (`:415-425`). `variationExcluded` is not even in `schema.prisma` (`:390-396` explains why) and has exactly two readers, both in this one service file — `/usr/bin/grep -rn "variationExcluded" apps/api/src packages apps/web/src` returns only `family-projection.service.ts` lines 384/401/419-423/1564/1566, so no feed builder, payload builder or publish path honours it. The cell's own reason line (`:547-553`) reassures about the local record and never says the variation is still purchasable. Searched for a channel-side counterpart: `/usr/bin/grep -rnE "publish|relist|delist|unpublish" over `_studio/variants` and `_studio/sheet` returns no send verb (only prose and CSS; positive control: 41 files under `_studio/` contain `fetch(`).

##### Proposed fix
Two changes. (a) Make the tick a `GridAction` in the DS registry (`design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts`) rather than a bare cell toggle, so a row whose `listing.externalId` is non-null gets `danger: true` and a `preflight()` returning `ActionImpact` with `level: 'confirm'`, consequences itemised per `useActionConfirm` (`grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx`) — naming the ItemID/ASIN, as `listingRisk.ts` already does for Delete child. (b) Change the copy so it states the channel truth, not the local one: `Excluded here — still on sale on eBay · IT (256789012345)` in the Listing cell, with a `Banner tone="warning"` on the mapping band whenever `children.some(c => !c.included && c.listing.externalId)`. Then add the missing verb: `POST /api/products/:id/studio/projection/children/delist` body `{ expectedVersion, changes: [{ id }] }` enqueuing one `OutboundSyncQueue` row per child (`syncType: 'DELETE_LISTING'` for eBay's `ReviseFixedPriceItem Delete=true` variation removal, `UNPUBLISH_LISTING` for Amazon/Shopify), so exclusion and delisting are one reviewed act rather than two unrelated ones.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
1. "Another surface has the verb." The channel projection's overflow only has `Preflight` (ChannelProjection.tsx:399-406), which mounts ProjectionPreflight.tsx — an information check whose own subtitle is "Nothing is sent from here" (:52). The row menu is useVariantRowMenu.tsx → familyActions.ts, whose only destructive verbs are `delete-variant` (:420) and `demote` (:495); `delete-variant`'s preflight (:436-460) REFUSES outright when any listing has an externalListingId ("This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record."), so it is not a route to taking a live variation down — it is a second confirmation that the studio has no such route. `/usr/bin/grep -rniE "delist|unpublish|remove from|take down|end listing|withdraw"` over the whole `_studio/` tree returns only images-restore prose, an eBay image "Remove from this bucket" button and comments — no variation-removal verb in any tab, drawer, dialog or overflow.
2. "The code is dead / never runs." It is mounted: StudioTabHost.tsx:32,53 registers `VariantsTab`, and the write is served by product-studio.routes.ts:241-242 (`writeProjectionInclusion`). The bulk import path reaches the same function (variant-transfer.routes.ts:170) under the note "No listing is published." (:140).
3. "The set claim rests on the broken grep." Re-ran with /usr/bin/grep: `variationExcluded` appears in apps/api/src, packages and apps/web/src ONLY in family-projection.service.ts (384, 401, 419-423, 1564, 1566); every other hit is a docs fixture/rehearsal copy. I also positively controlled the strongest downstream candidate: apps/api/src/services/ebay-variation-push.service.ts is 2848 lines with 23 `prisma` hits and **0** hits for `isPublished` — so neither the exclusion flag nor the lowered publish flag is consulted when the eBay variation set is rebuilt. The exclusion is therefore inert on the channel even across a later republish, not merely until one.

So the defect is real: a tick that reads "Excluded", is reassuring about the local record, has no confirmation, and leaves the size on sale — with no verb anywhere in the studio that would take it off.
Parts (a) and (b) are sound and DS-conformant: `familyActions.ts:420-460` already shows the exact pattern (danger + `preflight` returning an `ActionImpact` whose findings name the ItemID via `listingRisk.ts:52-66`), so making the tick a registered GridAction reuses an existing flow rather than forking one, and the copy change is the honest-UI rule applied literally.

Part (c) is the weak half and would be dangerous as written. The proposal is right that the vocabulary exists — `DELETE_LISTING` and `UNPUBLISH_LISTING` are both real `syncType` values in use, and `dispatchChannelDelist` (channel-delist.service.ts:91) accepts exactly those two. But for eBay that dispatcher does NOT remove a variation: `delistEbay` (:243-287) takes `job.externalListingId` and calls `endFixedPriceItem({ itemId })` — EndFixedPriceItem on the ItemID ends the WHOLE multi-variation listing. In the finding's own scenario every one of the 20 sizes carries the same parent ItemID (`256789012345` is what the child's reason line prints), so enqueuing one `DELETE_LISTING` row per excluded child would take all 20 sizes off sale, not Nero·XXS. The fix names `ReviseFixedPriceItem Delete=true` in prose but routes it through a queue type whose only existing eBay adapter is EndFixedPriceItem; that gap has to be closed explicitly (a new syncType plus an adapter alongside the existing ebay-variation-push/add/relabel services, keyed on the child SKU inside the variation set, not on the ItemID) or the fix is worse than the defect.

Two further omissions: eBay refuses to delete a variation that has sales or open orders (the recovery is quantity 0, "out of stock", not deletion), so the preflight needs that branch or it will promise a takedown it cannot deliver; and the asymmetry the service documents (`:1565-1567` — INCLUDE deliberately never raises `isPublished`) means the relist half of the owner's request is still missing even after this fix, which the proposal does not acknowledge.

[critical]verifiedALLmissing capability

#### Exclude→include is a one-way ratchet: a re-included variant is permanently frozen out of every push, and no studio control can undo it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Same jacket. Next season Nero·XXS comes back. The operator re-ticks it on the eBay·IT Variants page. The Listing cell turns green and reads `Listed`. What actually happened is that `variationExcluded` was cleared but `isPublished` was left at `false` — the value the exclude had lowered. The variant's hover text now reads "Live on this channel, with publishing turned off for this listing", and there is no control in the studio that can raise it again. Every future price, stock or content push skips that row for good.

##### What happens today
The asymmetry is deliberate and documented: "INCLUDE clears `variationExcluded` and nothing else. Raising `isPublished` could make a row eligible for an outbound sweep, so a tick can never restore publishing — that stays the explicit Publish action" (`family-projection.service.ts:1566-1567`, repeated at `:410-413`). The explicit Publish action it defers to does not exist for Amazon or eBay anywhere in the studio: `PublishMenu.tsx:13` returns `null` on any channel scope while the sheet tab is open, and on a non-sheet tab it renders a button that only calls `setTab('sheet')` (`:14-16`); `channelActions.ts` refuses every live-alias row for both of its write verbs (`:246-249` preflight `unavailable`, `:259-261` run refusal); `ProjectionPreflight.tsx:52` says "Nothing is sent from here." `/usr/bin/grep -rn "isPublished" over `_studio/` returns 20 hits, all type declarations and reads — no writer. The only server writer of `isPublished: true` is `POST /products/:id/listings/:channel/:marketplace/publish` (`marketplaces.routes.ts:1085`), which nothing under `_studio/` calls, and the sheet's own cell writer hardcodes `false` on insert and never touches the column on update (`channel-value-write.ts:11,16,19-22`). This is the literal second half of the Owner's sentence — "and then relist it again".

##### Proposed fix
The include verb must be able to complete its own round trip. Add `POST /api/products/:id/studio/projection/children/publish` body `{ expectedVersion, changes: [{ id }] }` that sets `isPublished: true`, clears `syncPaused`, and enqueues one `OutboundSyncQueue` row (`syncType: 'LISTING_SYNC'`) per child — gated on `listings.publish`. Surface it as a second `GridAction` on the projection grid (`Put back on sale`, `danger: false`, `preflight` naming the coordinate and the ItemID), and give the `Listed` cell a third state word between `Listed` and `Excluded` — `Held (not pushed)` — so the current condition is visible rather than dressed as green. Until that ships, the include tick must report what it did: a `Banner tone="warning"` from `design-system/components` stating "Re-included locally. This variant is not pushed to eBay · IT until it is published again" instead of a cell that reads `Listed`.

The direction is right but the proposal overbuilds and gets one detail wrong. Deriving a distinct state there (e.g. `held`) and adding it to `PROJECTION` in `design-system/grid/renderers/projection.ts:80-125` fixes the dishonest green everywhere at once, including the family page where no hover exists. (d) The interim `Banner tone="warning"` after the tick is weaker than it looks — the operator sees it once and the cell keeps lying afterwards; prefer the state word. (e) Until a studio path exists, the honest stopgap is that the held state's hint names where publishing actually lives today (the product's channel listing tab), rather than implying nothing can be done.

The DS piece is the existing `useActionConfirm` dialog; no new pattern is needed.

#### Add child's confirmation promises "created as a draft with channel sync disabled" — false on the copy-from-sibling path, which clones unpaused listing rows the stock cascade will push

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator adds GALE-JACKET-NERO-XXL to a family that is already live on Amazon IT/DE and eBay IT, and uses `Copy from` on a sibling so the new size starts with the family's content. The confirmation says: "It is created as a draft with channel sync disabled. Review it before publishing." They accept. Later that day a stock count lands for the new SKU. The cascade picks up the cloned Amazon and eBay rows and enqueues QUANTITY_UPDATE pushes for a SKU nobody reviewed.

##### What happens today
The confirmation sentence is at `familyActions.ts:386-390` and is repeated in the ops contract at `familyOps.ts:94-96`. The endpoint it fronts is `POST /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children`; its copy branch clones every one of the sibling's `ChannelListing` rows (`catalog.routes.ts:1299-1336`) with `isPublished: false` and `listingStatus: 'DRAFT'` — but it never sets `syncPaused`, which defaults to `false` (`schema.prisma:1649`). The studio's other creator of the same row shape sets it deliberately and says why: "It is born `syncPaused: true` because `cascadeQuantityToListings` selects every listing of a product with no status filter at all, and Amazon's dispatch PATCHes by SKU rather than by external id" (`family-projection.service.ts:1569-1573`, code at `:1643-1644,1657-1660`). That description of the cascade is accurate: `cascadeQuantityToListings` selects `findMany({ where: { productId } })` with no status, no `isPublished` and no `externalListingId` filter (`stock-movement.service.ts:695-713`); `syncPaused` is the only gate (`:786`), and a row that passes it gets a `QUANTITY_UPDATE` queue row for AMAZON|EBAY|SHOPIFY|WOOCOMMERCE (`:807-828`). So one creator pauses and the other does not, and the confirmation asserts the safety property of the one that does.

##### Proposed fix
Make the code true rather than the sentence softer: add `syncPaused: true` to the cloned-row `create` at `catalog.routes.ts:1310-1335`, matching `family-projection.service.ts:1643-1644`, and add a vitest asserting every ChannelListing row created by the children endpoint is born paused (the asymmetry is the kind only a test keeps closed). Until it lands, the `Add child` preflight must not claim sync is disabled: change the `sideEffects` entry at `familyActions.ts:388` to name what the copy actually does — `Channel records are copied from <sibling> on <n> coordinates. They are not published, but they join stock pushes until you pause them.` — and only show the reassuring sentence when `copyFromProductId` is absent. Same `ActionImpact` shape, no new DS piece.

Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find any path that makes the sentence true.

It is NOT branched on `copyFromProductId`; the copy case only adds a separate `consequences` line at :375-378. familyActions.ts:409 confirms the studio really does send `copyFromProductId` + `copyGroups: ['content','attributes']`, and AddVariationDialog.tsx:136-137 is the picker that sets it — so the copy branch is a live UI path, not dead config.

It also omits `fulfillmentMethod` and `followMasterQuantity`, so the row is born non-FBA with follow=true (schema default) — exactly the two states that keep it inside the cascade's push path.
- schema.prisma:1649 — `syncPaused Boolean @default(false)`. The cloned row is born unpaused.

For a freshly cloned row, syncPaused is the only gate that could have fired, and it is false; the follow math then returns FOLLOW and a push is queued.

No other route creates children. The UI path is reachable and the dispatch has no compensating guard.

It is one of four (FBA, offer-closed, channel policy, listing pause) — it just happens to be the only one a cloned row can trip, because the clone copies neither `fulfillmentMethod` nor `offerClosedAt`. The conclusion stands; the wording should be tightened.
The direction is right — make the code true rather than soften the sentence — and `syncPaused: true` at catalog.routes.ts:1310-1335 does match family-projection.service.ts:1644. Three amendments:

1. Do not ship the interim wording if the one-line server fix lands in the same change; a false-safe sentence for even one release is the worse half. Land `syncPaused: true` first, and the existing sentence becomes true with no branching. If the copy is branched anyway, branch on `copyFromProductId` — note the non-copy path creates NO ChannelListing rows at all, so "channel sync disabled" is vacuously true there and the sentence is only wrong on the copy branch.

2. The fix is incomplete against the state it promises to hold. stock-import.service.ts:1660-1666 clears `syncPaused` for every listing of a product named in a stock sheet with an explicit FOLLOW/PINNED mode (`updateMany({ where: { productId: { in: resumeProducts }, syncPaused: true }, data: { syncPaused: false } })`). A born-paused child silently un-pauses on the next stock import touching that SKU, so the same operator-facing promise breaks one step later. Either the confirmation says the rows stay paused *until you resume them or import stock for them*, or that resume excludes never-published rows.

3. The proposed vitest ("every ChannelListing row created by the children endpoint is born paused") passes vacuously if the copy branch creates zero rows. Assert the created row COUNT equals the sibling's listing count first, then assert every row's `syncPaused === true`. Also assert `fulfillmentMethod` and `followMasterQuantity`, since it is the combination (not-FBA + follow + unpaused) that produces the push — a future clone that starts copying `fulfillmentMethod` would change which gate fires and the pause assertion alone would not notice.

#### Creating a listing alias is a one-way door that permanently freezes a product's family structure, and the studio has no way back

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator on the eBay·IT channel sheet uses `⋯ → + Add listing alias` to plan a second listing for the family (the Variants spec's "listing split"). A toast says "Listing alias created as a Nexus draft." Weeks later they try to split the family — unlink two sizes and move them under a new parent. Every family verb refuses: "This action affects products with listing aliases. Resolve their listing relationships before changing the family. Archived aliases are protected too." Nothing in the studio can remove or archive the alias.

##### What happens today
`ChannelSheet.tsx:2017-2023` offers `+ Add listing alias` and creates a real `ProductListingAlias` via `POST /api/products/:id/aliases` (`useChannelSheet.ts:420-435`), confirming with a plain success toast (`ChannelSheet.tsx:1997`) that says nothing about consequences. From that moment `relationshipAliasConflicts` (`relationship-alias-guard.ts:4-11`) returns the product for any owned alias OR any ChannelListing with a non-empty `aliasKey`/`aliasId`, and that set is asserted by attach (`product-relationship.service.ts:57`), reparent (`:77`), unlink (`:92`), demote (`:116`) and delete (`:124`) — every family verb the studio has. Archiving is the documented escape and is deliberately not wired: "Archiving (`DELETE`) is deliberately NOT wired here" (`useChannelSheet.ts:438-441`); the guard's own comment says archived aliases are protected too (`relationship-alias-guard.ts:10`), so archiving would not help even if it were wired. The same trap is set implicitly by `Add child` with `Copy from`, which clones the sibling's `aliasKey` onto the new child (`catalog.routes.ts:1315`), and by projection include under a non-primary alias (`family-projection.service.ts:1655-1656`). None of the family verbs' preflights mention aliases at all, so the refusal arrives only at press time, from the server.

##### Proposed fix
Three parts. (1) Say it before, not after: give `+ Add listing alias` a `preflight` (it is already an overflow item, so wrap it in the same `GridAction`/`useActionConfirm` flow the family verbs use) whose `sideEffects` state "While this alias exists, this product cannot be attached, unlinked, moved, demoted or deleted." (2) Wire the exit: surface `DELETE /api/products/:id/aliases/:aliasId` as a `danger` action on the alias band with a type-to-confirm on the alias label, and decide with the Owner whether an ARCHIVED alias should still block — the guard comment says it must, but then archive is not an exit and the alias must instead be deletable once its coordinate has no `externalListingId`. (3) Make the family verbs honest in advance: add the alias check to each verb's `available()`/`preflight()` in `familyActions.ts` using the existing `family` payload, so the refusal is a disabled item with a reason at the surface rather than a server error after the confirm — the pattern `needsPermission` (`familyActions.ts:100-107`) already establishes for permissions.

#### Splitting or merging a live family is a local-only rename of the parentage; the channel keeps the old variation family and nothing reconciles it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a 20-child jacket family live on Amazon IT as a parent ASIN with child ASINs, and on eBay IT as one multi-variation listing. They decide to split it: the 10 Nero sizes move under a new parent, the Giallo ones stay. They select the Nero children and use `Move to another parent…`, one at a time. Each confirm tells them "<SKU> leaves GALE-JACKET and joins GALE-JACKET-NERO" and nothing else. On Amazon, those 10 child ASINs are still children of the old parent ASIN; on eBay they are still variations inside the old ItemID. Nexus and the channels now disagree, and nothing will tell anyone.

##### What happens today
`reparentProduct` writes `parentId` and bumps `version` and nothing else (`product-relationship.service.ts:69-83`); `unlinkProducts` (`:85-97`) and `demoteProduct` (`:109-121`) are the same shape. None of them touch `ChannelListing`, so `externalParentId` — "For Amazon parent ASIN" (`schema.prisma:1546`) — survives pointing at the old parent, and no sync row is created: `/usr/bin/grep -c "outboundSyncQueue"` returns 0 in both `product-relationship.service.ts` and `pim.routes.ts` (positive control: 5 in `stock-movement.service.ts`), and the `/api/amazon/pim/unlink-child` handler is a bare call into the same transaction (`amazon.routes.ts:1159-1185`). The UI states this as reassurance rather than as a warning: unlink's `sideEffects` say "Channel listings are not changed — unlinking only breaks the parent/child link" (`familyActions.ts:210`), reparent's say nothing about channels at all (`familyActions.ts:256-260`), and demote's mention only that the children survive locally (`:517-522`). Notably the studio DOES have a real eBay push for the cosmetic half of this domain — `Variation order` publishes through `PublicationReview` (`PresentationTab.tsx:27`, `PublicationReview.tsx:32` `POST /api/ebay/presentation-publications/:jobId/execute`) — so the one variation-lifecycle verb that reaches the channel is the one that does not change what is for sale.

##### Proposed fix
Make every family verb's preflight read the channel, the way Delete child already does. `familyActions.ts` already has `ops.listings()` and `classifyListings()`; call them in unlink/reparent/demote too and put each live coordinate in `findings` with `severity: 'warn'`, replacing "Channel listings are not changed" with the true sentence: "Amazon IT still shows GALE-JACKET-NERO-M under parent ASIN B0XXXXXXX. Nexus and the channel will disagree until the listing is rebuilt." Then close the loop with a durable marker rather than a silent divergence: on any relationship write that touches a product with a live `externalListingId`, stamp `ChannelListing.validationStatus = 'FAMILY_DRIFT'` (existing column, `schema.prisma:1678`) and surface those rows in the existing `Needs attention` tab (`channel-ops/ErrorsSyncTab.tsx`) with a `Go to row` link — so a split family shows up as work to do instead of as nothing at all. No new DS component: `findings` + `useActionConfirm` + the existing Needs-attention filter chips.

### Amazon6

[critical]verifiedAMAZONcorrectness risk

#### Every Amazon delist calls SP-API DELETE with the ASIN in the SKU slot — the offer is never removed, and the queue reports success

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket live on Amazon IT under SKU JKT-NAVY-42 / ASIN B08XYZ1234. They bin the product and choose 'Also remove it from the channels' (the /products BulkActionBar hard-delete, channelAction 'delete'). Nexus enqueues DELETE_LISTING and reports the cascade fired. The offer is still buyable on amazon.it the next morning.

##### What happens today
`dispatchChannelDelist` → `delistAmazon` takes `job.externalListingId` and, on the strength of a comment that says 'externalListingId for Amazon is typically the SKU' (channel-delist.service.ts:139-141), passes it straight into `amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem({ sellerId, sku, marketplaceId })` (channel-delist.service.ts:162). That value is not the SKU. The schema says so twice in its own comments: ChannelListing.externalListingId is annotated 'Amazon: Parent ASIN (non-buyable) or child ASIN (buyable)' (schema.prisma:1542-1545), and the queue column that carries it is annotated 'Amazon ASIN or eBay ItemID' (schema.prisma:6860). Every Amazon writer of that column writes an ASIN (amazon.routes.ts:1263,1270,1451,1458; flat-file-pull.service.ts:267; submission.service.ts:1482,1486; listing-reconciliation.service.ts:375,390,520,533; inbound-sync.service.ts:69,81). The producer copies it verbatim into the queue row (products-catalog.routes.ts:1889). The SP-API call then issues DELETE /listings/2021-08-01/items/{sellerId}/{ASIN} (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1160) against an endpoint the client's own doc describes as 'Removes the seller's offer for the SKU' (:1117-1120). Amazon has no such SKU, so the offer survives. The one caller that gets this right is the recovery service, which passes `preview.before.sku` (recovery.service.ts:320) — so the bug is a divergence inside one codebase, not a missing convention. Compounding it: when the operator picks the *reversible* option, `channelAction:'unpublish'` → UNPUBLISH_LISTING, `delistAmazon` logs 'Amazon UNPUBLISH falling back to DELETE (PATCH client TODO)' and falls through to the same delete (channel-delist.service.ts:151-160) — so the safe choice is silently the destructive one, aimed at the wrong key.

##### Proposed fix
Server, two parts. (1) `ChannelDelistJob` gains an explicit `sellerSku: string | null` — an explicit flag, never inferred from `externalListingId` — and `delistAmazon` refuses (`retryable:false`, errorCode `AMAZON_DELIST_NO_SKU`) rather than guessing when it is absent. Populate it at every producer: products-catalog.routes.ts:1849-1866 already selects the listing rows, so add `product: { select: { sku: true } }` and carry `sellerSku` in the payload; amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:53-56 likewise. (2) Delete the unpublish→delete fallthrough. UNPUBLISH_LISTING on Amazon must route to `closeMarketOffers` (amazon-market-offer.service.ts) — the documented, reversible purchasable_offer delete — and return `SKIPPED` with a named reason for FBA rows, exactly as SCT.6 already does. Until (2) lands, `delistAmazon` should hard-refuse `action==='unpublish'` instead of quietly performing a delete. A vitest fixture in the ebay-flat-file-delete style should assert the SP-API call receives the Product.sku and not the ASIN — a zero-change round trip cannot catch this, so the fixture must carry a SKU and an ASIN that differ.

WHERE THE FINDING IS MIS-STATED (hence corrected title, severity unchanged):
1. "the queue reports success" is only provable on the gated/dry-run path. deleteListingsItem short-circuits at client:1143-1155 when AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE is unset or dry-run and returns `success:true, dryRun:true` with no HTTP — that is a genuine silent green (applyDelistResultToQueue:317-325 → SUCCESS). In live mode an unknown SKU yields a 4xx, and request() throws at client:267 (`throw new Error(HTTP ${res.status} …)`), which delistAmazon catches (:174) into `retryable:true` → eventually FAILED/isDead. So in live mode the operator likely sees a failure, not a green. The invariant that holds in every mode is "the offer is never removed".
2. The finding missed the worse sibling path. amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts DELETES the ChannelListing rows (lines 58-64) BEFORE dispatching the delist (line 71) with the same ASIN-as-SKU value, passes a synthetic queueId (`amz-rm-…`) so applyDelistResultToQueue never runs, and swallows any throw in `catch { /* best-effort */ }` (line 82). That path loses the ASIN from the DB and reports only `delisted:false` — no queue row, no retry, no /sync-logs trace.
3. Aggravator not noted: deleteListingsItem reads `process.env.AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE` directly (client:1143) instead of `getAmazonPublishMode()` (used at client:519, 669, 792, 884). getAmazonPublishMode returns 'gated' when NEXUS_ENABLE_AMAZON_PUBLISH is off (amazon-publish-gate.service.ts:35-52). So the DELETE is the one SP-API write that escapes the master kill switch — with the flag off and AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE=live, everything else is gated and this destructive call still fires.
Directionally right, incomplete in four places.
(1) The `sellerSku` plumb-through is correct and must be producer-side, because by drain time the Product row is gone (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:132-140 says so explicitly) — a late lookup inside delistAmazon cannot work for the cascade. But ChannelListing has no sku column (verified absent across schema.prisma:1509-1887), so the producer must join `product: { select: { sku: true } }`, matching the convention already used at amazon-market-offer.service.ts:97 and flat-file-pull.service.ts:190.
(2) The fix names amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:53-56 but understates it: that service deletes the ChannelListing rows at lines 58-64 BEFORE dispatching at line 71, so the SKU must be read into memory before the transaction, not after; and its `catch { }` at line 82 plus the synthetic queueId (`amz-rm-…`, line 73) mean the failure is invisible today — the fix must also surface that error, or the corrected refusal (AMAZON_DELIST_NO_SKU) will be swallowed exactly like the current one.
(3) Missing from the fix: deleteListingsItem bypasses the master publish gate by reading process.env.AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE directly (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1143) while every other write uses getAmazonPublishMode() (:519, :669, :792, :884). Route it through the gate in the same change, otherwise the corrected delete becomes a correctly-aimed destructive call that the kill switch still cannot stop.
(4) Missing: FBA. closeMarketOffers has an explicit `SKIPPED_FBA` rule (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:104-110, "FBA is Amazon-managed — never close it"); delistAmazon has no such guard, so once the SKU is correct the delete path becomes newly capable of removing FBA offers. Add the same skip before shipping the corrected key.
The proposed vitest fixture is the right shape — a SKU and an ASIN that differ, asserting the value handed to deleteListingsItem — and matches the memory rule that a zero-change round trip cannot test the write.

[critical]verifiedAMAZONdata integrity risk

#### 'Remove from Amazon IT' deletes the local row first, discards the SP-API result, and reports success from the local delete alone

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator wants the jacket off Amazon DE only, keeping IT. They open the Amazon flat-file sheet on DE, select the row, and hit Remove. The toast says 'Removed 1 listing from Amazon DE — product and stock kept.' In fact the DE offer is still live (see AMZ-1), and Nexus has permanently destroyed the ASIN link, the flat-file snapshot, the channel overrides and the offer-close snapshot for that coordinate — so nothing in the system now knows the DE listing exists.

##### What happens today
`removeAmazonListing` deletes the ChannelListing rows inside a transaction (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:59-65) and only afterwards loops the captured external ids to fire `dispatchChannelDelist` (:68-83). Order is fatal: the local record is already gone when the remote call is attempted. Every remote failure is then swallowed by a bare `catch { /* best-effort; never blocks the committed removal */ }` (:82), so the returned `delisted` flag is false with no error text. The UI discards even that: the response type it destructures declares only `{ productId, channelListingsRemoved, error }` (AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1892), success is computed as `channelListingsRemoved > 0` (:1893) — a count of *local rows deleted* — and the toast asserts 'Removed N listings from Amazon {marketplace}' (:1896). The confirmation that precedes it is a native `confirm()` (:1908, and a second copy at :4231) reading 'The product and its stock stay in Nexus; other channels are untouched' — true, and silent about everything it does destroy. By FK cascade that is ChannelListingSnapshot, ChannelListingOverride, Offer, ChannelListingImage, SyncAttempt, AmazonSuppression and ListingIssue (schema.prisma cascade set), plus the row's own `flatFileSnapshot`, `overrideData` and `offerCloseSnapshot`. No ChannelListingSnapshot is captured first and no ListingRecoveryEvent is written, so there is no artefact to relist from. The `deleteMany` filter is `{ productId in ids, channel:'AMAZON', marketplace }` (:61) with no `channelConnectionId` and no `aliasKey`, so on a multi-account or multi-alias coordinate one market removal wipes every account's row for that market.

##### Proposed fix
Server first (the flat-file editor is untouchable, so the fix must hold even if its UI never changes): invert the order in `removeAmazonListing` — capture a ChannelListingSnapshot and write a ListingRecoveryEvent, call `dispatchChannelDelist`, and only delete the local row when the remote call succeeded; on failure keep the row and set `{ listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false, offerActive:false }`, the one shape that is relistable (the pattern flat-file/import/apply.ts:588 already uses). Never swallow: return `{ delisted, delistError }` per target. Narrow the `deleteMany` to include `channelConnectionId` and `aliasKey`. Then give the studio the honest verb the Owner asked for, as a DS grid action on the Amazon channel sheet: a `GridAction` with `danger:true`, `scope: ROW`, `confirm: 'type-to-confirm'` with the real SKU as the phrase (grid/actions/registry.ts:167-198, rendered by useActionConfirm), whose `preflight` itemises exactly what is lost — ASIN, snapshot, overrides, offers — as `consequences`, and whose `unavailable` names any FBA row (see AMZ-5). Because MenuItemDef carries no tone and both DS menu adapters drop `GridAction.danger` (menuAdapters.tsx:75-91,150-169), file that gap rather than hand-rolling a red menu item.

#### The studio's Amazon 'Pause offer' confirmation promises buyers stop seeing the offer; nothing is sent to Amazon

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A stockout hits the jacket on Amazon FR. The operator opens the studio on scope AMAZON · FR, selects the SKU rows and picks 'Pause 3 offers on Amazon FR'. The confirmation says buyers will stop seeing the offer. They confirm, get a success, and close the tab. Amazon keeps taking orders on FR.

##### What happens today
The verb's `preflight` sets the unconditional consequence 'Buyers stop seeing this offer on this channel and market. The listing itself is not ended and its reviews and identifiers are untouched.' (channelActions.ts:230). `run` PATCHes /api/products/:id/offer-availability (:265). That handler does exactly one thing: `prisma.channelListing.upsert({ update: { offerActive } })` (marketplaces.routes.ts:308-322). There is no SP-API call on the pause branch; only the *activate* branch does anything outbound, and that is an inventory resync (:326). Downstream, `offerActive:false` has two consumers and neither suppresses a buy box: outbound-sync.service.ts:645-656 skips *pushing* to the row, and only behind the opt-in env gate `NEXUS_RESPECT_OFFER_ACTIVE === '1'` whose own comment says 'default OFF'; and amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3415-3420 injects `skip_offer` — but only on the *next* Amazon flat-file submit, an operator-driven act on a different page that the studio cannot perform (PublishMenu.tsx:13 renders nothing on a channel sheet). So at the moment of the act, the dialog's claim is false, and the same claim is repeated as a tooltip in the record drawer: 'The listing still exists on the marketplace; its buy box is suppressed.' (drawer/panes/ListingsPane.tsx:130, contract restated at drawer/types.ts:166-171). The dialog also contradicts itself in one breath: the sideEffect line for non-live rows reads 'the change stays local until they are published' (:238) while the consequence above it says buyers stop seeing it.

##### Proposed fix
Either make the verb true or make the copy true; do not ship the gap. Truthful copy today: the consequence becomes 'Marks this offer paused in Nexus. Amazon is not contacted — the offer stays buyable until the next Amazon submit carries skip_offer.' and the drawer's Offer row renders `paused (in Nexus only)` with that tooltip instead of 'its buy box is suppressed'. Truthful verb (preferred, and it is already built): route the Amazon branch of the pause verb at `closeMarketOffers`/`reopenMarketOffers` (amazon-market-offer.service.ts) via a new `POST /api/products/:id/listings/amazon/:marketplace/offer` `{ action: 'close' | 'reopen', reason? }`, so the DS confirmation can name the real consequence — the marketplace's purchasable_offer instance is deleted, the SKU, content, ASIN and reviews survive, sibling markets and the shared EU quantity are untouched — and the FBA refusal becomes a `disabled(reason)` in `available()` rather than a surprise. Keep the existing `GridAction` shell and useActionConfirm; only the deps and the copy change.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Exactly the Owner's sentence. Its header states the invariant the Owner is asking for: SKU, content, ASIN, reviews, sibling markets and the shared EU quantity are untouched (:8-14). It is exposed only through `POST /api/stock/sync-control/actions` with action CLOSE_OFFER/REOPEN_OFFER (sync-control.routes.ts:579, 811-819). Because SCT.6 deliberately never writes `listingStatus` or `offerActive`, the drawer prints Status = ACTIVE and Offer = 'selling' (ListingsPane.tsx:103,127) for a market whose offer Amazon no longer has.

##### Proposed fix
Two additive moves, no new mechanism. (1) Put the close state on the wire: add `offerClosedAt`, `offerClosedBy`, `offerCloseReason` to the studio-sheet projection's ChannelListing select (studio-sheet.service.ts:463 already selects offerActive alongside followMaster* — same line) and to `SheetListing`. Then the drawer's Listings pane gains a third fact beside 'Pushed to channel' and 'Offer' — `Market offer: closed on 14 Nov by awais · reopenable from snapshot` — and the channel sheet's readiness vocabulary gains a `closed` state so a closed market is never painted 'live'. This alone removes the lie even if no verb ships. (2) Surface the verb where the Owner looks for it: a single DS `GridAction` pair on the Amazon channel sheet, `Close offer on Amazon DE…` / `Reopen offer on Amazon DE…`, label following state exactly as `offerVerb` already does (channelActions.ts:170-183), `preflight` naming what survives (ASIN, reviews, IT offer, shared EU quantity) and what is required to come back (the snapshot), `available()` returning `disabled('FBA row — Amazon owns FBA logistics; close it in Seller Central')` for FBA rows so SCT.6's fail-closed refusal is taught rather than discovered. API shape: `POST /api/products/:id/listings/amazon/:marketplace/offer { action:'close'|'reopen', reason? }` delegating to the existing service, so there is one implementation, not a second one.

#### The row-level Amazon removal path bypasses the codebase's own FBA stranded-inventory warning

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The jacket is FBA on Amazon IT with 140 units sitting in the Castel San Giovanni fulfilment centre. The operator removes the IT listing from the Amazon sheet to stop selling it. The units stay in Amazon's warehouse bound to the SKU's FNSKU, unfulfillable, accruing storage and eventually long-term storage fees, with no removal order created and nothing in Nexus saying so.

##### What happens today
The codebase knows this hazard precisely and warns about it on exactly one path. `findFbaDeleteRows` (amazon/flat-file.service.ts:2615-2645) flags every FBA SKU a batch would delete — Product.fulfillmentMethod 'FBA' or positive AMAZON-EU-FBA stock — and `POST /amazon/flat-file/preflight` turns it into an operator-grade warning: 'FBA inventory present — deleting this listing will NOT remove the units from Amazon's warehouse; they stay bound to this SKU's FNSKU and become unfulfillable. In Seller Central, create a removal order or sell through first; if relisting under a new SKU, relabel the units to the new FNSKU.' (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:764, 806-811). That warning only fires for a row whose `record_action` is 'delete' inside the preflight of a *submit*. The Remove path never runs preflight: `deleteSelected` goes straight from a native confirm to `removeFromAmazon` → `POST /amazon/flat-file/remove` (AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1905-1912, :1885-1891), and `removeAmazonListing` is 86 lines with no FBA signal read anywhere — it selects only `{ externalListingId }` (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:53-56) and deletes. The asymmetry is stark against SCT.6, which refuses FBA rows fail-closed on the far gentler *close* operation (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:61-63): Nexus refuses to reversibly close an FBA offer but will irreversibly delete one without a word. In the studio there is no FBA awareness at all — /usr/bin/grep over `_studio/` for FBA|fnsku|stranded|fulfillmentMethod returns no Amazon-fulfilment hit (the `stranded` matches are images/publish/schedule.ts, an unrelated scheduling state).

##### Proposed fix
Move the rule into the layer every path crosses instead of leaving it in one route's preflight. `removeAmazonListing` calls `findFbaDeleteRows`-equivalent logic on its targets and returns `action:'REFUSED_FBA'` with the existing warning text unless the caller passes an explicit `acknowledgedFba: true` — an explicit flag, never inferred. The same fact then drives the studio verb from AMZ-2/AMZ-4: the `GridAction.preflight` reads the row's fulfilment signal and emits a `findings` entry at severity 'error' per FBA SKU with its on-hand FBA quantity, and the DS `useActionConfirm` type-to-confirm phrase is the SKU (grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx rules), so an FBA takedown cannot be a single click. Since the studio sheet has no fulfilment column at all today, add `fulfillmentMethod` and the AMAZON-EU-FBA on-hand quantity to the Amazon channel projection (studio-sheet.service.ts:463 select) so the grid can show an FBA badge at rest — the operator should see it before they reach for a destructive verb, not inside the dialog.

- apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:762-765
- apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:806-811

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and the asymmetry is real. The hazard rule exists and is precise: flat-file.service.ts:2605-2645 — `findFbaDeleteRows` collects every record_action='delete' SKU whose Product.fulfillmentMethod is FBA or which holds positive stock at location code AMAZON-EU-FBA — and amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:762-765, 806-811 turn it into the operator-grade warning quoted, but only for a row already marked `record_action='delete'` inside the SUBMIT preflight. The Remove path never crosses it: AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1903-1912 goes from a native `confirm()` straight to `removeFromAmazon`, which POSTs /api/amazon/flat-file/remove (:1885-1891); the route (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1806-1820) calls `removeAmazonListing` with no preflight; and the service reads no fulfilment signal at all — it selects `{ externalListingId }` only (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:53-56), deletes the ChannelListing rows in a transaction (:58-64), then calls `dispatchChannelDelist` per external id (:67-83). I confirmed that is a real irreversible marketplace call, not a stub: channel-delist.service.ts:105-106 routes AMAZON and :162-174 invokes `amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem`, with the header at :16-17 stating 'Seller offer is removed; catalog ASIN persists'. The contrast with the reversible operation is exactly as stated — amazon-market-offer.service.ts:59-63 and :104 refuse FBA rows fail-closed on CLOSE. And the studio has no fulfilment signal of its own: the Amazon channel projection's ChannelListing select (studio-sheet.service.ts:468) carries no fulfillmentMethod. I could not refute this by finding the warning on another path.
Putting the rule in `removeAmazonListing` is the right layer and is compatible with the flat-file-untouchable rule (the service and route are not the editor). One caveat the fix understates: `findFbaDeleteRows` keys on `record_action` and `item_sku` from sheet rows, so the remove path needs the equivalent query by productId, not that function as-is. The studio half is speculative until the studio actually grows a remove verb — today the only row-level Amazon removal UI is the flat-file page.

Give each row two verbs: 'Mark resolved' (PATCH /listings/amazon/suppressions/:id, already built) and, for a listing Amazon has made inactive, a DS `Menu` item 'Recover this listing…' opening /products/:id/recover pre-scoped to this channel×market — the D9 ruling that removed the header link-outs equated Recover with History, but RestoreMode.tsx:133 states restore makes no marketplace call while recovery.service.ts:318-322 really does delete and re-put, so they are not the same capability and the equivalence should be put back to the Owner. The consuming surface is live legacy code, not dead code: SuppressionCard.tsx:1-24 header comment matches the described features (per-reason 'Fix in <card>' jump, Mark resolved, Seller Central link), it fetches the endpoint at :179 and PATCHes at :239, and it is rendered by AmazonCockpit.tsx:791 from the legacy page still mounted at /products/[id]/edit (page.tsx → ProductEditClient.tsx:1566). No `_studio/` file imports from `../tabs` (verified by /usr/bin/grep for "tabs/|cockpit" in the studio tree — only prose references).
5. Recovery is a separate, non-equivalent capability: recovery.service.ts:5-30 lists the five modes, :155-161 carries the ~30-day SKU-cooldown warning, and :318-330 calls `amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem` — a real marketplace delete — while the studio's restore explicitly tells the operator "it makes no marketplace call: nothing is published by restoring" (RestoreMode.tsx:131-134). The D9 ruling that removed the header `⋯` (including Recover) does equate them: pes-claims.md #214 "Recover → time-travel restore inside History (D3)". So the equivalence really is unsound and the studio has no link to /products/[id]/recover (page exists: recover/page.tsx, RecoverClient.tsx; zero references from `_studio/`).

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED
- Drawer/alias-band status: the studio does render raw `listingStatus` (ListingsPane.tsx:103, AliasBandCell.tsx:132), and the manual POST path sets `listingStatus:'SUPPRESSED'` (listings-syndication.routes.ts:2330-2332), so that one path would surface the word. But the SP-API ingest path — the one that actually populates from defect reports — never writes listingStatus (/usr/bin/grep for "listingStatus|channelListing.update" in amazon-suppression-ingest.service.ts: zero matches). So for the real ingest the drawer still reads ACTIVE, and the reason text, suppressedAt and resolve verb are unreachable anywhere in the studio.
- The drawer's nearest vocabulary, "Offer: paused" (ListingsPane.tsx:122-133), is driven by `offerActive`/buy box, not suppression.
- Mitigation that caps severity, not the defect: the capability still exists outside the studio (legacy cockpit, and /listings/amazon resolves suppressions at AmazonListingsClient.tsx:274). Medium is the right level — the studio is the replacement surface and offers no path.

MIS-STATEMENT CORRECTED: "invisible" is true of the SP-API ingest path; a manually-opened suppression does flip listingStatus and would print as a bare status string. Title tightened accordingly.
The fix is sound and mostly reuses built parts, with three corrections. (1) Do not describe the console as merely "not reading" the source — the sharper defect is the SP-API ingest path never writes `ChannelListing.listingStatus` (amazon-suppression-ingest.service.ts has zero listingStatus writes), while the manual POST path does (listings-syndication.routes.ts:2330-2332). That split means even the drawer's Status fact (ListingsPane.tsx:103) is inconsistent between the two ways a suppression is born; the fix should either state that the console is the only honest surface or route the inconsistency to the API lane, not silently rely on status. (2) "Populated" is over-claimed: `ingestAmazonSuppressionAllMarketplaces` has exactly one caller, the manual `POST /api/amazon/suppression/backfill` (amazon.routes.ts:1862) — no cron reference found. The row count on prod is unmeasured, so the honest-empty branch of the proposal is the likely one, and the fix should lead with it rather than treat it as the fallback. (3) The Recover link-out proposal reopens a decided Owner ruling (pes-claims #214/D9 removed the whole `⋯` menu). Raising the Recover≠History distinction to the Owner is right; shipping a `Menu` item to /products/:id/recover before that ruling is reversed would violate the standing rule that lanes ask rather than rule. Reusing the cockpit's reason→card regex is correct in spirit but the mapping targets cockpit card names; in the studio it must map to sheet rows/attribute keys, which is a re-derivation the fix understates.

[critical]verifiedEBAYcorrectness risk

#### eBay UK can never be delisted: region 'GB' throws in siteIdForMarket and the queue row dies non-retryable

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket live on eBay UK (ebay.co.uk) and eBay IT. The UK line is discontinued, so they select the product in /products, send it to the bin and hard-delete it with the channel action set to 'Unpublish (recommended)'. The IT rows are ended correctly. The UK listing keeps selling on ebay.co.uk with a product that no longer exists in Nexus — orders keep arriving for stock that has been purged.

##### What happens today
eBay UK ChannelListing rows are written with region = 'GB' AND marketplace = 'GB' (flat-file-unified.routes.ts:614 writes `region, marketplace: region` where `region = mp === 'UK' ? 'GB' : mp` at :581; the same UK→GB normalisation is used for every eBay read, e.g. ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1906, :1927). The delist cascade stamps `targetRegion: l.region ?? l.marketplace ?? null` (products-catalog.routes.ts:1886), so the queue row carries 'GB'. delistEbay then calls `siteIdForMarket(job.targetRegion ?? 'IT')` (channel-delist.service.ts:274), and SITE_ID_BY_MARKET has IT/DE/FR/ES/UK and no GB (ebay-trading-api.service.ts:10-16), so siteIdForMarket throws `unknown eBay market: GB` (:19-21). The throw is caught by the auth try/catch at :275-281, which returns `retryable: false` with code EBAY_DELIST_AUTH_ERROR — applyDelistResultToQueue then marks the row FAILED + isDead immediately (:325-340). No EndFixedPriceItem is ever attempted. Both fallbacks are 'GB' too, so the `?? l.marketplace` branch does not rescue it.

##### Proposed fix
Normalise at the boundary, not at every call site: make `siteIdForMarket` accept the region spelling by adding `GB: '3'` to SITE_ID_BY_MARKET (ebay-trading-api.service.ts:10) and export a single `ebayMarketOf(regionOrMarket)` that folds GB↔UK, then use it in delistEbay. Add a vitest case per market code actually present in ChannelListing.region for channel='EBAY' — derived from the DB at test time, not a hardcoded list (a hardcoded member list is exactly the set-claim trap). Surface the failure: a dead EBAY_DELIST_AUTH_ERROR row must render in the studio's Needs attention tab (channel-ops/ErrorsSyncTab) as a DS Banner tone="danger" reading 'eBay UK listing was NOT ended — it is still live', not only in /sync-logs.

[critical]verifiedEBAYux defect

#### 'Unpublish (recommended)' promises a reversible pause; on eBay it is an irreversible EndFixedPriceItem and the local listing record is destroyed

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is cleaning up the catalog and bins a summer dress that is live on eBay IT. The hard-delete dialog opens with 'Unpublish (recommended)' already selected and the body text 'Pause the offer on each channel — keeps the listing record so you can republish later.' They type DELETE and confirm, expecting to put the dress back next season. The eBay listing is ended for good, the ItemID is gone from Nexus, and there is no republish.

##### What happens today
The dialog defaults to `channelAction = 'unpublish'` (BulkActionBar.tsx:1097) and the copy says 'Pause the offer on each channel — keeps the listing record so you can republish later. Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing.' (en.json:5223). Three things in that sentence are false for eBay. (1) delistEbay ignores the action entirely — the parameter is `_action` (channel-delist.service.ts:242-243) and both UNPUBLISH_LISTING and DELETE_LISTING run the same EndFixedPriceItem (:284-286). (2) 'keeps the listing record' is false: the queue row is created inside the same transaction that deletes the Product (products-catalog.routes.ts:1880 then the product delete), and ChannelListing cascades off Product, so the local record with the ItemID is gone. (3) 'so you can republish later' is false: eBay cannot re-activate an ended fixed-price item — a relist mints a NEW ItemID — and there is no relist implementation anywhere; SellSimilarItem appears only as prose in channel-delist.service.ts:21, and /usr/bin/grep over apps+packages for RelistFixedPriceItem|SellSimilarItem returns only that comment and test strings. The confirm phrase is the literal word DELETE (en.json:5230), which the DS ruling on type-to-confirm explicitly forbids.

##### Proposed fix
Make the dialog say what each channel will actually do, per channel, computed not asserted. Move the flow onto the DS GridAction registry (design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts) with `confirm: 'type-to-confirm'` and the phrase set to the real SKU (never the word DELETE), rendered by useActionConfirm (grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx) so consequences are itemised per listing rather than counted: one line per (channel, market, ItemID) reading 'eBay IT — item 257584954808 will be ENDED. eBay cannot reopen an ended item; relisting creates a new ItemID.' Drive it from the existing GET /products/hard-delete-preflight (products-catalog.routes.ts:1666) extended to return a per-row `reversible: boolean` + `channelEffect` string. Rename the eBay arm from 'Unpublish' to 'End listing' and drop '(recommended)' for any selection containing an eBay row.

##### Evidence

- apps/web/src/lib/i18n/messages/en.json:5222-5227,5230
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:242-243,284-286,21
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1878-1890

So "Amazon: discontinued" is also a lie; two of the three named channels do a destructive delete under a label reading "Unpublish (recommended)".
