Directionally right, but three gaps and one thing it can do more cheaply than it thinks.

(1) It scopes the fix to eBay. The Amazon arm is equally false — channel-delist.service.ts:150-164 logs 'Amazon UNPUBLISH falling back to DELETE (PATCH client TODO)' and then calls deleteListingsItem. Only Shopify actually honours a reversible DRAFT (delistShopify). So the per-channel effect string must be computed for Amazon too, and 'Unpublish (recommended)' must lose '(recommended)' for any selection containing an Amazon row, not just an eBay one.

(2) For an eBay-only (or Amazon-only) selection the 'Unpublish' and 'Delete on channel' radios are the SAME operation — dispatchChannelDelist:91-109 routes both to the same function. Renaming the eBay arm to 'End listing' is not enough; two radios that do identical things must collapse to one, or the dialog is still lying by implication.

(3) The confirm phrase is under-specified. registry.ts:117 mandates a SKU, but this is a BULK dialog over up to 200 ids. The fix says 'the real SKU' without saying what the phrase is for count > 1. validateImpact (registry.ts:267-268) refuses type-to-confirm with no confirmPhrase rather than downgrading, so an unresolved bulk phrase will hard-fail the DS gate rather than degrade. Define it: the SKU when count === 1, and a defined multi-row convention otherwise.

(4) Cheaper than proposed: GET /products/hard-delete-preflight already returns productId, channel, marketplace, region and externalListingId per row (products-catalog.routes.ts:1676-1690). Per-(channel, market, ItemID) itemisation needs NO API change — the client already has the tuples and only renders a count (en.json:5210). `reversible`/`channelEffect` are a pure function of channel + action and can be derived client-side; adding them server-side is optional and risks a second source of truth diverging from channel-delist.service.ts. If they are added server-side, derive them from the same table the dispatcher switches on, or you have reintroduced the exact drift that caused this bug.

(5) Missing from the fix: nothing addresses the underlying capability gap the owner actually asked about — there is still no way to end/relist a single market or channel while KEEPING the product, and no republish path after the cascade. Honest copy makes the dialog truthful; it does not give the operator the reversible per-channel delist they wanted.

[critical]verifiedEBAYdata integrity risk

#### Binning one variation child ends the whole shared-ItemID eBay listing — the two guards that exist in the eBay delete service are absent from the delist cascade

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket family live on eBay IT as ONE multi-variation listing (item 257584954808, Colore × Taglia, 12 children). The Black/XS child is discontinued, so they bin just that child and hard-delete it with a channel action. The whole jacket listing ends on eBay IT — all 12 variations, including the 11 children that were never selected and whose ChannelListing rows still read ACTIVE.

##### What happens today
An eBay variation child's ChannelListing carries the FAMILY listing's ItemID — the codebase states this itself and built two guards around it: 'A VARIATION CHILD's ChannelListing carries the FAMILY listing's ItemID — delisting it would end the whole multi-variation listing because one row was deleted' (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:676-679), GUARD 1 keyed on DB `product.parentId` rather than caller input (:681-685), and GUARD 2 refusing any ItemID still referenced by another ChannelListing row or an ACTIVE SharedListingMembership, reported as `delistSkippedShared` (:695-719). The bulk-hard-delete cascade has NEITHER: products-catalog.routes.ts:1853-1890 selects every ChannelListing with listingStatus ACTIVE|INACTIVE and a non-null externalListingId and enqueues one DELETE_LISTING/UNPUBLISH_LISTING job per ROW, with no parentId check and no cross-reference check, and delistEbay calls EndFixedPriceItem on whatever ItemID it is handed (channel-delist.service.ts:284-286). Ending a variation listing on eBay ends it as a whole — there is no per-variation end in EndFixedPriceItem; the per-variation primitive is ReviseFixedPriceItem Delete=true / quantity 0, which the delete service does use (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:180-196) and the cascade does not. The confirmation the operator sees compounds this: GET /products/hard-delete-preflight returns one `channelListings` entry per row (products-catalog.routes.ts:1676-1690, 1733-1739) with no indication that several rows are the same ItemID, so a 12-variation family reads as 12 independent listings.

##### Proposed fix
Hoist both guards out of ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts into the dispatcher so every caller inherits them. In `dispatchChannelDelist`, before the eBay End: (a) if the job's product has a non-null parentId, refuse the whole-listing end and instead run the variation-scoped removal (ReviseFixedPriceItem Delete=true with the reviseInventoryStatus qty-0 fallback already implemented at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:180-196); (b) count surviving references to the ItemID across ChannelListing and ACTIVE SharedListingMembership and refuse with a reported `delistSkippedShared` when any remain. Change the preflight to group by (channel, marketplace, externalListingId) and return `sharedWith: string[]` of sibling SKUs, so useActionConfirm (grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx) can itemise 'item 257584954808 is ONE eBay listing shared by 12 variations; 11 are not in this selection' as a danger consequence rather than a count.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:676-685,695-719,180-196
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1853-1890
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:284-286
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1676-1690,1733-1739

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find the guard on any other path.

CONFIRMED, line by line:
1. apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:676-679 carries verbatim the comment "A VARIATION CHILD's ChannelListing carries the FAMILY listing's ItemID — delisting it would end the whole multi-variation listing because one row was deleted". GUARD 1 at :681-684 is `const isVariationChild = product.parentId != null || Boolean(target.parentSku && target.parentSku !== sku)` — DB truth, exactly as described. GUARD 2 at :695-719 queries `channelListing.findMany({ channel:'EBAY', externalListingId:{ in: ids } })` and `sharedListingMembership.findMany({ itemId:{ in: ids }, status:'ACTIVE' })` and pushes to `delistSkippedShared` instead of ending. The comment even names the real ItemID 257584954808 as an averted incident.
2. The per-variation primitive exists at :169-203 (`tryRemoveVariationFromListing`: ReviseFixedPriceItem `<Variation><SKU>…<Delete>true</Delete>` with a `reviseInventoryStatus` qty-0 fallback), used at :367, :462, :584.
3. The cascade at apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1853-1890 is as described: `tx.channelListing.findMany({ productId:{in:ids}, listingStatus:{in:['ACTIVE','INACTIVE']}, externalListingId:{not:null} })` → one OutboundSyncQueue row per ChannelListing ROW. No parentId read, no cross-reference count. The eligibility query at :1872-1875 filters only on `deletedAt: { not: null }` — a binned variation child is eligible with no parent/child distinction.
4. apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:91-124 `dispatchChannelDelist` switches straight to `delistEbay`; the only grep hit for parentId/variation/SharedListingMembership in that 343-line file is a doc comment at :38 (checked with /usr/bin/grep). delistEbay at :242-283 takes `_action` UNUSED and calls `endFixedPriceItem({ itemId })` on whatever it is handed — so the modal's "safer" default is equally fatal here.
5. The drain path has no guard either: apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:136-158 explicitly says it "skip[s] every downstream check (publishing controls, pricing recompute, VARIATION_SYNC routing) and go[es] straight to the channel adapter using only the data on the OutboundSyncQueue row itself".
6. Preflight at products-catalog.routes.ts:1676-1690 selects per-row and :1731-1739 maps one entry per row with no ItemID grouping. The consumer, apps/web/src/app/products/_components/BulkActionBar.tsx:1129-1139, reduces those into a `channel · marketplace` COUNT — so 12 sibling rows on one ItemID render as "EBAY · IT: 12". /usr/bin/grep over that file returns no "variation"/"ItemID"/"parentId" anywhere in the delete modal (only the unrelated PIM AttachFamily modal). BulkActionBar.tsx:1107 defaults `channelAction` to 'unpublish' whenever listings exist, and :333-348 POSTs it to /api/products/bulk-hard-delete — the path is live from the recycle-bin UI, not theoretical.

Refutation attempts that failed: (a) no second guard anywhere on the queue path — /usr/bin/grep for parentId in outbound-enqueue.ts and bullmq-sync.worker.ts returns nothing; (b) the shared-ItemID premise is not the auditor's inference, it is asserted by the codebase in three independent places (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:676, pim/family-projection.service.ts:1344, web variants/channel/types.ts:189); (c) the code is not dead — dispatchChannelDelist has exactly one production caller chain (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:18,142) plus amazon-flat-file-remove and the eBay delete service. The only live mitigation I found is environmental, not logical: apps/api/src/services/ebay-trading-api.service.ts:235-244 gates real Trading API calls behind NEXUS_EBAY_REAL_API and THROWS in production when unset — that does not appear in apps/api/.env, so I cannot confirm it is on in prod. But the guard comments citing a live IT ItemID imply it is, and an env flag is not a guard.
The direction is right but the placement is wrong and, as written, the fix cannot work.

1. dispatchChannelDelist is the WRONG layer for GUARD 1. bullmq-sync.worker.ts:136-141 states that by the time the delist branch drains, "the Product + ChannelListing rows are typically gone" — they are deleted inside the same transaction that enqueued the job (products-catalog.routes.ts:1853-1898 enqueues, then the Product FK cascade drops the ChannelListing rows). So "if the job's product has a non-null parentId" resolves against a row that no longer exists: the lookup returns null and the guard silently degrades to a vacuous pass — the most dangerous shape of green. Either apply both guards at ENQUEUE time, inside the tx at :1853-1890 where `product.parentId` and the sibling ChannelListing rows are both still readable, or snapshot `parentId`, the child SKU and the sibling-reference count onto the OutboundSyncQueue payload (which today carries only source/channelAction/marketplace/externalParentId, :1888-1893).

2. The variation-scoped fallback needs the child SKU, which nothing on the queue row carries and which cannot be recovered at drain time because the Product row is gone. `tryRemoveVariationFromListing` also takes `(itemId, sku, marketplace)` and is module-private (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:169, no `export`), so hoisting means exporting it or moving it into a shared eBay module — and the SKU must be captured pre-delete regardless.

3. GUARD 2 at the dispatcher would be counting a moving target. In the single-child scenario the sibling rows survive and the count fires correctly, but when the operator selects the whole family the siblings are deleted too and the count reaches zero — which is the correct answer for a different reason and masks the case where a DE row or an ACTIVE SharedListingMembership on another market still holds the ItemID (the exact case GUARD 2 was built for, :700-706). Run the count inside the enqueue tx against rows NOT in the deletion set, and keep the SharedListingMembership arm, which is unaffected by the product cascade.

4. Do not forget delistEbay's `_action` parameter (channel-delist.service.ts:243): unpublish and delete both End the listing, so any guard must cover channelAction 'unpublish' as well — otherwise the modal's default (BulkActionBar.tsx:1107) walks straight past it.

5. The preflight change is right and is the cheap half: group by (channel, marketplace, externalListingId) at products-catalog.routes.ts:1731-1739 and surface sibling SKUs, but note the current consumer is BulkActionBar.tsx:1129-1139 (a plain count reducer inside a hand-rolled modal), not `grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx` — the finding names the wrong consumer, so the UI half of the fix must land in BulkActionBar's HardDeleteDialog or that dialog must first be migrated to the DS confirm pattern.

[critical]verifiedEBAYcorrectness risk

#### A delist that could not even see the item is reported as SUCCESS — the 'already ended' matcher swallows 'Item cannot be accessed' and 'Invalid item'

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator ends an eBay DE listing from the bin cascade. The ItemID belongs to the second eBay account (or is stale after a relist, or the site ID is wrong for that item). eBay replies with error 291 'Item cannot be accessed' — meaning the token cannot see that item, not that the item is ended. Nexus marks the sync job SUCCESS, /sync-logs is green, and the listing goes on selling.

##### What happens today
delistEbay resolves the account with the DECLARED scope `tryResolveConnection({ channel: 'EBAY', primary: true })` (channel-delist.service.ts:263) even though the job carries the ItemID and the resolver offers a DERIVED `{ itemId, marketplace }` form for exactly this case (connection-resolver.service.ts:109, 212-224). Its own sibling in the same flow uses the derived form and says why: 'MAP.3 — DERIVED from the eBay ItemID being edited, so this is correct for two accounts as well as one' (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:174-176). When the End then fails, ALREADY_ENDED_PATTERNS matches `/item cannot be accessed/i`, `/invalid item/i`, `/item not found/i`, `/listing (is )?not (active|available|found)/i` (channel-delist.service.ts:223-232) and isAlreadyEndedError returns true, so :288-296 logs 'already ended (idempotent)' and returns `{ success: true }`; applyDelistResultToQueue writes syncStatus SUCCESS (:311-319). Those four patterns are not 'already ended' — they are 'this token cannot see this item', which is precisely the wrong-account, wrong-site and stale-ItemID case. The row that held the ItemID is destroyed by the Product cascade in the same transaction, so nothing can re-check afterwards.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes. (1) Resolve the account the way the sibling does: `tryResolveConnection({ itemId, marketplace: job.targetRegion })` with the primary scope only as an explicit last resort, so a second eBay account can never be delisted with the wrong token. (2) Split the matcher: keep `/already ended/i`, `/already closed/i`, `/auction already closed/i`, `/item has already been (deleted|removed)/i` as idempotent success, and move 'item cannot be accessed', 'invalid item', 'item not found', 'not currently available' to a new UNVERIFIED outcome that returns `{ success: false, retryable: false, errorCode: 'EBAY_DELIST_UNVERIFIED' }`. Better still, verify rather than guess: the codebase already has GetItem readback (`getItemQuantities` / `parseGetItemQuantities`, ebay-trading-api.service.ts:330-398 returns ListingStatus) — call it on an ambiguous failure and only claim success when ListingStatus comes back Completed/Ended. Render UNVERIFIED rows in the studio's Needs attention tab as a DS Banner tone="warning" with the ItemID, since by then the local row is gone.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:263,223-232,288-296,311-319
- apps/api/src/services/connection-resolver.service.ts:109,212-224
- apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:174-176

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find any path that rescues the outcome.

CONFIRMED FROM CODE I OPENED:
1. channel-delist.service.ts:223-234 — ALREADY_ENDED_PATTERNS literally contains /item cannot be accessed/i (:227), /item (is )?not (active|available)/i (:228), /listing (is )?not (active|available|found)/i (:229), /item not found/i (:230), /invalid item/i (:231), /not currently available/i (:232). The block comment at :217-221 shows the conflation is deliberate and names eBay codes 291/219/17 as "already ended".
2. channel-delist.service.ts:263 — `tryResolveConnection({ channel: 'EBAY', primary: true })`, annotated `// MAP.3 — DECLARED.` (:262), even though `itemId` is already in hand at :248 and `job.targetRegion` at :274.
3. connection-resolver.service.ts:212-224 — the DERIVED `{ itemId, marketplace }` form exists and resolves via SharedListingMembership.channelConnectionId; the header at :90-99 states DERIVED is "Preferred: it cannot drift".
4. ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:173-176 — the sibling in the SAME delete flow uses `tryResolveConnection({ itemId, marketplace })` with the comment "MAP.3 — DERIVED from the eBay ItemID being edited, so this is correct for two accounts as well as one." So in one delete operation the variation removal can go to account B while the End goes to account A's primary token.
5. The error text really does reach the matcher: ebay-trading-api.service.ts:277-281 — callTradingApi throws `eBay ${callName} Failure: ${LongMessage|ShortMessage} (code N)` on Ack=Failure, and endFixedPriceItem (:442-449) does not catch. So a 291 surfaces as a thrown Error whose message contains "Item cannot be accessed" → isAlreadyEndedError (:236-239) true → :290-296 returns `{ success: true }`.
6. Downstream: applyDelistResultToQueue :311-319 writes syncStatus SUCCESS + syncedAt on `result.success`; bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158 calls dispatchChannelDelist then applyDelistResultToQueue and counts it a success.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
- Is there a readback that would catch it? getItemListingStatus exists (ebay-trading-api.service.ts:316-325) but /usr/bin/grep shows its only non-test caller is jobs/ebay-item-status-reconcile.job.ts:75, a daily 02:30 job over ACTIVE SharedListingMembership rows. It only marks memberships ENDED; it never re-attempts the End, never touches the queue row, and cannot rescue a product whose rows the cascade removed. Notably that job's own header (:14-16) says "GetItem errors (invalid/deleted item ids, code 17) are counted + logged, never acted on" — the same message class the delist matcher treats as proof of ended. The codebase contradicts itself on the exact premise.
- Is the code dead or unreachable? No. /usr/bin/grep -rn "channel-delist" over apps+packages gives three live importers: workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:18, services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:35, services/amazon/amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:7. The strongest live path is ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:205-235 `tryDelist` → dispatchChannelDelist, whose boolean becomes the per-target result for the `delete-product` / `remove-channel-listing` intents (:39-53) — i.e. exactly the owner's "delete it from a specific channel or market" verb reports DONE.
- Is the behaviour just untested speculation? The opposite: ebay-trading-api.endlisting.vitest.test.ts:183-192 pins it — `mockEndFixedPriceItem.mockRejectedValue(new Error('eBay EndFixedPriceItem Failure: Item cannot be accessed'))` then `expect(result.success).toBe(true)`. The wrong premise is frozen by a green test.
- Is the failure inert in dev? No: callTradingApi:236-245 refuses fake-success in production and only returns a DRYRUN Success when NEXUS_EBAY_REAL_API is off outside production.

MIS-STATEMENTS I CORRECTED (why the title/severity change, not why it dies):
(a) "nothing can re-check afterwards" is overstated. OutboundSyncQueue keeps externalListingId and targetRegion (schema.prisma:6858-6860; written at products-catalog.routes.ts:1886-1889), so the ItemID does survive on the queue row — a re-check is possible, it simply is not done.
(b) The finding frames the blast radius as the bin cascade + /sync-logs. The bin cascade is the WEAKER arm: those queue rows are created with productId and channelListingId inside the same transaction that deletes the Product (routes:1882-1890, then :1972 product.deleteMany), and both FKs are onDelete: Cascade (schema.prisma:6822-6826), so the delist rows may be cascade-deleted before fireOutboundJobs (:2000-2003) can fire them — a separate question I did not resolve. The arm that certainly runs, and that the operator actually reads, is the eBay flat-file delete service's channel-scoped intents.
(c) Fix critique below: proposed fix (1) as written can fail closed on ordinary listings.
Fix (2) — splitting the matcher into idempotent-success vs UNVERIFIED, and verifying with GetItem before claiming success — is right and is already buildable in-repo: getItemListingStatus (ebay-trading-api.service.ts:316-325) is a narrow ReturnSummary GetItem, and jobs/ebay-item-status-reconcile.job.ts:31 already defines ENDED_STATUSES = {'Completed','Ended'}. Reuse that constant rather than restating it (a set claim restated in two files drifts).

Fix (1) is wrong as written and would turn a false success into a false failure. `{ itemId, marketplace }` resolves ONLY through SharedListingMembership (connection-resolver.service.ts:212-218); a plain single-item eBay listing that was never pooled has no membership row, so resolveConnection throws NoConnectionError and delistEbay would return EBAY_DELIST_NO_CONNECTION for listings that delist fine today. The obvious alternative, `{ listingId: job.channelListingId }`, is also unavailable on the cascade path: the ChannelListing is deleted in the same transaction (products-catalog.routes.ts:1972) and OutboundSyncQueue has no channelConnectionId column of its own (schema.prisma:6815-6875), so by the time the worker drains there is no row to derive from. The correct shape is to CAPTURE the account at enqueue time — add channelConnectionId to the OutboundSyncQueue delist row (ChannelListing already carries it, schema.prisma:1736-1737, and the cascade's select at products-catalog.routes.ts:1861-1868 simply omits it) and resolve NAMED `{ accountId }`, with `{ itemId, marketplace }` then the primary scope as ordered fallbacks. Note this is a producer+consumer change and must land in one write.

Two further gaps the fix should cover: the pinned test ebay-trading-api.endlisting.vitest.test.ts:183-192 asserts the defective behaviour and must be inverted, or the fix cannot land green; and the UNVERIFIED outcome needs a retryable/errorCode contract that applyDelistResultToQueue (:311-330) will not silently retry into isDead — a wrong-account End will never succeed on retry, so retryable:false is correct but must not be reported as a transient failure. The UI half (a DS Banner in Needs attention) is unverified by me — I did not open the studio tree for this finding, and the harm is already visible without it via the flat-file delete per-target result.

[high]refutedEBAYmissing capability

#### No reversible per-market eBay end exists anywhere, and the eBay primitive that would give one (quantity 0 / out-of-stock) is implemented but never exposed

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a wool coat live on eBay IT and eBay DE. Winter is over, so they want it off eBay IT only — keeping DE live, and keeping the IT listing's ItemID, watchers, sales history and search ranking so it can go back up next October with one click. On Amazon this exact operation exists (SCT.6 CLOSE_OFFER / REOPEN_OFFER, which snapshots the offer and replays it verbatim). On eBay there is nothing.

##### What happens today
Every eBay removal path is terminal. EndFixedPriceItem is the only end primitive wired (channel-delist.service.ts:284-286; ebay-trading-api.service.ts:412-449), and eBay cannot reopen an ended fixed-price item — a relist mints a new ItemID. The flat-file 'end' action calls withdraw_by_inventory_item_group / DELETE offer and then nulls the ItemID with the message 'listing ended on this market (ItemID retired — a future publish creates a new one)' (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1955-1963, 1976-1985). Amazon's reversible pair has no eBay counterpart. Meanwhile the correct eBay mechanic — hold the listing at quantity 0 under out-of-stock control, which keeps the ItemID, the ranking and the history and restores in one revise — is already implemented as `reviseInventoryStatus` (ebay-trading-api.service.ts:296) and `reviseInventoryStatusBatch` (:403), and is used only as a fallback when a variation delete is refused (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:193). /usr/bin/grep over apps/api/src and apps/web/src for OutOfStockControl|out_of_stock returns zero eBay hits (all matches are unrelated stock metrics), so the Trading-API OutOfStockControl flag is never set. In the studio itself there is no eBay lifecycle verb at all: /usr/bin/grep over apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio for end.?listing|relist|sell.?similar|EndFixedPriceItem|withdraw|delist|remove-channel-listing|flat-file/delete returns zero lifecycle hits against a positive control of 41 files in that tree containing `fetch(`; the eBay channel sheet declares only offer-toggle, broadcast-to-listings and open-record (channelActions.ts:163, 309, 381) and both write verbs refuse any live row as 'wave-1 channel verbs are preview-only' (:250, 260, 344, 351).

##### Proposed fix
Build the eBay analogue of SCT.6 and put it in the studio's eBay scope. API: `POST /api/products/:id/listings/EBAY/:marketplace/hold` with body `{ mode: 'out-of-stock' | 'end', aliasId?, accountId?, reason? }` and `POST .../release`. 'out-of-stock' sets OutOfStockControl on the listing and drives every SKU to quantity 0 via the existing reviseInventoryStatusBatch (≤4 nodes per call, ebay-trading-api.service.ts:403), snapshots the prior quantities into a new `offerCloseSnapshot`-style column on ChannelListing exactly as amazon-market-offer.service does, and sets `offerClosedAt` — reversible in one call, ItemID and ranking intact. 'end' remains the terminal EndFixedPriceItem and must be a separately confirmed, differently-worded verb. UI: per CH.1 these are ITEMS of the single channel-sheet ⋯ overflow (SheetToolbar's one overflow), routed through the DS GridAction registry with `danger: true`, `preflight()` returning an itemised ActionImpact, and `confirm: 'type-to-confirm'` with the real SKU as the phrase for 'end' and `confirm` (not typed) for 'out-of-stock'. Note the DS blocker first: MenuItemDef has no tone and both menu adapters drop GridAction.danger (design-system/grid/actions/menuAdapters.tsx), so 'End listing' would render identically to 'Cell details' — that DS gap must land before the verb does. Closed state shows as a DS Pill tone="warning" in the alias band ('On hold since 12 Sep — 0 available'), never as ACTIVE.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/ebay-trading-api.service.ts:296,403,412-449
- apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:193
- apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1955-1963,1976-1985
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts:163,250,260,309,344,351,381
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:284-286

##### Verifier
The load-bearing claims are both false against code I opened.

1) "No reversible per-market eBay end exists anywhere" — REFUTED. The eBay flat-file editor ships a per-row, per-market lifecycle `Action` column whose `deactivate` option is exactly the reversible market exit the finding says does not exist. Column definition: /Users/awais/nexus-commerce/apps/web/src/app/products/ebay-flat-file/ebay-columns.ts:152-164 — label "Action", enum `['', 'deactivate', 'end', 'skip']`, description "Applied on Push, to this market only: blank = publish/update · deactivate = set the live offer to quantity 0 (keeps the ItemID — the safe hide…) · end = … the ItemID is lost". The server half is live, not dead: /Users/awais/nexus-commerce/apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1841-1846 (action semantics), :1848 (`deactivateRows`), :1874-1888 (the deactivate branch zeroes `<market>_qty`/`quantity` and calls `pushOffersOnly` for the target marketplace, reporting "deactivated — quantity 0 on the live offer (ItemID kept)"), with per-row unhandled-row hardening at :1890-1897. The reverse verb is the DEFAULT action (blank = publish/update, :1841-1842, :1850), so deactivate-now / republish-later round-trips on the same ItemID, scoped to one market — the exact wool-coat-off-IT-keep-DE scenario. It is also gated as destructive in the import wizard (/Users/awais/nexus-commerce/apps/web/src/app/products/ebay-flat-file/EbayImportWizard.tsx:1081-1089) and typed in the client (EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:115-116, 2178-2185). The brief explicitly listed "a flat-file editor" as a surface to check before claiming absence; the finding's own studio-scoped regex (end.?listing|relist|sell.?similar|withdraw|delist|…) could never match `row_action: 'deactivate'`, so the "anywhere" half is an unestablished set claim.

2) "the qty-0 primitive … is implemented but never exposed / used only as a fallback when a variation delete is refused" — REFUTED. `reviseInventoryStatusBatch` is the routine shared-SKU Trading quantity push, not a delete fallback: imported at /Users/awais/nexus-commerce/apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:40-52 and called in the live `syncSharedTradingQuantity` loop at :1750-1762 (with the ≤4-entry chunking and the ~250 revises/day counter). Separately, Sync Control exposes an operator-reachable, channel-agnostic, reversible per-(product, channel, marketplace) quantity-0 hold: `ZERO_PIN` writes `quantity: 0, quantityOverride: 0, followMasterQuantity: false` and enqueues a QUANTITY_UPDATE per listing at /Users/awais/nexus-commerce/apps/api/src/routes/sync-control.routes.ts:934-963, reversed by FOLLOW (:706, :921-932), with eBay selectable in the UI at /Users/awais/nexus-commerce/apps/web/src/app/fulfillment/stock/sync-control/SyncControlClient.tsx:460, 795.

What the cited evidence does support, and it is narrower than the title: the finding's file:line citations are accurate (ebay-trading-api.service.ts:296 reviseInventoryStatus, :403 batch, :412-449 EndFixedPriceItem; ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:194 qty-0 fallback; ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1960 and :1983 null `externalListingId` with "ItemID retired"; channel-delist.service.ts:286; channelActions.ts:163/250/260/309/344/351/381 verbatim — only three verbs, both writes refuse live rows "wave-1 channel verbs are preview-only"), and I confirmed the master sheet has no lifecycle verb either (familyActions.ts:122-496: attach/unlink/reparent/promote/open-record/add-child/delete-child/demote, with delete-child refused outright when a listing is live, :454). I also confirmed Amazon's CLOSE_OFFER/REOPEN_OFFER deliberately refuses non-Amazon channels — sync-control.routes.ts:810-816, whose comment states the design position outright: "SCT.6 — per-market offer CLOSE/REOPEN (Amazon only; eBay has real per-listing quantities and never needs this)". So the residual, defensible issue is a STUDIO PLACEMENT/discoverability gap ("the reversible per-market eBay hold exists in the eBay flat-file editor and in Sync Control, but no studio surface offers or even names it"), not a missing capability — a different kind, a different severity (medium at most), and a different fix (surface/deep-link the existing verb) from the one proposed. The finding as written would have the team build a primitive that already ships.
The proposed fix builds a primitive that already ships, and one detail of it is technically wrong. (a) `deactivate` in the eBay flat-file editor already performs the per-market qty-0 hold with the ItemID kept (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1874-1888); a new POST /hold + /release pair would be a second, divergent writer for the same operation — and the flat-file editors are on the untouchable list. (b) "sets OutOfStockControl on the listing" is not a per-listing field in the eBay Trading API: out-of-stock control is an ACCOUNT-level preference (SetUserPreferences / Seller Hub), so no per-listing write can set it, and whether a qty-0 listing survives on eBay's side depends on that account preference — a fact this repo cannot assert either way, so it must be verified against the seller account before any "the ItemID and ranking survive" promise is shown to an operator. (c) The `offerCloseSnapshot` mirror of Amazon's SCT.6 is contradicted by the in-code design position at sync-control.routes.ts:810-812 ("eBay has real per-listing quantities and never needs this") — if that position is now wrong it must be re-ruled by the hub, not quietly reversed inside a lane. (d) The only part worth keeping is the UI half: surface the EXISTING deactivate/end pair (and its reverse) in the studio's eBay scope, plus the DS blocker the finding correctly names — MenuItemDef has no tone and the menu adapters drop GridAction.danger, which I did not verify and which should be re-checked before it is relayed as fact.

[high]refutedEBAYdata integrity risk

#### The eBay ItemID is erased on end and hard-deleted on remove, with no capture anywhere — a relist can only be reconciled by retyping the new ItemID in a legacy editor outside the studio

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator ends a handbag on eBay IT (item 257584954808) to re-shoot the photos. Two weeks later they relist it from eBay Seller Hub; eBay mints a new ItemID. They now want Nexus to know that the new item continues the old one — for order and return matching, for the ads index, and so the flat file stops showing a dead ID. Nexus no longer holds the old ItemID at all.

##### What happens today
The flat-file end writes `{ listingStatus: 'ENDED', offerActive: false, externalListingId: null }` (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1958-1962 for a parent, :1979-1984 for a child) — the ItemID is overwritten with null and nothing captures it first; the operator message even says 'ItemID retired' (:1963). handleRemoveChannelListing goes further and hard-deletes the ChannelListing rows outright (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:645), taking externalListingId, overrideData, flatFileSnapshot and the whole override history with them — in a service whose own header asserts 'HARD DELETE IS NEVER PERFORMED' (:24). The only parent-level survivor, Product.ebayItemId, is a single String with no market dimension (schema.prisma:94-95, comment 'shared eBay listing ID'), so it cannot hold IT and DE separately. The schema has the right field for the relist link — EbayListingIndex.relistedFromItemId (schema.prisma:14108) — and /usr/bin/grep over apps and packages returns ZERO code references to it (positive control: `endedAt` in the same model matches in ebay-ads.routes.ts:131,292,347,433,611,655,1321 and is written at services/marketing/ebay-listing-index.service.ts:255). The only reconciliation path that exists is manual: RelinkItemIdModal (apps/web/src/app/products/ebay-flat-file/RelinkItemIdModal.tsx:83) → POST /api/ebay/relink-item-id (ebay-description-push.routes.ts:35) → relinkEbayItemId, which verifies the typed ItemID against eBay with GetItem before writing (ebay-itemid-relink.service.ts:10-16, 59-68). It lives in the legacy eBay flat-file editor, not the studio, and it requires the operator to already know the NEW ItemID — while the OLD one, needed to prove the two are the same listing, has been destroyed.

##### Proposed fix
Never let an ItemID leave the system unrecorded. (1) Before any eBay end or ChannelListing removal, call the existing captureSnapshot (services/pim/listing-snapshot.service.ts) so the ChannelListingSnapshot holds the ItemID, quantities and offer shape — this also discharges ruling #110's 'every publish captures a snapshot' clause on the delist side. (2) Stop nulling: keep `externalListingId` and add `endedListingId` + `endedAt` on ChannelListing, so 'ENDED with item 257584954808' is expressible; make handleRemoveChannelListing archive (status + endedListingId) instead of deleteMany, matching the promise its own header already makes. (3) On any end, upsert EbayListingIndex with endedAt, and on a relist write `relistedFromItemId` — the column exists and is currently dark. (4) Surface it in the studio: an 'Listing history' group in the record drawer (design-system/components/Drawer, KeyValue rows) showing ended ItemIDs with dates, plus a 'Link a new ItemID' item in the channel sheet's single ⋯ overflow that reuses POST /api/ebay/relink-item-id and pre-fills the old ItemID so the verify step can prove continuity, rendered with the DS Field + Modal rather than the legacy Tailwind RelinkItemIdModal.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1958-1963,1979-1985
- apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:24,645

##### Verifier
The mechanical half of the finding is accurate, but its two load-bearing set-claims — "no capture anywhere" and "the only reconciliation path that exists is manual, in a legacy editor" — are both false against code I read, and the harm story built on them collapses.

WHAT CHECKS OUT (I opened each):
- ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1960 and :1983 do write `{ listingStatus: 'ENDED', offerActive: false, externalListingId: null }`; :1963 does say 'ItemID retired'. Confirmed verbatim.
- ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:645 is `tx.channelListing.deleteMany({ where: { productId: { in: productIds }, channel: 'EBAY', marketplace } })`, and :24 does assert 'HARD DELETE IS NEVER PERFORMED'. Confirmed.
- schema.prisma:94-95 Product.ebayItemId is a single String under the comment 'shared eBay listing ID' — no market dimension. Confirmed.
- schema.prisma:14107 relistedFromItemId is genuinely dark: /usr/bin/grep -rn 'relistedFromItemId' apps packages returns exactly two hits — the schema line and migrations/20260703_e2_ebay_ads_data_layer/migration.sql:155. No code reference. That sub-claim survives.
- The relink UI is legacy-only: /usr/bin/grep -rln 'relink' apps/web/src hits only products/ebay-flat-file/{EbayFlatFileClient,RelinkItemIdModal}.tsx; /usr/bin/grep over the whole _studio tree for 'delist|itemId|relist' hits only variants/channel/projection.vitest.test.ts and images/types.ts. The studio has no end/relist/re-link affordance. That sub-claim also survives.

WHAT REFUTES IT:
1. The old ItemID IS captured, per market, and is never deleted. EbayListingIndex is keyed @@unique([workspaceId, marketplace, itemId]) (schema.prisma:14115) and carries productIds + endedAt. discoverEbayListings (services/marketing/ebay-listing-index.service.ts:153) is a registered cron ('ebay-listing-discovery', jobs/cron-registry.ts:162) that upserts every active listing and, on end, only sets endedAt (:255-262) — /usr/bin/grep for any ebayListingIndex delete/deleteMany across apps+packages returns ZERO hits, so ended rows persist with their ItemID, marketplace and product link. "Nexus no longer holds the old ItemID at all" is false. Product.ebayItemId is also never nulled by non-test code (/usr/bin/grep 'ebayItemId: null' apps/api/src hits only ebay-flat-file-delete.service.vitest.test.ts), and OutboundSyncQueue.externalListingId (schema.prisma:6860) retains it too.
2. The old ItemID is not needed to prove continuity anyway. relinkEbayItemId verifies the NEW ItemID by SKU ownership from GetItem — checkItemIdOwnership(liveSkus, familySkus, listingStatus) at ebay-itemid-relink.pure.ts:42-82, which rejects non-Active listings and computes matched/foreign SKUs. The old ItemID is read only for the before/after report (ebay-itemid-relink.service.ts:113-124). The finding inverts the actual verification rule.
3. An automated, non-legacy reconciliation path exists and the auditor did not look at it. listing-reconciliation.service.ts:766-841 runs a per-market eBay reconciliation (EBAY_MARKETPLACE_ID_MAP IT/DE/FR/ES/UK at :756-761), pulls live offers (:731-754), auto-matches by SKU, and confirmReconRow (:465-585) UPSERTS the ChannelListing with externalListingId and listingStatus 'ACTIVE' — an upsert, so it even recreates a row that handleRemoveChannelListing hard-deleted. Exposed at routes/reconciliation.routes.ts:40,96,111,152,190 with a nav-linked page (apps/web/src/app/reconciliation/page.tsx; app-nav.ts:303 'Reconciliation' → /reconciliation, permission pages.listings). A relist from Seller Hub is re-attached by running reconciliation and confirming the SKU match — no retyping, no old ItemID.

What remains is a different, narrower defect than the one filed: the hard delete takes overrideData/flatFileSnapshot/override history with it against the service's own header, the eBay recon path writes an `offer.offerId` into a column documented as the ItemID (listing-reconciliation.service.ts:815 vs schema.prisma:1542-1544), and the studio exposes no end/relist/re-link affordance at all. Those deserve their own findings; this one, as titled and scenario'd, does not stand.
Step (1) of the proposed fix is factually wrong and would ship a silent no-op: listing-snapshot.service.ts:60-68 states that externalListingId must NEVER be captured or restored ('writing a stale externalListingId back would re-point the local record at whatever listing it used to be'), and SNAPSHOT_FIELDS (:70-83) omits it by design. captureSnapshot before an end would not put the ItemID anywhere. Step (3) largely duplicates what the discovery cron already does (ebay-listing-index.service.ts:246-262). Only (2) and (4) retain content once the existing /reconciliation path is accounted for, and (4) should be re-scoped to 'the studio has no delist/relist/re-link affordance at all', built on the existing reconciliation confirm path rather than the relink endpoint.

### Shopify6

[critical]verifiedSHOPIFYcorrectness risk

#### Shopify "unpublish" sends a double-wrapped REST body — the product is never set to draft, and the job reports success

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator bins a discontinued jacket in Nexus and chooses the "unpublish from channels" option rather than "delete", precisely because they want the Shopify storefront product kept as a draft so the handle, SEO and reviews survive and it can be brought back next season. The queue row is UNPUBLISH_LISTING for SHOPIFY. They watch /sync-logs turn green and move on. The jacket is still ACTIVE on the storefront and keeps taking orders for a product Nexus has already deleted.

##### What happens today
delistShopify calls `svcAny.updateProduct(productId, { product: { id: Number(productId), status: 'draft' } })` (channel-delist.service.ts:193-195). But ShopifService.updateProduct already wraps its second argument: `makeRequest("PUT", `/products/${productId}.json`, { product: updates })` (shopify.service.ts:387-389). The body therefore serialises as `{"product":{"product":{"id":…,"status":"draft"}}}` — the status attribute is nested one level too deep and is not a product attribute Shopify reads. Either Shopify returns 200 having changed nothing (makeRequest only throws on !response.ok, shopify.service.ts:139-145) and delistShopify returns `{ success: true }` at :196, or it rejects and the row retries forever (`retryable: true`, :206). In neither arm does the product reach DRAFT. The fallback-to-delete branch at :198-203 is dead, because `typeof svcAny.updateProduct === 'function'` is true (the method exists at shopify.service.ts:383). Compounding this, the whole Shopify adapter is pinned to `private apiVersion: string = "2024-01"` (shopify.service.ts:79) — a REST Admin version well outside Shopify's 12-month support window as of today — so deleteProduct (:407-418) sits on the same stale surface.

##### Proposed fix
Two parts. (a) Correctness: pass the flat update object — `svc.updateProduct(productId, { status: 'DRAFT' })` — and, better, retire the REST path entirely by routing the Shopify branch through the already-present GraphQL admin client (`shopifyAdmin(accountId).graphql`, used by content-sync.service.ts:89) with `productUpdate(input:{id,status:DRAFT})`, then READ BACK `product { status }` and only return `{success:true}` when the readback says DRAFT — the same verify-after-write discipline information-publications.ts:35 already applies to publications. (b) Honesty in the UI: the unpublish/delete choice must not report success on an unverified write. Surface the readback result on the Needs attention tab (channel-ops/ErrorsSyncTab) as a DS `Banner` tone="danger" row rather than a green sync-log line.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:180-207
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:193-196
- apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:383-400
- apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:117-152
- apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:79
- apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:407-418

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and the path is live and reachable by default.

CONFIRMED FROM CODE I OPENED:
1. channel-delist.service.ts:192-196 — `if (typeof svcAny.updateProduct === 'function') { await svcAny.updateProduct(productId, { product: { id: Number(productId), status: 'draft' } }); return { success: true } }`. Verbatim as quoted.
2. shopify.service.ts:383-392 — `updateProduct(productId, updates: Partial<ShopifyProduct>)` calls `this.makeRequest("PUT", `/products/${productId}.json`, { product: updates })`. The wrap is unconditional, so the emitted body is `{"product":{"product":{"id":…,"status":"draft"}}}`. `status` IS a real flat field of the interface (shopify.service.ts:30), so the finding's fix (a) is right.
3. The `svcAny` cast at :191 is what lets the wrong shape past the compiler; the method genuinely exists (shopify.service.ts:383), so the fallback-to-delete at :198-203 is unreachable for `unpublish` — dead exactly as claimed.
4. makeRequest throws only on `!response.ok` (shopify.service.ts:136-145) — no body validation, no readback — so a 200 on an ignored attribute returns cleanly and delistShopify returns `{success:true}` at :196.
5. apiVersion pin `private apiVersion: string = "2024-01"` at shopify.service.ts:79, used by getBaseUrl():110-113. Confirmed.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED (the defect survives):
- Dead path? No. bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158 routes UNPUBLISH_LISTING/DELETE_LISTING straight to dispatchChannelDelist; it maps UNPUBLISH_LISTING→'unpublish' (channel-delist.service.ts:94-95) and `case 'SHOPIFY': return delistShopify(job, action)` (:110-111).
- Reachable from the UI? Yes, and it is the DEFAULT. products-catalog.routes.ts:1853-1891 enqueues one queue row per live SHOPIFY ChannelListing, syncType from `channelAction === 'unpublish'` (:1879); the hard-delete confirm dialog initialises `channelAction` to `'unpublish'` (BulkActionBar.tsx:1097) and posts it at :334-341.
- Green from elsewhere? No — applyDelistResultToQueue writes `syncStatus:'SUCCESS', syncedAt` on success (channel-delist.service.ts:317-325) and the worker counts SUCCESS (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:152-155).
- Does a correct Shopify unpublish exist somewhere the auditor did not look? There is a GraphQL publications path (services/shopify/information-publications.ts:31, `publishableUnpublish`), but it belongs to the Information-tab publications editor; nothing in the delist branch reaches it.
- Shadowed class? No. /usr/bin/grep over apps/api/src: the only `ShopifyService` construction sites are channel-delist.service.ts:186 and stock.routes.ts:2716 (GET-only shim), and the ONLY caller of `.updateProduct` on it is channel-delist.service.ts:193.
- Would requireLegacyCredentials (shopify.service.ts:112 → lib/workspace-legacy-credentials.ts:4-8) short-circuit it? Only when NEXUS_WORKSPACES_ENABLED=1 AND the workspace is non-legacy; on the legacy workspace the REST PUT goes out.

MIS-STATEMENTS TO CORRECT (verdict unchanged):
(a) "retries forever" is wrong — applyDelistResultToQueue caps it: `exhausted = !result.retryable || newRetry >= (row?.maxRetries ?? 3)` → FAILED + isDead + diedAt (channel-delist.service.ts:331-341). The rejection arm ends as a dead FAILED row, not an infinite retry.
(b) The "Shopify returns 200 having changed nothing" arm is an external-API behaviour assumption I cannot verify from this repo (no fixture, no recorded response). What is code-certain: no arm ever sets status=draft, and the success arm returns with no readback. Treat the false-green as high-likelihood, not proven.
(c) The scenario is framed as a studio action; the actual operator entry point is the products-list bin hard-delete dialog (BulkActionBar.tsx:1070-1320), where 'unpublish' is preselected.
(d) The 2024-01 pin is real but secondary — it is not what breaks the unpublish.

Severity stays critical: the local Product row is hard-deleted in the same transaction that enqueues the job (products-catalog.routes.ts:1826-1891), so in every arm the Shopify storefront product remains ACTIVE and sellable while Nexus has destroyed its record — and on the likely arm the operator is told it worked.

[critical]verifiedSHOPIFYdata integrity risk

#### Every Shopify listing the studio creates keeps listingStatus "DRAFT", so it is invisible to the only delist cascade — deleting the product leaves a live storefront listing and destroys its only identity record

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator builds a wool coat in the studio, opens the Shopify "Listing information" tab, synchronises, confirms it Active, and the coat goes live on the webstore. Six months later they delete the coat from Nexus via /products with channelAction 'delete', expecting it to come off the storefront. Nothing is enqueued for Shopify. The coat stays live and orderable on the webstore forever, and the ChannelListing row that held its Shopify product id, variant ids, inventory item ids and content hash is cascade-destroyed in the same transaction — so nobody can even find out which Shopify product to remove.

##### What happens today
The Shopify synchronise path writes `{ platformAttributes, externalListingId, platformProductId, isPublished }` and nothing else (content-sync.service.ts:139), on both the update (:140) and create (:141) arms. `listingStatus` is never in the payload, so the row keeps the schema default `@default("DRAFT")` (schema.prisma:1615) even when the product is verified ACTIVE in Shopify (`const isPublished = verifiedProduct.status === 'ACTIVE'`, content-sync.service.ts:136). The one and only delist enqueuer filters `listingStatus: { in: ['ACTIVE','INACTIVE'] }` (products-catalog.routes.ts:1857, and the parallel filter at :1681), so the row is excluded. Set claim, /usr/bin/grep for `listingStatus` over apps/api/src/services/shopify/ and apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts: the only two hits are read-side — channel-sheet.service.ts:41 (projection passthrough) and channel-sheet-projection.ts:62 (an in-memory row relabel, not a DB write). Positive control: `isPublished` matches 3× in content-sync.service.ts. A separate /usr/bin/grep for `listingStatus: 'ACTIVE'` across apps/api/src returns Amazon, eBay, syndication and the generic marketplaces.routes.ts:1085 publish route — no Shopify writer. Then `Product`→`ChannelListing` is `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:1514), so platformAttributes (holding shopifyProductId, variantId, inventoryItemId, the published handle) goes with it.

##### Proposed fix
Make the synchronise transaction write the lifecycle column it already computed: in content-sync.service.ts:139 extend `mapping` to `{ …, isPublished, listingStatus: verifiedProduct.status === 'ACTIVE' ? 'ACTIVE' : verifiedProduct.status }` (Shopify's ProductStatus ACTIVE|DRAFT|ARCHIVED maps 1:1 onto the column's vocabulary, which already carries ARCHIVED semantics at channel-sheet-projection.ts:62). Producer and consumer must land together (the delist filter is the consumer): in the same change, widen products-catalog.routes.ts:1857/:1681 to select on `externalListingId: { not: null }` alone — liveness is the external id, exactly the rule the studio's own listingRisk.ts already encodes — rather than on a status string five services write inconsistently. Add a vitest over the Shopify branch asserting the row reads ACTIVE after a verified sync, since a zero-change round trip cannot test this write.

- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1615

So the lifecycle column is never written on the studio's Shopify synchronise.
- The row is born DRAFT elsewhere too: apps/api/src/services/shopify/content-workspace.service.ts:103 and apps/api/src/services/shopify/linked-products.service.ts:60 create the parent SHOPIFY ChannelListing with `isPublished: false` and no listingStatus.

[high]verifiedSHOPIFYmissing capability

#### "Remove from one market" cannot be expressed for Shopify at all: one seeded GLOBAL marketplace, and Shopify Markets (per-market publishing, per-market pricing) is unmodeled end to end

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator runs a Shopify Markets store selling a linen shirt into Italy, Germany and the UK from one webstore, with a UK price uplift. Import duty makes the UK unprofitable, so they want the shirt off the UK market only — Italy and Germany untouched, and the UK switched back on for spring. In the studio they pick the SHOPIFY channel and look for a market to scope to. There is only one, and it is called "Shopify Store".

##### What happens today
The market axis for Shopify has exactly one member: the seed creates a single row `{ channel: 'SHOPIFY', code: 'GLOBAL', name: 'Shopify Store', region: 'GLOBAL', currency: 'EUR', language: 'en' }` (seed-marketplaces.ts:40), and every Shopify server path hardcodes that coordinate — `market: 'GLOBAL'` (channel-sheet.service.ts:27), `marketplace: 'GLOBAL'` in the identity query (:21) and in the attribution query (:133), and `channelMarket: 'SHOPIFY_GLOBAL', region: 'GLOBAL'` on create (content-sync.service.ts:141). The studio scope layer treats GLOBAL as a pseudo-market and excludes it from the landing default (scopes.ts:42-43, 146, 175). Set claim, /usr/bin/grep over apps/api/src + apps/web/src for `contextualPricing|priceList|marketWebPresence|marketLocalizations`: zero hits (positive control in the same sweep: `publishablePublish|publishableUnpublish|resourcePublications` returns information-publications.ts:10,31,32 plus linked-products-gateway.ts:93). So Shopify Markets publishing, per-market price lists and market localizations have no representation anywhere. The nearest lever that does exist — per-sales-channel publication membership via publishableUnpublish (information-publications.ts:31) — is store-wide across every market and is reachable only as a sheet cell (`salesChannels`, shopify-information.ts:35), never as a lifecycle verb. Because the base `price` field (shopify-information.ts, nativeFieldKeys:135) is the only price the studio reads or writes, a market price-list uplift is invisible: the sheet shows the base price as if it were the price everywhere.

##### Proposed fix
Model Shopify markets as real market rows rather than one GLOBAL pseudo-market: read `markets { nodes { id name handle enabled webPresence { rootUrls } } }` once per connection into the store schema alongside `publications` (linked-products-gateway.ts:93 is the existing hook) and seed one Marketplace row per enabled Shopify market so the studio's own market switcher works unchanged. Then add a Shopify market-availability field to the Information registry beside `salesChannels`, edited by the same DS `Checkbox` list already used at ShopifyNativeEditor.tsx:33-36, and applied with `productUpdate`/market catalog publication the way applyInformationPublications reconciles each publication independently (information-publications.ts:20-35). Until that lands, the honest fix is a DS `Banner` tone="info" on the Shopify scope stating that this connection is managed as one webstore and that per-market removal must be done in Shopify admin — visibility over silence.

#### ARCHIVED — Shopify's own reversible "off sale, keep everything" state — is never used by the delist path; the operator's exact request is an untitled cell in a sheet, not a verb

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator wants the seasonal Christmas jumper off the Shopify storefront now, with the handle, SEO ranking, reviews, variant ids and order history intact so it can be relisted in November. Shopify has a first-class state for exactly this: ARCHIVED. What the operator can reach in the studio is a cell called "Status" in the Shopify Listing information sheet; what any delist the platform performs on their behalf does is DRAFT or destroy.

##### What happens today
channel-delist.service.ts models exactly two channel actions, `'unpublish' | 'delete'` (:53), and the Shopify branch maps them to status draft (:193-195) and `deleteProduct` (:203). ARCHIVED appears nowhere in that file. It IS reachable elsewhere: `['status', 'Status', 'General', P, 'status']` is a writable native field (shopify-information.ts:30, nativeFieldKeys:135), validated against ACTIVE|DRAFT|ARCHIVED|UNLISTED (:214) and against the live store enum (:119-120), and the projection already understands the state (`if (row.listing && (providerStatus === 'DRAFT' || providerStatus === 'ARCHIVED')) row.listing = { …, isPublished: false, listingStatus: providerStatus }`, channel-sheet-projection.ts:62), as does the publish guard ("This product is live or archived…", content-publisher.ts:196). So the capability exists — but only as a free-text-ish cell in a 25-field sheet, with no explanation anywhere of what ARCHIVED costs versus DRAFT versus delete, and it is not offered by any of the three channel verbs the sheet exposes (channelActions.ts declares only open-record, offer-toggle, broadcast-to-listings) nor by the ⋯ overflow (ChannelSheet.tsx:2002-2023: Cell details, Check Information, + Add listing alias).

##### Proposed fix
Promote the three Shopify off-sale states into one named verb on the channel sheet's single ⋯ overflow (CH.1 says scope verbs are items of the one overflow, never buttons), built as a `GridAction` in the DS registry with `scope:'row'|'selection'`, `danger` set only for the destroying arm, and `preflight()` returning an itemised `ActionImpact`: "Archive — hidden from storefront and admin lists; handle, SEO, reviews, variant ids and order history kept; reversible from this menu" / "Set to draft — same, plus stays in admin lists" / "Delete — handle released, variant ids and translations destroyed; not reversible" rendered by useActionConfirm with ConfirmLevel 'confirm' for the first two and 'type-to-confirm' on the real Shopify handle for delete (never the word DELETE, per ruling #133). Widen ChannelAction to `'archive' | 'unpublish' | 'delete'` in channel-delist.service.ts:53 and map archive→`productUpdate(input:{status:ARCHIVED})`. Note for the hub: menuAdapters.tsx drops GridAction.danger today (DS-GAPS:330-344), so the destructive item will render identically to Archive until that gap is closed — file it, don't hand-roll a red menu item.

#### A Shopify delete destroys the handle, SEO, variant ids, translations and publication memberships with no snapshot anywhere, and there is no relist verb to put them back

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator deletes a discontinued bag from Nexus with channelAction 'delete'. It is removed from Shopify. Two months later it comes back into stock and they want it relisted at the same URL — /products/canvas-weekender-bag — so the ads, the blog links and the Google ranking still land. Nothing in Nexus knows what the handle was.

##### What happens today
`delistShopify` calls `svc.deleteProduct(productId)` (channel-delist.service.ts:203) → REST DELETE /products/{id}.json (shopify.service.ts:407-418). Nothing is captured first: /usr/bin/grep for `handle` across channel-delist.service.ts and marketplaces/shopify.service.ts returns one hit, the `handle: string` field on the ShopifyProduct interface (shopify.service.ts:23) — no read, no persist (positive control: `product` matches 10× in channel-delist.service.ts). The one place the handle IS known is the publish result (`handle: verified.handle`, content-publisher.ts:307) checkpointed into ChannelListing.platformAttributes — and that row is `onDelete: Cascade` from Product (schema.prisma:1514), destroyed in the same transaction that enqueues the delist (products-catalog.routes.ts:1879-1900, :1973). The variant ids and inventoryItemIds stored at content-sync.service.ts:139 go with it, and Shopify translations live on the deleted resources. On a relist, `publishContent` re-creates via `productSet` with `identifier: { customId: { namespace:'nexus', key:'family_id', … } }` (content-publisher.ts:222-226) — the metafield died with the product, so it always creates a NEW product, forced to `status: 'DRAFT'` and `templateSuffix: 'nexus'`, with no `handle` in the input, so Shopify mints a fresh handle from the title and all publication memberships reset. Shopify's own `deleteProduct` is the only lifecycle path here; the studio never reaches it (the studio has no delist verb at all), so this runs only from /products bulk-hard-delete where the operator is picking from a three-way `channelAction` with no consequence copy.

##### Proposed fix
Capture before you destroy, and keep the capture outside the cascade. Before the Shopify DELETE, read and persist `{ handle, status, seo, variants { id sku }, resourcePublicationsV2, translations }` — every piece is already selected somewhere (PRODUCT_SELECTION, content-publisher.ts:27; readInformationPublications, information-publications.ts:8-16) — into a row that survives the Product cascade. `ListingRecoveryEvent` (schema.prisma:2335) already has `productId` with no ChannelListing FK and already outlives the listing; extend it with a `snapshot Json` column (additive migration, pre-approved) rather than inventing a table. Then add `POST /api/products/:id/listings/shopify/relist` that replays the snapshot through publishContent with `handle` explicitly in the productSet input and the captured publications reapplied via applyInformationPublications. In the studio, surface it as a "Relist on Shopify" item in the channel sheet's ⋯ overflow, gated on a surviving snapshot, with a DS `Modal` (size sm) listing the handle and variant count it will restore and naming what it cannot (reviews, existing order links). Also fix the enqueue/cascade ordering flagged upstream: the OutboundSyncQueue delist rows created at products-catalog.routes.ts:1879 carry `channelListingId` and are themselves cascade-deleted by the product delete at :1973 before fireOutboundJobs at :1999.

Per the schema the rows are gone and the Shopify DELETE never fires — leaving a live orphan Shopify product Nexus no longer tracks. I did not query the DB (read-only, no API calls), so I report this as an unresolved fork: either arm is a defect, and in both arms the snapshot/relist capability is missing.
B. There is no channel-scoped Shopify delete at all. The only enqueuers of DELETE_LISTING are products-catalog.routes.ts:1879 (whole-product purge from the bin), amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:78 and ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:157 (Amazon/eBay only). So the owner's literal ask — remove from one channel/market and relist later — has no Shopify implementation whatsoever, which makes the finding stronger than stated, not weaker.

Severity lowered to high, not critical: the trigger is a deliberate purge of an already-binned product where the operator loses the entire Nexus product by design, and per the schema the destructive Shopify call may not even fire today.
The direction (capture before you destroy, then a replay verb) is right, but three specifics are wrong or unbuildable as written:

1. The parking spot does not survive. ListingRecoveryEvent is `product Product @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)` at schema.prisma:2341 — it outlives the ChannelListing (as its own comment says) but NOT the Product, which is exactly what the hard-delete scenario destroys. A snapshot column there would be deleted by the same `tx.product.deleteMany` at products-catalog.routes.ts:1972-1974. The snapshot must live in a table with no Product FK at all (the pattern the route already uses for AuditLog, :1904-1910), keyed by workspaceId + family identity + channel + marketplace + sku.

2. The relist route cannot be keyed `POST /api/products/:id/...`. After the purge there is no Product with that id — every route in listing-recovery.routes.ts is `/products/:id/...` and would 404. The verb has to be reachable from a listing-recovery surface keyed on the surviving snapshot, not on the product.

3. "Every piece is already selected somewhere" overstates it. PRODUCT_SELECTION (content-publisher.ts:27) has `id handle status updatedAt variants media metafields` — no `seo`. SEO comes from a different query, information-gateway.ts:15 (`productNativeSelection`). readInformationPublications (information-publications.ts:7-16) does exist as claimed. So the capture needs to compose two selections, and it must run before the DELETE inside the delist adapter — which is a different transaction boundary from the route that enqueues it.

Also: the fix treats the enqueue/cascade ordering as an aside ("also fix"), when per schema.prisma:6822-6826 it decides whether the destructive path runs at all. That ordering has to be settled first, because it determines whether today's bug is "destroyed with no recovery" or "silently left live on Shopify" — the two need different remediations for existing data. And gating the studio verb on "a surviving snapshot" silently disables it for every product deleted before the change ships; the UI needs to say why it is unavailable rather than hide the item.

6) No gate anywhere on this path. I searched for one rather than assuming: (a) /usr/bin/grep for "confirm" across the whole studio shopify dir returns confirmations only in InformationMediaDialog.tsx:24/:31 (shared alt text), EntryEditor.tsx:42 and ShopifyLinkedWorkspace.tsx:33/:358 — none in ShopifySheetReview, whose primary Button at :85 calls `synchronize(false)` → POST `/synchronize` at :38 directly. (b) The route adds only RBAC gates, for media and for `field === 'inventory'` (shopify-linked-products.routes.ts:37-52) — nothing for salesChannels or status. (c) `beginLinkedSync` (linked-products.service.ts:236-257) checks revisions, automation, syncPaused/Locked and a prior operation — no confirmation flag of any kind. (d) `applyInformationPublications` fires `publishableUnpublish` (information-publications.ts:31) with no confirm parameter. (e) No consequence text exists: the warning list at linked-products.service.ts:192-199 and :211-212 covers cleared metafields, batching, shared alt text, gallery variant loss and readback — nothing about losing publications or moving off ACTIVE, so the `plan.warnings` banners at ShopifySheetReview.tsx:69 fire nothing for this case.

The one mis-statement: `confirmActive` (content-sync.service.ts:61; content-publisher.ts:196 — both verified verbatim) is not "the only gate in this flow"; it belongs to the separate content-publication flow (`synchronizeContent`) and is absent from the linked-sheet /synchronize path entirely. That strengthens the finding rather than refuting it, hence the corrected title.

Severity stays high: this Modal is the last human checkpoint before a real `publishableUnpublish` against a live store, the operator is shown gids instead of channel names, and nothing distinguishes "renamed the vendor" from "pulled the product off every sales channel" except a count in the button label.
The proposed fix is sound but needs three corrections before it is implementable.

(a) Null-safety: `schema` arrives as `ShopifyStoreSchema | null | undefined` (ShopifySheetReview.tsx:14) and `publications` is itself optional — the gateway only attaches it when the connection holds read_publications/write_publications (linked-products-gateway.ts:92). So the name lookup must fall back to the gid (or to "a publication no longer visible to this connection"), never assume `schema.publications` exists. ShopifyNativeEditor.tsx:33 already guards this as `(schema.publications ?? [])`.

(b) The same defect exists on a second surface and the fix must be shared, not local: ShopifyLinkedWorkspace.tsx:354 renders nativeEdits through the identical `<pre>{e.value ?? 'Not set'}</pre>` block in the Product family tab. Fixing only ShopifySheetReview leaves the Owner's scenario reachable one tab away — and per the "shared = exactly the same" rule this should be one extracted renderer consumed by both.

(c) The status tone map must cover four values, not three: `nativeFieldValueError` accepts ACTIVE, DRAFT, ARCHIVED and UNLISTED (shopify-information.ts:214), and the Select can also surface a current value absent from the store enum (ShopifyNativeEditor.tsx:44), so the Pill needs a neutral default rather than an exhaustive switch.

One addition worth folding in: the consequence sentence should be generated server-side as a `plan.warnings` entry (linked-products.service.ts:192-199 is where every other destructive consequence is authored — cleared metafields, shared alt text, variant image loss), so the automation path and any future client get it too. Rendering it only in React repeats the split the warnings list was built to avoid.

### Etsy6

[critical]verifiedETSYcorrectness risk

#### Hard delete counts the Etsy listing in the warning, then silently skips it — the product is purged locally while the Etsy listing stays live and sellable

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a hand-printed linen apron listed on Amazon IT, eBay IT and the Etsy shop. They retire the product, move it to the bin, and permanently delete it. The confirm dialog tells them it is "Live on 3 channel listings" and lists AMAZON · IT, EBAY · IT and ETSY · GLOBAL. They leave the default radio on "Unpublish (recommended) — Pause the offer on each channel", type DELETE, and confirm. They now believe the apron is off all three channels.

##### What happens today
The preflight query has no channel filter, so the ETSY row is counted and shown (products-catalog.routes.ts:1679-1689, with `listingStatus: { in: ['ACTIVE','INACTIVE'] }` at :1681), and BulkActionBar renders it in the channel summary (BulkActionBar.tsx:1213-1232, summary built at :1135-1142). The delist enqueue then filters the same rows against `SUPPORTED = ['AMAZON','EBAY','SHOPIFY','WOOCOMMERCE']` (products-catalog.routes.ts:1875-1876) — ETSY is dropped with no counter, no warning and no audit note; only `channelCascadeEnqueued = enqueueable.length` is returned (:1899). `tx.product.deleteMany` (:1973) then cascade-destroys the ChannelListing row (schema.prisma:1515 `onDelete: Cascade`), taking `externalListingId` (the Etsy listing_id) with it. Net result: the Etsy listing remains active and orderable on etsy.com, and Nexus no longer holds the id needed to find it. The dialog copy names only three channels — "Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing; Shopify: status DRAFT" (en.json `products.hardDelete.channelAction.unpublish.body`) — but the count above it includes Etsy, so the number and the promise disagree.

##### Proposed fix
Split the preflight result server-side: `GET /products/hard-delete-preflight` returns `channelListings` partitioned into `cascadeCovered` and `cascadeUnsupported` (derived from the same SUPPORTED list, not a second hand-written copy — one concept defined once), and `POST /products/bulk-hard-delete` returns `channelCascadeSkipped` alongside `channelCascadeEnqueued`. In the UI, route this through the DS destructive contract rather than the bespoke Tailwind dialog: a `GridAction` with `danger: true` whose `preflight()` returns an `ActionImpact` with the consequences itemised and the side effects separated (grid/actions/registry.ts:167-198), rendered by `useActionConfirm` (grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx) with `ConfirmLevel: 'type-to-confirm'` and the real SKU as the phrase. The unsupported rows must appear as their own named consequence line — "Etsy · GLOBAL: this listing will stay live on Etsy; Nexus will lose its listing id" — using a DS `Banner` tone="warning" inside the confirm body. Until an Etsy delist adapter exists, the safest behaviour is to refuse the whole hard delete when an unsupported live listing is present (runAction's `refused` outcome, grid/actions/runAction.ts:38-98) rather than proceed with a partial cascade.
