##### Verifier
Mechanism confirmed line-by-line from code I opened. products-catalog.routes.ts:1679-1689 counts EVERY live ChannelListing with no channel filter; BulkActionBar.tsx:1135-1142 and :1213-1232 render that unfiltered count plus a per-channel list ("ETSY · GLOBAL") in the confirm dialog; the cascade at :1875-1876 then filters the same rows to SUPPORTED=['AMAZON','EBAY','SHOPIFY','WOOCOMMERCE'] and drops the rest with no counter, no log, and no audit note (AuditLog metadata at :1904-1932 carries only {source, channelAction}); the route returns only channelCascadeEnqueued (:1899, :1987) and the client discards the response entirely (BulkActionBar.tsx:334-350 checks res.ok only). tx.product.deleteMany (:1973) then cascade-destroys the ChannelListing row via schema.prisma:1515 onDelete: Cascade, taking externalListingId with it. The filter is structural, not incidental: SyncChannel (schema.prisma:57-66) has no ETSY, and channel-delist.service.ts:105-112 switches on those four channels only. Refutation attempts all failed: no Etsy delist path exists (services/marketplaces/etsy.service.ts never touches channelListing; services/listings/recovery.service.ts:80 puts ETSY in SHOPIFY_LIKE and rejects destructive actions), the dialog has no unsupported-channel warning anywhere (BulkActionBar.tsx:1200-1335), and the modal is live (ProductsWorkspace.tsx:1845). The copy mismatch is real: en.json products.hardDelete.channelAction.unpublish.body promises "Pause the offer on each channel" and names only Amazon/eBay/Shopify. MIS-STATED IN ONE RESPECT: the Etsy framing is narrower than the defect and its precondition is not produced by any first-class Etsy flow — Etsy listing ids live on Product.etsyListingId (jobs/etsy-sync.job.ts:84-85, services/sync/etsy-sync.service.ts:143-155), and etsy.service.ts writes no ChannelListing. An ETSY row matching the preflight predicate (ACTIVE/INACTIVE + non-null externalListingId) is reachable only via generic paths (matrix.routes.ts:240 create with arbitrary body.channel, matrix.routes.ts:149 update setting externalListingId, services/images/product-media.service.ts:72 create with channel: input.scope) or imported data. The defect itself is channel-agnostic and unconditional, so it should be stated that way; severity drops from critical to high because the Etsy-live instance depends on rows no first-class publish flow creates.
The proposed fix is directionally right but overreaches in one place and under-specifies in another. Right: partitioning the preflight server-side into cascadeCovered/cascadeUnsupported derived from ONE exported SUPPORTED constant (today it exists only as a function-local literal at products-catalog.routes.ts:1875, and channel-delist.service.ts:105-112 restates the same set as a switch — that is already two copies; the fix must collapse all three, not add a fourth), and returning channelCascadeSkipped alongside channelCascadeEnqueued (:1899/:1987) is the minimum honest contract. Also correct and cheap: an AuditLog note for the skipped rows, since :1904-1932 currently records nothing about them, and the client must stop discarding the response (BulkActionBar.tsx:334-350). Overreach: 'refuse the whole hard delete when an unsupported live listing is present' changes behaviour the owner may rely on — the 'Local-only' radio explicitly exists to purge locally while leaving channel listings alone (en.json products.hardDelete.channelAction.none.body), so a blanket refusal would break a documented, deliberate path. The correct rule is narrower: refuse only when the operator picked 'unpublish' or 'delete' AND an unsupported live listing is in scope, and offer 'proceed as Local-only for those rows' as an explicit second confirmation, with the operator given the externalListingId first so the listing can still be found on Etsy afterwards. Under-specified: the fix says nothing about the ids the cascade destroys. Even with a perfect warning the operator loses the Etsy listing_id at schema.prisma:1515; the preflight response should surface externalListingId per unsupported row (it is already selected at products-catalog.routes.ts:1679-1689) and the audit row should persist it, since AuditLog has no FK to Product and survives the purge. Finally, the DS re-plumbing (GridAction/useActionConfirm/ActionConfirm/runAction) is a separate, larger piece of work from the correctness fix and should not gate it — the bespoke Tailwind dialog can carry a DS Banner tone='warning' today; conflating the two risks the honesty defect shipping late behind a refactor.

[high]verifiedETSYmissing capability

#### Etsy has no deactivate / reactivate / renew verb anywhere, while the Etsy sheet's own help text tells the operator those actions exist

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator sells a seasonal wool scarf on Etsy. Etsy listings expire after four months, and the seller's normal seasonal move is: deactivate the listing in spring, then reactivate or renew it in autumn so the listing keeps its favourites, views and reviews. They open the scarf in the studio, pick the Etsy scope, and look for a way to take it down for the season.

##### What happens today
There is no such control, and no API behind one. The studio's Etsy sheet shows a read-only "Listing status" column whose help text says "Reported by Etsy. Publishing, renewing and deactivating are separate channel actions" (channel-specs/etsy.ts:123 — `state` is forced non-writable at :84 by `key !== 'state'`), and an editable "Automatic renewal" toggle whose help text says "Renewal preference saved in Nexus. Publishing and renewal are separate channel actions" (etsy.ts:55). Those "separate channel actions" do not exist: the modern Etsy client is read-only by construction and refuses any non-GET (etsy/read-client.ts:5-24, only `get` is exported; its three callers are etsy/taxonomy.ts:34, etsy/information-references.ts:27 and categories/schema-sync.service.ts:201). `channel-delist.service.ts` has no ETSY branch at all (/usr/bin/grep -ni etsy → zero hits in that file). `resync.service.ts:94` throws `ChannelNotSupportedError` for ETSY. The legacy `EtsyService` can only push price and quantity (etsy.service.ts:398, :423, :448) and is gated shut by `requireLegacyCredentials('Etsy')` (etsy.service.ts:263, lib/workspace-legacy-credentials.ts:4-8) plus env vars the OAuth connection flow never sets (utils/config.ts:105-112). So "Automatic renewal" is an editable toggle that writes only to Nexus, and "Listing status" documents a verb set that has no implementation.

##### Proposed fix
Add one Etsy lifecycle endpoint and surface it as grid actions, not as new chrome. API: `POST /api/products/:id/listings/ETSY/GLOBAL/state` with `{ accountId, aliasKey, action: 'deactivate' | 'activate' | 'renew', expectedVersion }`, implemented against Etsy Open API v3 `PATCH /shops/{shop_id}/listings/{listing_id}` (`state: inactive|active`) and `POST .../listings/{listing_id}/renew`; it must write `listingStatus` and capture a `ChannelListingSnapshot` before the call so reactivation has a before-state. UI: three entries in `channelActions.ts`'s registry (the same list that today holds only open-record, offer-toggle and broadcast) so they inherit the one CH.1 overflow — CH.1 says scope verbs are ITEMS of the single `⋯`, never buttons (SheetToolbar.tsx:15-30). Deactivate carries `danger: true`, `ConfirmLevel: 'confirm'`, and a `preflight()` that itemises the consequence ("the listing keeps its favourites and reviews and can be reactivated"). Make "Automatic renewal" honest in the same pass: either route the toggle through the same endpoint, or mark it `editable: false` with a `readOnlyReason` until it can be delivered — a control that silently only writes locally is exactly what the 100%-honest-UI rule forbids.

(:266-267). The only disclosure the operator gets is a tooltip on the save indicator — "Information edits save as Nexus drafts. Saving does not publish or deliver them to Etsy." [high]verifiedETSYdata integrity risk

#### The SyncChannel enum has no ETSY value, so no Etsy job of any kind can ever be written to the single outbound delivery queue

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A developer implements the Etsy deactivate verb from ETSY-2 and follows the pattern every other channel uses — enqueue an `UNPUBLISH_LISTING` row on `OutboundSyncQueue` and let `bullmq-sync.worker.ts` drain it. The write fails at the database layer, because the queue's `targetChannel` column cannot hold the value 'ETSY'. The same wall blocks a price push, a quantity push and a delist.

##### What happens today
`SyncChannel` is declared as AMAZON | EBAY | SHOPIFY | WOOCOMMERCE | GOOGLE | META | TIKTOK (schema.prisma:57-66) — ETSY is absent — while `ChannelListing.channel` is a free `String` that does carry 'ETSY'. `products-catalog.routes.ts:1872-1876` documents exactly this ("OutboundSyncQueue.targetChannel is the SyncChannel enum … ChannelListing.channel is a free String including 'ETSY'") and works around it by filtering Etsy out and then casting `targetChannel: l.channel as any` (:1885) — the cast is what hides the mismatch from the type checker. So Etsy is not merely missing a delist adapter; it has no outbound lane at all, and therefore no retry, no dead-letter and no `/sync-logs` visibility for anything Etsy. The contradiction is visible elsewhere: `inventory-oversell-watchdog.service.ts:51` lists ETSY in `PER_LISTING_QUANTITY_CHANNELS`, i.e. the system is prepared to raise an Etsy oversell alarm on a channel it has no mechanism to push a quantity to.

##### Proposed fix
Additive Prisma migration adding `ETSY` to `enum SyncChannel` (additive migrations are pre-approved), then remove the `as any` at products-catalog.routes.ts:1885 so the compiler — not a hand-maintained `SUPPORTED` array — is what proves the channel is routable. Add an `ETSY` case to `dispatchChannelDelist` (channel-delist.service.ts:105-124) returning a typed non-retryable `unsupported` result with an operator-readable reason until the adapter lands, matching the WooCommerce shape at :112-117; that makes the gap visible as a SKIPPED queue row with a message instead of an invisible filter. Note while doing this that the free-String `syncType`/`listingStatus` columns make every such mismatch silent — the same enum-vs-String split is what let this sit undetected.

##### Evidence

- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:6859
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1872-1876
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1885
- apps/api/src/services/inventory-oversell-watchdog.service.ts:51
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts (zero ETSY references)

##### Verifier
The core mechanism is confirmed from code I opened myself, and no Etsy delist/relist path exists anywhere I searched. SyncChannel has no ETSY (schema.prisma:57-66) and the live DB enum matches (migrations 20260502...:17 creates four values, 20260529_um9...:6-8 adds only GOOGLE/META/TIKTOK), while OutboundSyncQueue.targetChannel is that enum (schema.prisma:6832). products-catalog.routes.ts:1872-1885 reads exactly as quoted, including the `as any` cast, and the Etsy listings it filters out are reported nowhere: channelCascadeEnqueued (:1899, returned :1987) counts only the enqueued rows, and the delete then proceeds (:1970-1975), so a hard delete with channelAction=unpublish/delete leaves the Etsy listing live on Etsy with no queue row, no error and no operator-visible reason. channel-delist.service.ts:105-124 has no ETSY branch (/usr/bin/grep -ci etsy = 0), and marketplaces/etsy.service.ts exposes no deactivate/delete-listing method at all (only getListing/getAllListings/updateListingPrice:398/updateListingQuantity:423/updateVariationQuantity:448/receipts; `state` appears only as a read field), so the missing capability is shown missing, not assumed. inventory-oversell-watchdog.service.ts:51 lists ETSY verbatim, and stock-movement.service.ts:684-687 names the enum as the reason the quantity cascade skips it. It is mis-stated in two places, which is why the title and framing need correcting rather than the verdict. Both bypass OutboundSyncQueue entirely, so the accurate statement is "no GOVERNED lane; only ungoverned legacy direct pushes keyed on Product.etsyListingId, outside retry/dead-letter/audit". (2) "no /sync-logs visibility for anything Etsy" is not established: sync-logs.routes.ts:115-143 reads outboundApiCallLog, not the queue, and jobs/etsy-sync.job.ts:31-46 writes SyncLog rows with channel "ETSY" under a registered cron (cron-registry.ts:235). Neither error touches the delist/relist gap the Owner asked about, which is real and silent.

1) Adding ETSY to the enum makes ETSY rows enqueueable by every existing producer, and only ONE of the two dispatchers is patched. outbound-sync.service.ts:611-617 switches on item.targetChannel with `default: throw new Error("Unknown channel: ...")`. Any ETSY case must be added at outbound-sync.service.ts:612 as well as channel-delist.service.ts:105, or the enum change converts a silent drop into a noisy retry storm.

2) "remove the `as any` ... so the compiler — not a hand-maintained SUPPORTED array — is what proves the channel is routable" is wrong on this codebase. GOOGLE, META and TIKTOK are already enum members (schema.prisma:62-65) and have no case in either dispatcher, so enum membership demonstrably does not imply routability. The compiler would prove only that the string is a legal column value. If routability is what must be proven, the invariant belongs in a derived map keyed off the dispatcher switch (one exhaustive `satisfies Record<SyncChannel, Handler>`), which would also convict the three existing marketing channels.

[medium]verifiedETSYdata integrity risk

#### The only Etsy listing importer writes master Product columns and never a ChannelListing, so the Etsy "Listing status" column can never show a value and a sync would overwrite master content

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator wants to see, in the studio's Etsy scope, whether their leather journal is currently `active`, `sold_out` or `expired` on Etsy — the single most important fact about an Etsy listing, since sold_out and expired are what a renew would fix. They look at the sheet's "Listing status" column.

##### What happens today
It is always blank. `EtsySyncService.syncListing` — the only code that ingests Etsy listings — writes to `Product` directly and never creates a `ChannelListing`: `product.findFirst({ where: { etsyListingId } })` (etsy-sync.service.ts:143) then `product.create`/`product.update` setting `name`, `basePrice`, `totalStock`, `variationTheme` and `status` (:152-176). Nothing in the repo writes an ETSY `ChannelListing.platformAttributes` from Etsy's API — the modern client is read-only and its three callers only fetch taxonomy and reference lists (read-client.ts:5-24; callers at etsy/taxonomy.ts:34, etsy/information-references.ts:27, categories/schema-sync.service.ts:201). The only writer of an ETSY row is the operator's own cell edit (channel-value-write.ts:13-18), which leaves `listingStatus` at its `"DRAFT"` default (schema.prisma:1615) and `platformAttributes` holding only what the operator typed — so the read-only `state` field the spec defines (channel-specs/etsy.ts:123) has no source. Worse, if the legacy sync were ever enabled (it needs ETSY_SHOP_ID/API_KEY/ACCESS_TOKEN/REFRESH_TOKEN/WEBHOOK_SECRET, utils/config.ts:105-112; the cron key `etsy-sync` is already registered at cron-registry.ts:235) it would overwrite master `name`, `basePrice` and `totalStock` with Etsy's values on every tick, and its `findFirst` carries no workspace filter.

##### Proposed fix
Rewrite the Etsy ingest to target the coordinate the studio actually reads: upsert `ChannelListing` on (workspaceId, productId, channel='ETSY', marketplace='GLOBAL', channelConnectionId, aliasKey) with `externalListingId = listing_id`, `listingStatus` mapped from Etsy's `state` (active→ACTIVE, inactive→INACTIVE, sold_out/expired→ENDED, draft→DRAFT), and the verbatim Etsy payload into `platformAttributes` so `state`, `should_auto_renew`, `shop_section_id` and `language` have a real source; it must never write master `Product.name`/`basePrice`/`totalStock`. Run it on the CX OAuth connection (etsyReader's account-scoped token) rather than the env-var legacy client, and delete the legacy `EtsyService` write methods once price/quantity move onto the queue lane from ETSY-4. Until that lands, mark the `state` column with an explicit `readOnlyReason` that says the value is not being imported yet, rather than rendering a permanently empty "Listing status".

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/sync/etsy-sync.service.ts:143
- apps/api/src/services/sync/etsy-sync.service.ts:152-176
- apps/api/src/services/etsy/read-client.ts:5-24
- apps/api/src/services/pim/channel-value-write.ts:13-18
- apps/api/src/services/pim/channel-specs/etsy.ts:123
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1615
- apps/api/src/utils/config.ts:105-112
- apps/api/src/jobs/cron-registry.ts:235
- apps/api/src/jobs/etsy-sync.job.ts:34

##### Verifier
The defect is confirmed from code I read, though the finding overstates two sub-claims.

CONFIRMED:
1. `etsy-sync.service.ts:142-176` says exactly what is claimed: `product.findFirst({ where: { etsyListingId } })` (no workspace filter, line 142-143), then `product.create` (149-161) / `product.update` (164-176) writing master `sku`, `name`, `basePrice`, `totalStock`, `etsyListingId`, `variationTheme`, `status`. No `channelListing` write appears anywhere in that file (the only other model touched is `channel`/`listing` at 202-207 and `productVariation` at 246-257).
2. The studio really does read Etsy "Listing status" from `ChannelListing.platformAttributes.state`: `channel-specs/etsy.ts:123` labels `state` "Listing status"; the default `channelStore` for a generated field is `pa(key)` (etsy.ts:7, 12); `writable = ... && key !== 'state'` (etsy.ts:85) forces `editable: false` + readOnlyReason "Reported by Etsy…" (etsy.ts:105); and `channel-inheritance.ts:19-21` resolves that store by `readPath(row.platformAttributes, ['state'])`.
3. Nothing imports an Etsy listing into `ChannelListing`. Checked with `/usr/bin/grep` (not the shell `grep` function): every `channelListing.create|update|upsert|updateMany` site in apps/api/src, plus each plausible Etsy path — `listings/resync.service.ts:22,94` ("ETSY — NotImplementedError"), `listing-wizard/channel-publish.service.ts:92` ("WooCommerce + Etsy stay in NOT_IMPLEMENTED"), `workers/channel-sync.worker.ts:184-190` (AMAZON/EBAY/SHOPIFY only), `cx/catalog.ts` (ETSY appears only as a connection key, no listing ingest), `inbound.routes.ts` (no Etsy at all). The modern read client's production callers all fetch taxonomy/reference lists only — `taxonomy.ts:34` and `taxonomy/providers.ts:36` (`/seller-taxonomy/nodes`), `categories/schema-sync.service.ts:201` (`/seller-taxonomy/nodes/{id}/properties`), `information-references.ts:32` limited to `ETSY_REFERENCE_PATHS` = shipping-profiles / sections / policies/return / readiness-state-definitions (information-references.ts:4-7). No `/listings` fetch exists in `apps/api/src/services/etsy/`.
4. Supporting citations check out: `schema.prisma:1615` `listingStatus String @default("DRAFT")` is inside `model ChannelListing` (starts 1509, no intervening model); `config.ts:105-112` requires all five ETSY_* env vars; `cron-registry.ts:235` registers `'etsy-sync': () => runAllEstySyncJobs()`; `etsy-sync.job.ts:16-24` builds `EstySyncService` from `ConfigManager.getConfig("ETSY")`.

MIS-STATEMENTS (not fatal):
- "three callers" of the read client is four production callers (taxonomy/providers.ts:34-36 was missed); all four are still non-listing reads, so the set claim survives.
- "The only writer of an ETSY row is the operator's own cell edit (channel-value-write.ts:13-18) … platformAttributes holding only what the operator typed" conflates two stores: `channel-value-write.ts` merges into `overrideData`, while Etsy platformAttributes-store fields are written through `channel-value-mutation.ts:51-61` + `applyPlatformMutations` as invoked by `products/bulk-edit.service.ts:9,16`.
- "can never show a value" is very slightly too strong: `catalog-transfer-plan.ts:335` rejects a read-only field only when a prior listing exists (`if (!field.editable && before)`), so a workbook import that CREATES the Etsy listing could seed `state`; the cell editor itself blocks it (`bulk-edit.service.ts:618-625`, "Unknown or read-only category attribute"). The accurate claim is "never populated from Etsy".

The master-overwrite half is real but dormant and conditional, as the finding itself states: `EtsyService.request` calls `requireLegacyCredentials('Etsy')` (workspace-legacy-credentials.ts:4-7), which throws for any non-legacy workspace, and `ConfigManager.loadEtsyConfig` needs all five env vars. It therefore supports "risk if enabled", not "happening today".
The proposed fix is directionally right but has three problems. (1) It says the legacy writer's replacement must "never write master Product.name/basePrice/totalStock" — good — but it omits that the same file also writes ProductVariation by etsyListingId with no workspace filter (etsy-sync.service.ts:246-257), which has the identical cross-workspace collision. (2) It proposes upserting on (workspaceId, productId, channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId, aliasKey), which matches the existing ON CONFLICT target in channel-value-write.ts:19 — but an ingest has no productId until it matches on externalListingId, so the matching key has to be (workspaceId, channel, externalListingId) first; the upsert key as stated cannot be evaluated on a first import. (3) The interim mitigation ("mark the state column with an explicit readOnlyReason") is partly already there: etsy.ts:85,105 already sets readOnlyReason 'Reported by Etsy. This field cannot be edited in the information sheet.' for every non-writable field, and etsy.ts:123 replaces the helpText for state. The change needed is to the wording ("not imported yet"), not to add a reason — and it should cover the whole read-only block (created/updated timestamps, rich_description, price__amount/divisor, price_currency_code), not just state, since all of them are blank for the same reason.

#### The studio refuses to link an Etsy listing on a false premise — Etsy listing URLs need no shop domain, and the same repo builds them

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is reviewing a beeswax candle on the Etsy scope and wants to open the real listing on etsy.com to compare what a buyer sees. They click the listing id in the record drawer.

##### What happens today
Nothing — it renders as plain text. `listingUrl()` returns `null` for Etsy, with the comment "Shopify, WooCommerce and Etsy listings are not addressable from a marketplace code alone — they need the shop's own domain, which this scope does not carry" (drawer/listingUrl.ts:57-60; pinned by a test at drawer/listingUrl.vitest.test.ts:31). That premise is true for Shopify and WooCommerce and false for Etsy: Etsy is a single global marketplace and a listing is addressable from its id alone. The same repo already builds it — `listings-syndication.routes.ts:113-114` returns `https://www.etsy.com/listing/${externalId}`. ##### Proposed fix
Move the ETSY case above the TLD lookup in `listingUrl()` — `case 'ETSY': return `https://www.etsy.com/listing/${id}`` — since the market code is irrelevant for Etsy, and amend the comment so it no longer asserts a property Etsy does not have (it should name Shopify and WooCommerce only). Update the test at listingUrl.vitest.test.ts:31 to assert the URL instead of `null`, and add a case pinning `marketplace: 'GLOBAL'`. The link itself should stay the existing DS treatment used for the eBay/Amazon cases in the drawer's identity band — no new component. Better still, derive the mapping from one place: `listings-syndication.routes.ts:100-120` and this file are two hand-rolled copies of the same table, which is how they drifted apart.

##### Scenario
An operator runs a WooCommerce storefront alongside Amazon. WOOCOMMERCE_STORE_URL/CONSUMER_KEY/CONSUMER_SECRET are set, so the `woocommerce-sync` cron imports their catalogue and a rain jacket lands in Nexus carrying Product.woocommerceProductId = 4412. Months later the jacket is discontinued: they soft-delete it, open the recycle bin, select it and choose Delete permanently. The confirmation dialog reads its preflight, finds no channel listings, silently pre-selects 'Local-only', and they type DELETE.

##### What happens today
The WooCommerce sync writes ONLY Product.woocommerceProductId — it never creates a ChannelListing (woocommerce-sync.service.ts:137-205 upserts Product; /usr/bin/grep -in 'channellisting' over that file returns rc=1, positive control: 19 `prisma` matches in the same file, so the file was read). Every delete surface keys on ChannelListing: the preflight queries `prisma.channelListing.findMany` only (products-catalog.routes.ts:1678-1691) and the delist cascade queries `tx.channelListing.findMany` only (products-catalog.routes.ts:1853-1858). Because the list comes back empty, BulkActionBar.tsx:1117 sets channelAction='none' and the Channel-action radio at :1283 is not even rendered (`hasListings` false). The product row is destroyed, and the jacket stays live and purchasable on the WooCommerce store with nothing in Nexus that remembers it exists. `woocommerceProductId` is read by exactly 18 lines repo-wide (/usr/bin/grep -rn over apps/api/src + apps/web/src) — none of them a delete, delist or preflight path, and ZERO of them under apps/web/src.

##### Proposed fix
Two parts, both server-side first. (1) Make the WooCommerce importer produce the same coordinate every other channel produces: in woocommerce-sync.service.ts, alongside the Product upsert, upsert a ChannelListing at (productId, channel:'WOOCOMMERCE', marketplace:'GLOBAL', channelConnectionId, aliasKey:'') with externalListingId = the Woo product id and listingStatus 'ACTIVE'. Until then WooCommerce is invisible to readiness, the sheet, the drawer's ListingsPane and every lifecycle path. (2) Until (1) lands, widen the preflight so it cannot under-report: have GET /products/hard-delete-preflight also select Product.woocommerceProductId / shopifyProductId / ebayItemId / amazonAsin and return them as `parentLevelListings: [{ productId, channel, externalId }]`. Render them in the same warning block as `channelListings` using the DS `Banner` (tone="warning") the dialog should already be using, with copy that names the channel and says plainly that Nexus cannot end this listing for you. Do not let the radio default to 'Local-only' while any parent-level id is present.

- apps/api/src/services/sync/woocommerce-sync.service.ts:189-205
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1678-1691
- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1853-1858
- apps/web/src/app/products/_components/BulkActionBar.tsx:1111-1118
- apps/web/src/app/products/_components/BulkActionBar.tsx:1283-1284
- apps/api/src/jobs/woocommerce-sync.job.ts:84-85
- apps/api/src/utils/config.ts:69-97

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find any surface that closes the gap.

CONFIRMED BY READING:
1. woocommerce-sync.service.ts:137-150 and :189-205 upsert `product` with `woocommerceProductId` only (parent branch and simple-product branch). `/usr/bin/grep -in channellisting` on that file returns rc=1 (positive control: 19 `prisma` matches, 597 lines) — the importer creates no ChannelListing. The job wrapper is also clean: `/usr/bin/grep -in channelListing apps/api/src/jobs/woocommerce-sync.job.ts` → rc=1.
2. products-catalog.routes.ts:1678-1691 — the preflight's only channel query is `prisma.channelListing.findMany` filtered on `externalListingId: { not: null }`; the documented response shape (:1660-1663) has no parent-level field.
3. products-catalog.routes.ts:1854-1860 — the cascade enqueues OutboundSyncQueue rows exclusively from `tx.channelListing.findMany`; zero listings ⇒ zero queue rows, whatever channelAction is.
4. BulkActionBar.tsx:1117 sets `channelAction = data.channelListings.length === 0 ? 'none' : 'unpublish'`; :1143 `hasListings = (preflight?.channelListings.length ?? 0) > 0`; the whole warnings block (:1212) and the channel-action fieldset (:1283) are gated on `hasListings`. I read the entire warnings region :1201-1280: with an empty list the dialog renders no channel warning of any kind — no generic fallback copy.
5. `/usr/bin/grep -rn woocommerceProductId apps/api/src apps/web/src packages` → 18 lines under apps/api/src, 0 under apps/web/src, 2 in packages/database (schema.prisma:98, one migration). None is a delete/delist/preflight path. The only external-id resolver that would help, outbound-sync.service.ts:2293, is inside `getExternalListingId` and is reached only from an already-created queue row.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
- Another creation path? I enumerated every `channelListing.create/upsert/createMany` in apps/api/src (40 sites). None is WooCommerce-specific; the only channel-agnostic ones (marketplaces.routes.ts:309 offer-availability upsert, :644 products/listings PUT, channel-sync.worker.ts:136) create rows with no `externalListingId`, which the preflight filter at :1682 excludes anyway.
- Another UI/route that warns? WooCommerce appears in 68 web files (scopes.ts, list-wizard, ChannelListingTab, settings/channels), but not one references `woocommerceProductId`, so no surface knows the Woo id exists.
- Dead/unreachable code? No. WOOCOMMERCE is a first-class channel (schema.prisma:61/5386/12239, connections.routes.ts:26/68), and the importer is reachable via CRON_REGISTRY['woocommerce-sync'] (cron-registry.ts:237) drained by the manual trigger at sync-logs.routes.ts:512, plus unified-sync-orchestrator.ts:94.

MIS-STATEMENTS (do not refute, but bound the claim):
- The env gate is FOUR vars, not three: config.ts:75 also requires WOOCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
- "the woocommerce-sync cron imports their catalogue" is imprecise: CRON_REGISTRY is the manual-trigger map (sync-logs.routes.ts:512); I found no scheduler entry that fires 'woocommerce-sync' on a timer.
- The proposed fix part (1) is wrong on its own: even with a ChannelListing present, dispatchChannelDelist returns `'WooCommerce delist adapter not yet implemented'` (channel-delist.service.ts:112-116, non-retryable), and live Woo publish is likewise unwired (channel-publish.service.ts:80-87). Creating the listing row would only convert silent data loss into a permanently failing queue row — the honest-UI half of the fix is the load-bearing part.

Severity corrected critical → high: the harm is real and silent, but it requires a configured Woo store plus an operator- or orchestrator-driven import, and the Woo write side of the platform is stubbed throughout, so the affected population is narrower than "critical" implies.
Part (2) — widening the preflight to return parent-level ids and rendering an honest warning that Nexus cannot end the listing, plus refusing to default to 'Local-only' while any parent id is present — is correct and is the part that actually protects the operator. Part (1) is stated as if minting a ChannelListing would make the delist work; it would not. channel-delist.service.ts:112-116 rejects every WOOCOMMERCE job with a non-retryable 'adapter not yet implemented', so part (1) alone turns a silent loss into a permanently failed OutboundSyncQueue row while the store keeps selling. Sequence it as: (a) honest preflight + warning + no Local-only default (ships value immediately), (b) the Woo delist adapter, (c) only then the ChannelListing upsert in the importer — otherwise the cascade at products-catalog.routes.ts:1854 starts enqueueing jobs that can never succeed. Also note the proposed upsert must supply channelMarket/region consistent with the composite key used at marketplaces.routes.ts:310 (productId_channel_marketplace with workspaceKey), or it will collide with rows created by the offer-availability path.

#### bulk-hard-delete enqueues WooCommerce delist jobs the dispatcher refuses, and the queue row is cascade-deleted before the worker can even record the failure

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A workspace has a WooCommerce ChannelListing row for a discontinued kettle (written by hand, by a migration, or by the importer once WOO-1 is fixed). The operator bins the kettle, opens the permanent-delete dialog, sees 'WOOCOMMERCE · GLOBAL: 1' in the channel summary, and picks the default 'Unpublish (recommended)' because the copy promises it 'keeps the listing record so you can republish later'.

##### What happens today
products-catalog.routes.ts:1875 declares `const SUPPORTED = ['AMAZON','EBAY','SHOPIFY','WOOCOMMERCE']` and enqueues an UNPUBLISH_LISTING row for the kettle. The comment directly above it (:1870-1873) excludes ETSY for exactly the reason that also applies to WooCommerce — "Etsy doesn't have a delist adapter yet" — but WooCommerce was left in, and dispatchChannelDelist refuses it non-retryably: `error: 'WooCommerce delist adapter not yet implemented', retryable: false` (channel-delist.service.ts:112-117). The failure is never even recorded: OutboundSyncQueue.productId is `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:6822-6823), so `tx.product.deleteMany` inside the same transaction destroys the queue row, and when the post-commit `fireOutboundJobs` job drains, bullmq-sync.worker.ts:104-111 finds `!queueRecord` and throws 'Queue record not found'. No dead-letter row, no /sync-logs entry, no adapter call. The operator-facing copy compounds it: en.json:5223 promises 'Pause the offer on each channel — keeps the listing record so you can republish later. Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing; Shopify: status DRAFT' — WooCommerce is named nowhere, and the listing record is in fact destroyed by the same cascade on every channel.

##### Proposed fix
Immediately: drop 'WOOCOMMERCE' from SUPPORTED (products-catalog.routes.ts:1875) so it is refused at enqueue time exactly as ETSY is, and have the route return the refused coordinates as `channelActionUnsupported: [{ channel, marketplace, count }]`. Surface that in the dialog BEFORE the operator commits, not after — a DS `Banner` tone="warning" inside the existing Modal: “1 WooCommerce listing cannot be ended by Nexus. Deleting here removes it from Nexus only; end it in your WooCommerce admin first.” Separately, the copy at en.json:5222-5225 must derive its per-channel sentence from the set of channels actually present in the preflight rather than hardcoding Amazon/eBay/Shopify. While this dialog is being touched it should also move onto the DS: it is hand-rolled Tailwind (raw `<input type="radio">` at BulkActionBar.tsx:1288, `bg-rose-600` at :1358) where the DS has `RadioCard`, `Modal` and `Button`, and its type-phrase is the literal string 'DELETE' (en.json:5230), which DS ruling #133 forbids — the phrase must be the real SKU.

- apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1878-1900
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:104-117
- apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:104-111
- apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-159

- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:6821-6827

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find any path that rescues it.

CONFIRMED VERBATIM:
- products-catalog.routes.ts:1875 — `const SUPPORTED: ReadonlyArray<string> = ['AMAZON', 'EBAY', 'SHOPIFY', 'WOOCOMMERCE']`, with the comment at :1870-1873 excluding ETSY because "Etsy doesn't have a delist adapter yet (D.2 covers Amazon/eBay/Shopify only)" — WooCommerce is enqueued anyway (:1876 filter, :1878-1898 createManyAndReturn).
- channel-delist.service.ts:112-117 — `case 'WOOCOMMERCE': return { success: false, error: 'WooCommerce delist adapter not yet implemented', retryable: false }`. The switch is unconditional; no other route reaches an adapter.
- bullmq-sync.worker.ts:104-111 — `if (!queueRecord) { logger.warn('Queue record not found'); throw ... }`, i.e. no DB row is written on a missing queue record; the delist branch that would call `applyDelistResultToQueue` is at :141-159 and is never reached.
- schema.prisma:6822-6826 — BOTH `productId ... onDelete: Cascade` and `channelListingId ... onDelete: Cascade`.
- I went further than the finding and verified the cascade is real at the DB level, not just declared: packages/database/prisma/migrations/20260502_phase31b_channellisting_marketplace/migration.sql:232-240 emits `OutboundSyncQueue_productId_fkey ... ON DELETE CASCADE` and `OutboundSyncQueue_channelListingId_fkey ... ON DELETE CASCADE`. `/usr/bin/grep -rn "OutboundSyncQueue_productId_fkey" packages/database/prisma/migrations` returns exactly that one hit — no later migration re-points it to SET NULL. `relationMode` is not set (schema.prisma:5-8), so Prisma uses real FKs. ChannelListing itself cascades from Product (schema.prisma:1515-1516).
- The rows are created at :1878 and `tx.product.deleteMany` runs at :1973 inside the SAME `prisma.$transaction`; `fireOutboundJobs` runs post-commit at :2001-2003. So the queue rows provably cannot exist by the time the worker drains.
- en.json:5223 is the exact promised copy ("keeps the listing record so you can republish later. Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing; Shopify: status DRAFT."), en.json:5230 is `"DELETE"`, and BulkActionBar.tsx:1129 arms on `typed.trim().toUpperCase() === 'DELETE'`.
- The WooCommerce coordinate really does surface in the dialog: the preflight query (products-catalog.routes.ts:1676-1690) applies NO channel filter, and the summary key is built as `${l.channel}${l.marketplace ? ` · ${l.marketplace}` : ''}` at BulkActionBar.tsx:1134-1138, rendered at :1223.
- DS claims check out: raw `<input type="radio">` at BulkActionBar.tsx:1288-1296 (repeated :1303-1311, :1318-1326), `bg-rose-600` className override on a DS Button at :1358.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: no alternate delist path exists — `/usr/bin/grep -rn "WOOCOMMERCE" apps/api/src` shows WooCommerce only in config/webhook/sync-job/syndication surfaces, none of which is reachable from `dispatchChannelDelist`. There is no test pinning this behaviour (`/usr/bin/grep -rln "bulk-hard-delete|channelCascadeEnqueued" apps/api/src` → only the route, the worker, the service and three unrelated comment hits), so nothing contradicts the read.

WHY IT IS MIS-STATED: the WooCommerce framing is the small half. The cascade defect is channel-agnostic — the same FK destroys the AMAZON, EBAY and SHOPIFY delist rows in the same transaction. So the entire D.1/D.2 channel cascade is inert for every channel: an operator who picks "Unpublish (recommended)" or "Delete on channel" gets the local Product wiped while the Amazon/eBay/Shopify listing stays live, with no queue row, no dead-letter, no /sync-logs entry and no error. The design comment at :1843-1850 ("the queue rows still carry productId + externalListingId + channel so the adapters can finish the channel-side work") asserts a property the schema forbids. WooCommerce is then a second, narrower defect layered on top (enqueued despite a stub adapter, contradicting the ETSY exclusion two lines above).

One caveat I could not resolve read-only: products.routes.ts:1276-1281 records that in production a Product-cascade FK did NOT fire for ListingWizard ("DB FK ON DELETE NO ACTION due to migration drift"). If OutboundSyncQueue has drifted the same way in the live DB, the failure mode flips from "silent row loss" to "the whole hard-delete transaction aborts on an FK violation". Broken either way; only the symptom differs.
The immediate fix (drop 'WOOCOMMERCE' from SUPPORTED at :1875) treats the smaller half and would leave the programme believing the Amazon/eBay/Shopify cascade works. The load-bearing fix is the FK: the delist rows must survive the Product delete — either change OutboundSyncQueue.productId / channelListingId to `onDelete: SetNull` (with a migration, and only if every reader tolerates nulls — the worker already reads productId/channelListingId off the queue row itself at bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-149, so it would), or create the delist rows AFTER the transaction commits from data captured inside it, rather than inside it. Until that lands, `channelAction: 'unpublish' | 'delete'` should not be offered at all. The proposed `channelActionUnsupported` preflight banner and the derived per-channel copy are both right and should additionally state that the local listing record is destroyed regardless of choice (en.json:5223 currently promises the opposite). The DS/type-phrase cleanup is correct but strictly cosmetic next to the cascade.

#### The studio can never scope to WooCommerce, because nothing in the repo can create a WooCommerce ChannelConnection — while the WooCommerce cron actively syncs the store

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has WooCommerce credentials in env, the woocommerce-sync cron is importing their catalogue nightly, and Marketplace carries a seeded WOOCOMMERCE/GLOBAL row. They open a jacket at /products/[id]/edit/studio expecting to find a WooCommerce scope chip next to Amazon and eBay so they can edit the store copy. There is no chip, and nothing on the page says why or that a WooCommerce store exists at all.

##### What happens today
The studio's channel chips come from `options.channels`, which deriveScopeOptions builds only from marketplaces whose `connected` flag is true (scopes.ts:112-119), and studio-data.ts sets `connected` from ACTIVE, non-'pending' ChannelConnection rows (studio-data.ts:107-116). No code anywhere writes a WooCommerce connection: `/usr/bin/grep -rn "channelType: *['\"]WOOCOMMERCE" apps/api/src apps/web/src packages` returns rc=1 (positive control: the same pattern for SHOPIFY matches 5+ files). The CX connection catalogue's ChannelKey union is 'EBAY'|'AMAZON_SP'|'AMAZON_ADS'|'SHOPIFY'|'ETSY' (cx/catalog.ts:17) and services/cx/connectors/ contains exactly amazon-ads, amazon-sp, ebay, etsy, shopify — no woocommerce directory — so the Connect tab, which renders one card per catalogue entry (ConnectTab.tsx:4-6), never offers it. seedEnvManagedConnections creates only an Amazon row (index.ts:394-431). So the channel gate is honest by accident, but the consequence is that a channel the platform syncs on a cron (cron-registry.ts:237, credentials from utils/config.ts:69-97) is structurally unreachable and unmentioned in the Product Edit Studio: 15 WooCommerce hits under the whole _studio/ tree, every one of them a type-union member, a label constant or a test — no UI, no route, no fetch.

##### Proposed fix
Decide and then say so in the product, rather than leaving it silently absent. If WooCommerce stays env-only, add a CX catalogue entry with authMode 'api_key' and `available: false` plus a reason, so ConnectTab renders a HELD card (the pattern it already has at ConnectTab.tsx:211, 'This channel cannot be connected yet.') instead of WooCommerce simply not existing in the UI; and in the studio, render the chip from `options.channels` including unconnected seeded channels with DS ScopeBar readiness `{ state: 'absent', note: 'WooCommerce is synced from server credentials and cannot be edited here yet.' }` — ScopeBar already accepts exactly that shape (StudioBar.tsx:16-26). If WooCommerce is meant to be a first-class channel, the real work is a cx/connectors/woocommerce spec (store URL + consumer key/secret, authMode 'api_key') writing a ChannelConnection with channelType 'WOOCOMMERCE'; that single row is what unlocks the chip, the accounts Listbox and the destination resolver with no further studio change.

No route accepts an arbitrary channelType. Meanwhile the marketplace row is seeded (seed-marketplaces.ts:41) and the cron is registered (cron-registry.ts:237) with env credentials (config.ts:69-97). So the capability gap is real and was not established with the broken grep function. TWO overstatements corrected, and they cost the finding its 'high': (a) 'nothing on the page says ... that a WooCommerce store exists at all' is false — the studio's Variants family grid renders a per-channel column for every family channel and states the reason explicitly, `${channel.label} is not set up — no account is connected` (variants/family/columns.tsx:166, plus the projection renderer hint at design-system/grid/renderers/projection.ts:117), and the family read on GALE-JACKET measured a `WOOCOMMERCE:GLOBAL(not set up)` column (docs/pes-claims.md:36170); (b) the 'no UI, no route, no fetch under _studio/' census is a literal-string census that misses exactly this generic, server-driven rendering. If a chip is added, it must be non-selectable, or WOO-4's empty sheet becomes reachable by design. The variants column already carries the honest wording to reuse.

#### A WooCommerce channel sheet would be structurally empty and report itself as merely 'no required attributes', not as unimplemented — the dangerous-green shape readiness.service.ts itself names

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Someone adds the one missing ChannelConnection row (by hand, by a migration, or when a Woo connector lands) and an operator finally selects the WooCommerce scope on a jacket, expecting the same information sheet Amazon and eBay give them. They see a sheet, a Requirements button, and a scope chip.

##### What happens today
There is no WooCommerce channel spec. sheet-columns.service.ts:1112-1184 walks each coordinate with three branches — AMAZON (:1114), SHOPIFY|ETSY (:1145), EBAY (:1166) — and no `else`, so a WOOCOMMERCE coordinate pushes nothing to `specs` AND nothing to `schemaMissing`; channel-specs/ contains amazon.ts, ebay.ts, etsy*.ts, shopify.ts and store.ts (whose `spec()` is typed `channel: 'SHOPIFY' | 'ETSY'`, store.ts:92) — no woocommerce file. Downstream, readiness.service.ts:199 sets `requiresCategory: coordinate.channel === 'AMAZON' || coordinate.channel === 'EBAY'`, i.e. false for WooCommerce, which switches OFF the productType-null error the same file calls "the most dangerous shape a readiness pill can take" (:211-217). With `required.total === 0` and `schemaMissing` empty, scope-readiness.service.ts:67-73 emits state 'absent' with the note "No required attributes are defined for this scope" — wording that reads as a deliberate configuration choice, not as "this channel has no contract at all". The Requirements dialog is worse: SchemaStatus.tsx:18 treats only SHOPIFY as a store, so WooCommerce takes the marketplace branch and the operator is told "Requirements depend on the listing category and marketplace" and "Select a listing category to load its requirements" (:43-44) for a channel with no category concept, while the primary 'Refresh requirements' button is permanently disabled on `!categories.length` (:36). This is latent today only because WOO-3 makes the scope unreachable.

##### Proposed fix
Close the fall-through rather than leaving a silent empty. Add a final `else` in the coordinate loop (sheet-columns.service.ts:1184) that pushes `schemaMissing.push(`${coordinate.channel}:*`)` for any channel with no spec branch — that one line turns the WooCommerce scope chip from 'absent / no required attributes' into 'blocked / Category metadata is incomplete', and makes the next unimplemented channel fail loudly by construction instead of silently. Then either ship a `channel-specs/woocommerce.ts` modelled on store.ts's flat webstore spec (wc/v3 product fields: name, description, short_description, sku, regular_price, stock_quantity, categories, images) and widen `spec()`'s union to include it, or — if WooCommerce is not being built — make visibleTabs() return `[]` for it (scopes.ts:219) per layout-v2 §14.3, "a tab that cannot do anything must not be a tab". Also widen SchemaStatus's `store` test (SchemaStatus.tsx:18) from `channel === 'SHOPIFY'` to the GLOBAL_CHANNELS set the server already maintains (sheet-columns.service.ts:907) so a webstore is never asked to pick a listing category.

Every cited line says what the finding claims. The coordinate loop at sheet-columns.service.ts:1113-1184 has exactly three branches — `coordinate.channel === 'AMAZON'` (:1114), `=== 'SHOPIFY' || === 'ETSY'` (:1145), `=== 'EBAY'` (:1166) — and no else, so a WOOCOMMERCE coordinate pushes nothing to `specs` and nothing to `schemaMissing`, while GLOBAL_CHANNELS at :907 proves WOOCOMMERCE is a valid SheetChannel that does produce coordinates (labelled '· GLOBAL' at :958; the docs record a live `WOOCOMMERCE:GLOBAL` family column, pes-claims.md:36170). channel-specs/ has no woocommerce file and `spec()` is typed `channel: 'SHOPIFY' | 'ETSY'` (store.ts:93). readiness.service.ts:201 sets `requiresCategory: coordinate.channel === 'AMAZON' || coordinate.channel === 'EBAY'`, and :223 guards the productType error with `v.requiresCategory !== false`, so the branch the file itself calls 'the most dangerous shape a readiness pill can take' (:220-222) is switched off for WooCommerce. scope-readiness.service.ts:64-73 then yields state 'absent' on `required.total === 0`. SchemaStatus's store test is `channel === 'SHOPIFY'` (actual line 17, cited as 18 — a one-line citation slip, content exact), so WooCommerce would take the marketplace branch with 'Requirements depend on the listing category and marketplace' (:41), 'Select a listing category to load its requirements' (:43) and a Refresh button disabled on `!categories.length` (:35). ONE claim is not quite right: the note wording is chosen by an ordered ternary at scope-readiness.service.ts:70-73 in which `mappingUnavailable` is tested BEFORE `required.total === 0`, so the operator may instead read 'Channel mapping values have not been fully checked'; either way the state is 'absent', so the defect survives, but the quoted string is not guaranteed. Latency is correctly disclosed: WOO-3 makes the scope unreachable today, which is why this is medium, not high.
The one-line `else { schemaMissing.push(...) }` is the right shape and matches hub ruling #315's adopted criterion — 'an unexplained zero is a failure; an explained zero is an answer' (pes-claims.md:14786-14788) — which is the strongest support the finding has and it does not cite it. Two cautions: schemaMissing feeds the operator-facing string 'Category metadata is incomplete: …' (scope-readiness.service.ts:70), which is the wrong sentence for a channel that has no category concept, so the pushed token needs its own wording, not `${channel}:*`; and #315 also records the settled interim message for exactly these GLOBAL store scopes, so the copy should reuse it rather than invent a fourth phrasing. The visibleTabs()-returns-[] alternative conflicts with scopes.ts:219-222, where variants is deliberately offered on EVERY scope per the variants spec §1.1.

[medium]verifiedWOOCOMMERCEmissing capability

#### WooCommerceService has no product create, update or delete method at all — there is nothing for a delist or relist adapter to call

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The Owner asks for the jacket to come off WooCommerce and go back on next season. A lane picks up 'WooCommerce delist adapter not yet implemented' expecting to fill in the Woo arm of dispatchChannelDelist the way the Shopify arm was filled in, and discovers the client cannot express the operation.

##### What happens today
WooCommerceService implements getProduct(:269), getAllProducts(:299), updateProductPrice(:347), updateVariationPrice(:368), updateProductStock(:390), updateVariationStock(:411), getOrders(:433), getOrder(:469), updateOrderStatus(:489), addOrderNote(:505) — price, stock and orders only. `/usr/bin/grep -n 'createProduct|deleteProduct|updateProduct\b'` over that file returns rc=1; positive control: the same pattern on shopify.service.ts matches createProduct(:338), updateProduct(:383) and deleteProduct(:407), which is precisely why channel-delist.service.ts:192-203 can implement Shopify unpublish as `updateProduct(status:'draft')` and Shopify delete as `deleteProduct`. Every other WooCommerce write path is also inert: outbound-sync.service.ts:2148-2172 builds a Woo payload and then returns a failure reading 'WooCommerce outbound sync not yet wired — see roadmap C.19 (Wave 6 Path A)', channel-publish.service.ts:81-88 returns 'Live WooCommerce wp/v2/media + wc/v3/products upload is not yet wired' in live mode (only `sandbox` returns ok with a FAKE random attachment id, :62-77), and the wizard adapter registers WOOCOMMERCE as 'WooCommerce createProduct not yet implemented — see TECH_DEBT #35' (listing-wizard/channel-publish.service.ts:93-94). So today WooCommerce is read-only in one direction: the cron pulls products, inventory and orders in, and nothing Nexus does ever reaches the store.

##### Proposed fix
Sequence the work honestly and say so in the UI meanwhile. Step 1 is the client, not the adapter: add `updateProduct(id, body)` (PUT /wp-json/wc/v3/products/:id) and `deleteProduct(id, { force })` (DELETE /wp-json/wc/v3/products/:id) to WooCommerceService, reusing its existing `request<T>()` (:213) so rate limiting and MarketplaceSyncError classification come for free. Step 2 makes the delist arm real, mirroring Shopify exactly: `unpublish` → updateProduct(id, { status: 'draft' }) (genuinely reversible, the correct default), `delete` → deleteProduct(id, { force: true }); return `{ success:false, retryable:false }` only for a real refusal, never as the whole implementation. Step 3, relist: WooCommerce's draft→publish flip is a single updateProduct(id,{status:'publish'}), which makes it the cheapest channel in the repo to give a true per-market close/reopen pair — model it on amazon-market-offer.service.ts's offerClosedAt/offerCloseSnapshot so the reopen replays the captured state rather than rebuilding it. Until step 1 lands, WOO-2's enqueue guard and WOO-3's held card are what keep the UI honest.

- apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:338
- apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:383
- apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:407
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:192-203
- apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:2148-2172
- apps/api/src/services/channel-publish.service.ts:59-88
- apps/api/src/services/listing-wizard/channel-publish.service.ts:92-94

##### Verifier
Verified line by line, including the negative set claim. /usr/bin/grep -nE 'async [a-zA-Z]+\(' over woocommerce.service.ts returns exactly getProduct(:269), getAllProducts(:299), updateProductPrice(:347), updateVariationPrice(:368), updateProductStock(:390), updateVariationStock(:411), getOrders(:433), getOrder(:469), updateOrderStatus(:489), addOrderNote(:505) — no create/update/delete of a product. Positive control on shopify.service.ts matches createProduct(:338), updateProduct(:383), deleteProduct(:407), and channel-delist.service.ts:186-203 does exactly what the finding says with them (unpublish via updateProduct status draft, else deleteProduct). The Woo arm of that same switch is channel-delist.service.ts:112-115, `error: 'WooCommerce delist adapter not yet implemented'`. Every other write path reads as claimed: outbound-sync.service.ts:2148-2172 logs a gated attempt and returns success:false with 'WooCommerce outbound sync not yet wired — see roadmap C.19 (Wave 6 Path A)'; channel-publish.service.ts:59-88 returns a fabricated random attachment id in sandbox (:63-78) and an honest not-wired error in live (:80-88); listing-wizard/channel-publish.service.ts:93-94 registers 'WooCommerce createProduct not yet implemented — see TECH_DEBT #35'. Severity medium is right: this is a documented, tracked deferral (TECH_DEBT #35, roadmap C.19) rather than a hidden defect, and the code refuses honestly at every arm.
Sequencing (client before adapter) is correct and the Shopify mirror is the right model. But it understates the blocker: WooCommerceService's request path is driven by ConfigManager env credentials (config.ts:69-100), not by a ChannelConnection, so a delist adapter written this way would write to whatever single store the server env names, with no account selection — the same asymmetry that makes WOO-3's connection row the actual prerequisite. Also note channel-delist.service.ts:186-192 already shows the anti-pattern to avoid: Shopify's arm falls back to DELETE when updateProduct is absent, i.e. an irreversible action substituted for a reversible one; the Woo arm must not copy that fallback.

[medium]verifiedWOOCOMMERCEdesign inconsistency

#### The studio's content-language control is gated on a hardcoded ['SHOPIFY','ETSY'] list, so a WooCommerce scope would be the one webstore with no language switcher

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
With a WooCommerce connection in place, an operator scopes to WooCommerce to fix the Italian product copy on their store. On Shopify and Etsy the scope bar gives them a Content language picker; on WooCommerce the control simply is not there, and the locale silently stays whatever defaultLocaleFor derived from the seeded WOOCOMMERCE/GLOBAL row ('en').

##### What happens today
StudioBar.tsx:35 renders the locale Listbox with `['SHOPIFY','ETSY'].includes(scope)` — a hardcoded two-member list. The server, meanwhile, classes all three webstores together: sheet-columns.service.ts:907 declares `const GLOBAL_CHANNELS: SheetChannel[] = ['SHOPIFY','WOOCOMMERCE','ETSY']` and labels each coordinate '· GLOBAL' on that basis (:958). The same hardcoded-channel-list pattern repeats in contracts.tsx:672 and :675, where locale narrowing and locale validation both key on `['AMAZON','EBAY']`, so a WooCommerce locale is neither narrowed to the store's languages nor validated against them. Under D11 ("the SAME UI on all scopes; any master-only surface is a parity defect") and §14.5 ("locales derive from the market"), a webstore scope that cannot choose its content language is a parity defect written into a literal array. The same class of literal is what makes SchemaStatus.tsx:18 call WooCommerce a marketplace (WOO-4) and what left WOOCOMMERCE inside the delist allow-list (WOO-2) — one concept spelled out four times, drifting differently each time.

##### Proposed fix
Define 'is this a single-store, GLOBAL-market webstore?' exactly once and let every surface read it. Export `GLOBAL_CHANNELS` / `isStoreChannel(channel)` from _studio/scopes.ts (it already owns CHANNEL_LABELS and CHANNEL_ORDER, scopes.ts:25-69), seeded from the same list the server keeps at sheet-columns.service.ts:907, and replace all four literals: StudioBar.tsx:35 (`isStoreChannel(scope)` — keeps the DS `Listbox size="sm" width="auto"` exactly as-is, no new component), SchemaStatus.tsx:18, and both contracts.tsx:672/675 narrowing tests. Then give the store scopes their locale list the way Shopify already gets it: WooCommerce exposes store languages via the WPML/Polylang REST surfaces, so the same `registerShopifyLocales` shape (contracts.tsx:640-643) generalises to `registerStoreLocales(accountId, locales)` with no change to the scope bar's rendering at all.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/StudioBar.tsx:35
- apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-columns.service.ts:907
- apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-columns.service.ts:955-960
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:670-676
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/SchemaStatus.tsx:18
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/scopes.ts:69

##### Verifier
The code observations are accurate. StudioBar.tsx:36 gates the Content-language Listbox on `['SHOPIFY', 'ETSY'].includes(scope)` (the finding cites :35 — one-line slip, content exact); sheet-columns.service.ts:907 declares `const GLOBAL_CHANNELS: SheetChannel[] = ['SHOPIFY', 'WOOCOMMERCE', 'ETSY']` and :958 labels coordinates '· GLOBAL' from it; contracts.tsx:672 narrows `options.locales` on `['AMAZON', 'EBAY'].includes(scope)` and :675 validates `localeParam` against supportedLanguages on the same literal. So the same 'which channels are webstores' concept is spelled out in at least four places with three different memberships. What drops this to low: the defect is wholly contingent on a scope that cannot be selected (WOO-3, verified), so no operator can meet it; and the class it belongs to — 'Shopify/Etsy/Woo content layer: no per-channel write route exists; scope chips are offered and explain themselves. Fixture-vs-defer' — is an explicitly open Owner-queue item (docs/pes-claims.md:13330-13331, and hub ruling #315 at :14775-14792), so the content-language surface for store channels is not an unnoticed parity defect but part of a decision the Owner has not yet taken. The D11/§14.5 framing is also strained: master and channel scopes already differ here by design (Amazon and eBay get no picker either — their locale derives from the market, contracts.tsx:670-675), so a missing picker on a market-less store scope is a consequence of that rule, not a violation of it.
Exporting one isStoreChannel() from scopes.ts is the right consolidation and is genuinely low-risk for StudioBar.tsx:36 and SchemaStatus.tsx:17. The contracts.tsx:672/675 half is NOT the same concept and should not be folded in: those two literals answer 'does this channel's locale list come from the marketplace row?', which is the complement of store-ness only by accident today — replacing `['AMAZON','EBAY'].includes(scope)` with `!isStoreChannel(scope)` silently changes behaviour for MASTER and for any future non-store channel, and :675 is a validation gate, so a widened predicate can start rejecting locales that are currently accepted. Keep the two definitions separate and name each after what it decides. The WPML/Polylang claim is asserted, not evidenced anywhere in this repo, and should be marked as unverified research rather than a design premise.

## What a takedown touches
Stock, ads, compliance, accountability, and what happens when a channel says no.

### Stock and fulfilment6

[critical]refutedALLcorrectness risk

#### The master sheet's always-visible Stock cell fires a real multi-channel quantity push with no confirmation and only a client-side undo

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has GALE-JACKET live on Amazon IT, Amazon DE and eBay UK. They open the studio master sheet to fix a typo in the brand column. The default view already shows the Stock cell (it is in the COMMERCE_SPINE, on screen without any Customise click). They mis-key while arrowing across the row and commit 5 into Stock where the warehouse holds 500. They see the mistake instantly and press Ctrl+Z; the cell returns to 500 on screen.

##### What happens today
The first commit already went out. `totalStock` is registered `editable: true` (field-registry.service.ts:106) in the `master:inventory` group (sheet-columns.service.ts:302) and sits in the master sheet's always-on commerce spine (views.ts:172), so it renders as an ordinary number cell with no confirmation, no preflight and no danger styling. The commit posts to `PATCH /api/products/bulk` (masterWrite.ts:123-133). The bulk engine treats `totalStock` as a master-data field and routes it post-commit to `applyStockMovement` with the delta (bulk-edit.service.ts:1833-1846, 2390-2412), which calls `cascadeQuantityToListings` (stock-movement.service.ts:519). That rewrites `ChannelListing.quantity` on every following listing and creates a `QUANTITY_UPDATE` OutboundSyncQueue row per listing for AMAZON|EBAY|SHOPIFY|WOOCOMMERCE (stock-movement.service.ts:807-845), held only `DEFAULT_HOLD_MS = 30 * 1000` (stock-movement.service.ts:162). AG's undo is `undoRedoCellEditing` with a 200-step limit (GridSheet.tsx:109-110) — a client-side cell-value undo that issues no compensating write. Within 30 seconds three marketplaces are told the jacket has 5 units. The reverse keystroke (500 typed where 5 exists) is the oversell direction and behaves identically.

##### Proposed fix
Make Stock a parameterised verb, not a bare cell. Register it in the DS grid action registry as a `GridAction` with `scope: row`, `danger: true` and a real `preflight()` returning an `ActionImpact` (registry.ts:78-119, 191-197) rendered by `useActionConfirm`: `consequences` itemising the per-coordinate pushes the cascade will produce (Amazon·IT 500 -> 5, Amazon·DE 500 -> 5, eBay·UK 500 -> 5 — collapsing the Amazon EU rows to one line, since they are one merchant number), `sideEffects` naming the 30s hold window as the only recall opportunity, and `level: 'type-to-confirm'` with the real SKU as the phrase when the delta crosses a configurable magnitude (e.g. |delta| >= 50% of current, or the new value would leave a live listing over-committed). Server side: add `GET /api/products/:id/stock-impact?newTotal=N` returning `{ perListing: [{channel, marketplace, aliasKey, from, to, pooled}], reservedHeld, fbaExcluded }` computed by the SAME `resolveIntendedQuantity` core the cascade uses, so the confirmation is the cascade's own prediction and not a second implementation. Until that exists, the minimum honest fix is to set `editable: false` on `totalStock` in the studio sheet and route stock edits to /fulfillment/stock, which is where the ledger UI lives.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/pim/field-registry.service.ts:106
- apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-columns.service.ts:302
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/views.ts:172
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/masterWrite.ts:123
- apps/api/src/services/products/bulk-edit.service.ts:1833
- apps/api/src/services/products/bulk-edit.service.ts:2399
- apps/api/src/services/stock-movement.service.ts:519
- apps/api/src/services/stock-movement.service.ts:807
- apps/api/src/services/stock-movement.service.ts:162
- apps/web/src/design-system/grid/hosts/GridSheet.tsx:109

##### Verifier
The finding's plumbing is real, but its two decisive claims — the ones that make it "critical" — are false against the code.

VERIFIED AS CITED (the harmless half):
- `totalStock` is `editable: true` in the shared field registry (apps/api/src/services/pim/field-registry.service.ts:106), emitted to the wire as editable (apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-columns.service.ts:501, writeField=field.id at :483) and grouped `master:inventory` (sheet-columns.service.ts:303).
- Visible by default — in fact more so than the finding says: the studio builds EVERY server column (master/columns.tsx:1-14) and `useSheetColumns` lands on `{ kind: 'all' }` (useSheetColumns.ts:88, :202). The cited views.ts:172 `COMMERCE_SPINE` only feeds the Essentials preset, which views.ts:293 says is "offered nowhere" — so that particular citation is the wrong reason for a conclusion that happens to hold.
- Editability has no stock-specific veto (master/columnRules.ts:33-40 `cellIsEditable` = col.editable && columnApplies && cell.editable !== false).
- The write does reach the cascade: masterWrite posts PATCH /api/products/bulk (masterWrite.ts:111-133) → `isMasterDataField('totalStock')` (bulk-edit.service.ts:1877-1879, 2025-2026) → `applyStockMovement({reason:'MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT'})` (bulk-edit.service.ts:2435-2441) → `cascadeQuantityToListings` (stock-movement.service.ts:519) → per-listing quantity rewrite + QUANTITY_UPDATE rows held `DEFAULT_HOLD_MS = 30s` (stock-movement.service.ts:162, 762-763, 807-845). No confirmation, no danger styling anywhere in the studio (searched the studio tree with /usr/bin/grep for stock+confirm/warn/danger/impact/preflight — nothing).

REFUTED (the half the severity rests on):
1. "AG's undo … a client-side cell-value undo that issues no compensating write" is FALSE. The master sheet routes undo through the same writer: MasterSheet.tsx:1191 `onCellValueChanged`, with the explicit contract at :1205-1208 ("Undo needs no code of its own: AG fires this event for 'undo' and 'redo', so an undone cell travels the same writer"), and the gate only refuses `source: 'data'` / self-inflicted / unchanged (design-system/grid/editors/writeGate.ts:31, 104-110; the deny-list rationale is in its header, and writeGate.vitest.test.ts:17 asserts 'undo' writes). Ctrl+Z therefore issues a real PATCH restoring 500 → a second `applyStockMovement` with delta +495.
2. "Within 30 seconds three marketplaces are told the jacket has 5 units" is FALSE for the finding's own scenario. Before inserting the fresh rows, the second cascade calls `coalescePendingQuantityRows(tx, replacedListingIds)` (stock-movement.service.ts:869-874), which flips every still-PENDING QUANTITY_UPDATE row for those listings to CANCELLED (apps/api/src/services/sync-coalesce.ts:24-33) in the same transaction. The worker then re-reads the DB row and skips it — apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:104-121, whose comment names this exact case: "If user hit 'Undo' during grace period, syncStatus will be CANCELLED". The 30s hold is the recall mechanism the finding treats as the danger; the undo is precisely what consumes it.

What survives is much weaker than claimed: an UNNOTICED mis-key (nobody presses undo within 30s) does push, exactly as any editable master-data field does, on a path with a designed grace window, coalescing and a working undo. That is a UX hardening opportunity (no danger affordance / no impact preview on a cell whose blast radius is multi-channel), not a critical correctness defect, and it is not what the finding says. Per the lens, the finding as written cannot be positively confirmed and its central mechanism claim is contradicted by code I read.
The proposed "minimum honest fix" — set `editable: false` on `totalStock` and route stock edits to /fulfillment/stock — is actively harmful and mis-scoped. (a) It is not studio-scoped: field-registry.service.ts:106 feeds `getSheetColumns`, which serves BOTH /api/products/sheet (legacy sheet, apps/web/src/app/products/_sheet/useMasterSheet.ts:62) and the studio route (apps/api/src/routes/product-studio.routes.ts:25), so it locks stock editing on a surface nobody audited, and BulkSetControl.tsx:45 filters on `c.editable` so the bulk-set control silently loses the field too. (b) It removes an edit path that already has the recall the finding says is missing (30s hold + `coalescePendingQuantityRows` + worker CANCELLED check), trading a real capability for no measured gain. (c) The proposed `GET /api/products/:id/stock-impact` is worth having, but the finding's own premise for it ("the confirmation is the cascade's own prediction") is undercut by the fact that the cascade's resolution is per-listing and includes FOLLOW/UNCOUNTED/PAUSED branches (stock-movement.service.ts:795-812) — any preview must reproduce those three states or it will confidently predict pushes that the guard skips. If anything is done here, the honest version is a danger affordance + impact preview on the cell (and possibly lengthening the hold for MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT), not disabling the field.

[critical]refutedALLdata integrity risk

#### Drawer restore writes Product.totalStock directly, bypassing the stock ledger and the cascade, while its confirmation claims the write reaches every channel

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator notices a bad AI rewrite of the GALE-JACKET description made at 14:02. They open the studio record drawer, switch to Restore, pick the 13:00 restore point and tick the fields to put back. The checklist also offers `totalStock` (the stock was adjusted at 13:40 by a goods-in), so they leave everything ticked and confirm the dialog, which tells them the restore "affects every channel that inherits these fields".

##### What happens today
`totalStock` is in `RESTORABLE_FIELDS` in the drawer (useRecordState.ts:107-113) and in the server's `RESTORABLE_MASTER_FIELDS` (restorable-fields.ts:20), so it is genuinely offered and genuinely written. But `POST /api/products/:id/restore` builds its changes with `cascade: false` (products.routes.ts:781) and then does a plain `prisma.product.update` on the whole `data` bag (products.routes.ts:830-836). It never calls `applyStockMovement`, never writes a `StockMovement` row, and never touches `StockLevel` — the exact opposite of the bulk PATCH path, which deliberately routes `totalStock` out of the transaction into `applyStockMovement` so the cascade fires (bulk-edit.service.ts:1833-1846, 2399). Two consequences. (1) `Product.totalStock` now disagrees with the StockLevel ledger, and the cascade derives its pushes from `StockLevel.available` over WAREHOUSE locations (stock-movement.service.ts:719-729), not from `totalStock`, so the restored number reaches no channel at all — the very next real stock movement recomputes and silently discards it. (2) The confirmation copy states "This writes the master record, so it affects every channel that inherits these fields — but it makes no marketplace call" (RestoreMode.tsx:131-134). For `totalStock` the first clause is false and the second is true, and the operator has no way to tell which half applies to which ticked field. They walk away believing stock was restored.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, both small. Server: in `POST /products/:id/restore`, split `totalStock` out of the direct `product.update` bag exactly as bulk-edit.service.ts:2390-2412 does and route it through `applyStockMovement({ reason: 'MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT', notes: 'restore to <at>' })` inside the same transaction, so a restored stock figure produces a real ledger movement and a real cascade — or, if the hub prefers stock to be non-restorable, remove `totalStock` and `lowStockThreshold` from `RESTORABLE_MASTER_FIELDS` (restorable-fields.ts:20) and let `notRestorableReason` (useRecordState.ts:116-130) show "Stock is restored on the fulfilment ledger, not here" — the drawer already renders a per-field reason rather than hiding the row. UI: the RestoreMode confirmation body must stop making one claim for a mixed set. Render the ticked fields in two DS groups inside the existing `DrawerConfirm` body — "Inherited by channels" and "Local only" — derived from the field's own routing, so the sentence is attached to the fields it is true of. Both halves land together (producer + consumer in one write).

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/drawer/useRecordState.ts:107
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/drawer/useRecordState.ts:112
- apps/api/src/services/pim/restorable-fields.ts:20
- apps/api/src/routes/products.routes.ts:779
- apps/api/src/routes/products.routes.ts:781
- apps/api/src/routes/products.routes.ts:830
- apps/api/src/services/products/bulk-edit.service.ts:1833
- apps/api/src/services/products/bulk-edit.service.ts:2399
- apps/api/src/services/stock-movement.service.ts:719
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/drawer/panes/RestoreMode.tsx:131

##### Verifier
The finding's load-bearing claim — that POST /api/products/:id/restore does "a plain prisma.product.update on the whole data bag (products.routes.ts:830-836)" and "never calls applyStockMovement, never writes a StockMovement row, never touches StockLevel" — is false in the working tree I read. products.routes.ts:835 calls `applyProductBulkEdits({ changes, expectedVersion, marketplaceContexts }, { formulaCascade: false, ... })`, i.e. the very bulk PATCH engine the finding holds up as the correct contrast. The `data` bag built at ~:794 is used only for `Object.keys(data)` in the emitted event and the response payload; it is never handed to Prisma. `/usr/bin/grep -n "prisma.product.update" apps/api/src/routes/products.routes.ts` returns exactly one hit, line 1783, which sits in an unrelated handler well below the restore route's close at ~:862 (restore spans ~:739-862). Inside the engine, `totalStock` is explicitly excluded from the in-transaction scalar update and routed post-commit: bulk-edit.service.ts:1878-1879 defines `isMasterDataField = f === 'basePrice' || f === 'totalStock'`; :2024-2026 collects it into `stockDeltas` and `continue`s past the direct write; :2414-2450 computes the delta against current `Product.totalStock` and calls `applyStockMovement({ productId, change: delta, reason: 'MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT', notes: 'bulk grid edit', tx: activeDatabaseTransaction() })`. So a real StockMovement row is written, StockLevel moves, and stock-movement.service.ts:719-729 (which I opened and which does read `StockLevel.available` over WAREHOUSE rows, inside the caller's tx) runs the channel cascade. Consequence (1) — "Product.totalStock disagrees with the ledger and the restored number reaches no channel" — therefore does not occur. Consequence (2) collapses with it: the RestoreMode.tsx:131-134 copy ("This writes the master record, so it affects every channel that inherits these fields — but it makes no marketplace call") is verbatim as quoted, but under the actual code path its first clause is TRUE for totalStock, because applyStockMovement fans out to the channels; so there is no mixed-truth sentence to split. The proposed server fix is a no-op: it asks the restore route to "split totalStock out of the direct product.update bag exactly as bulk-edit.service.ts:2390-2412 does and route it through applyStockMovement" — which is precisely what the route already achieves by delegating to applyProductBulkEdits at products.routes.ts:835. The alternative arm (remove totalStock from RESTORABLE_MASTER_FIELDS) would remove a capability that currently works correctly. The UI half (split the confirmation into "Inherited by channels" / "Local only" groups) rests on the same false premise for totalStock; if there is a genuine grouping case it would have to be re-derived from fields that truly do not cascade, which this finding did not establish.
