#### Delete child enumerates the listings it destroys but never the stock ledger, open reservations or order links it also destroys

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is tidying the GALE-JACKET family. The XXS child was never listed anywhere (a sizing experiment), but the warehouse holds 40 units of it, two of which are held by a PENDING_ORDER reservation against an eBay order that shipped this morning but has not yet been marked SHIPPED. They select the XXS row in the master sheet, choose Delete child…, read the confirmation and type through it.

##### What happens today
The confirmation is honest about exactly one dimension. `familyActions.ts:461-476` lists as consequences "<SKU> is deleted permanently — there is no undo and no trash" and "It is not listed on any channel", and as side effects the channel-listing cascade and the removal from the parent's listing payload. Nothing about inventory. The preflight calls `ops.listings(row.id)` only (familyActions.ts:442) — it reads listings and nothing else. `run` calls `DELETE /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children/:childId`, which after `assertCanDeleteRelationshipProduct` does a hard `tx.product.delete` (catalog.routes.ts:1837). That guard checks marketplace listings only — `channelListing.findFirst` on `externalListingId`/`isPublished` (product-relationship.service.ts:123-129) — and has no stock, reservation or order clause. The FK cascade then removes every `StockLevel` row for the product (schema.prisma:9124) and, through them, every `StockReservation` (schema.prisma:9168) — including the live PENDING_ORDER hold and its `reserved`/`available` bookkeeping (stock-level.service.ts:103-113). Lot, SerialNumber and the FIFO receipt layers go with them. `OrderItem.productId` is `onDelete: SetNull` (schema.prisma:5874), so the eBay order survives but silently loses its product link, and `consumeReservation` (stock-level.service.ts:227-281) has nothing left to consume when the order is finally marked shipped. Forty counted units and a live order line vanish from the ledger under a dialog whose only inventory-adjacent sentence is "It is not listed on any channel".

##### Proposed fix
Extend the existing preflight rather than adding a second dialog — the verb already has the right shape. Add `GET /api/products/:id/delete-impact` returning `{ stock: [{ locationCode, type, quantity, reserved }], reservations: [{ reason, quantity, orderId, expiresAt }], openOrderLines: [{ orderId, channel, quantity, status }], lots, serials }`, and have `familyActions.ts` preflight fetch it beside `ops.listings`. Feed it into the `ActionImpact` the DS already renders: counted units and held units as itemised `consequences` (never a bare count — ActionConfirm itemises), the order lines as `findings` with `severity: 'error'`, and raise `level` to `'type-to-confirm'` with the child's real SKU as the phrase whenever any HARD reservation or non-terminal order line exists (registry.ts:78-119, 253-273 already encode that escalation). Server side, mirror the refusal the way listings are already mirrored: extend `assertCanDeleteRelationshipProduct` (product-relationship.service.ts:123-129) with an un-released `StockReservation` clause so the transaction refuses what the preflight refuses — the same two-sided guard the listing check already has.

#### The FBA stranded-units warning exists in the Amazon flat-file preflight and nowhere in the studio, and no endpoint exposes the fact the studio would need to raise it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket live on Amazon IT with 60 units sitting in Amazon's Italian fulfilment centre. They want it off IT for the season. On the /products Amazon flat-file page, setting record_action = delete produces a preflight warning telling them the units will be stranded against the SKU's FNSKU and that they must raise a removal order or relabel first. They now do the same job from the studio, where the Owner wants this lifecycle verb to live.

##### What happens today
The knowledge is real and it is one surface deep. `amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:761-764` collects the affected SKUs via `flatFileService.findFbaDeleteRows(rows)` and `:805-809` emits the warning verbatim: "FBA inventory present — deleting this listing will NOT remove the units from Amazon's warehouse; they stay bound to this SKU's FNSKU and become unfulfillable. In Seller Central, create a removal order or sell through first; if relisting under a new SKU, relabel the units to the new FNSKU." `findFbaDeleteRows` derives the fact from `Product.fulfillmentMethod === 'FBA'` or a positive `StockLevel` at location code `AMAZON-EU-FBA` (flat-file.service.ts:2615-2646). None of that is reachable from the studio: it is a service method called by one route handler, with no product-scoped endpoint. In the studio tree, `/usr/bin/grep -rniE "fba|stranded|fnsku|unfulfillable|removal order"` returns one substantive hit — the label map `AFN: 'Fulfilled by Amazon (FBA)', FBA: 'Fulfilled by Amazon (FBA)'` at referenceLabels.ts:46 (positive control: 41 files in that tree contain `fetch(`). The channel sheet moreover synthesises no stock or quantity column at all, by an explicit design decision recorded at ChannelSheet.tsx:1116-1124, and carries no fulfilment-method column — so on the Amazon·IT scope there is nothing on screen that tells the operator this SKU is FBA, let alone that 60 units back it. The same gap sits under the sibling verb: `removeAmazonListing` performs no FBA check whatsoever (`/usr/bin/grep -n "stockLevel|StockLevel|fba|FBA" apps/api/src/services/amazon/amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts` returns rc=1, against a positive control of 4 `prisma.` hits in the same file).

##### Proposed fix
Promote the fact out of the flat-file route before any studio lifecycle verb ships. Add `GET /api/products/:id/fulfilment-posture?channel=AMAZON&marketplace=IT` returning `{ fulfillmentMethod, fbaUnits, fbaLocationCode, fbmAvailable, reservedHeld, pooledWith: ['DE','FR','ES'] }`, implemented by lifting `findFbaDeleteRows`' derivation (flat-file.service.ts:2626-2643) into a shared `fba-posture` helper so there is one definition, not a second copy. Consume it in two places: (a) a persistent, non-destructive DS `Banner` with `tone="warning"` in the channel scope's `StudioTabHost` region whenever `fbaUnits > 0`, reading "Fulfilled by Amazon — 60 units in AMAZON-EU-FBA. Ending or deleting this listing does not remove them"; (b) the `preflight()` of whatever delist/delete verb the studio grows, as an `ActionImpact` `sideEffects` entry carrying the Seller Central instruction verbatim, with `level: 'type-to-confirm'` and the SKU as the phrase when `fbaUnits > 0`. The DS pieces already exist (components/Banner, grid/actions/registry.ts:78-119); only the endpoint is new.

[critical]verifiedAMAZONcorrectness risk

#### Per-market Amazon removal commits the local delete before the SP-API call and swallows its failure, leaving a live offer with no row to cascade stock to

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator wants the jacket off Amazon IT for the season, keeping DE and keeping the ability to put IT back. The only implementation of that today is the Amazon flat-file remove path. The SP-API delete fails — a throttle, an expired token, a cold start. Amazon IT keeps showing the offer. The jacket keeps selling on eBay UK and Amazon DE and the warehouse pool drains to zero.

##### What happens today
`removeAmazonListing` deletes the local rows first and asks Amazon afterwards. `amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:59-65` runs `tx.channelListing.deleteMany({ productId in ids, channel: 'AMAZON', marketplace })` and commits, with the comment "Product intentionally untouched"; only then, at `:67-83`, does it loop the captured `externalListingId`s into `dispatchChannelDelist` with a synthetic `queueId` (`amz-rm-...`), no queue row, and a bare `catch { /* best-effort; never blocks the committed removal */ }` at `:82`. So a failed delete is invisible: no OutboundSyncQueue row, no retry, no dead letter, nothing in /sync-logs. The consequence is an inventory one. With the AMAZON·IT `ChannelListing` row gone, `cascadeQuantityToListings` — which selects purely `where: { productId }` (stock-movement.service.ts:695-696) — has no row for IT and will never enqueue another `QUANTITY_UPDATE` for that coordinate (the enqueue is per surviving listing, stock-movement.service.ts:807-845). The live Amazon IT offer therefore freezes at whatever quantity it last received, forever, while the merchant pool is drained by every other channel. The oversell watchdog cannot see it either: `computeCommitments` reads `prisma.channelListing.findMany({ where: { productId } })` (inventory-oversell-watchdog.service.ts:178-195) and filters `listingStatus === 'ACTIVE'` (`:94`) — a deleted row is not a non-ACTIVE row, it is no row, so the commitment is not merely excluded, it is unknown. The deleteMany is additionally unscoped by `channelConnectionId` and `aliasKey`, so on a multi-account or multi-alias coordinate it removes every account's row for that market in one shot.

##### Proposed fix
Do not give the studio a verb that wraps this service. Invert the order and make the remote step durable: enqueue an `OutboundSyncQueue` row with `syncType: 'DELETE_LISTING'` inside the transaction (the worker's short-circuit at bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141 already routes it to `dispatchChannelDelist` with retries and dead-lettering), set the local row to `{ listingStatus: 'ENDED', isPublished: false, offerActive: false, quantity: 0 }` rather than deleting it, and only reap the row — if ever — after the queue row reports SUCCESS. Keeping the row is what makes the Owner's "put IT back next season" possible at all: it preserves `externalListingId`, `overrideData`, `flatFileSnapshot` and the coordinate the cascade needs, and it is the one shape that is already relistable (the flat-file import's own end path does exactly this at flat-file/import/apply.ts:588). For the studio surface, express it as a `GridAction` with `scope: row`, `danger: true`, a `preflight()` that shows the FBA posture from INV-4 plus the per-market quantity that will be zeroed, and `ConfirmLevel: 'type-to-confirm'` on the SKU; render the outcome with the DS `Banner` plus the existing sync-status column rather than a fire-and-forget toast, so a failed delist is visible instead of swallowed.

The mechanism is confirmed line-by-line, and it is live, not dead code — but the finding's headline inventory consequence is overstated in its own scenario.

UI: apps/web/src/app/products/amazon-flat-file/AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1880-1900 (`removeFromAmazon`) → :1903-1912 (`deleteSelected`, a native `confirm()`) → Button at :4185. Worse than the finding states: the client computes success purely from `channelListingsRemoved > 0` (:1893) and ignores the `delisted` flag entirely, then toasts "Removed N listings from Amazon {mp} — product and stock kept." (:1896). A failed SP-API delete is reported to the operator as a success.

The deleteMany filters only productId/channel/marketplace, so it removes every account's and every alias's row for that market at once — and is not workspace-scoped either.

Cited cascade/watchdog lines say what is claimed: stock-movement.service.ts:695-696 (`findMany({ where: { productId } })`, no listingStatus filter), :807-845 (per-surviving-listing update + QUANTITY_UPDATE enqueue); inventory-oversell-watchdog.service.ts:178-188 (`channelListing.findMany({ where:{ productId } })`), :90-100 (`listingStatus === 'ACTIVE'` filter). A deleted row is indeed absent, not merely non-ACTIVE.
6. Nothing recreates the row automatically. The only AMAZON ChannelListing re-creators are listing-reconciliation.service.ts:503 (operator confirmation of a recon row; run only via reconciliation.routes.ts:55/59) and inbound-sync.service.ts:56 (legacy phase-10 `as any`, keyed on a `productId_channel_region` unique that is not the current compound key, reachable only via inbound.routes.ts:8). Neither is a cron.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG — the stated scenario defeats its own mechanism. The scenario is "off Amazon IT, keeping DE". Enqueuing a durable DELETE_LISTING OutboundSyncQueue row inside the transaction is correct — bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158 already routes that syncType to dispatchChannelDelist and writes the outcome via applyDelistResultToQueue (channel-delist.service.ts:313-343), giving retries, FAILED/isDead and /sync-logs visibility. Ending rather than deleting the row is also right and matches flat-file/import/apply.ts:588-591. BUT the proposed end-state includes `quantity: 0`: for AMAZON that is the exact trap in reference_amazon_shared_eu_quantity (proved 2026-07-26 — zeroing DE zeroed IT), so if any push path can pick that row up it zeroes every EU marketplace for the SKU. #### "Pause offer" promises buyers stop seeing the offer, but offerActive is read by nothing on eBay, Shopify or WooCommerce and by Amazon only at the next flat-file submit

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the jacket live on eBay UK and wants to stop selling it for two weeks without ending the listing and losing its watchers and item history. On the studio eBay·UK channel sheet they select the row, choose the offer verb, and read the confirmation: "Buyers stop seeing this offer on this channel and market. The listing itself is not ended and its reviews and identifiers are untouched." They confirm and stop watching the product.

##### What happens today
Two layers of untruth, and the second survives even after the first is lifted. (1) Today the verb refuses outright on any live alias — `channelActions.ts:249-250` puts the refusal into the impact's `unavailable` and `:259-262` repeats it in `run`, so for a genuinely live eBay listing nothing happens at all. (2) If that wave-1 refusal is lifted, the verb writes only `ChannelListing.offerActive` via `PATCH /products/:id/offer-availability` (marketplaces.routes.ts:295-325), and `offerActive` has almost no consumer on the outbound side. Sweeping `apps/api/src` for `offerActive` outside tests returns: flat-file writers setting it, `control-tower.routes.ts:144` reading it for display, `content-auto-publish.service.ts:39` filtering on it, `listing-activation-sync.service.ts` firing when it flips TRUE (marketplaces.routes.ts:326-327), and exactly one outbound consumer — `flat-file.service.ts:3413-3419`, which injects `skip_offer` into an Amazon payload, and only when an Amazon flat-file export/submit is next run. Nothing in the eBay, Shopify or WooCommerce push paths reads it; the cascade does not read it either (its listing select takes `syncPaused` and `offerClosedAt`, not `offerActive` — stock-movement.service.ts:696-712), so the paused listing keeps receiving `QUANTITY_UPDATE` pushes and keeps advertising stock. On eBay UK the sentence "Buyers stop seeing this offer" describes something that never happens, and the operator's units stay sellable for two weeks. The confirmation's second line, "Other markets are unaffected", is true — Amazon's `skip_offer` is stamped per `marketplace_id` — so the defect is specifically the buyer-visibility claim, not the scoping claim.

##### Proposed fix
Make the copy match the mechanism per channel, then make the mechanism exist. Short term, derive the `ActionImpact.consequences` from the channel rather than hardcoding one sentence: on AMAZON, "Amazon suppresses the buy box for this market at the next listing push — until then the offer stays visible"; on EBAY/SHOPIFY/WOOCOMMERCE, mark the verb `disabled('Pausing an offer is not implemented for eBay yet — use quantity 0 or end the listing')` via the registry's `available()` (registry.ts:167-198), which is the DS-sanctioned way to withhold a verb with its reason attached, instead of shipping a promise the backend cannot keep. Longer term, give `offerActive=false` a real outbound consumer per channel and enqueue it from the route: eBay `ReviseFixedPriceItem` with quantity 0 (reversible, keeps the ItemID, watchers and history — exactly the operator's intent), Shopify `updateProduct(status:'draft')` (the method already exists, shopify.service.ts:383), Amazon the existing `skip_offer` but pushed immediately as an `OFFER_SYNC` queue row rather than waiting for a flat-file run. Also add `offerActive` to the cascade's listing select and to `resolveIntendedQuantity`'s PAUSED branch, so a paused offer stops consuming the pool the moment it is paused.

#### A price push RE-CREATES a closed Amazon market offer — the one guard that exists is on the other code path

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator sells the GALE jacket on Amazon IT and Amazon DE. Cross-border FBM shipping to DE is unprofitable this season, so they use the per-market close (SCT.6) to delete the DE purchasable_offer: the ASIN, reviews, content and the shared EU quantity stay, and DE goes Inactive. A week later the pricing engine recomputes the jacket's price (FX move, competitor pull, a master-price cascade) and someone — or a script — calls POST /api/pricing/push for sku=GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-XL, channel=AMAZON, marketplace=DE. The jacket goes back on sale in Germany.

##### What happens today
pricing-outbound.service.ts:51 `pushPriceUpdate` loads the newest PricingSnapshot for (sku, channel, marketplace) and, for AMAZON, calls `pushAmazonPrice` (:100). That function reads the ChannelListing at :138-147 selecting ONLY `{ id, platformAttributes }` — it never looks at `offerClosedAt`, `syncPaused`, `listingStatus` or `isPublished` — and then calls `amazonSpApiClient.patchListingPrice` (:167). That client builds `op: 'replace'` on `/attributes/purchasable_offer` (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:687-699) — the exact attribute instance the close deleted with `op: 'delete'` (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:165-172). A `replace` on an absent attribute creates it, so the offer is restored and the market reopens. The system already knows this is forbidden: the OTHER dispatch path, OutboundSyncService.syncToAmazon, refuses it explicitly — outbound-sync.service.ts:903-906, `"SCT.6 — a CLOSED market offer receives NO pushes of any kind. Reopen is the only way back; a stray queue row must never resurrect the offer."` pricing-outbound does not go through OutboundSyncService and inherits none of it. On success it writes a ChannelListingOverride and stamps `syncStatus: 'IN_SYNC'` (:183-196), so the local record then reads healthy while `offerClosedAt` is still set — the row now claims to be both closed and in sync.

##### Proposed fix
Two parts. (a) API: lift the SCT.6/pause refusal out of `OutboundSyncService.syncToAmazon` into one shared `assertPushable(channelListingId)` helper that returns a discriminated refusal (`market-offer-closed | sync-paused | listing-ended | not-published`) and call it from `pushAmazonPrice`/`pushEbayPrice` before any client call — one concept defined once, per the DS README rule. Because pricing-outbound resolves the listing with `findFirst` on (channel, marketplace, sku) and no connection/alias filter (:138-147), make the helper take the resolved row and refuse when it resolved more than one. (b) UI: the refusal must be readable where the operator sets prices. In the studio channel sheet, a price cell on a row whose listing carries `offerClosedAt` should render the DS `Pill` tone="warning" state "Market closed" in the identity band and make the cell's editor refuse with the DS cell-refusal reason (the same `available() -> disabled(reason)` shape as `GridAction` in design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts:167-198), so D14's "every attribute writable … or the cell says why not" is honoured rather than silently writing a price that will reopen a market.

#### Hard-deleting a product orphans its Amazon ads ENABLED, and the guard built to catch exactly this then reports the campaign "ok"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator bins the discontinued GALE jacket and runs the /products bulk hard delete with channelAction 'delete', so the Amazon SP-API listing is deleted and the Product row goes. Two Sponsored Products campaigns were advertising its ASIN B0BMSH19GY at ~40 EUR/day. The operator believes the product is gone. The campaigns keep serving and keep spending, and the nightly retail guard — the feature whose whole premise is "don't advertise what you can't sell" — now reports both campaigns as healthy.

##### What happens today
`AdProductAd.productId` is `onDelete: SetNull` (schema.prisma:3318-3319), so deleting the Product nulls the link and leaves the ad row intact — `asin`, `sku`, `externalAdId`, accumulated `spendCents`, and `status CampaignStatus @default(ENABLED)` (schema.prisma:3320-3326). No teardown runs: `/usr/bin/grep -in "campaign|productad|advertis"` over apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts and apps/api/src/routes/catalog.routes.ts (the two delete routes) returns nothing, against controls of 67 and 25 `prisma` hits in the same files; the only writer of `adProductAd.status` anywhere in apps/api/src is the explicit operator mutation at ads-mutation.service.ts:963. Worse, the orphaning disarms the detector: `analyzeRetailReadiness` collects products with `if (pa.productId && !seen.has(pa.productId))` (ads-retail-readiness.service.ts:74-75), so null-productId ads are skipped entirely; if they were the campaign's only ads, `productsN === 0` and the verdict is hard-coded `'ok'` with `'No locally-linked products to check.'` (:82-83). And when a product id is present but the row is missing, `readiness()` fails OPEN — `if (!p) return { … inStock: true … }` (:61-62) — an unknown product is counted as in stock. `applyRetailGuard` only acts on `verdict === 'pause'` (:104-108), so nothing is floored.

##### Proposed fix
API: the delete/delist cascade must have an ads leg. Before the Product delete, resolve `AdProductAd` rows by `productId` OR `asin` and (i) record them on the delete's impact so the operator sees them BEFORE confirming, and (ii) after the channel delist succeeds, route them through the existing gated write path — `suppressCampaignBids` (the codebase's NO-PAUSE policy, ads-retail-readiness.service.ts:106) rather than a raw status flip. Separately fix the two fail-open branches: `readiness()` must return a fourth signal `productMissing` instead of `inStock: true`, and the collect loop must count `productId === null` ads as unsellable rather than skipping them. UI: this is the shape the DS grid action registry exists for — the delete verb's `preflight()` should return an `ActionImpact` whose consequences are ITEMISED, not counted ("2 campaigns · 39.80 EUR/day will keep spending on B0BMSH19GY"), rendered by `useActionConfirm` at `ConfirmLevel: 'type-to-confirm'` with the real SKU as the phrase (design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts:69,167-198,215).

The IT-only Sponsored Products campaign keeps running. Every night the retail guard checks it and says the advertised product is in stock, holds the Buy Box and is competitively priced — because it is reading DE.

##### What happens today
`readiness(productId, marketplace)` in ads-retail-readiness.service.ts:59-67 resolves the listing as `p.channelListings.find(x => x.channel === 'AMAZON' && (!marketplace || x.marketplace === marketplace)) ?? p.channelListings.find(x => x.channel === 'AMAZON')` (:63) — when the campaign's own market has no row, or the row is ENDED, it takes ANY Amazon listing, i.e. DE's price and DE's competitor price. Buy Box does the same: `p.buyBoxHistory.find(… marketplace …) ?? p.buyBoxHistory[0]` (:65). Stock is `p.stockLevels.reduce(...)` summed across every location with no market scoping (:62) — and on Amazon EU the quantity is shared anyway, so IT being ended changes nothing. Crucially, the selected listing's `listingStatus` is never read: `select: { marketplace, channel, price, lowestCompetitorPrice }` (:52) does not even fetch it, and `/usr/bin/grep` for `listingStatus|ENDED|delist` across apps/api/src/services/advertising/ returns only a keyword-tracker count (keyword-tracker.service.ts:569) and SQP ordering (sqp.service.ts:181-188) — no readiness or bidding consumer. So the verdict is `'ok'` / `'All advertised products sellable.'` (:81) for a market where nothing is for sale.

##### Proposed fix
API: delete both `??` fallbacks. A campaign's marketplace is a hard coordinate — if there is no ChannelListing for (product, AMAZON, campaign.marketplace), or the row is `listingStatus` ENDED / `isPublished: false` / `offerClosedAt` non-null, the correct `ProductReadiness` is a new `listed: false` flag, and `listed === false` for every advertised product must yield verdict `'pause'` with the reason naming the market ("not listed on IT — every click is wasted"), never `'ok'`. Add `listingStatus`, `isPublished`, `offerClosedAt` to the select at :52. The existing `ads-eligibility.service.ts` doctrine is the precedent to follow: unknown is neither eligible nor ineligible (:14-19) — a missing market row should read as a third state, not as health. UI: surface it on the studio's channel scope as a DS `Banner` tone="warning" above the sheet ("2 campaigns are still advertising this product on Amazon IT, where it is no longer listed") with a link-out to the ads console, since D9 forbids parity link-outs but this is a new coordinate, not an old surface.

- apps/api/src/services/advertising/ads-retail-readiness.service.ts:81

- apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3198-3204

#### eBay's end-listing path leaves isPublished true, so the only lifecycle guard in the sync worker lets price pushes through to a listing whose ItemID was erased

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator ends the GALE jacket on eBay IT from the eBay flat file. The offer is withdrawn at eBay, the ItemID is retired, and the local row reads ENDED. Three days later the pricing engine's snapshot for that SKU moves more than the 1% threshold and the always-on repricer enqueues a PRICE_UPDATE for the ended eBay row. Nothing stops it reaching eBay.

##### What happens today
The eBay end path writes `{ listingStatus: 'ENDED', offerActive: false, externalListingId: null }` (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1958-1960 for the parent, :1980-1982 for a child) and does NOT set `isPublished: false`. That matters because `isPublished` is the ONLY lifecycle gate in the dispatcher: bullmq-sync.worker.ts:177-190 skips a row when `!channelListing.isPublished` and checks nothing else — not `listingStatus`, not `offerActive`. Compare the Amazon flat-file end, which does set `isPublished: false` (amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3198-3204), and the importer's channel delete, which sets all three (flat-file/import/apply.ts:586-590). So eBay's ENDED rows are the one shape that stays dispatchable. Upstream, the repricer selects the row with `where: { productId, channel, marketplace }` and no status filter at all (repricer-scheduler.service.ts:135-148) and enqueues PRICE_UPDATE carrying `externalListingId: listing.externalListingId` — which the end path just set to null (:214). Downstream, `syncToEbay`'s pause guard is nested inside `if (payload.quantity !== undefined && product?.id)` (outbound-sync.service.ts:1134-1148), so a price-only row never reaches the `syncPaused` check either; there is no `listingStatus` check anywhere on that path.

##### Proposed fix
API, smallest correct change first: add `isPublished: false` to both eBay end writes so the existing worker guard actually covers them — that is one field, and it makes eBay consistent with the two other end paths. Then make the guard non-accidental: extend bullmq-sync.worker.ts:177 to refuse on `listingStatus === 'ENDED'` and on `offerClosedAt != null` as well as `!isPublished`, with distinct `errorMessage` values so /sync-logs says which. Move `syncToEbay`'s pause guard out of the quantity branch so it covers price-only rows. Finally, give the repricer a selection filter — `where: { …, isPublished: true, listingStatus: { notIn: ['ENDED'] }, offerClosedAt: null }` at repricer-scheduler.service.ts:135 — so ended rows are never counted as `skippedNoListing` noise but are simply not scanned.

- apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1979-1984

- apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3198-3204

- apps/api/src/services/repricer-scheduler.service.ts:135-155
- apps/api/src/services/repricer-scheduler.service.ts:188-215
- apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:1134-1148

##### Verifier
CONFIRMED at the code level, with two corrections to the framing.

What I confirmed by opening the files:
1. eBay end writes omit isPublished. apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1958-1961 (parent, `withdraw_by_inventory_item_group` → `data: { listingStatus: 'ENDED', offerActive: false, externalListingId: null }`) and :1981-1984 (child, offer DELETE → same three fields). No isPublished write anywhere in that file (`/usr/bin/grep -n "isPublished" apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts` → zero hits). The route is live and UI-reachable: POST `/ebay/flat-file/push` at :1493, called from apps/web/src/app/products/ebay-flat-file/EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:2328,2441.
2. isPublished stays true. packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1629 — `isPublished Boolean @default(true)`. Nothing on the eBay end path clears it, so the ENDED row is still `isPublished: true`.
3. isPublished is the only lifecycle gate in the dispatcher. apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:177-190 skips only on `!channelListing.isPublished`; the only other check is the OFFER_SYNC active-offers branch at :193-210, which does not apply to PRICE_UPDATE. `/usr/bin/grep -n "listingStatus|offerActive|isPublished|ENDED"` over that worker returns hits only at 177/181/187 — no listingStatus check exists anywhere in it.
4. The comparison paths are as claimed: Amazon flat-file end sets `isPublished: false` (apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3198-3204); the importer channel delete sets all three (apps/api/src/services/flat-file/import/apply.ts:586-590). `/usr/bin/grep -rn "listingStatus: 'ENDED'"` across apps/api/src returns exactly 5 writers — the two eBay ones are the only ones that leave isPublished alone (listings/recovery.service.ts:341 is the fifth; the eBay flat-file *delete* path removes ChannelListing rows outright, so it carries no dispatch risk).
5. eBay's dispatch-time guards are asymmetric, exactly as claimed. apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:1134 opens `if (payload.quantity !== undefined && product?.id) {` and the syncPaused check sits inside it at :1149, with the channel-policy pause at :1152-1156 — a price-only row reaches neither. The Amazon lane by contrast checks `syncPaused` unconditionally at :899 and `offerClosedAt` at :904. There is no offerClosedAt or listingStatus check on the eBay lane at all.
6. Producers do not filter lifecycle. repricer-scheduler.service.ts:135-148 selects `{ productId, channel, marketplace }` with no status filter and enqueues `externalListingId: listing.externalListingId` at :205.

Refutation attempts that FAILED to kill it:
- Opt-in belt exists but is default-off: outbound-sync.service.ts:645-655 skips on `offerActive === false` only when `NEXUS_RESPECT_OFFER_ACTIVE === '1'`. Default off by the comment's own words, so it does not save the default deployment.
- The "always-on repricer" framing is wrong, but it does not save the finding: repricer-scheduler.service.ts:74 (`liveMode = process.env.NEXUS_REPRICER_LIVE === '1'`) plus index.ts:1106-1112 (`NEXUS_ENABLE_PRICING_CRON === '1'` gates `startRepricerCron`) make it doubly default-off. However master-price.service.ts:200-203 selects cascade targets with `where: { productId }` and NO lifecycle filter, and enqueues PRICE_UPDATE at :263 — an unconditional, operator-driven producer that hits the identical gap every time someone edits the master price from the Studio. The defect therefore stands without the repricer.
- No alternative capability closes it: there is no second eBay "end" path that sets isPublished false, and the guard does not exist elsewhere on the eBay dispatch lane.

Corrections to the finding's stated harm (why it is mis-stated, not dead):
- A price push cannot relist. outbound-sync.service.ts:1487-1502 resolves the offer by SKU and PUTs pricingSummary; with no offer it returns a 404-classified EBAY_VALIDATION failure, not a republish. So the real harm is (a) a price write landing on a withdrawn parent offer, (b) paused/ended eBay rows bypassing operator intent on every master-price cascade, and (c) a sharper edge: that offer lookup at :1488 omits `marketplace_id` (unlike the quantity path at :1395 which includes it) and takes `offers[0]`, so a market whose offer was deleted by the child-end path can resolve ANOTHER market's live offer and overwrite its price.
- "Nothing stops it reaching eBay" is conditional on NEXUS_ENABLE_EBAY_PUBLISH / EBAY_PUBLISH_MODE=live (ebay-publish-gate.service.ts:40-46, default dry-run); I could not read prod env from here, so that arm is unverified.
Direction is right, details need work. (1) `isPublished: false` on the eBay end writes is the smallest change but it is NOT free — isPublished is read as a published/visible signal by many readers (product-read-cache.service.ts:129, list-products.service.ts:940, sync-control.routes.ts:636,713, listings-syndication.routes.ts:708,971); check the relist/republish path before flipping it, or the ended row becomes invisible to the very screen the operator would use to bring it back. (2) The worker guard should use `listingStatus: { notIn: ['ENDED','REMOVED'] }` — REMOVED is already the paired value elsewhere (outbound-sync.service.ts:1007, sync-control.routes.ts:636) — not ENDED alone. (3) `offerClosedAt` does not need inventing for the worker: the Amazon lane already enforces it at outbound-sync.service.ts:904; the correct move is hoisting eBay's syncPaused/policy/closed checks out of the `if (payload.quantity !== undefined …)` block at :1134 so they run for every payload shape, mirroring :899-911. (4) The repricer filter is fine but is not where the unconditional leak is — master-price.service.ts:200-203 cascades with `where: { productId }` and no lifecycle filter, and that fires on every Studio master-price edit regardless of env flags; fix that selection too or the scenario survives the repricer fix. (5) Independent of this finding, the price path's offer lookup at outbound-sync.service.ts:1488 omits `marketplace_id` and takes `offers[0]`, unlike the quantity path at :1395 — an ended market can resolve a sibling market's offer and get its price overwritten. That deserves its own fix and should not be folded into a lifecycle-guard change. (6) The parent-end updateMany at ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1958-1960 scopes by `product: { OR: [{id: pid},{parentId: pid}] }, channel: 'EBAY', region` — verify that region scoping is per-market before adding a field to it, since it already blanks externalListingId across the whole family.

#### Promotions and pricing snapshots are written to ended listings, and the price-history timeline records a promo that started on a listing nobody can buy

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A Black Friday retail event has a PERCENT_OFF action scoped to channel AMAZON, marketplace IT. The GALE jacket's IT listing was ended in October. When the event window opens, the scheduler writes a sale price onto the ended IT row, stamps it `promotion:<eventId>`, and records "promo … started" on the product's price timeline — which is what the operator reads in the studio to understand what happened to this product's price.

##### What happens today
`promotion-scheduler.service.ts:58-75` selects the listings to promote with only `{ channel?, marketplace?, product.productType? }` — no `listingStatus`, no `isPublished`, no `offerActive`, no `deletedAt`. Every matching row, ENDED included, gets `salePrice` written plus `lastOverrideAt` / `lastOverrideBy: 'promotion:<id>'` (:106-114), and `recordPriceChange(... reason: 'promo "<name>" started', source: 'PROMO_START')` is appended to the unified price timeline (:117-137). The exit pass is symmetrical and equally unfiltered (:145-160). The same blindness is upstream: `pricing-snapshot.service.ts:73-74` and :88-93 build snapshots for `channelListing.findMany({ where: { productId: { in: productIds } } })` with no lifecycle predicate, so ended rows keep producing the PricingSnapshot rows the repricer then scans. Pricing rules cannot express the coordinate at all — `PricingRuleProduct` binds a rule to a Product only (schema.prisma:2779-2792), with no channel, marketplace, connection or alias column, so "stop this rule for IT" is not representable and ending IT removes nothing. Amazon coupons are the one clean case and should not be reported as a defect: `amazon-coupon.service.ts:1-32` is a pure spec-builder with "No DB writes. No outbound HTTP.", so there is no stored coupon to orphan.

##### Proposed fix
API: add one shared `LIVE_LISTING_WHERE` predicate (`isPublished: true, listingStatus: { notIn: ['ENDED'] }, offerClosedAt: null, product: { deletedAt: null }`) exported from a single module and applied at promotion-scheduler.service.ts:60 and :150, pricing-snapshot.service.ts:74 and :90, and repricer-scheduler.service.ts:137 — one concept defined once, and one place to change when a sixth off-switch appears. Give `PricingRuleProduct` the coordinate it lacks (nullable `channel` + `marketplace`, matching how `AdProductSet` is scoped, schema.prisma:3365-3370) so a rule can be scoped to, and retired with, a market. UI: the studio's price timeline should not print a PROMO_START event against a coordinate that was ENDED at that moment — render such rows through the DS `Pill` tone="warning" with "listing was ended" rather than dropping them, since the history is real even when the promotion had no effect.

- apps/api/src/services/promotion-scheduler.service.ts:106-137
- apps/api/src/services/promotion-scheduler.service.ts:145-160

The backend defect is real and I confirmed it from the code, not from the write-up. But one load-bearing leg of the finding is false and the severity is overstated.

CONFIRMED (read verbatim):

No listingStatus, no isPublished, no offerClosedAt, no product.deletedAt.
- :105-137 — every matching row is updated with `salePrice`, `lastOverrideAt`, `lastOverrideBy: 'promotion:<eventId>'`, and `recordPriceChange(... source:'PROMO_START', reason: 'promo "<name>" started')` is appended.
- :145-160 / :180-206 — the EXIT select is likewise lifecycle-blind and writes `salePrice: null` + a PROMO_END timeline row.
- apps/api/src/services/pricing-snapshot.service.ts:73-75 and :88-92 — both `channelListing.findMany({ where: { productId: { in: productIds } } })`, no lifecycle predicate.
- The predicate is expressible and is simply not used: packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1615 (`listingStatus String @default("DRAFT") // DRAFT, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, ENDED, ERROR`), :1629 (`isPublished Boolean @default(true)`), :1591 (`offerClosedAt DateTime?`), :422 (`Product.deletedAt`).
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:2779-2792 — `PricingRuleProduct` binds ruleId+productId only; no channel/marketplace/connection/alias column. "Retire this rule for IT" is genuinely not representable.
- Set claim re-run with /usr/bin/grep (the shell `grep` is the ugrep function): `/usr/bin/grep -n "listingStatus|isPublished|offerClosedAt|ENDED"` over pricing-engine, pricing-outbound, price-history, repricer-scheduler and pricing-snapshot returns nothing at all — no lifecycle gate anywhere in the pricing chain.
- Not dead code: apps/api/src/jobs/pricing-refresh.job.ts:27,75 schedules it hourly, and apps/api/src/routes/pricing.routes.ts:765-773 exposes an ungated `POST /pricing/run-promotions` that runs it regardless of the NEXUS_ENABLE_PRICING_CRON gate. The feature is reachable: pricing.routes.ts:861-931 creates RetailEvent + RetailEventPriceAction from /pricing/promotions (apps/web/src/app/pricing/promotions/PromotionsClient.tsx), and advertising/automation-action-handlers.ts:559-575 creates them too.
- The amazon-coupon exclusion is accurate: apps/api/src/services/amazon-coupon.service.ts:1-32 is a documented pure spec-builder, "No DB writes. No outbound HTTP."

REFUTED SUB-CLAIM (why the title/fix must be corrected): "the product's price timeline — which is what the operator reads in the studio". There is no price timeline in the studio. `/usr/bin/grep -rn "PriceChange|priceHistory|price-history|timeline"` over apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio returns one unrelated comment (images/useImageWorkspace.ts:81). The only consumer of PH.1/PH.2 is apps/web/src/app/pricing/PricingMatrixClient.tsx:1675, :1709-1718, :1798. The enqueue loop is default-OFF: repricer-scheduler.service.ts:14-19 and :74 (`NEXUS_REPRICER_LIVE === '1'`), and its listing lookup (:135-140) is equally lifecycle-blind but dry-run by default. So the blast radius today is DB state + a misleading /pricing timeline + polluted PricingSnapshot rows the matrix and alerts read — bad, but not an outbound write to a dead listing. Medium.

Also worth noting for the fix author: the EXIT pass is not "equally unfiltered" in the way implied — it is constrained by `lastOverrideBy: 'promotion:<eventId>'` (:157), so it can only touch rows the ENTER pass already stamped. It is lifecycle-blind, not scope-blind.
The API half of the fix is right and I would keep it: one shared LIVE_LISTING_WHERE applied at promotion-scheduler.service.ts:60 and :150, pricing-snapshot.service.ts:74 and :90, and repricer-scheduler.service.ts:136. All four fields it names exist (schema.prisma:1615 listingStatus, :1629 isPublished, :1591 offerClosedAt, :422 Product.deletedAt), so the predicate is writable as stated. Two corrections. (1) Drop the UI clause entirely, or re-aim it: there is no studio price timeline — the PH.2 feed is rendered only by apps/web/src/app/pricing/PricingMatrixClient.tsx:1675-1798, so the DS Pill tone="warning" change belongs there, and this item is not a PES/studio finding at all. (2) The EXIT-pass fix needs care the write-up does not give it: adding the live predicate to :150 would strand salePrice on any row that was ended while a promo was active, because EXIT is the only thing that clears the `promotion:<id>` stamp. Either exempt EXIT from the lifecycle filter (clearing is always safe) or add a one-off sweep for stamped rows that fell out of the live set. The PricingRuleProduct coordinate column is a genuine schema gap and correctly diagnosed, but it is a separate, larger change from the predicate fix and should not ride in the same edit.

The operator closes the GALE jacket's DE offer, then opens the studio on scope Amazon · DE to check. The record drawer's Listings pane tells them the offer is "selling". The close writes only `offerClosedAt/By/Reason/Snapshot` (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:178-195); `offerActive`, `isPublished` and `listingStatus` are all left untouched. `ListingsPane.tsx:125-133` renders the Offer fact from `offerActive` alone — true → the literal string `'selling'`. `offerClosedAt` reaches the web tree nowhere: `/usr/bin/grep -rn "offerClosed" apps/web/src` returns zero hits, against a live control in the same tree (`offerActive` matches in drawer/types.ts:161-172, ListingsPane.tsx:125-127, channelActions.ts:149,211,270). On the ads half, `AnalyticsAdsTab.tsx:138-140` builds its request via `adsQuery({ productId, sku, asin, windowDays })` (readAds.ts:28-37) — the function takes no marketplace, and the tab's `load` never reads the studio's `market` scope, so the summary tiles at :384-385 are an all-markets total on a market-scoped page (the per-campaign grid does carry a Market column, :168, so the detail is honest and only the headline is not). And there is no verb: grepping the whole `_studio/` tree for `retail-readiness|retailGuard|repric|pricing/push|suppressCampaign|PricingRule` returns nothing but the word "campaigns" inside this one read-only tab, against a control of 41 files containing `fetch(` in that tree. The studio's three channel verbs remain open-record, offer-toggle and broadcast (channelActions.ts:403), and the first two refuse any live alias as wave-1 preview-only.

##### Proposed fix
Three changes, all inside existing DS surfaces. (1) Put `offerClosedAt` on the wire in the studio listing payload and make ListingsPane's Offer fact a three-state read — `selling` / `paused` / DS `Pill` tone="warning" "market offer closed" with the close reason and actor in its title — so "selling" stops being the default for a deleted offer; today's two-state render is a 100%-honest-UI violation. (2) Pass the scope's market into `adsQuery` and add `marketplace` to GET /api/advertising/product-ads (the route already selects `campaign.marketplace`, advertising.routes.ts:2898-2904, so filtering is a where-clause), and label the tiles with the scope — an unscoped total on a scoped page is the same class of defect the tab's own header comment already fixed for parents vs variants. (3) Add ONE ads consequence row to the channel scope's readiness, not a new tab: when a coordinate is closed/ended and campaigns still reference its ASIN, the sheet shows a DS `Banner` tone="warning" whose action opens a `Drawer` (mode="modal", confirmation via its `overlay` slot per design-system/styles/components.css:588-601) offering the gated `suppressCampaignBids` floor — the codebase's existing NO-PAUSE policy — rather than inventing a pause verb the ads lane has ruled out.

#### The compliance rules engine (expired CE certificate, hazmat, missing EU responsible person) never runs in the studio — the sheet calls a listing with an expired CE certificate "ready"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator sells a CE-marked PPE motorcycle jacket (ppeCategory CAT_II) live on Amazon IT and eBay DE. Its CE certificate expired last month; the daily cron already counted it. She opens /products/GALE-JACKET/edit/studio, switches to the Amazon · IT scope, and reads the readiness chip on the row: it says the row is ready/live, with no compliance issue anywhere on the sheet, in the record drawer, or on Needs attention. She keeps selling, and she has no signal that this listing must come down until Amazon or a market-surveillance authority acts.

##### What happens today
There are two independent validators in this repo and the studio only inherits one. `evaluateCompliance` (compliance-resolver.service.ts:156-210) is the EU/PPE/CE/REACH/hazmat/customs/GPSR-Art.16 engine: an absent CE certificate for a CAT_II/CAT_III product on an EU market is `severity: 'block'` (:170-172) and an expired one is `'block'` (:173). `complianceBlockers` (:211-218) is described in its own comment as "the publish gate". Its consumers are the LEGACY surfaces only: the Amazon flat-file editor pushes every issue into the row and blocks on the block-severity ones (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:474-481), the legacy eBay cockpit gates publish on it (ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:101,1166), and the legacy wizard exposes it as /listing-wizard/:id/compliance-status (listing-wizard.routes.ts:4740, consumed by list-wizard/steps/Step9Review.tsx:421). The studio's readiness path imports six pure checkers and does not import evaluateCompliance at all (readiness.service.ts:52-64); `evaluateRow` (readiness.service.ts:207-305) is the complete list of what the studio grades and contains no compliance-engine call. Set claim, positive-controlled: /usr/bin/grep -rni "compliance|certificate|ce_cert|hazmat|gpsr" over apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio returns 6 hits, every one of them a comment (formulaCandidates.ts:67, images/types.ts:163, sheet/views.ts:29,162, master/columns.tsx:395, MasterSheet.tsx:642) — zero code; control: the same tree has 41 files containing `fetch(`. The expiry sweep that does exist is observability-only: cert-expiry-alert.job.ts:9-13 states "Observability-only for now" and :56-71 writes counts and a top-5 sample to the cron log — no notification, no listing action, no studio surface. The studio's own Needs attention tab reads only the publish gate config and the sync queue (ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:124 /api/listings/publish-readiness, :156 /products/:id/sync-queue), neither of which knows what a certificate is.

##### Proposed fix
Delegate the second validator the same way readiness.service.ts already delegates the first. (1) API: in studio-sheet.service.ts, resolve the compliance payload once per sheet (resolveComplianceForSkus already batches, compliance-resolver.service.ts:461) and fold `evaluateCompliance(payload, coordinate.marketplace, coordinate.channel)` into the row's `readiness.issues` with `field: 'compliance'`, mapping `block` → error and `warn` → warning — byte-identical to amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:474-481, so the two surfaces cannot disagree. Add a `readiness.state` value that a block produces (or reuse `errors`), because "live" plus a blocking compliance issue is the state the sheet must never render as clean. (2) UI, no new components: the compliance issues land in the existing issue list, so the DS `FilterChip` view-chip row in sheet/SheetToolbar.tsx gains one chip — `Compliance (n)`, state-first per §14.4 — beside the existing warnings/validation-errors chips, and the record drawer's ListingsPane renders them in the issue block it already has. (3) For the takedown that follows, see SC-C5's action; the chip must link to it rather than dead-end.

#### Changing brand or GTIN on a LIVE Amazon listing is silently accepted in the studio — the warning that exists is wired only to the flat-file editor

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator fixes a typo: the jacket's `brand` reads "Xavia " with a trailing word, and its EAN was keyed wrong. She corrects both in the master sheet of the studio. Amazon locks `brand` and `externally_assigned_product_identifier` after creation, so on the live IT and DE offers the change is ignored or rejected. Nexus now holds one brand and one GTIN; Amazon holds another; nothing on the screen ever said so, and the next readiness pass validates her new (correct) GTIN against a mod-10 rule while Amazon keeps the old one.

##### What happens today
`checkNonEditableChanges` (listing-preflight.service.ts:277-296) exists precisely for this: it diffs the row against the last-saved flatFileSnapshot and warns "'{label}' cannot be changed on an existing listing (Amazon locks it after creation) — the new value will likely be ignored or rejected". Its only two production call sites are the legacy Amazon flat-file editor (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:473 and :796); every other hit is its own definition or a test (/usr/bin/grep -rn over apps/api/src + apps/web/src, dist excluded). The studio's `evaluateRow` never calls it and readiness.service.ts:52-64 never imports it. The same file's own header is the giveaway: readiness.service.ts:12-19 enumerates "what the sheet's copy was missing, measured against the shipped preflight" and lists four checkers including `checkRequiredWithParent` — and `checkRequiredWithParent` is ALSO absent from evaluateRow (readiness.service.ts:207-305) and from the import list, so the module that exists to guarantee "exactly one answer" (:21-23) delegates two of the four things it says it delegates. The studio's own GTIN check is present but narrower than the flat-file one: readiness.service.ts:113 covers gtin/ean/upc/externally_assigned_product_identifier while the preflight's GTIN_FIELDS (listing-preflight.service.ts, the const above preflightRow) also covers `barcode`. The write itself is unguarded — brand and GTIN are ordinary master cells.

##### Proposed fix
Add both missing delegations in readiness.service.ts so the module keeps the promise in its own header. `CoordinateValidators` gains `nonEditable: RequiredColumn[]` (derived from the schema's `editable:false` columns, exactly as nonEditableByType is built in amazon-flat-file.routes.ts) and `subRequiredGroups`; `evaluateRow` gains `checkNonEditableChanges(row, v.nonEditable, snapshot)` and `checkRequiredWithParent(row, v.subRequiredGroups)`. The snapshot the check needs is `ChannelListing.flatFileSnapshot`, which studio-sheet.service.ts already excludes from the payload — pass it into the validator server-side rather than shipping it to the browser. In the UI this needs no new component: a locked-attribute warning is an issue on the cell, so the existing cell warning glyph and the drawer's field-level issue line render it, and the cell's DS `InfoTip` carries the full "revert to X or request via Seller Support" sentence. Correct the header comment in the same change, or delete the two names from it — a doc that claims a check the code does not run is what let this survive.

#### Amazon Ireland is hard-coded as a non-GPSR market, and the studio's GPSR gate covers 8 of the 17 EU markets the compliance engine recognises

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator lists the same jacket on Amazon IE alongside IT and DE. On the IT and DE scopes the sheet shows the familiar GPSR pair flagged (`dsa_responsible_party_address`, `gpsr_safety_attestation`) and she fills them in. On the IE scope the same two cells are silently clean — the readiness pill is green with no GPSR issue at all. Ireland is an EU member state and GPSR (EU) 2023/988 applies there in full; the listing is exposed to the same suppression the code's own message warns about for IT.

##### What happens today
`checkGpsrCompliance` returns an empty array before evaluating anything when the marketplace is not in `GPSR_EU_MARKETPLACES` (listing-preflight.service.ts:354-355). That set is exactly eight codes — ES, FR, BE, NL, DE, IT, SE, PL (listing-preflight.service.ts:308-309). The very same repo's compliance engine defines `EU_MARKETS` as seventeen — IT, DE, FR, ES, NL, PL, SE, BE, IE, AT, PT, FI, DK, GR, CZ, HU, RO (compliance-resolver.service.ts:88-89, whose comment says these are "the exact sets the compliance-status endpoint uses") and fires its GPSR Art. 16 responsible-person rule across all of them (:203-206). The studio's sheet readiness calls the narrow one (readiness.service.ts:274-279). IE is not a hypothetical market: `A28R8C7NBKEWEA: 'IE', // the real Ireland` is in the canonical marketplace map (marketplace-code.ts:39), added when a prior defect had confused it with Belgium. And the studio-facing comment states the wrong classification in words: readiness.service.ts:14-16 says "NINE of the twenty active Marketplace rows are GPSR EU markets (IT DE FR ES BE NL SE PL, + IE/UK non-GPSR)" — it names eight while saying nine, and puts IE on the non-GPSR side next to the UK. The test suite only pins the exemptions that are correct (US and UK, flat-file-ufx6-gpsr.vitest.test.ts:316-317) and never exercises IE, so nothing fails.

##### Proposed fix
Delete `GPSR_EU_MARKETPLACES` and have `checkGpsrCompliance` import the single EU market set from compliance-resolver.service.ts (export `EU_MARKETS` and, if the UK's separate regime still needs distinguishing, keep `UK_MARKETS` separate as it already is). One set, one definition — the 'one concept defined once' rule in the DS README applies to market taxonomies as much as to tokens. Add a test arm per EU market code derived FROM the set rather than from a hand-written list (a hardcoded member list is the thing that went stale here), plus a positive control asserting US/UK still return []. Correct the readiness.service.ts:14-16 comment in the same change; it is the sentence a future lane will cite. No UI change: the existing flagged-cell path already renders the warnings once they fire.

#### eBay EU listings get no GPSR readiness in the studio, and the publish path silently strips the GPSR container and still reports LIVE

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator publishes the jacket to eBay DE from the list wizard. eBay rejects createOffer because the `regulatory` container is malformed (say the responsible-person country is missing). The adapter retries without GPSR data, the offer is created, and the operator is shown a plain LIVE result with a listing URL. She then opens the studio on the eBay · DE scope to check — the readiness pill is clean, because the studio runs no GPSR check on an eBay coordinate at all. The listing is live in Germany with no economic-operator data attached, and nothing in the product any operator can see records that.

##### What happens today
Publish side: ebay-publish.adapter.ts:660-688 builds the GPSR `regulatory` container from the canonical compliance resolver, and on any non-ok createOffer WITH regulatory it sets `regulatoryWarning`, deletes the container and retries — the comment states the intent outright ("so a compliance-data problem never blocks the listing (surfaced as a warning)"). The warning is returned on the result (:746-747), and its caller drops it: channel-publish.service.ts:200-206 returns `{ status: 'LIVE', submissionId, listingUrl }` and carries no warning field. Set claim: /usr/bin/grep -rn "regulatoryWarning" over apps/api/src + apps/web/src (dist excluded) returns four hits, all four inside the adapter — nothing reads it, so it exists only in the server log line at :679. Readiness side: every branch of checkGpsrCompliance is gated on `has(col)` over `applicableColumns` (listing-preflight.service.ts:359, 371-372, 395-397), and the column ids it looks for are Amazon flat-file attribute names — `gpsr_manufacturer_reference`, `dsa_responsible_party_address`, `gpsr_safety_attestation`, `compliance_media__*` (listing-preflight.service.ts:361-367); the studio passes the coordinate's own applicable keys (readiness.service.ts:193, :274-279). Those keys are Amazon channel facts (source-definition-plan.ts:46-49) and appear nowhere else under apps/api/src/services/pim (/usr/bin/grep -rn "gpsr|dsa_responsible|compliance_media" over that directory returns only source-definition-plan.ts:48-49 and readiness.service.ts's own comments), so on an eBay coordinate every GPSR branch is skipped and the checker contributes zero issues. eBay's real GPSR data is product-level (buildEbayRegulatory, ebay-publish.adapter.ts:180-210, fed by the compliance resolver) — and per SC-C1 the studio never calls that resolver either.

##### Proposed fix
Two halves, and they must land together (a producer without a consumer is what produced this). Producer: propagate the warning — add `warnings?: string[]` to the publish result in channel-publish.service.ts and persist a `regulatory_not_sent` ListingIssue row against the ChannelListing, so the fact outlives the request. Consumer: make it channel-agnostic in the studio — implement SC-C1's `evaluateCompliance` fold (it is already channel-parameterised: `evaluateCompliance(payload, marketplace, 'EBAY')`), which gives every eBay EU coordinate the responsible-person and CE/REACH checks it has none of today, and render the persisted `regulatory_not_sent` issue in the record drawer's ListingsPane issue block and on the Needs attention tab. Surface it in the chrome with the DS `Banner` (tone="warning", with its `action` slot pointing at Brand Settings) on the channel scope when the bound listing carries that issue — a Banner is already the studio's established pattern for a scope-level statement (StudioTabHost.tsx renders scopeError that way).

(Cited line numbers 193 / 274-279 are off by 2-8; content is there.)

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG — the narrated scenario cannot happen:

So on the LIST WIZARD path `payload.compliance` is undefined → buildEbayRegulatory returns null (adapter:184) → `regulatory` is never attached → the strip/retry branch never fires and channel-publish.service.ts:200-206 never has a regulatory warning to drop. The wizard defect is different and arguably worse: eBay EU offers from the wizard NEVER carry economic-operator data at all, silently.

The only path where the described strip CAN occur is the eBay cockpit route: ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:1161 `resolveComplianceById(productId)`, :1209-1217 passes `compliance` to the adapter, :1233-1241 flips ChannelListing to isPublished/ACTIVE recording nothing about a strip. That is neither the list wizard nor the studio.

But the finding's headline mechanism belongs to a route it does not cite, and the route it does cite fails for a different reason.
The producer half is aimed at the wrong link. Fix order must be (1) compose compliance into the wizard's eBay payload the way ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:1161/1209-1217 already does (resolveComplianceById + complianceBlockers), then (2) propagate. Also, no new `warnings` field is needed — channel-publish.service.ts:62-68 already defines it with a documented wizard yellow-strip UI and Amazon already populates it (:157, :170); the eBay branch at :189-205 simply has to fill it (with compatibilityWarning too, which is dropped identically). On the cockpit path the producer is already done — ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:1250 spreads the warning into the response — so the gap there is purely the consumer, PublishDrawer.tsx:102-115. The persistence idea is the right instinct but should hang off the ChannelListing write at ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:1233-1241 (and the wizard's `submissions` JSON at listing-wizard.routes.ts:2746-2754), not be invented as a new subsystem. The consumer half should also reconcile with the existing per-market compliance grid (datasheet/CompliancePerMarketTab.tsx) rather than adding a second, divergent compliance verdict; and the readiness change must respect readiness.service.ts:38-51, which deliberately documents partial GPSR coverage — an `evaluateCompliance` fold that is not fed by any eBay column set will need its own product-level inputs, not `applicableColumns`.

[critical]verifiedALLdata integrity risk

#### "Stop selling in this market" deactivates the Marketplace row: the studio hides the coordinate entirely while the listings stay live and the sync worker keeps pushing to them

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A compliance notice says the jacket may no longer be sold in Poland. The only market-level lever in the product is marketplace configuration, so an admin deactivates Amazon · PL. The operator then opens the jacket in the studio to confirm: the PL market is gone from the switcher, and a deep link to ?market=PL falls back to another market with the banner "This market is unavailable. Choose an available market." She reads that as done. The Amazon PL offer is still live, still selling, and the outbound sync worker keeps pushing price and quantity updates to it. Separately: if Amazon suspends the seller's PL authorisation instead, the studio shows PL as a completely normal, healthy scope.

##### What happens today
Arm 1 — deactivation. `GET /api/marketplaces/grouped`, the studio's only market source (studio-data.ts:82), filters `where: { isActive: true }` (marketplaces.routes.ts:237-241). The deactivation lever is real: `PATCH /api/admin/marketplace-config/:id { isActive }` (dashboard.routes.ts:227-240). The studio then drops the market from the option set (scopes.ts:108-141), `contracts.tsx:645-649` falls back to `defaultMarket`, and `contracts.tsx:677` raises "This market is unavailable. Choose an available market." — a chrome-level statement about the SCOPE BAR that reads as a statement about the listing. Meanwhile nothing acts on the flag: /usr/bin/grep for `prisma.marketplace.find*` in apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts and apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts returns nothing at all, and the only `isActive` in either file is `Offer.isActive` (outbound-sync.service.ts:934) and an offer filter (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:195) — positive control: both greps do return those hits, so the search is live. Arm 2 — suspension. `participationStatus` can be written 'SUSPENDED' or 'NOT_PARTICIPATING' automatically (amazon-participations.service.ts:117-121, :148-158) and SUSPENDED deliberately keeps `isParticipating` true (:94). The studio cannot see either: `MarketplaceLite` (types.ts:77-89) carries id/channel/code/name/language/languages/accounts/connected and nothing about participation, and /usr/bin/grep -rni "participat" over the whole _studio tree returns one unrelated comment (masterWrite.ts:203). The nearest per-market off-switch the studio offers, offer-toggle, refuses every live row by design (channelActions.ts:249-251, :258-261: "Refused: this would change a live listing, and wave-1 channel verbs are preview-only").

##### Proposed fix
A market a product still has listings on must never disappear from the studio. (1) API: add `?includeInactive=1` to /marketplaces/grouped and project `isActive`, `isParticipating`, `participationStatus` onto the row; widen `MarketplaceLite` (types.ts:78-89) with those three. (2) scopes.ts keeps an inactive/suspended market in `markets` but tags it, so the DS scope-bar chip renders present-but-attention rather than absent — the studio already has the vocabulary for this ("A chip outside its markets is disabled, not hidden", scopes.ts:198). (3) On such a coordinate, StudioTabHost shows a DS `Banner` tone="danger" stating the true position — "Amazon · PL is deactivated in marketplace settings, but this product still has a live listing there (ASIN …). Deactivating a market does not end a listing." — with the Banner's `action` slot invoking the per-market takedown verb. (4) That verb is the thing that has to exist: a channel-scope `GridAction` in the DS registry (registry.ts:167-198) with `danger: true`, a real `preflight()` that names the ASIN/ItemID and whether the removal is reversible per channel, and `ConfirmLevel: 'type-to-confirm'` on the real SKU per ruling #133, backed by an API that reuses the already-implemented `dispatchChannelDelist` path through an OutboundSyncQueue row (never the inline synthetic-queueId shortcut) and, on Amazon FBM, prefers the reversible `CLOSE_OFFER` snapshot path (amazon-market-offer.service.ts) so the market can be reopened next season. (5) Make the flag load-bearing server-side too: outbound-sync must skip a marketplace that is not `isActive && isParticipating`, rather than pushing into a market the operator believes is off.

[high]verifiedAMAZONux defect

#### Changing the Amazon product type or primary category of a LIVE listing is a plain cell edit / a reassuring modal — no live-listing impact, no confirmation, and no path back if Amazon refuses

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The jacket is live on Amazon IT and DE as OUTERWEAR. To pick up the correct size chart the operator retypes the `productType` cell in the master sheet to MOTORCYCLE_PROTECTIVE_GEAR, or opens the Classification dialog and changes the primary category. Autosave commits. On Amazon, changing an existing offer's product type is frequently refused and can require deleting and recreating the offer; here she is told nothing before or after. The required-attribute set silently changes underneath her, previously-satisfied required fields become missing (and vice versa), and the studio offers no delist/relist verb to execute the recreation that Amazon may now demand.

##### What happens today
`productType` is an ordinary editable master field — field-registry.service.ts:85 declares it `editable: true`, help text "Master Amazon productType — drives category-specific attribute fields"; it is labelled "Amazon product type (default)" in the classification group (sheet-columns.service.ts:483, :280) and, being `storage: 'column'`, routes straight to master truth (studio-sheet.service.ts:569, :573-583). It is also pinned into the default Essentials view as part of the commerce spine (sheet/views.ts:172), so it is on screen and editable by default. The Classification dialog is the other write path and it actively reassures: ClassificationDialog.tsx:61 says "Changing it keeps all saved attribute values", :90 says "Existing Amazon product types and eBay listing categories take precedence over category defaults", and :91 lists the per-market channel mappings — nowhere does it say a listing is live on any of them. Its save (ClassificationDialog.tsx:38-51) is a straight PATCH inside a DS `Modal`, with no preflight, no impact, no confirm step. Server-side `updateProductClassification` (product-classification.ts:41-57) validates family, category existence and an optimistic `version` CAS and queries ChannelListing not at all — there is no live-listing guard. Yet the change is load-bearing for the channel: for an Amazon coordinate the product types come from the category context (studio-sheet.service.ts:895-897) and the mapping resolver picks each listing's category from it (:1007-1009). The one warning in the repo that covers "you changed something Amazon locks after creation" is `checkNonEditableChanges`, which per SC-C2 is wired only to the flat-file editor.

##### Proposed fix
Treat a classification change on a product with live listings as a parameterised destructive verb, which the DS already models. (1) API: add `GET /api/products/:id/studio/classification/impact?familyId&categoryIds&primaryId` returning, per coordinate, the live listing ref, the resolved before/after channel category or product type, the required attributes gained and lost, and a per-channel verdict ('accepted in place' | 'requires delete and recreate' | 'unknown'). (2) UI: keep the existing DS `Modal` but give it the COLLECT → PREFLIGHT → CONFIRM → RUN order the registry mandates (registry.ts:215) — the Save button becomes a preflight, and the impact renders as itemised consequences, never a count (ActionConfirm's rule), with `ConfirmLevel: 'confirm'` normally and `'type-to-confirm'` on the real SKU when any coordinate returns 'requires delete and recreate'. (3) Fix the copy: "Changing it keeps all saved attribute values" is true of Nexus and false of the channel — replace it with what the impact actually returned, per the 100%-honest-UI rule. (4) Make the same impact available for the `productType` cell: because it is a single cell edit, route it through the grid action registry's cell-level confirmation rather than letting autosave commit it, and mark it `danger: true` when the row's readiness reports a live listing. (5) This finding depends on SC-C5's takedown/relist verb existing — a dialog that tells an operator the change requires deleting and recreating the offer, in a studio with no delist and no relist, is the Owner's dead end again.

#### The only channel-lifecycle destructive endpoint stamps its audit rows with the literal string 'default-user'

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has GALE-JACKET live on Amazon IT, Amazon DE and eBay UK. They select it in /products, move it to the bin, and the BulkActionBar fires POST /api/products/bulk-hard-delete with channelAction:'delete'. Three DELETE_LISTING jobs are enqueued and the worker calls deleteListingsItem on Amazon and endFixedPriceItem on eBay: the ASIN and the ItemID are gone for good. A week later the merchandising lead asks who ended the UK listing.

##### What happens today
An AuditLog row IS written per product, inside the transaction, before the cascade (products-catalog.routes.ts:1906-1912). But its actor is `userId: actor` where `const actor = userIdFor(request)` (:1797), and `userIdFor` at :83-85 is `function userIdFor(_req: any): string { return 'default-user' }` — it ignores the request entirely and returns a hardcoded constant. The real identity is available at that point: rbacHook attaches `req.authUser` at rbac-hook.ts:46-55 before any handler runs (registered as a global preHandler, index.ts:634). The row also sets no `ip` (the createMany data at :1908-1922 lists userId/entityType/entityId/action/before/after/metadata only), even though AuditWriteInput supports it (audit-log.service.ts:23). The same constant is duplicated in fulfillment.routes.ts:287-289. So the audit trail for permanently ending live marketplace listings names nobody, on every row, in a single-value way that cannot be disambiguated after the fact. The programme memory's recollection of `userId: null` is half right: the value is not null here, it is a fixed non-null string, which is worse — it LOOKS like an actor.

##### Proposed fix
Delete `userIdFor` and route every lifecycle audit write through `writeAuthAudit`-style attribution: `auditLogService.write({ userId: request.authUser?.id ?? null, ip: truncateIp(request.ip), ... })`, using `truncateIp` from lib/auth/session.ts as the auth audit already does (audit.ts:36-53). Refuse the write rather than invent an actor: if `channelAction !== 'none'` and `request.authUser?.id` is absent, 401 before enqueueing any DELETE_LISTING row — an unattributable irreversible channel call must not be allowed to run. Add `apiKeyId: request.apiKey?.id` to the audit `metadata` so machine callers are named too. Ship a pre-push guard in the family of scripts/check-*.mjs asserting that no file under apps/api/src/routes defines a `userIdFor`-shaped constant-returning actor helper.

"The only channel-lifecycle destructive endpoint" is defensible only in the narrow sense I verified: /usr/bin/grep for DELETE_LISTING|UNPUBLISH_LISTING across apps/api/src/routes returns exactly one hit (products-catalog.routes.ts:1879). Other destructive channel paths (ebay-flat-file-delete.service, delist services) were not audited by the probe, so "the only" should be scoped to the delist-cascade.

That is a compliance/forensics defect on an irreversible action, i.e. high, not critical.
The attribution half of the fix is right and cheap: `userId: (request as any).authUser?.id ?? null` plus `ip: truncateIp(request.ip)` at products-catalog.routes.ts:1909/1925, matching what catalog-transfer.routes.ts:16 and lib/auth/audit.ts:35-52 already do. Prefer null over an invented constant — a null actor reads as "unknown", 'default-user' reads as a person who does not exist.

Two parts of the proposed fix are wrong or risky as written:

1. "401 before enqueueing any DELETE_LISTING row if request.authUser?.id is absent" would break the feature today. rbac-hook.ts:30-32 defaults NEXUS_RBAC_MODE to 'shadow', and no .env in the tree sets it (checked apps/api/.env, apps/api/.env.local, .env) — shadow deliberately allows unauthenticated requests through while the rollout is staged. Hard-401'ing inside this one handler unilaterally flips enforcement for one route, out of band from the manifest, and permanently breaks the bin's channel-cascade delete for any session without a cookie. The right home for that gate is the enforce flip (or a per-route enforce override), not an ad-hoc reply.code(401) in the handler.

2. "Delete userIdFor" is far larger than stated. It has 6 more callsites in this file alone (:925, :1082, :1427, :1562, :2113, :2270), and :2113 feeds `createdBy` on a persisted row, not an audit row — changing that to null may violate a NOT NULL column or break `where: { userId: 'default-user' }` lookups (dashboard.routes.ts:2181, 3506, 3731, 3870 all query by that literal). Deleting the helper without auditing those readers would orphan existing saved views/notifications. Scope the change to the audit writes first; migrate the ownership reads separately.

Also: the pre-push guard as specified ("no file under apps/api/src/routes defines a userIdFor-shaped constant-returning actor helper") would fail red on day one against at least orders.routes.ts:37, notifications.routes.ts:23, saved-view-alerts.routes.ts:39 and fulfillment.routes.ts:288, which the fix does not touch. Ship it as an allow-list-with-shrinking-baseline or scope it to files that write auditLog rows, or it is a gate that can only be silenced.

Finally, the worker side is unaddressed: the OutboundSyncQueue rows carry only `payload.source` (:1888-1894) and channel-delist.service.ts / bullmq-sync.worker.ts write no audit at all, so even a fixed enqueue-time row leaves the actual marketplace call (deleteListingsItem / endFixedPriceItem) unattributed at execution time. Put the actor into the queue payload so the worker can stamp the completion row too.

#### Per-market and per-channel removal writes no audit row and no product event at all — the destructive verbs the Owner is asking for already exist and are entirely unrecorded

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket live on Amazon IT and Amazon DE and wants it off IT only. Today the only way is the /products/amazon-flat-file page, which calls POST /api/amazon/flat-file/remove with {productId, marketplace:'IT'}. That hard-deletes the IT ChannelListing row (taking the ASIN, flatFileSnapshot, overrideData, offerCloseSnapshot, offers, images and issues with it by FK cascade). Next season the operator wants IT back and asks the log what the IT row used to hold, and who removed it.

##### What happens today
Nothing is recorded anywhere. /usr/bin/grep for `auditLog|productEvent|eventStore|recordEvent|emitEvent|publishEvent` returns rc=1 (no match) on all five lifecycle services: amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts, ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts, channel-delist.service.ts, amazon-market-offer.service.ts and pim/listing-alias.service.ts. Positive control: the same files carry real domain writes — ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts has 9 write calls (:331, :350, :431, :435, :540, :547, :554, :645, :668) and amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts has 1 (:60, the `channelListing.deleteMany`). The Amazon route never even reads the caller's identity: amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1806-1819 destructures only `request.body.targets` and passes `(prisma, t)` to `removeAmazonListing`. The worker's delist branch is the same — bullmq-sync.worker.ts hands `dispatchChannelDelist` a queue row, and channel-delist.service.ts writes no record of the SP-API delete or the EndFixedPriceItem it issues. So the single most destructive class of action in the product — the one the Owner is asking to be given a UI — is the class with zero accountability today, and building the studio verb on top of these services would inherit that.

##### Proposed fix
Make attribution a precondition of the destructive primitive, not a decoration on the route. Give `dispatchChannelDelist`, `removeAmazonListing`, `handleRemoveChannelListing`, `closeMarketOffers`/`reopenMarketOffers` and `archiveAlias` a REQUIRED `actor: { userId: string; ip: string | null; apiKeyId?: string }` parameter (TypeScript-required, so every call site must be updated and the typecheck is the gate). Each writes one `auditLogService.write({ entityType: 'ChannelListing', entityId: listing.id, action: 'listing.end' | 'listing.remove' | 'offer.close' | 'offer.reopen' | 'alias.archive', before: <the row it is about to destroy, verbatim>, after: null, metadata: { channel, marketplace, aliasKey, channelConnectionId, externalListingId, source } })` BEFORE the mutation, so the trail survives the cascade exactly as bulk-hard-delete already does. When the studio grows the per-market verb, express it as a DS GridAction on the channel sheet — `{ scope: 'row', danger: true, preflight() → ActionImpact }` with `level: 'type-to-confirm'` and `confirmPhrase` = the real SKU (grid/actions/registry.ts:69, :117, :184), rendered by useActionConfirm so the consequences are itemised, not counted.
