CORE DEFECT CONFIRMED, BUT THE FINDING IS OVERSTATED AND ITS FIX IS PARTLY ALREADY BUILT.

What I confirmed myself:
1. apps/api/src/services/amazon/amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:58-63 — `tx.channelListing.deleteMany({ where: { productId: { in: ids }, channel: 'AMAZON', marketplace } })`. Hard delete, market-scoped, no audit, no actor parameter anywhere in the file (/usr/bin/grep for audit|productEvent|eventStore|recordEvent|emitEvent|publishEvent → rc=1).
2. apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1806-1819 — the handler destructures only `request.body?.targets` and calls `removeAmazonListing(prisma, t)`. No `request.user`/`authUser`/`request.ip` is read. Verified verbatim.
3. Live, not dead code: apps/web/src/app/products/amazon-flat-file/AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1886 POSTs `/api/amazon/flat-file/remove`, behind a native `confirm()` at :1912 — no type-to-confirm, no itemised impact.
4. apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:645 — the same market-scoped `tx.channelListing.deleteMany` for EBAY inside handleRemoveChannelListing (:604). /usr/bin/grep on apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts for "audit" returns only three prose comments (:954, :1710, :2097) — no audit write on that route either.
5. SET CLAIM re-established with /usr/bin/grep (not the shell function): the only ChannelListing delete call sites in apps/api/src are amazon.routes.ts:1381, catalog.routes.ts:1086/:1120 (both whole-product deletes), amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:60 and ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:645. So exactly two market-scoped hard-delete paths exist and neither audits.
6. The loss is real and cascading: packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1894 — `ChannelListingSnapshot.channelListing … onDelete: Cascade` (and :2001, :2413, :19061 for other children). The snapshot history whose own comment (schema.prisma:1897-1899) says it stays "queryable and readable after a listing row is replaced" is destroyed with the row. ChannelListing has flatFileSnapshot (:1585), offerCloseSnapshot (:1595), externalListingId (:1546) and no deletedAt/archivedAt.
7. The asymmetry the fix relies on is genuine: apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1903-1935 writes `tx.auditLog.createMany` with `userId: actor`, `action: 'hard-delete'`, `before: {…}` explicitly BEFORE the cascade, with the comment "so the trail survives the actual deletion". A ChannelListing UPDATE is even event-logged (listings-syndication.routes.ts:1310-1318, CHANNEL_LISTING_UPDATED) while the market-scoped DELETE is not.
8. No global safety net: apps/api/src/index.ts hooks are onRoute (:485), onRequest (:498), onSend (:530), preHandler workspace/rbac (:633-634), preSerialization (:641) — none audits; /usr/bin/grep found no `$use`/`$extends` Prisma middleware. Audit is per-call-site (returns/pim/fulfillment/products), so an omitted call site is a real hole.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG (why the title and severity must change):
A. "Per-market and per-channel removal … writes no audit row and no product event at all" is FALSE as a blanket claim. The Amazon per-market offer CLOSE/REOPEN verb — the closest existing thing to "take it off IT, put it back next season" — is fully attributed: apps/api/src/services/amazon-market-offer.service.ts:84-87 already takes a REQUIRED `actor: string`; :186-201 writes `offerClosedAt`, `offerClosedBy: opts.actor`, `offerCloseReason` and a verbatim before-state `offerCloseSnapshot` (live purchasable_offer + control flags) onto the row; and the route writes a real audit row per committed change — apps/api/src/routes/sync-control.routes.ts:835-843 calls the `audit()` helper defined at :552-571, which does `prisma.syncControlAudit.createMany` with `actor` from `actorOf(request)` (:550, the user email). The auditor's whole-file grep for the string "audit" inside the service produced a true grep result but a false conclusion — the accountability lives one layer up and in the row itself.
B. The proposed fix is partly a no-op: `closeMarketOffers`/`reopenMarketOffers` already have the required `actor` the fix asks to add.
C. `archiveAlias` (apps/api/src/services/pim/listing-alias.service.ts:193-197) is a reversible `status: 'ARCHIVED'` flip that keeps the row — the route (product-studio.routes.ts:986-990) documents "ARCHIVE, not delete". Including it in "the single most destructive class of action" is padding; its only real gap is that it records no archivedBy while createAlias records createdBy (product-studio.routes.ts:963).
D. "channel-delist.service.ts writes no record of the SP-API delete" is overstated on the worker path: bulk-hard-delete creates an OutboundSyncQueue row carrying source/channelAction/marketplace (products-catalog.routes.ts:1880-1897) and applyDelistResultToQueue (channel-delist.service.ts:318-343) stamps SUCCESS/FAILED on it. That nuance actually sharpens the real hole: the flat-file remove path bypasses the queue entirely with a synthetic `queueId: 'amz-rm-…'` (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:69-78), so that one path leaves no queue row either.

Net: the defect survives on the two flat-file hard-delete paths, which are the ones the Owner's example actually runs, and building the studio verb on them would inherit the hole. Severity high, not critical: no live-listing corruption, the reversible per-market verb is already audited, and the damage is unrecoverable-history plus unattributable action on an existing page.
Two corrections. (1) Drop the `actor` addition to closeMarketOffers/reopenMarketOffers — amazon-market-offer.service.ts:84-87 already requires it, and :186-201 already persists offerClosedBy + a verbatim offerCloseSnapshot; that verb is the MODEL to copy, not a defect to fix. (2) Drop archiveAlias from the destructive set (listing-alias.service.ts:193-197 is a reversible status flip); at most add archivedBy to mirror createdBy. The fix should be scoped to removeAmazonListing and handleRemoveChannelListing: read identity at the route (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1807 and the eBay delete route currently read none — the idiom already used is `(request as {authUser?:{id?:string}}).authUser?.id`, product-studio.routes.ts:962), pass it in as a required parameter, and write the AuditLog row inside the same transaction and BEFORE the deleteMany, with `before` = the full row incl. externalListingId/flatFileSnapshot/overrideData, exactly as products-catalog.routes.ts:1903-1912 does. Because ChannelListingSnapshot cascades (schema.prisma:1894), the audit `before` is the only surviving copy, so a slim diff is not enough here — this is the one place the audit-log service's own "pass slim before/after" guidance (audit-log.service.ts:5-8) should be overridden deliberately. The DS GridAction/type-to-confirm half of the fix is sound but unverified by me.

#### `products.delete` is a grantable permission that no route requires: ending live listings needs only `products.edit`

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A workspace owner hires a catalogue assistant and grants them the copywriting set — products.view + products.edit — deliberately withholding products.delete so they can fix titles but not remove anything. The assistant multi-selects 40 products in /products, moves them to the bin and confirms the hard delete with channelAction:'delete'. Every live Amazon ASIN and eBay ItemID in that selection is ended on the marketplace. The permission the owner thought they were withholding was never checked.

##### What happens today
`products.delete` is declared at packages/shared/permissions.ts:53 and is assigned to a role's permission array at :229, so it appears in the role editor as a real, withholdable grant. It is referenced ZERO times in the route→permission manifest: /usr/bin/grep for `productsDelete|F.productsDelete` over apps/api/src/lib/auth/permissions-manifest.ts returns rc=1, against a positive control of 13 occurrences of `productsEdit` in the same file. Every destructive lifecycle route therefore falls into a catch-all keyed on an EDIT permission — `RW(F.productsView, F.productsEdit, pfx('/api/products'))` at :439 covers POST /api/products/bulk-hard-delete; `RW(F.productsView, F.productsEdit, pfx('/api/catalog'))` at :427 covers the studio's own DELETE /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children/:childId, which is a hard `tx.product.delete` (catalog.routes.ts:1838); and `P(F.listingsFlatfileEdit, pfx('/api/amazon/flat-file'))` / `pfx('/api/ebay/flat-file')` at :347-348 cover the per-market removal endpoints. The manifest's own doc comment says its contract is COMPLETENESS, not correctness (:15-19) — this is exactly the gap it warns about. Compounding it, the gate defaults to shadow: rbac-hook.ts:30-32 returns 'shadow' unless NEXUS_RBAC_MODE === 'enforce', and in shadow a would-be denial is logged and the request PROCEEDS (:74-99), with plain 'unauthenticated' denials not even logged (:94). I could not read the production environment, so I do not claim prod is in shadow — only that the code's default is.

##### Proposed fix
Add explicit manifest entries ABOVE the /api/products and /api/catalog catch-alls, first-match-wins: `P(F.productsDelete, (m,p) => m==='POST' && p==='/api/products/bulk-hard-delete')`, `P(F.productsDelete, (m,p) => m==='DELETE' && /^\/api\/catalog\/products\/[^/]+\/children\/[^/]+$/.test(p))`, and a new `F.listingsDelist` for the per-market removal endpoints (`POST /api/amazon/flat-file/remove`, the eBay `remove-listing`/`remove-channel-listing` intents, and any studio delist route that lands) so 'edit a flat file' and 'end a listing on a marketplace' stop sharing one grant. Extend the existing permission-matrix test to assert that every declared FEATURES key appears at least once in ENTRIES — the absence of `products.delete` would have failed that assertion. #### An API key satisfies any permission in its coarse family and is granted it verbatim, so `products:write` can end every live listing on 200 products with no session, no CSRF, no MFA and no actor

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An integration partner is issued a key scoped `products:write` so their PIM can push descriptions in. The key is committed to a repo. Someone POSTs /api/products/bulk-hard-delete with {productIds:[…200…], channelAction:'delete'} and the x-nexus-workspace-id header. Every live Amazon ASIN and eBay ItemID across those 200 products is ended on the marketplace.

##### What happens today
workspace-hook.ts (global preHandler, index.ts:633, running BEFORE rbacHook at :634) handles the bearer path at :53-71. It resolves the route's required permission from the manifest (:61) — `products.edit` for bulk-hard-delete — then asks `apiKeyPermission(result.scopes, required, method)` (:62). That function (workspace-api-key.ts:2-13) throws the grain away: it takes `permission.split('.')[0]`, maps the whole `products|pim|assets` family to the single scope family `products`, and returns true if the key holds `products:write` for any non-GET. It then writes `request.__rbacResolved = { isOwner:false, permissions: new Set([required]) }` at :66 — the key is auto-granted exactly the permission the route demanded, so rbacHook's later `hasPermission` check at rbac-hook.ts:67-71 reads the cached grant and passes unconditionally. The bearer branch returns at :70-71 before the CSRF check (:83) and before the MFA check (:85), which is defensible for machine callers, but it also sets `actorUserId: null` (:58) and nothing propagates `scope.apiKeyId` (:64) into the audit row — bulk-hard-delete's audit metadata (products-catalog.routes.ts:1917-1922) carries only `source`. So one key scoped 'write products' can permanently end listings, and the resulting audit row says 'default-user' (PA-1) with no indication a machine did it. There is no key scope that means 'edit but not destroy'.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes. (1) Break the family collapse for destructive permissions: give `apiKeyPermission` an explicit deny-list of permissions no family scope can satisfy — `products.delete`, the new `listings.delist`, `listings.recover` — requiring a named scope (`products:delete`, `listings:delist`) held literally, so a `products:write` key is refused with the existing typed `scope_denied` 403 (workspace-hook.ts:62). (2) Carry the machine actor through: set `request.apiKey` metadata into every lifecycle audit row (`metadata.apiKeyId`, `metadata.apiKeyLabel`) so a delist by an integration is distinguishable from a delist by a person, and surface it in the API-keys settings page (DS `SummaryTable`, components/index.ts:77) as 'this key has ended N listings' — a key whose blast radius includes irreversible marketplace calls should say so on the screen where it is issued.

#### The two lifecycle paths that DO keep a record write a false actor — recovery reads as 'triggered by automation', offer-close as 'sync-control'

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator uses /products/[id]/recover to run DELETE_RELIST_SAME on an Amazon DE listing whose ASIN is suppressed: the service calls deleteListingsItem and marks the row ENDED. Separately, a colleague closes the Amazon IT offer for the season via the fulfilment page's CLOSE_OFFER. Two weeks later a reconciliation finds the DE ASIN gone and IT unpurchasable, and asks the logs whether a human or a cron did it. Both logs answer 'a machine did it'.

##### What happens today
ListingRecoveryEvent is the only durable per-listing lifecycle record in the schema and it has an `initiatedBy` column — schema.prisma:2386 declares it `initiatedBy String? // User ID; null when triggered by automation`, so null has a DEFINED meaning in this vocabulary. recovery.service.ts:256 writes `initiatedBy: req.initiatedBy ?? null`, and the route — the only caller — hardcodes `initiatedBy: undefined` with an unfinished TODO: listing-recovery.routes.ts:86-87 reads `// TODO: thread real user identity once auth is wired.` / `initiatedBy: undefined,` while `request.authUser` is populated by the global hook. So every operator-initiated Amazon delete-and-relist is stored, and returned by GET /products/:id/recover/events (listing-recovery.routes.ts:97-108), as having been triggered by automation. This is not a missing field: it is an actively wrong one. The parallel case: sync-control's SyncControlAudit is written with `actor` from `actorOf = (request) => request.user?.email ?? 'sync-control'` (sync-control.routes.ts:549-550), and `request.user` is never assigned anywhere in apps/api/src (/usr/bin/grep for `req.user =|request.user =|decorateRequest('user'` returns rc=1; positive control: `request.authUser =` matches 9 times, including rbac-hook.ts:51 and workspace-hook.ts:77) — the auth stack populates `authUser`, not `user`. So every CLOSE_OFFER/REOPEN_OFFER audit row, including the only reversible per-market delist in the product, is attributed to the literal string 'sync-control', indistinguishable from the cron.

##### Proposed fix
Fix both readers of the wrong field in one pass: `initiatedBy: request.authUser?.id ?? null` at listing-recovery.routes.ts:87, and `actorOf = (request) => request.authUser?.email ?? request.authUser?.id ?? null` at sync-control.routes.ts:549 — and change the `?? 'sync-control'` fallback to a distinct literal such as `'system:cron'` so an unattributed row cannot be confused with a named surface. Because the schema's comment makes null mean 'automation', add `initiatedBy` NOT NULL for route-originated events (or a companion `initiatedVia 'OPERATOR' | 'AUTOMATION'` discriminator) so the distinction is stated rather than inferred from a null. Add a vitest that injects a session and asserts the persisted row carries that user's id — a zero-change round trip cannot test this, so the test must flip the actor between two users and read both rows back. Surface it in the studio with the DS `KeyValue` component (components/index.ts:6) on the record drawer's history pane: 'Ended by — <name> · <when>', and where the record genuinely does not know, print 'the log does not record who' rather than a machine name, which is the honesty rule the studio's own auditEvents.ts:27-28 already applies.

#### The studio can never show the history of a lifecycle action: Activity reads the event store, lifecycle writes the audit log, and the one studio surface that reads the audit log is disabled

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens /products/GALE-JACKET/edit/studio?scope=amazon&market=IT, sees the IT row reading 'unlisted' where it used to be live, and goes to the Activity tab to find out what happened and when. They are told 'No attributed activity has been recorded in this scope.'

##### What happens today
The studio's Activity tab is backed solely by the event store: getWorkspaceActivity queries `prisma.productEvent` and nothing else (workspace-observations.ts:10-16), and readEvents.ts:71-120 renders exactly three event types measured on a live product — IMAGES_UPDATED, FLAT_FILE_IMPORTED, BULK_OP_APPLIED — with every other type falling to a humanised default. No lifecycle service writes a ProductEvent (PA-2: grep rc=1 across all five), so a delist, an end, an offer close, an alias archive or a hard delete can never appear there. The audit log, where bulk-hard-delete's row actually lands (products-catalog.routes.ts:1906), is exposed by GET /api/products/:id/activity (products-catalog.routes.ts:1345-1393) and by the /audit-log page (app-nav.ts:301, gated `audit.view` per permissions-manifest.ts:112) — the LEGACY edit page's tabs/ActivityTab.tsx uses it, but /usr/bin/grep over the whole _studio/ tree finds no caller of `/activity` and no link to `/audit-log`. The single studio surface that does read the audit log, images/publish/PublishHistory.tsx:56 (`/api/audit-log/search?entityType=Product&entityId=…`), is unreachable because ImagesTab.tsx:46 pins `const publicationAvailable = false`. And the coverage banner the operator IS shown says the rest 'remain in the audit log' (workspace-observations.ts:16) while offering no route to it. Even if they got there, the studio's own measured note records that the log cannot answer the question: auditEvents.ts:27-28 — 'userId is null on every one of the 71 entries, so this log cannot say who did anything'.

##### Proposed fix
Make the lifecycle audit row the studio's source of truth for 'what happened to this listing'. Server: add `GET /api/products/:id/listings/:channel/:marketplace/history` returning the union of AuditLog rows for `entityType:'ChannelListing'` on that coordinate (created by PA-2's fix), ListingRecoveryEvent rows, SyncControlAudit rows and OutboundSyncQueue delist rows, each as `{ at, action, actor: { userId, displayName } | null, channel, marketplace, aliasKey, before, after, source }`, mapped in the manifest to `F.listingsView` for reads so it does not require the separate `audit.view` grant. Client: merge it into the existing Activity tab as a second, labelled section rather than a new tab (§14.3 — a tab that cannot do anything must not be a tab), reusing the tab's current row shape: DS `Pill` for the verb, `KeyValue` for the before/after pair, `Banner` tone='warning' for the coverage note. Replace the current 'No attributed activity' empty state with a DS `EmptyState` that distinguishes 'nothing happened' from 'we cannot see it' — the could-not-measure vs measured-empty rule — and, until PA-1/PA-5 land, render the actor slot as 'the log does not record who' exactly as auditEvents.ts:27-28 already instructs, never as a machine name.

[critical]verifiedALLdata integrity risk

#### The whole-product channel cascade deletes its own queue rows inside the same transaction, so no delist ever runs — and nothing anywhere records that

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has finished with the GALE jacket. It is soft-deleted, sitting in the bin, live on Amazon IT and eBay IT. They select it, choose Delete permanently, and the confirm modal defaults to "Unpublish (recommended) — Pause the offer on each channel … Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing". They type DELETE. The response is ok:true with channelCascadeEnqueued: 2. The local rows are gone. The Amazon offer and the eBay ItemID are still live and still selling — and there is no queue row, no error, and no screen anywhere that says so.

##### What happens today
products-catalog.routes.ts:1880 creates the UNPUBLISH_LISTING/DELETE_LISTING rows with `productId: l.productId` and `channelListingId: l.id` INSIDE the same `$transaction` that hard-deletes the products at :1973. Both of those FKs are `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:6821 product, :6824 channelListing), so Postgres destroys the freshly-created queue rows at commit. `fireOutboundJobs(delistFireEntries)` then fires post-commit at :2003 against ids that no longer exist; the worker's `findUnique` returns null and it throws `Queue record ${queueId} not found` (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:104-110), BullMQ retries and the job dies. A second, independent defect on the same path would kill it even if the row survived: `fireOutboundJobs` puts only queueId/productId/syncType/source in job.data (outbound-enqueue.ts:49-62), but the worker reads `targetChannel` from **job.data**, not from the queue row it just loaded (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:86, 146) — every other field in that call comes from `queueRecord`. So dispatchChannelDelist receives `targetChannel: undefined`, falls to `default:` and returns `Unknown channel: undefined`, retryable:false (channel-delist.service.ts:118-124). The only other UI-reachable delist producers bypass the queue entirely and are best-effort (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:68-81 with a bare `catch {}`; ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:142-157 with a synthetic queueId). Read from source; not observed executing.

##### Proposed fix
Three changes, none of them UI. (1) The delist rows must outlive the product: build `delistRows` BEFORE the deleting transaction (or inside it with `productId: null, channelListingId: null` and the coordinate carried only in the row's own columns — targetChannel/targetRegion/externalListingId/payload, which is exactly what channel-delist.service.ts:31-38 already documents it reads). A queue row that is FK-bound to the thing it is cleaning up after cannot survive the cleanup. (2) The worker must read `targetChannel` from `queueRecord.targetChannel`, not from `job.data`, so it cannot disagree with the row it loaded — change bullmq-sync.worker.ts:146 to `queueRecord.targetChannel`; the fix is one word and closes the whole class. (3) Add a vitest at the route level asserting `outboundSyncQueue.count({ where: { syncType: { in: ['UNPUBLISH_LISTING','DELETE_LISTING'] } } })` is non-zero AFTER the transaction commits — the positive control this path has never had. UI side: the studio's DS `Banner` (tone="warning") on the channel scope should render whenever a delist row for this coordinate is PENDING or dead, so the operator's next screen tells them the channel side is unfinished.

- outbound-enqueue.ts:49-62: the job payload is exactly `{queueId, productId, syncType, source}`. No targetChannel. I checked a second producer (master-status.service.ts:272-279) — same four keys; no producer in apps/api/src puts targetChannel in job.data.

- channel-delist.service.ts:105 switches on `job.targetChannel`; :118-123 `default: { success:false, error: 'Unknown channel: ${job.targetChannel}', retryable:false }`. Confirmed.

No other queue-based producer, no alternate consumer.
- A cron backstop that would rescue it: outbound-sync.service.ts:683 `processPendingSyncs` selects PENDING rows at :703-704 (`syncType: { notIn: AD_SYNC_TYPES }`) — it has no delist branch at all (its dispatch switch is at :612 and :1848 destructures `product` from the row). Irrelevant here anyway, since the rows do not exist, but it means there is genuinely no second drain that could have covered this.
- Dead/superseded code: the route is live (registered at :1773), the modal that calls it is live — BulkActionBar.tsx:1097 `useState<...>('unpublish')` is the default, :1053-1055 `onConfirm` → `hardDeleteBulk(channelAction)`, :334-347 POSTs channelAction. The i18n strings the scenario quotes are en.json:5222-5223 verbatim. The web caller ignores the response body entirely (:344-348 only emits an invalidation), so channelCascadeEnqueued is never even shown.
- Existing coverage: `/usr/bin/grep -rln "channelCascadeEnqueued" apps packages` matches exactly ONE file — the route itself. No test asserts the rows survive.

Not observed executing (read-only audit, no API calls, no worker run) — but the mechanism is fully established from source and the DB-level constraint text, and the two defects are independent, so either alone is fatal.
Fix (2) is exactly right and is a one-word change at bullmq-sync.worker.ts:146 (`queueRecord.targetChannel`); it also removes a live disagreement between job.data and the row for the logging at :94/:304/:329/:411, which no producer populates.

A delist row with `productId: null` would go down the normal push path with a null product. So fix (1) must be paired with a delist branch (or an explicit skip) in processPendingSyncs, not only in the BullMQ worker — otherwise the instant lane works and the cron backstop crashes on the same row. Also note `productId`/`channelListingId` being nullable is only enforced by a comment ("At least one must be set", schema.prisma near :6820); nulling both is legal at the DB level but should be checked against any reader that assumes one is present.

It should assert the specific ids returned by createManyAndReturn are still readable AFTER the transaction resolves, and assert the job actually dispatched with a defined targetChannel — otherwise it tests leg 1 and leaves leg 2 uncovered.

The UI banner suggestion is sound but secondary, and note the response field the operator would need is already lying: channelCascadeEnqueued is computed at :1893 before the delete and never re-read (:1985), and BulkActionBar.tsx:344-348 discards the response body anyway. Whatever surfaces the unfinished channel work must read the queue, not that number.

[critical]verifiedAMAZONcorrectness risk

#### "Unpublish (recommended) — keeps the listing record so you can republish later" performs an irreversible Amazon SKU delete and keeps no record

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is clearing out last season's GALE jacket but expects to bring it back in autumn. They pick the recommended option, whose own text promises a pause that "keeps the listing record so you can republish later" and says "Amazon: discontinued". What they have actually authorised is a hard SP-API delete of the SKU offer, which starts a ~30-day cooldown during which re-creating the same SKU may fail or be silently held — and the ChannelListing row carrying flatFileSnapshot, overrideData and offerCloseSnapshot is destroyed by the same cascade, so there is nothing to republish from.

##### What happens today
Amazon `unpublish` is not implemented. channel-delist.service.ts:151-160 logs `Amazon UNPUBLISH falling back to DELETE (PATCH client TODO)` and falls straight through to `deleteListingsItem` at :162 — the identical call `delete` makes. The client documents the consequences it is about to cause: "The SKU enters a ~30-day cooldown — re-creating with the SAME SKU during that window may fail or be silently held" (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1121-1123). Nothing in that warning reaches the operator: the confirm modal's body text is the i18n string promising a reversible pause (en.json:5223), and the modal's radio defaults to 'unpublish' whenever any channel listing exists (BulkActionBar.tsx ~1097, 1117). Meanwhile the 'record kept' half is false on every path: the ChannelListing row is cascade-deleted with the Product (schema.prisma:1515). The genuinely reversible per-market mechanism exists one service away and is never used here — `closeMarketOffers`/`reopenMarketOffers` snapshot the verbatim offer into `offerCloseSnapshot` and replay it (amazon-market-offer.service.ts), reachable only from /fulfillment sync-control, never from the studio or the bin.

##### Proposed fix
Until `patchListingsItem(availability: DISCONTINUED)` exists in the client, the 'unpublish' option must not be offered as a reversible pause on Amazon. Two parts. (a) Copy + capability: route Amazon 'unpublish' to the reversible path that already works — `closeMarketOffers` (offerClosedAt + offerCloseSnapshot, replayed by `reopenMarketOffers`) — and reserve `deleteListingsItem` for the explicit 'Delete on channel' choice. If that routing is out of scope, `delistAmazon` must return `{ success:false, errorCode:'AMAZON_UNPUBLISH_NOT_IMPLEMENTED', retryable:false }` rather than silently escalating to a delete: a channel adapter may never perform a more destructive act than the one it was asked for. (b) Confirmation surface: the destructive choice belongs in the DS grid action registry — a `GridAction` with `danger: true`, `preflight()` returning an `ActionImpact` that itemises the real consequences ("the Amazon IT SKU offer is removed", "same-SKU re-listing may be refused for ~30 days", "the local listing record, its overrides and its flat-file snapshot are destroyed") and `ConfirmLevel: 'type-to-confirm'` with the real SKU as the phrase, rendered through `useActionConfirm` (grid/actions/registry.ts:69,167-198,215; grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx). That pattern itemises consequences instead of counting them, which is exactly what this modal's prose does not do.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:151-166
- apps/api/src/clients/amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1115-1128
- apps/web/src/lib/i18n/messages/en.json:5222-5225
- apps/web/src/app/products/_components/BulkActionBar.tsx:334-347
- packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:1515

##### Verifier
Every load-bearing citation checks out, and I could not find any path that rescues it.

1) The copy. `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/messages/en.json:5223` is verbatim: "Pause the offer on each channel — keeps the listing record so you can republish later. Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing; Shopify: status DRAFT." Label at :5222 is "Unpublish (recommended)". The modal is live, not dead: `BulkActionBar.tsx:550` opens it, :1046-1056 renders `HardDeleteConfirmModal` and passes the chosen `channelAction` into `hardDeleteBulk` (:334-347), and the radio state defaults to `'unpublish'` at :1097 and is re-set to `'unpublish'` whenever preflight returns any channel listing at :1117.

2) "Amazon: discontinued" is false. `channel-delist.service.ts:149-160`: on `action === 'unpublish'` the code only emits `logger.warn('Amazon UNPUBLISH falling back to DELETE (PATCH client TODO)')` and falls through to the same `amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem({ sellerId, sku, marketplaceId })` at :162 that `delete` uses. No DISCONTINUED patch anywhere on this path. The client's own doc comment at `amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1119-1123` states the consequence: "The SKU enters a ~30-day cooldown — re-creating with the SAME SKU during that window may fail or be silently held."

3) "Keeps the listing record" is false on every path, and the route knows it. `products-catalog.routes.ts:1773` is the endpoint; :1840-1848 comments "by then the local Product + ChannelListing are gone"; the enqueue happens at :1874-1893 (`syncType = 'UNPUBLISH_LISTING'`), then `tx.product.deleteMany` runs in the same transaction (~:1955), cascading `ChannelListing` via `schema.prisma:1516` (`onDelete: Cascade` — the finding said 1515, off by one, immaterial). `bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-152` confirms `UNPUBLISH_LISTING` dispatches to `dispatchChannelDelist`, skipping every downstream check. Only an AuditLog row (sku/name) and the queue row survive; `flatFileSnapshot`/`overrideData`/`offerCloseSnapshot` are gone.

4) The reversible mechanism is real and unreachable from here. `/usr/bin/grep -rn "closeMarketOffers|reopenMarketOffers|offerCloseSnapshot" apps/api/src apps/web/src packages` returns exactly `sync-control.routes.ts:31,818,819`, `amazon-market-offer.service.ts:70,84,184,215,247`, one migration and `schema.prisma:1595`. The only web callers of that route live under `apps/web/src/app/fulfillment/stock/sync-control/`. Nothing in the studio tree, the bin, or the delist service touches it.

Two things the finding UNDERSTATES, both strengthening it rather than refuting it:
- `deleteListingsItem` at `amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1143` reads `process.env.AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE` DIRECTLY, unlike every other write in the client which calls `getAmazonPublishMode()` (:519, :669, :792, :884). `amazon-publish-gate.service.ts:45-47` shows that resolver returns `'gated'` whenever the master flag `NEXUS_ENABLE_AMAZON_PUBLISH` is off. So the DELETE is the one SP-API write the master kill-switch does not gate, and `mode === 'sandbox'` also falls through to a real HTTP DELETE (:1143 only short-circuits on `dry-run`/`dryrun`).
- Conversely, the finding never mentions that the delete is env-conditional at all: with the default `AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE=dry-run` (`.env.example:96`) nothing reaches Amazon. The local record destruction is unconditional either way. I could not read prod env (read-only, no API calls), so the Amazon-side arm is "fires whenever the deployment is in live or sandbox mode", not "always fires" — that is why I downgrade critical to high rather than confirming as stated.
Part (b) is sound. Part (a)'s primary route is not implementable as written, and shipping it would fail silently.

(a) primary route — "route Amazon 'unpublish' to closeMarketOffers" cannot work on this path. closeMarketOffers resolves its target via loadRow (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:65-75), a prisma.channelListing.findFirst joined to product.sku, and persists onto cl.id (:177-196). By the time the delist job drains, both rows have been deleted inside the route's transaction (products-catalog.routes.ts:1840-1848 says so explicitly; product.deleteMany ~:1955). Every target would return SKIPPED_NO_LISTING (:98-101) and the operator would see "unchanged", not "closed". A reversible pause is structurally impossible *inside* a hard delete: there is nothing left to reopen. It also fail-closes on any FBA signal (:58-62), which the fix does not mention.

(a) fallback — returning `{success:false, errorCode:'AMAZON_UNPUBLISH_NOT_IMPLEMENTED', retryable:false}` from delistAmazon is the right immediate fix and the principle behind it ("a channel adapter may never perform a more destructive act than the one it was asked for") is correct. Note this leaves the offer live on Amazon after the local row is purged — an orphan listing — so it needs an explicit warning in the same modal, not just a queue-row failure nobody reads.

Missing from the fix, and arguably the real defect the owner is describing: the genuinely reversible per-market verb (closeMarketOffers/reopenMarketOffers) exists and is reachable only from /fulfillment/stock/sync-control. It should be surfaced in the studio as a first-class "close this market's offer" action taken while the product still exists — i.e. the alternative to deletion, not a mode of it. Fixing the copy without giving the operator that verb leaves them with no way to do what the copy currently pretends to do.

Also missing: deleteListingsItem should be routed through getAmazonPublishMode() like every other write in that client (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1143 vs :519/:669/:792/:884). As written, the single most destructive SP-API call is the only one the NEXUS_ENABLE_AMAZON_PUBLISH master switch does not gate, and 'sandbox' mode also falls through to a live HTTP DELETE.

Finally, the DS remediation should be checked against the memory pointer that the DS option list / registry has two copies — a GridAction added to grid/actions/registry.ts must be verified to be the registry this modal's surface actually consumes; I did not confirm that, and it is not a products-list surface today (BulkActionBar hand-rolls the modal with raw Tailwind at :1286-1352, which is itself a DS-conformance finding).

[critical]verifiedEBAYdata integrity risk

#### eBay delist always uses the PRIMARY account, and "item cannot be accessed" — the error a wrong account produces — is classified as success

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A workspace runs two eBay accounts. The GALE jacket's IT listing was created under the second account. An operator removes it. EndFixedPriceItem is called with the PRIMARY account's token; eBay answers error 291 "Item cannot be accessed" because that seller does not own the item. The queue row goes green SUCCESS, the console shows nothing wrong, and the listing stays live on eBay taking orders for stock we have just written off.

##### What happens today
`delistEbay` resolves its connection as `tryResolveConnection({ channel: 'EBAY', primary: true })` (channel-delist.service.ts:263) — the DECLARED primary, regardless of which account holds the ItemID it was handed. When the wrong token produces a refusal, `isAlreadyEndedError` tests the message against ALREADY_ENDED_PATTERNS (channel-delist.service.ts:223-239), which includes `/item cannot be accessed/` at :227 and `/invalid item/` at :231 — and the file's own comment at :218 states what that error means: "291 'Item cannot be accessed' — item gone / **seller doesn't own it**". Both readings land in the same bucket, and the bucket returns `{ success: true }` at :296. applyDelistResultToQueue then writes `syncStatus: 'SUCCESS', syncedAt` (:317-325). That this is a defect rather than a policy is shown by the sibling path in the same repo: `tryRemoveVariationFromListing` resolves the connection FROM the item — `tryResolveConnection({ itemId, marketplace })` (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:177) — under a comment reading "MAP.3 — DERIVED from the eBay ItemID being edited, so this is correct for two accounts as well as one". The same file's own history records the cost of a variation left live: "truth (Reconcile / verify) resurrected the row again and again" (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:163-166).

##### Proposed fix
(1) Derive the account from the coordinate, not from a default: `tryResolveConnection({ itemId, marketplace })` exactly as ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:177 does, and fail closed (`retryable:false`, `EBAY_DELIST_UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT`) when the ItemID resolves to no connection — never fall back to primary. (2) Split the idempotency bucket: only patterns that mean 'this listing is not live' (already ended / already closed / auction already closed) may return success. 'item cannot be accessed' and 'invalid item' are ownership/identity answers and must return `{ success:false, errorCode:'EBAY_DELIST_NOT_OURS', retryable:false }`. (3) Confirm the goal rather than inferring it: after any 'already ended' classification, call GetItem once and require SellingStatus.ListingStatus === 'Completed' before writing SUCCESS — a delist claiming success should have measured the state it claims, since this is the one place the queue's word is the only record. Studio side: surface the resulting `EBAY_DELIST_NOT_OURS` rows through the existing console with a DS `Banner` tone="danger" naming the account mismatch; syncQueue.ts's `causeOf` already keeps channel-supplied codes as the group name (syncQueue.ts:193-199), so a real code here renders correctly with no console change.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:258-271
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:212-239
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:288-297
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:313-325
- apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:173-180
- apps/api/src/services/connection-resolver.service.ts:113-117

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding says it says, and I could not find any path that rescues it.

CONFIRMED FACTS (all read directly):
1. `delistEbay` resolves the account as DECLARED primary, ignoring the coordinate it was handed: `channel-delist.service.ts:262-263` — comment `// MAP.3 — DECLARED.` then `const connection = await tryResolveConnection({ channel: 'EBAY', primary: true })`. I read the whole function (243-307): the ItemID (`job.externalListingId`) and `job.channelListingId` are never used to pick an account. The worker DOES hand it `channelListingId` (`bullmq-sync.worker.ts:142-150`), so a DERIVED handle is available and discarded.
2. `resolveConnection` supports two DERIVED forms that would answer correctly — `{ listingId }` (`connection-resolver.service.ts:190-199`, reads `ChannelListing.channelConnectionId`) and `{ itemId, marketplace }` (`:211-224`, reads `SharedListingMembership.channelConnectionId`). `SharedListingMembership.channelConnectionId` exists in the schema (`schema.prisma:17291-17292`). So the DECLARED choice is a choice, not a limitation.
3. The sibling path really does derive: `ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:175-177` — `// MAP.3 — DERIVED from the eBay ItemID being edited, so this is correct for two accounts as well as one` then `tryResolveConnection({ itemId, marketplace })`. The "resurrected the row again and again" comment is at `:163-166`.
4. The idempotency bucket does swallow ownership/identity answers: `ALREADY_ENDED_PATTERNS` at `channel-delist.service.ts:223-233` contains `/item cannot be accessed/i` (:227) and `/invalid item/i` (:231); the file's own doc comment at `:218` says 291 means "item gone / seller doesn't own it" — i.e. the author knew both readings collapse. `isAlreadyEndedError` (:236-239) → `return { success: true }` at `:290-296`.
5. The error text really can reach that matcher: `callTradingApi` throws `new Error('eBay ${callName} Failure: ${LongMessage…}')` on Ack=Failure (`ebay-trading-api.service.ts:277-281`), and eBay's 17/291 LongMessage carries exactly "Item cannot be accessed…". A test pins it: `ebay-trading-api.endlisting.vitest.test.ts:183-192` asserts `success === true` for "Item cannot be accessed", and `:216-224` for "Invalid item".
6. A `{success:true}` really writes a green row: `applyDelistResultToQueue` → `syncStatus: 'SUCCESS', syncedAt` (`channel-delist.service.ts:317-325`), called on the live worker path (`bullmq-sync.worker.ts:152`), not only in tests. Real enqueue site: `products-catalog.routes.ts:1879`.
7. No verification exists anywhere on the path: `/usr/bin/grep -rn "GetItem" channel-delist.service.ts ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts` → zero hits. And the reconcile job that might have caught it is itself DECLARED-primary (`ebay-status-reconcile.job.ts:78-92`), so a second account's still-live listing is invisible to it too.
8. Studio-side claim checked: `causeOf` keeps a channel-supplied code as the group name at `_studio/channel-ops/syncQueue.ts:193-199` — accurate.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: callers of the service (`/usr/bin/grep -rn "channel-delist" --include="*.ts"`) are only the worker, `amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:7` and `ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:35` — no wrapper re-resolves the account first; the code is not dead (the worker drains it, and `callTradingApi` REFUSES to fake success in production, `ebay-trading-api.service.ts:238-244`, so the real call is made when `NEXUS_EBAY_REAL_API=true`); no other tab/route/service delists eBay by a derived account except the flat-file variation path, which is a different operation.

WHERE THE FINDING OVERSTATES (why I corrected severity, not the verdict): the scenario asserts "a workspace runs two eBay accounts" as current fact. The database currently makes two ACTIVE eBay rows hard: the partial unique index is `ON "ChannelConnection" ("channelType", COALESCE("marketplace",'~'), COALESCE("externalAccountId",'~')) WHERE "isActive" = true` (`migrations/20260819a_map2_account_dimension/migration.sql:221-223`), and eBay rows have `marketplace = null` plus `externalAccountId` NULL "until MAP.4 adds eBay's identity scope" (`schema.prisma:6647-6651`) — two unidentified eBay accounts collide on ('EBAY','~','~'). MAP.4's identity scope IS now requested (`ebay-auth.service.ts:104-115`) and written when returned (`:361-363`), so the second account becomes admissible as soon as both accounts re-consent — but I cannot show from code that two are live today (and I am read-only, so I did not query the DB or any API). The false-SUCCESS arm, however, is live regardless of account count: any 291/17 answer — a stale or mis-recorded `externalListingId`, an alias pointing at an ItemID that is not ours — is written as a green delist with no state check, and the local ChannelListing is already gone by then (`bullmq-sync.worker.ts:134-140`).

So: mechanism confirmed, blast radius partly gated. High, not critical. The proposed fix is sound; item (3) (verify with GetItem before writing SUCCESS) is the part that fixes the arm that is live today, and item (1) should prefer `{ listingId }` when the queue row still has one and fall back to `{ itemId, marketplace }`, since the worker comment says the ChannelListing is usually already deleted by drain time.

[high]verifiedALLcorrectness risk

#### A failed delist is parked PENDING with no retry schedule, then re-routed through the UPDATE path, where it finishes as a green SUCCESS having sent nothing

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A delist for the GALE jacket on Amazon IT hits a transport failure — the SP-API call times out, so whether Amazon received the DELETE is genuinely unknown. A minute later the queue row reads SUCCESS with a syncedAt timestamp and the message "Skipped — empty patch (nothing to push)" is nowhere an operator will look. Nothing was ever re-sent, and the queue now asserts the removal completed.

##### What happens today
The worker's delist branch RETURNS on failure instead of throwing (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:150-157), so BullMQ never retries it — unlike the standard path, which throws at :421 to trigger a retry. `applyDelistResultToQueue` then writes `syncStatus: 'PENDING'` for any retryable failure (channel-delist.service.ts:333-342) and sets **no** `nextRetryAt` and **no** `holdUntil`. The 60s cron backstop selects every PENDING row with `holdUntil` null (outbound-sync.service.ts:701-709) and is not skipped — `buildBullMQSkip` only skips waiting/active/delayed jobs, and this job completed (sync.worker.ts:33-38). It dispatches through `dispatchSync`, which switches on `targetChannel` alone and **never inspects syncType** (outbound-sync.service.ts:607-619): there is no delist branch outside the BullMQ worker (verified: `/usr/bin/grep -rn 'DELETE_LISTING|UNPUBLISH_LISTING' apps/api/src` returns 9 non-test hits, and the only routing one is bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141). So a DELETE_LISTING row is handed to `syncToAmazon`, which builds a listing PATCH from a payload of `{source, channelAction, marketplace, externalParentId}` — no attributes — and returns `{ success: true, status: 'SKIPPED', message: 'Skipped — empty patch (nothing to push)' }` (outbound-sync.service.ts:1045-1059). The cron's success handler sees `result.success` true and `result.dryRun` undefined and writes `syncStatus: 'SUCCESS', syncedAt: new Date()` (:745-750). A genuinely unknown outcome has been converted into a recorded removal. Related and on the same branch: a dry-run delete already returns `success:true, dryRun:true` without any HTTP (amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1143-1155, default mode is 'dry-run'), and applyDelistResultToQueue ignores `dryRun` — dropping the rule the same worker enforces 170 lines away ("PD.3 — a dry-run/sandbox no-op published nothing; don't show it green", bullmq-sync.worker.ts:314-316).

##### Proposed fix
(1) Give the delist branch the retry contract the standard path already has: run the result through `computeFailureDisposition` (imported in the worker at :17 and used at :345 for every other syncType), write `nextRetryAt`, and `throw` on a retryable failure so BullMQ owns the retry and the dead-letter (`isDead`/`diedAt`) is reached on exhaustion. (2) Make the wrong path impossible rather than unlikely: `dispatchSync` should refuse a lifecycle syncType outright — `if (LIFECYCLE_SYNC_TYPES.has(item.syncType)) return { success:false, error:'Lifecycle sync types are dispatched by the delist worker only', retryable:false, errorCode:'LIFECYCLE_MISROUTED' }` — so a misrouted removal dead-letters loudly instead of reporting a push it never made. A shared `LIFECYCLE_SYNC_TYPES` constant exported from channel-delist.service.ts keeps the worker and the cron from drifting. (3) Honour PD.3 in `applyDelistResultToQueue`: `syncStatus: result.dryRun ? 'SKIPPED' : 'SUCCESS'`, the same expression already at bullmq-sync.worker.ts:316. (4) A transport failure is an unknown outcome, not a failed write: before re-sending a delete, re-read the channel (GetItem / getListingsItem) and treat 'already gone' as done — the eBay branch already has this instinct (channel-delist.service.ts:288-297), it just has no verification behind it.

- apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158
- apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:314-316
- apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:313-343
- apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:607-619
- apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:701-709
- apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:745-750
- apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync.service.ts:1045-1059
- apps/api/src/workers/sync.worker.ts:24-44
- apps/api/src/clients/amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1143-1155

##### Verifier
Confirmed end to end from the code I opened. (1) The worker's delist branch calls dispatchChannelDelist + applyDelistResultToQueue and on failure does `failureCount++; return { status:'FAILED' }` (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158) — no throw, so BullMQ never retries; the standard path 260 lines later does throw for a retryable failure (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:428 `throw new Error(syncResult.error) // BullMQ will retry`) and runs computeFailureDisposition (:341-345). ▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens the GALE jacket, eBay · IT scope, Needs attention. The console shows a group of dead writes whose cause is an eBay auth failure — the account token had expired. They re-link the eBay account in Settings. Now they want to re-run those writes. There is no control on the screen that does it: the only buttons are "Go to row" and "Open sheet". The writes stay dead forever unless someone finds /sync-logs/outbound-queue.

`ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx` issues exactly two fetches, both GETs (`/api/listings/publish-readiness` :124 and `/api/products/:id/sync-queue` :156); `/usr/bin/grep` for POST in that file returns nothing against a positive control of 2 `fetch(` hits. Its server half says so in its own header: "Read-only: nothing here enqueues, retries or cancels" (sync-queue.service.ts:1-3). The console even anticipates the gesture it cannot serve — "An operator looking at 36 dead writes will reach for Retry" (ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:224-230) — and answers it with a sentence about the publish gate instead of a verb. The capability is already built and already used elsewhere: `POST /api/outbound-queue/:id/retry` (outbound-queue.routes.ts:141), `/cancel` (:211), `/bulk-retry` (:231), `/bulk-cancel` (:277), consumed by InboxClient.tsx:129-160 and ControlTowerClient.tsx:714. `/usr/bin/grep -rn 'outbound-queue|/retry|/cancel'` over the whole `_studio/` tree returns zero hits (positive control: 'sync-queue?' 1 hit, 'Retry' 4 hits, all of them view-reload buttons). Two traps a naive wiring would hit: the retry endpoint re-enqueues a BullMQ job ONLY when `row.channelListingId` is set (outbound-queue.routes.ts:166-180) — a delist row whose listing is gone gets flipped to PENDING and enqueued nowhere, landing it in ER-4's wrong-path drain; and `EBAY_DELIST_NO_CONNECTION` / `EBAY_DELIST_AUTH_ERROR` are marked `retryable:false` (channel-delist.service.ts:266-281), so an expired token — the most recoverable failure there is — dead-letters on attempt one.

##### Proposed fix
Add two verbs at the CAUSE-GROUP level, not per row — the console's whole thesis is that 2,553 rows are three problems (syncQueue.ts:9-14), so 'Retry these 36' is the right granularity and 'retry row 14 of 36' is not. Use the DS grid action registry rather than hand-rolled buttons: two `GridAction`s with `scope: 'selection'`, `preflight()` returning an ActionImpact that names the coordinate and the count, `ConfirmLevel: 'confirm'` for Retry and `'confirm'` + danger for Cancel, rendered through `useActionConfirm` (grid/actions/registry.ts:167-198; ActionConfirm.tsx) — the same registry MasterSheet and ChannelSheet already mount. `available()` must return `disabled(reason)` — never hidden — when `gateNote(mode)` is non-null, so the existing "re-running these writes would be refused by the same gate that failed them" sentence becomes the disabled reason instead of a paragraph the operator reads and then clicks anyway. API: `POST /api/products/:id/sync-queue/retry` body `{ ids: string[] }` living beside the read in product-studio.routes.ts, delegating to the existing outbound-queue logic but (a) scoped to the product+coordinate, and (b) fixing the two traps above — re-enqueue from the row's own `targetChannel` when `channelListingId` is null, and treat `EBAY_DELIST_AUTH_ERROR`/`NO_CONNECTION` as retryable-after-operator-action rather than terminal. Note for whoever builds it: the DS Toast has no action slot (components/Toast.tsx:13-16) and there is no undo pattern in the DS, so a cancel must be confirmed up front — it cannot be offered back afterwards.

#### Nothing compares our listing state with the channel's, so every silent failure above stays silent — and the studio shows no reconciliation at all

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The GALE jacket's Amazon IT removal failed in one of the ways above — the queue row was cascade-deleted (ER-1), or it went green without sending (ER-4), or eBay answered with the wrong account's error (ER-3). Weeks pass. Our DB has no ACTIVE listing for IT; Amazon still shows the offer and keeps taking orders. Nothing detects the divergence, and no screen an operator opens will mention it.

##### What happens today
The one job named for this is DB-internal only: sync-drift-detection.job.ts compares `ChannelListing.price/quantity` against `Product.basePrice` and the computed available (`:1-23`), and states in its own header that re-fetching from the marketplace is NOT what it does — "Re-fetch from the marketplace. That's a future P.2.next commit" (:30-34). It never looks at existence. `channel-reconciliation.service.ts:1-13` does call the channel, but only for order counts, revenue and FBA units, Amazon-only, on an admin route. The only true existence reconcile is eBay's — `ebay-status-reconcile.job.ts`, which maps PUBLISHED→ACTIVE, UNPUBLISHED→DRAFT, 404→REMOVED — and it is gated default-OFF behind `NEXUS_ENABLE_EBAY_STATUS_RECONCILE_CRON !== '1'` (:73-76, documented :22-25). There is no Amazon equivalent. In the studio, `/usr/bin/grep -rnE 'sync-health|drift|reconcil'` over `_studio/` returns only code comments using those words about type-drift — zero fetches, zero surfaces (positive control in the same run: 'sync-queue?' matches ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:156). The console names three sources it is not showing (`DORMANT_SOURCES`, syncQueue.ts:296-300: ListingIssue, AmazonSuppression, validationStatus) and its coverage note explains what the product scope cannot see — but neither says the more important thing: that the channel has not been asked.

##### Proposed fix
A per-coordinate liveness check the operator can run on demand, plus a cron that runs it after every lifecycle write. API: `GET /api/products/:id/channel-state?channel=&market=&accountId=` returning `{ nexus: { listingStatus, isPublished, externalListingId, offerClosedAt }, channel: { exists, status, checkedAt } | { unavailable: reason }, verdict: 'agrees' | 'live-but-we-say-gone' | 'gone-but-we-say-live' | 'unknown' }` — backed by `getListingsItem` for Amazon and GetItem for eBay. The `unknown` member is load-bearing: 'we could not ask' must never render as 'they agree'. UI: a DS `Banner` at the top of the channel scope (tone danger for 'live-but-we-say-gone', warning for the reverse, neutral+quiet for 'unknown'), with the check re-run by the Reload item that CH.1 already puts in the single sheet `⋯` (SheetToolbar.tsx:15-30) — no new chrome, which keeps D11/§14.1's identical-bar rule. Enqueue the same check as a follow-up row after every UNPUBLISH_LISTING/DELETE_LISTING completes, so the delist lane verifies its own claim instead of asserting it; that single addition would have caught ER-1, ER-3 and ER-4 without any of them being understood first.

[critical]verifiedALLdata integrity risk

#### Switching market/scope orphans in-flight autosaves: the header, the ledger and the leave guard are all per-coordinate

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is fixing bullet points on a jacket in Amazon IT. They type into `bullet_point1`, and while the header still reads "Saving 1…" they flip the Market listbox to DE to check the German copy. The IT write is refused by the server (a length cap, or a 409 because a pricing job moved the listing). They never see it. They then click "Return to Products" and are not prompted. The IT bullet point was never saved and nothing on screen ever said so.

##### What happens today
The save ledger is keyed by the full coordinate — `useSaveMachine(JSON.stringify([product.id, scope, market, locale, accountId, listingId]))` (contracts.tsx:1045) — and `createWorkspaceSaveStore.forScope(key)` returns only that key's entry, with no aggregate accessor over the other entries (workspaceSave.ts:6-21). `SaveIndicator` renders `useStudioSave()`, i.e. the current coordinate's ledger only (SaveIndicator.tsx:30). The navigation guard reads the same single state — `useInFlightGuard(save.state)` (contracts.tsx:1046) → `pendingWrites(state)` (saveState.ts:101-110, 547) — so both the `beforeunload` handler (contracts.tsx:563-572) and the capture-phase anchor interceptor (contracts.tsx:574-611) disarm the instant the coordinate changes. Meanwhile `StudioTabHost` remounts the surface on exactly that key (StudioTabHost.tsx:79), so the ChannelSheet unmounts and `writer.destroy()` runs (ChannelSheet.tsx:563-566), which bumps `generation` (sheetWriter.ts:596) so the in-flight batch's result is dropped at `if (generation !== this.generation) return` (sheetWriter.ts:361) — no version advance, no `onConflict`, no `onSettled`, no reconcile. The commit closure still reports `resolved` into the OLD ledger entry (ChannelSheet.tsx:503), so the failure is recorded in a ledger nothing is rendering. Worse, when the write was `unreachable`, ChannelSheet.tsx:502 parks it in `unsettledWrites` and never calls `resolved` at all; `onReconciled` can no longer fire because the reconcile was dropped at sheetWriter.ts:361 — so that coordinate's ledger is stuck at `{kind:'saving', pending:1}` for the life of the page, and returning to it re-arms the nav guard permanently (clearable only by Reload, ChannelSheet.tsx:612).

##### Proposed fix
Make the ledger workspace-wide, not coordinate-wide. (a) Add `anyPending()` / `entriesWithWork()` to `createWorkspaceSaveStore` (workspaceSave.ts) that folds every entry in the `entries` map, and feed THAT to `useInFlightGuard` — the guard must arm on any in-flight write on this product, whatever coordinate produced it. (b) Gate the coordinate switch itself: `setMarket`/`setScope`/`setAccount`/`setLocale` in contracts.tsx are not anchor clicks, so `shouldInterceptLeave` never sees them; route them through the DS grid-action confirm (`useActionConfirm` + an `ActionImpact` of level `confirm`, grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx) reusing the exact shape of `reloadImpact` — "1 unsaved change on Amazon · IT — leave that market anyway?" with the pending/refused/unknown breakdown as `consequences`. (c) Render carried-over work from other coordinates as a DS `Banner` (tone `warning`) in the StudioFrame, one line per coordinate with a link that restores that coordinate — `2 changes not saved on Amazon · IT`. (d) Keep the reconcile loop alive across the remount by hoisting the writer's unreachable-write recovery into the frame-level store rather than the tab component, so a coordinate switch cannot cancel the only mechanism that can answer "did that write land?".

Every load-bearing citation checks out, and I could not find any surface that closes the gap.

CONFIRMED MECHANICS (all read directly):

No aggregate accessor. `workspaceSave.ts:5-22` exposes exactly one method, `forScope(key)`, returning `ledgerState(entry.ledger)` for that key. `/usr/bin/grep -rn "forScope|anyPending|entriesWithWork" apps/web/src` returns only contracts.tsx:294 and workspaceSave.vitest.test.ts — i.e. exactly one production caller, with the single coordinate key. This is a set claim established with /usr/bin/grep, not the shell function.
3. Nothing renders another coordinate's entry. The only consumers of `useStudioSave()` are SaveIndicator.tsx:30, StudioBar.tsx:14 and import/ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:28 (`/usr/bin/grep`), all reading the same single context value. StudioHeader.tsx:85 mounts `<SaveIndicator/>`; there is no cross-coordinate banner anywhere.
4. The guard is per-coordinate and deliberately exempts the studio's own controls. `pendingWrites` (saveState.ts:101-110) reads only that state; `shouldInterceptLeave` (saveState.ts:151-163) returns false when `dest.pathname === currentPathname`, documented at saveState.ts:144-146 as "the exemption that stops the guard firing on the studio's own controls". A Market listbox is not an anchor at all (`a.href == null` → false), so nothing intercepts it.

The one existing coordinate-switch gate does NOT cover autosave. `push()` (contracts.tsx:850-857) blocks scope/market/locale/account/listing/tab changes when `canChangeEditor()` is false, backed by `registerScopeChangeGuard` (contracts.tsx:630-634). `/usr/bin/grep -rn "registerScopeChangeGuard"` gives every registration: ManageAxesDialog:88, MappingDock:146, ShopifyLinkedWorkspace:48, ShopifyDraftCell:39, PresentationTab:57, productMediaColumn:31, and ChannelSheet:1984 — which registers `() => !aliasCreationPending.current` only. No registration anywhere reads `writer.pending`; MasterSheet registers none (`/usr/bin/grep` on MasterSheet.tsx returns only writer.pending at :565 and :600). So an in-flight cell autosave does not block the switch. This is the strongest refutation avenue and it fails.
6. Remount + generation drop. StudioTabHost.tsx:79 keys `<Surface>` on `[product.id, tab, scope, market, locale, accountId, listingId]`. ChannelSheet.tsx:563-566 is `useEffect(() => { writer.arm(); return () => writer.destroy() }, [writer])`. `destroy()` sets `this.generation++` (sheetWriter.ts:596), and the in-flight batch returns at sheetWriter.ts:361 `if (generation !== this.generation) return` — before the tracker paint, before `onSettled` (line 382) and before the `reconcile()` call (line 385-387). `reconcile()` itself re-checks generation at 458 and 463.

The refusal lands in an invisible ledger. `reporterRef` (ChannelSheet.tsx:239-241) survives unmount and the reporter closes over its own entry (workspaceSave.ts:3-4 says so explicitly), so `resolved(...)` at ChannelSheet.tsx:504 files the failure under the OLD key — real, retained, and rendered by nothing while the operator is on DE.

The stuck-pending case is real. `commitChannelRow` catches a thrown fetch and returns `{ok:false, unreachable:true}` (useChannelSheet.ts:405) rather than throwing, so ChannelSheet.tsx:503 parks it in `unsettledWrites` and never calls `resolved`; the only thing that could ever resolve it is `onReconciled` (ChannelSheet.tsx:513-519), which the generation check at sheetWriter.ts:361 has already prevented. That key's ledger keeps `inFlight.size === 1` forever → `ledgerState` returns `{kind:'saving', pending:1}` (saveState.ts:88) → the guard re-arms whenever the operator returns to that coordinate. Reload does clear it (ChannelSheet.tsx:613 → `ledgerCleared`), because `subject` (rows.ts:142) excludes `instanceId` and so matches across remounts — the finding's "clearable only by Reload" is correct.

MIS-STATEMENTS (all immaterial to the defect): the citation "saveState.ts:547" does not exist — that file is 211 lines (the substantive citation, 101-110, is right); ChannelSheet is 502/503→503/504 and 612→613, each off by one.

SEVERITY CORRECTION, hence not critical: the typed edit is still SENT (destroy() flushes queued cells, sheetWriter.ts:597-606), the failure is not destroyed but merely unrendered and reappears if the operator returns to that coordinate, and no server-side data is corrupted. The permanent stuck-`saving` state needs the unreachable/thrown-fetch branch specifically. Real, silent, and against this project's own honest-UI bar — but "high", not "critical".
Parts (a), (b) and (d) are right in substance; (c) is right in spirit but needs a correctness caveat.
- (a) Aggregate accessor over `entries` and feed it to `useInFlightGuard`: correct, and cheap. Note the guard also drives `registerProfileChanges` (contracts.tsx:551-561), whose `save()` polls `pendingRef` for 30s — an aggregate there is strictly better than today's per-coordinate value.

So the proposal's `useActionConfirm`/`reloadImpact` shape is needed anyway, and it belongs inside `push`'s guard path, not bolted on beside it, or the two gates will disagree.

Rendering both as "2 changes not saved" would restate the exact per-attempt dishonesty saveState.ts:29-32 was built to kill. The banner needs the three-way breakdown (refused / in flight / unknown) the ledger already distinguishes.
- (d) Hoisting the reconcile loop above the remount is the only part that actually recovers the lost verdict, and it is the hardest: `reconcile` reads through `opts.readBack`, which in ChannelSheet closes over `channelScopeUrl({productId, channel, marketplace, accountId, locale})` (ChannelSheet.tsx:509-513) and `recoverSheetRow`. Hoisting it means the frame-level store must own a coordinate-tagged read closure, and its verdict must be applied to a tracker/grid that may no longer exist — so the design has to define what a verdict does when there is no surface (record it in that coordinate's ledger entry and let the banner in (c) show it), otherwise it just moves the drop one layer up.

#### A 409 leaves the operator two options — lose their own edit or silently clobber the other writer's — because nothing ever shows the stored value

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Two merchandisers are both in the studio on the same jacket, Amazon DE. A edits `bullet_point2` and it saves. B, who loaded the sheet two minutes earlier, edits the same cell. B's write comes back 409 and the cell turns red with "Someone else changed this listing (now v83). Review the edit before reloading." B has no way to see what A wrote. B retypes the same text — and it saves, overwriting A's bullet point with no record anywhere that A's value ever existed.

##### What happens today
On the channel scope the client adopts the server's version from the SAME response that refused the write, and does it before the 409 branch is even reached: `if (versionOf === 'channelListing' && raw !== undefined && row.listing) row.listing.version = raw` (useChannelSheet.ts:333), with the 409 handled at :339-357. On master the same thing happens via `version = versionFromBody(body)` in the 409 branch (masterWrite.ts:174-178), applied by the writer at `if (typeof result.version === 'number') this.versions.set(rowId, result.version)` (sheetWriter.ts:362). This is deliberate and documented as "so the writer stays able to retry instead of stuck one version behind" (sheetWriter.ts:113-118, useChannelSheet.ts:343) — but it means the CAS guard degrades to exactly one refusal followed by unconditional last-writer-wins. The refusal copy says "Review the edit", and the only review verb is Reload, which explicitly destroys the operator's typed value (reloadGuard.ts:60-67: "Reloading replaces them with the stored values and clears the refusals"). No surface in the studio ever renders the conflicting stored value beside the typed one. On the channel scope there is not even a row-level signal that the conflict was a conflict rather than a validation refusal: `onConflict: () => {}` (ChannelSheet.tsx:506), where master and Variants both surface `N rows changed elsewhere — refresh` (MasterSheet.tsx:1835-1839, variants/family/FamilyVariants.tsx:616) — a D11 "same UI on every scope" break as well.

##### Proposed fix
Turn the 409 into a per-cell resolution, not a per-cell refusal. (1) On conflict, have the host issue the QUIET scoped read it already owns — `readBack` → `recoverSheetRow` (ChannelSheet.tsx:507-511) — for the conflicting row only, and store the stored value beside the typed one on the tracker mark. (2) Render the choice in the DS `Drawer` `overlay` slot (components/Drawer.tsx, `.nds-drawer-ov`) when the record drawer is docked, or a DS `Modal` size `sm` otherwise: two labelled panels, "Stored (v83, changed 14:52)" and "Your edit", with three buttons — Keep mine (re-sends with the fresh version), Keep theirs (drops the typed value and clears the mark), Merge (opens the cell editor seeded with theirs). (3) Wire `onConflict` on the channel scope to the same `conflicts` state master uses, so both scopes show the identical `N rows changed elsewhere — refresh` control (D11). (4) Do NOT adopt the server version until the operator has chosen: move the `row.listing.version = raw` assignment (useChannelSheet.ts:333) inside the non-409 path, and let "Keep mine" be the only thing that advances it. No new endpoint is needed — the existing `GET /api/products/:id/studio/sheet` scoped read supplies the stored row.

#### An unreachable write plus a listing row that changed identity locks the row out of saving forever, under a false "Connection lost" message

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is editing a jacket on eBay IT. The API restarts mid-save, so their `ebay_title` write dies on the wire and the writer enters its recovery loop. While it retries, the nightly eBay status reconcile (or a per-market flat-file remove, which hard-deletes the ChannelListing row) replaces the listing row for that coordinate. From then on the operator can type into that row all afternoon: every cell paints "saving", nothing is ever sent, and the footer says the connection is lost while every other request on the page succeeds.

##### What happens today
When a commit is unreachable the writer starts `reconcile()` (sheetWriter.ts:386-388, 441-502). While a row is in `unreachableRows`, both `schedule()` (sheetWriter.ts:264) and `flushRow()` (sheetWriter.ts:293) return early — so every subsequent edit is queued and never sent, after `set()` has already painted each cell `saving` (sheetWriter.ts:249). The loop only exits when `readBack` returns a non-null snapshot. The channel `readBack` is `recoverSheetRow` (ChannelSheet.tsx:507-511), which returns `null` — not "no match" — whenever the row cannot be re-identified: the row id/alias is absent from the page (sheetRecovery.ts:19-20), or the listing id differs from the one the write was made against (sheetRecovery.ts:21, `row.listing?.id !== request.row.listing.id`). A `null` read is treated as "still unreachable": the loop repaints every outstanding cell `unknown` with "Connection lost — checking whether this saved…" and backs off, capped at 30s, `while (!this.destroyed)` (sheetWriter.ts:493-500). There is no attempt ceiling and no branch that distinguishes "the read did not answer" from "the read answered and the row is gone". `writer.unreachable` then keeps the footer's offline note lit (ChannelSheet.tsx:2201-2202). This is the `could not measure` vs `measured empty` conflation the file's own comments warn about, and it is reachable by the Owner's own per-market removal flows, which hard-delete ChannelListing rows.

##### Proposed fix
Make `readBack` return a three-state answer instead of `T | null`: `{ kind: 'unreachable' } | { kind: 'gone', reason } | { kind: 'row', … }`. `recoverSheetRow` already knows which of its guards fired — a transport failure (ChannelSheet.tsx:509 `!response.ok`) is `unreachable`, while a 200 whose page no longer contains the row or whose listing id changed (sheetRecovery.ts:19-21) is `gone`. On `gone`, the writer must STOP the loop, release `unreachableRows` so the row can be edited and saved again, and hand the host a terminal outcome. Surface that outcome as a DS `Banner` (tone `warning`) above the grid: "This listing was replaced while your change was in flight. Your edit was not confirmed against the new listing — review it before saving again", with a `Button variant="link"` running the existing `onReload` through `reloadImpact`. Additionally give the loop a ceiling (e.g. 10 minutes of null reads) after which it reports `unknown` terminally rather than claiming an outage indefinitely — the footer's offline note is a page-level claim about the network and must not be produced by a row-identity mismatch.

#### The studio's live pipe refreshes only the readiness score, so the ScopeBar updates while the grid beneath it silently goes stale

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket open on the Amazon IT channel sheet, reviewing attributes. While the tab sits open, the nightly sync pulls a new title from Amazon and the repricer changes the price. The Amazon pill in the scope bar visibly re-scores. The grid under it keeps showing the values read when the page loaded. So the freshest thing on the screen is the summary pill (StudioBar.tsx:19-21 reads the SSE-refreshed readiness) and the stalest is the editable data. The legacy eBay cockpit it replaced had exactly this capability and said so in words — `CrossTabChangeToast.tsx:59` "This listing changed elsewhere", with a Refresh button and a 30s auto-dismiss. The studio's only "what changed elsewhere" mechanism is Reload plus the 409 on write, which SheetToolbar.tsx:247 states outright.

##### Proposed fix
Have the sheet subscribe to the pipe that is already open. In `useChannelSheet`/`useMasterSheet`, add `useInvalidationChannel(['product.updated','listing.updated','channel-pricing.updated'], …)` filtered to this product and coordinate, and set a `staleSince` timestamp rather than refetching under the operator's hands. Render it as transient STATUS in the sheet toolbar's `trailing` slot — which CH.1 reserves for exactly this ("a staleness pill", SheetToolbar.tsx:105) — as a DS `Pill tone="warning" size="sm"` reading `Changed elsewhere · 2m ago` wrapped in an `InfoTip` naming what changed, plus the existing Reload item in the one `⋯` overflow. Auto-refresh silently ONLY when the sheet has nothing at risk, reusing the predicate the save path already uses (`writer.pending === 0 && !tracker.hasUnconfirmedChanges && getEditingCells().length === 0`, ChannelSheet.tsx:534-538); otherwise leave the pill standing and let the operator choose, so a background refresh can never eat typing. No new API is needed — the SSE pipe and the scoped sheet read both exist.

#### No lifecycle or destructive verb flushes the pending autosave first — a record restore can be silently undone by the keystroke that preceded it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator on the shared scope notices the jacket's description was mangled by an import. They type a quick correction into `name`, then immediately open the record drawer's History and restore yesterday's version of the description and name. The drawer says the restore succeeded and the header says "Saved". The 40ms-old queued autosave then lands on top of the restored record, putting the mangled state back — and the restore's audit row says the restore worked.

##### What happens today
Set claim, verified with /usr/bin/grep over the whole `_studio/` tree: `.flush()` is called in exactly ONE place — `await writer.flush()` before a whole-list reset confirmation (ChannelSheet.tsx:639), whose own comment explains why it is needed ("Save earlier edits before presenting the list being replaced"). Nothing else flushes. `restoreRecord` issues `POST /api/products/:id/restore` with `expectedVersion: row.version` directly, with no flush and no check of `writer.pending` (RecordDrawer.tsx:247-255), and `row.version` is the drawer's copy from the last page read, not `writer.versionOf(rowId)` which the writer has been advancing on every save (sheetWriter.ts:362) — so the CAS token it sends can already be behind the operator's own session. Every family verb is in the same position: `delete-variant` `run` calls `ops.deleteVariant` with no flush (familyActions.ts:478-485), as do `unlink` (:215), `reparent` (:264), `promote` (:309) and `demote` (:527). The writer's queue holds edits for up to `DEFAULT_SHEET_FLUSH_MS` (sheetWriter.ts:166) and serialises in-flight batches per row, so there is always a window in which a structural or lifecycle write and a cell write to the same row race with no ordering anywhere.

##### Proposed fix
Put the flush in the ENGINE, not at each call site (per the grid-chrome-lives-in-the-engine rule). Add a `beforeRun` step to `runAction` (design-system/grid/actions/runAction.ts) between CONFIRM and RUN that awaits a host-supplied `settle()` — the studio passes `() => writer.flush()` — and make `preflight` report any still-pending cells on the subject rows as an `ActionImpact.findings` entry of severity `warning` ("2 unsaved cell edits on this row will be saved before this runs"), so the confirmation the operator reads is true. For the drawer restore, which is not a grid action, do the same explicitly: `await writer.flush()` before the POST, send `expectedVersion: writer.versionOf(row.id) ?? row.version`, and — because a restore is exactly the kind of write another editor can be racing — render its 409 (RecordDrawer.tsx:256-259) through the same conflict surface proposed in CC-2 rather than a message that only says "reload and try again".

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/ChannelSheet.tsx:639
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/drawer/RecordDrawer.tsx:247
