- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/familyActions.ts:478
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/familyActions.ts:215
- apps/web/src/design-system/grid/editors/sheetWriter.ts:166
- apps/web/src/design-system/grid/editors/sheetWriter.ts:362

##### Verifier
The mechanical facts are right and the harm is not. Verified: /usr/bin/grep over _studio and design-system/grid finds exactly one non-test `.flush()` — ChannelSheet.tsx:640; RecordDrawer.tsx:247-255 POSTs the restore with `expectedVersion: row.version` and no flush; familyActions.ts:215-218 and :478-485 call ops.unlink / ops.deleteVariant with no flush; DEFAULT_SHEET_FLUSH_MS = 40 at sheetWriter.ts:166. But the stated failure — the queued autosave silently landing ON TOP of the restore — requires the late write to pass CAS after the restore bumped the version, and it cannot. The writer always sends a version: it is seeded from the sheet read (useMasterSheet.ts:218 `writer.seed(next.rows.map(r => ({ id: r.id, version: r.version, row: r })))`, ChannelSheet.tsx:573 likewise) and sent on every batch (sheetWriter.ts:345 → masterWrite.ts:158). The only path that would hand the writer the POST-restore version is `onRestoredExternally` (RecordDrawer.tsx:114, 605-608, documented at :109-113 as 'Feed it to SheetWriter.seed()') — and I checked every consumer: the sole `<RecordDrawer>` mount is StudioDock.tsx:247, and neither MasterSheet.tsx:1916-1936 nor ChannelSheet.tsx:2229-2269 passes `onRestoredExternally`; /usr/bin/grep finds no other reference in apps/web/src. So a write queued before the restore carries the pre-restore version and is REFUSED with a visible 409, not silently applied. The finding's own premise ('the CAS token it sends can already be behind') is the safe-fail direction: it produces a spurious refusal, not a clobber, and the finding's 'no ordering anywhere' is wrong — the version guard IS the ordering, for editor-versus-editor writes, which is exactly the pair in the scenario (sheetWriter.ts:27-38). Same for the family verbs: a cell write racing a delete either lands before it or is refused against a missing row; no arm demonstrated where the structural op is undone. Refuted as stated. What IS real here, and would be a correctly-scoped finding, is narrower and different: `onRestoredExternally` is documented as the host's refetch/reseed hook and NO host wires it, so after a successful restore the sheet neither refetches nor learns the new version — the operator's next cell edit takes a 409 they did not cause, which is precisely what RecordDrawer.tsx:264-275 (#224) was written to prevent.
An engine-level `beforeRun` settle step is defensible on its own merits (the confirmation text would then be true), but it is not justified by the harm claimed here, and the drawer half of the fix — flush + `writer.versionOf(row.id)` — would if anything make the clobber the finding fears POSSIBLE by aligning the tokens. The change actually worth making is wiring `onRestoredExternally` from both sheets into `writer.seed()` + reload.

An operator on Amazon IT types a bullet point that exceeds the length cap. The cell goes red — correct. At the same moment the Amazon pill in the scope bar stops showing the listing's readiness score and shows a blocked state carrying the cell's refusal sentence. The operator reads it as "Amazon IT can't be listed", and the actual readiness percentage — the thing that answers whether it can be listed — is gone from the screen until the refusal is cleared.

##### What happens today
`StudioBar` overrides the readiness of the CURRENT scope with the save ledger: `if (id === scope && save.kind === 'error') return { pct: null, state: 'blocked', note: save.message }` and `if (id === scope && save.kind === 'saving') return 'loading'` (StudioBar.tsx:16-22). `save.message` is the server's verbatim refusal for one cell (saveState.ts:87, 200-209). So a per-cell, transient, coordinate-scoped fact replaces a per-listing, durable one in the same pixel, and destroys the readiness number rather than sitting beside it. It compounds CC-1: because the ledger is per coordinate, moving the Market listbox to DE makes the pill revert to the real score and the refusal disappear entirely, even though the IT refusal is still outstanding. The refusal already has two honest homes on this screen — the `SaveIndicator` in the header (SaveIndicator.tsx:70-80) and the footer's refused count with its "show refused only" toggle (ChannelSheet.tsx:2201-2207) — so this is a third rendering of the same event, placed in the one slot reserved for a different question.

##### Proposed fix
Remove both save-state overrides from `scored()` (StudioBar.tsx:17-18) and let the `ScopeBar` pill answer only its own question — the listing's readiness, from `useScopeReadiness()`. If a scope needs to advertise unsaved work, add it as a separate affordance on the same item rather than replacing the score: extend `ScopeBarItem` (design-system/patterns/ScopeBar.tsx) with an optional `badge?: { tone: Tone; label: string; title: string }` and render a small DS `Pill tone="warning"` ("1 unsaved") beside the score. Combined with CC-1's workspace-wide ledger, that badge then works for EVERY scope and market with outstanding work, not just the one currently selected — which is the behaviour that would actually have caught the lost IT edit.

#### A scheduled or bulk "take it down" (STATUS → INACTIVE) sends Amazon an EMPTY patch and records the push as SUCCESS — the offer stays buyable

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator sells a padded jacket on Amazon IT and Amazon DE. On 20 February they schedule it to go off-shelf on 1 March: /products → select the jacket → Schedule → Status → INACTIVE → 1 March 09:00 (ScheduleChangeModal.tsx:119). On 1 March the cron fires, the studio and the products grid both show the jacket INACTIVE, the sync log shows two green SUCCESS rows for AMAZON/IT and AMAZON/DE — and Amazon keeps selling it. The same is true of the bulk Status action over 200 SKUs.

##### What happens today
scheduled-changes.job.ts:59-70 routes a STATUS row to masterStatusService.update. That flips Product.status, flips every non-terminal ChannelListing.listingStatus to INACTIVE (master-status.service.ts:167-186), and enqueues one OutboundSyncQueue row per listing with syncType 'STATUS_UPDATE' and a payload containing ONLY source/productSku/channel/marketplace/old+newListingStatus/old+newProductStatus/reason (master-status.service.ts:186-206) — no price, no quantity, no content. The worker's delist branch does not match STATUS_UPDATE (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141), the isPublished gate does not fire because the cascade never touches isPublished (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:176), so the row reaches OutboundSyncService.processSingle (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:305) → syncToAmazon → buildAmazonListingPatch, which reads only title, description, bulletPoints, price and quantity (outbound-sync.service.ts:289-338) and therefore returns zero patches. outbound-sync.service.ts:1049-1059 then returns `{ success: true, status: "SKIPPED", message: "Skipped — empty patch (nothing to push)" }` with no `dryRun` field, and the worker writes `syncStatus: syncResult.dryRun ? 'SKIPPED' : 'SUCCESS'` → 'SUCCESS' (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:316). Nothing reaches SP-API. This is verbatim the bug class master-status.service.ts:7-12 claims to have closed ("buyers placing orders on items the seller had marked off-shelf"). The Shopify arm has an explicit guard against exactly this shape of fall-through for CONTENT_UPDATE (outbound-sync.service.ts:1935-1938) but STATUS_UPDATE is not keyed there either.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, one honest and one real. (1) HONESTY, immediately: at outbound-sync.service.ts:1049 stop reporting an empty patch as success for any syncType other than an FBA quantity push — return `{ success:false, status:'FAILED', retryable:false, errorCode:'no-adapter-for-syncType' }` so the row dead-letters and appears in the studio's Needs attention tab and the DLQ, instead of a green line. (2) CAPABILITY: give STATUS_UPDATE a real Amazon arm by routing INACTIVE/DRAFT to the existing, reversible closeMarketOffers (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:178-198 — it patchPurchasableOffer-deletes, snapshots the verbatim offer into offerCloseSnapshot and cancels racing pushes) and ACTIVE to reopenMarketOffers, rather than an attributes PATCH that has no status field. Surface the outcome in the studio with the DS Banner already used for scopeError, and the per-row state via the grid's readiness pill.

#### The channel sheet collects a multi-row selection and counts it twice, but mounts no selection bar — the DS BulkActionBar is master-only, so no channel verb can ever act on a selection

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is on the eBay·IT channel sheet of a 40-variation jacket family. They tick 12 sizes, the toolbar says "12 selected" and the footer strip says the same — and nothing appears to act on those 12. On the master scope the identical gesture raises a bar with Unlink / Reparent / Delete variation.

Checkboxes are wired on the channel scope (ChannelSheet.tsx:1967 calls the engine's gridSelection exactly as master does), the rows are stored (:1951) and the count is rendered in two places — SheetToolbar's `{p.selected > 0 && … selected}` (SheetToolbar.tsx:121) fed from ChannelSheet.tsx:2076, and GridSheetStatus at ChannelSheet.tsx:2182. The channel registry does declare a SELECTION-scope verb, broadcastToListings (channelActions.ts:311), and it currently reaches a surface only through the menu adapters' `offered()`, which calls actionsFor(…, SELECTION, [row]) with a single row (menuAdapters.tsx:56-58) — so it is a one-row verb reached by right-click, never a bulk one. The 12-row selection therefore feeds exactly one thing: "Apply formula to selected products" (ChannelSheet.tsx:2121). Do not build a second bar. Generalise FamilySelectionBar into `sheet/SheetSelectionBar.tsx` (it is already a thin wrapper over the DS BulkActionBar + actionsFor(SELECTION) + InfoTip-on-disabled, and already renders nothing at zero selection), and mount it in ChannelSheet's GridSheet `footer` with `rows={selected} actions={verbs} onClear={…} onDone={reload}` — the same `verbs` array the drawer and the row menu already read, so one definition still feeds every surface. That immediately gives broadcast-to-listings its real multi-row home and gives any future per-market delist/close verb a conformant place to appear, with the disabled reason kept on screen rather than the count promising an action that does not exist.

#### "End this brand / this supplier on eBay DE" is not expressible anywhere: the bulk engine has no lifecycle action type, and the only delist producer requires the products to be in the bin first and is whole-product

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A supplier drops a brand. The operator wants the 60 affected SKUs ended on eBay DE only — Amazon IT/DE and Shopify keep selling them. They filter /products by brand, select all 60, and look for "End on this channel/market".

##### What happens today
The bulk engine cannot express it. The runtime allow-list, derived from source rather than a doc, is PRICING_UPDATE, INVENTORY_UPDATE, STATUS_UPDATE, ATTRIBUTE_UPDATE, LISTING_SYNC, MARKETPLACE_OVERRIDE_UPDATE, LISTING_BULK_ACTION, AI_TRANSLATE_PRODUCT, AI_SEO_REGEN, AI_ALT_TEXT, CHANNEL_BATCH (bulk-action.service.ts:105-119) — no delist, end, unpublish or relist. STATUS_UPDATE is whole-product (ACTION_ENTITY.STATUS_UPDATE = 'product', bulk-action.service.ts:138) and, per SB-1, pushes nothing to Amazon anyway. The only enqueuer of UNPUBLISH_LISTING/DELETE_LISTING is POST /products/bulk-hard-delete, and it acts only on rows already soft-deleted (`deletedAt: { not: null }`, products-catalog.routes.ts:1804-1806), is whole-product with no market/channel/account scoping, and restricts the cascade to `listingStatus in ['ACTIVE','INACTIVE']` with a non-null externalListingId (products-catalog.routes.ts:1855-1860) — so every wizard-created listing, which is left at the DRAFT default, is silently skipped. The practical answer today is therefore "bin all 60 products entirely, losing Amazon and Shopify too, and hope none of the eBay rows are DRAFT". In the studio the situation is worse: it is single-product, and has no lifecycle verb at all (channelActions.ts:404 declares open-record, offer-toggle, broadcast-to-listings).

##### Proposed fix
Add one coordinate-scoped lifecycle action type — `DELIST_MARKET`, payload `{ channel, marketplace, channelConnectionId?, aliasKey?, mode: 'close'|'end' }` — to KNOWN_BULK_ACTION_TYPES, routing through a real OutboundSyncQueue row (so it gets retries, dead-lettering and /sync-logs visibility, which the flat-file remove paths deliberately skip) rather than the inline synthetic-queueId calls. Expose it from the existing /products DS BulkActionBar as a GridAction with `danger: true` and a preflight at level 'type-to-confirm' whose confirmPhrase is the channel/market code, not the word DELETE (ActionConfirm's rule, ruling #133), itemising the affected listings as `findings` so the operator sees WHICH 60 rows, not a count. The single-product equivalent lands on the studio channel sheet's ⋯ and on the selection bar proposed in SB-3, from the same declaration.

#### Undoing a bulk take-down silently under-restores: rollback re-runs the master status cascade, which skips every ENDED/ERROR listing, and the skipped list exists only in the audit log

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator bulk-set 200 seasonal SKUs to INACTIVE in January. Some of those listings had genuinely been ended on eBay earlier (listingStatus ENDED) or were sitting in ERROR. In March they open /bulk-operations/history, press Roll back on that job, get a success toast and a completed rollback job — and believe all 200 are selling again.

##### What happens today
Rollback is real and reachable (HistoryClient.tsx:616 → POST /api/bulk-operations/:id/rollback, bulk-operations.routes.ts:392-403 → bulk-action.service.ts:858). Its STATUS_UPDATE arm correctly routes back through masterStatusService.update rather than a bare product.update (bulk-action.service.ts:1026-1049 — note the docstring at bulk-action.service.ts:847 still describes the old, wrong `product.update(status = beforeStatus)` behaviour and is stale). But that cascade skips every listing whose listingStatus is in TERMINAL_LISTING_STATUSES = {ENDED, ERROR} (master-status.service.ts:68, applied at :168-171) and still returns `changed: true`; the skipped ids go only into AuditLog.metadata.skippedListingIds (master-status.service.ts:237-241). Nothing in the rollback result shape (`{ rollbackJobId, succeeded, failed, skipped }`, bulk-action.service.ts:858-863) or in the history UI distinguishes "restored to ACTIVE and pushed" from "Product.status says ACTIVE, this market is still ended". Compounded by SB-1, even the non-skipped rows push nothing to Amazon. The result is a product that reads ACTIVE across Nexus while an unknown subset of its markets are not selling, and no surface names the subset.

##### Proposed fix
Make the skip visible rather than silent. Return cascadedListingIds/skippedListingIds (with the reason per row) from rollbackBulkActionJob up through the route, and render them in the history detail with the DS SummaryTable — one row per listing, channel · market · outcome · why — instead of a bare succeeded/failed/skipped triple. Where a rollback is partial, the history row should carry a DS Banner tone="warning" naming the count of markets NOT restored and linking to the studio's channel scope for each, because the remedy (a relist) is a different flow, not a status flip — which is exactly what master-status.service.ts:22-23 already says and no UI repeats. Also correct the stale docstring at bulk-action.service.ts:847 so the next lane does not re-derive the pre-TECH_DEBT-#53 behaviour from it.

#### "Remove from Amazon <market>" reports unconditional success and hard-deletes the only copy of the listing's state

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the GALE jacket live on Amazon IT and Amazon DE and wants it off IT only for the season, keeping DE and keeping the ability to put IT back next spring. The studio offers no such verb (verified across the whole _studio tree), so they do what the team does today: open the Amazon flat-file editor on IT, select the rows, and use Delete selected.

##### What happens today
A native window.confirm asks "Remove N listings from Amazon IT? The product and its stock stay in Nexus; other channels are untouched." (AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1908) and POSTs /api/amazon/flat-file/remove. The service hard-deletes the ChannelListing rows first (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:59-64, a deleteMany scoped only by productId+channel+marketplace — no channelConnectionId, no aliasKey), which cascades away ChannelListingSnapshot, ChannelListingOverride, Offer, images and issues (schema.prisma:1893, 2000, 2182, 2221, 2253, 2285) and takes flatFileSnapshot (schema.prisma:1584), overrideData (:1604) and offerCloseSnapshot (:1594) with them. Only AFTER the commit does it attempt the SP-API delete, per listing, inside `try { … } catch { /* best-effort; never blocks the committed removal */ }` (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:68-82), skipping any row whose externalListingId is null (:70). The returned `delisted` flag is never read by the caller: the client filters on `channelListingsRemoved > 0` and toasts "Removed N listings from Amazon IT — product and stock kept." (AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1892-1896). So an SP-API failure produces a green success message, the listing keeps selling on Amazon, and every local record that could have re-created it has been destroyed.

##### Proposed fix
Two halves. (1) API: make the removal a two-phase, reversible operation — snapshot the ChannelListing into ChannelListingSnapshot via captureSnapshot (listing-snapshot.service.ts:117) BEFORE any write, dispatch the delist, and only then set {listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false, offerActive:false} rather than deleteMany; add channelConnectionId+aliasKey to the filter; return a per-listing outcome array {listingId, delisted:boolean, error?}. (2) UI: express it as a DS GridAction in the grid action registry (grid/actions/registry.ts:167-198) with danger:true, a preflight() returning an ActionImpact that itemises the consequences ("Amazon IT offer ends · ASIN link kept · DE untouched"), ConfirmLevel 'type-to-confirm' with the real SKU as the phrase, rendered by useActionConfirm (grid/actions/ActionConfirm.tsx) — never window.confirm. Render the per-listing outcome as a DS Banner tone="warning" listing the rows whose channel delete failed, instead of one success toast.

[critical]verifiedAMAZONcorrectness risk

#### A deliberately removed Amazon listing comes straight back in the flat file — the eBay guard for exactly this incident has no Amazon equivalent

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Same jacket, the day after: the operator removed it from Amazon IT (keeping DE). Next week they open the Amazon flat file for IT to fix a bullet point on the other SKUs of the family, or simply reload the editor on the product, and press Save.

##### What happens today
The removed SKU is still a row. Two independent reasons. First, when the editor is opened for one product, getExistingRows ignores the listing scope entirely — the anchor product (and its parent/siblings) is returned whether or not a ChannelListing exists (flat-file.service.ts:2094-2124). Second, the list-mode scope 'listed' resolves to "this product OR its parent OR any child has a ChannelListing on this channel/market" (listing-scope.ts:14-26), so a family whose parent still has an IT row keeps every child in the file, and the filter never looks at listingStatus — an ENDED listing is indistinguishable from an ACTIVE one. Saving that row calls syncRowsToPlatform, whose create branch re-creates the listing. eBay solved precisely this: ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:649-671 stamps a per-market Product.categoryAttributes.ebayFileExcluded after a removal, with the incident recorded in the comment — "Without it, a product with no eBay listing … had NOTHING to remove — and the family loader resurrected its row on every reload" — and the stamp is honoured by GET /rows (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:262). /usr/bin/grep for `fileExcluded` across apps/api/src returns eBay hits only (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:262/1451/3141, ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:664-670, family-sheet-schema.ts:7) and no Amazon equivalent; amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts writes no such stamp anywhere in its 86 lines.

##### Proposed fix
Mirror the eBay stamp: write Product.categoryAttributes.amazonFileExcluded[MARKET]=true inside the same transaction as the removal, honour it in GET /amazon/flat-file/rows (the same place ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:262 does), and auto-clear it when the operator explicitly saves that SKU in that market's file again. Independently, teach the scope filter about state: buildListingScopeWhere should treat listingStatus ENDED / isPublished false as 'not listed' for the default scope, and rows in that state that are still shown must carry a DS Pill tone="neutral">Ended</Pill> in the identity band plus a FilterChip ("Ended (n)") in the sheet toolbar, so the file can never present a dead listing as an ordinary editable row.

4) The eBay guard exists exactly as cited and has no Amazon twin. apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:649-673 (incident-#12 comment + per-market `ebayFileExcluded` stamp inside the delete transaction); honoured in GET /rows at apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:251-263. Set claim re-run with /usr/bin/grep -rn -i "fileexcluded" over apps/api/src apps/web/src → 11 hits, all eBay: ebay-flat-file.routes.ts (262/1451/1457/3141/3147), ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts (664/665/670), its vitest, and pim/family-sheet-schema.ts:7. Zero Amazon hits, and zero hits in apps/web/src (so no client-side compensation either). Positive control: the same grep returned matches, so it was not a vacuous zero.

5) The resurrection write exists: apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3502-3509 — when no `existing` ChannelListing is found for (product, AMAZON, mp), `channelListing.create({productId, ...listingPayload})`; the payload sets `isPublished:true, listingStatus:'ACTIVE'` when `opts.isPublished` (3458).

Refutation attempts that FAILED to kill it: the SCT.6 closed-offer guard (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:371-397) only drops rows whose ChannelListing has `offerClosedAt` — after removeAmazonListing there is no row at all, so it cannot fire; `_ghost` is just the Sheets blank-canvas filler (AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:398-404), not an "unlisted" marker; the studio genuinely reaches this data (apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/useHeaderPrefetch.ts:153-160 warms /amazon/flat-file/rows?productId=familyId, and the client uses productId whenever familyId is set: AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1559-1561, 1676-1678, 2947).

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG: the "or simply reload the editor and press Save" arm does not fire. Grid Save posts only DIRTY rows — onGridSave → `syncToPlatform(dirty, false)` at AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:2747 — so an untouched resurrected row is not sent, and no listing is recreated. The arms that DO fire: (a) an import applies `syncToPlatform(next.filter(r => !r._ghost), false)` over EVERY row (:3269); (b) Publish with scope 'all' sends every row (`gatherRows`, :2263) and /submit runs syncRowsToPlatform on the whole body before the feed (routes:499) — that both recreates the listing and puts the removed SKU back in the JSON_LISTINGS_FEED when publish mode is live; (c) any edit/fill-down that dirties the row. Also "an ENDED listing is indistinguishable from an ACTIVE one" is slightly overstated: ENDED listings do surface `_listingStatus` (service:2333) and the health overview renders it (client:6807) — it is the DELETED case that carries no marker at all, and neither case is filtered.
The stamp half is right and is the only viable carrier — removeAmazonListing deletes the ChannelListing, so flatFileSnapshot/listingStatus die with it and nothing else can remember the removal. Two corrections to the proposal: (1) honouring it in GET /amazon/flat-file/rows alone is not enough — the eBay filter sits in the route because eBay's loader is in the route, whereas Amazon's single-product path lives inside getExistingRows' `if (productId)` branch (flat-file.service.ts:2095-2124), which the route never post-filters; the check has to go in the service (or in both), or the studio/family view keeps resurrecting the row. (2) The second half — making buildListingScopeWhere treat ENDED/isPublished=false as "not listed" by default — collides with the deliberate delete-sync design at flat-file.service.ts:3159-3205, where a record_action=delete row is kept as ENDED with its snapshot precisely so the row round-trips the delete op on reload; filtering those out by default would erase the operator's visible record of their own delete. The Pill/FilterChip presentation is the right answer for that case; the scope change is not.

[critical]verifiedALLmissing capability

#### The per-market "end this listing" IS expressible in an import file — but it only writes Nexus, never the channel, and no UI can reach it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The Owner's exact ask, as an import: an operator wants a file-driven way to say "end the IT row of this jacket, keep DE", and to be able to undo it next season. The capability was built for flat-file imports and then stranded.

##### What happens today
A channel-sheet row carrying Action=DELETE is recorded as a scoped end — diff.ts:316-327 pushes {sku, sheet, channel, markets: scope.markets} and explicitly refuses cross-channel and unscoped deletes. applyDeletes then ends each market individually with a per-market inverse capture for rollback, a typed-confirm gate, and a skip when no market scope was given (apply.ts:519-556, 562-600). It is a better-designed lifecycle verb than anything in the studio. But: (a) the write is local only — it sets {listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false, offerActive:false} (apply.ts:586-590) and nothing in apps/api/src/services/flat-file/ ever calls dispatchChannelDelist or enqueues DELETE_LISTING/UNPUBLISH_LISTING (/usr/bin/grep over that tree returns only pending-sync-stamp.ts's unrelated outboundSyncQueue read at :13,:31), so Amazon/eBay are never told and the offer keeps selling; and (b) it is unreachable — /usr/bin/grep -rn "flat-file/import/" over apps/web/src returns zero hits (positive control: many apps/web files match "flat-file/"), so nothing in the web app calls POST /api/flat-file/import/preview or /:id/apply, which are the only callers of applyDeletes (flat-file-import.routes.ts:175).

##### Proposed fix
Finish the half that is missing rather than building a third path. In applyDeletes, after the ENDED write, enqueue one OutboundSyncQueue row per ended coordinate with syncType 'UNPUBLISH_LISTING' (the worker already short-circuits it to dispatchChannelDelist at bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158) and record the returned dispatch outcome on the import's ApplyRowResult so the report can say ended-locally vs ended-on-channel. Then expose the same service as the studio's channel-scope verb: a DS GridAction "End on this market" (danger, ConfirmLevel 'type-to-confirm', preflight listing the sibling markets that stay) in the channel sheet's selection bar and row menu, and its inverse "Relist on this market" driven by the inverse capture the import already produces.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/flat-file/import/diff.ts:314-327
- apps/api/src/services/flat-file/import/apply.ts:519-556
- apps/api/src/services/flat-file/import/apply.ts:562-600
- apps/api/src/services/flat-file/import/apply.ts:586-590
- apps/api/src/routes/flat-file-import.routes.ts:160-190
- apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find the capability anywhere reachable from the studio.

CONFIRMED, code I read myself:
1. diff.ts:314-330 — Action=DELETE on a channel sheet pushes `{sku, sheet, channel: SHEET_CHANNEL[sheetName], markets: scope.markets}` only when `SHEET_CHANNEL[sheetName] === scope.channel`; cross-channel rows are silently skipped. Exactly as stated.
2. apply.ts:562-575 — typed-confirm gate throws before any write; apply.ts:584-590 — `endData = {listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false, offerActive:false}`; apply.ts:591-600 — `markets === undefined` → SKIPPED 'delete skipped: no market scope'; apply.ts:601-651 — both the 'ALL' and string[] arms do per-market `findFirst` → `captureInverse` → `updateMany`, one inverse per market. The write is a plain `tx.channelListing.updateMany`. No dispatch, no enqueue, in either arm.
3. Set claim (a) re-established with /usr/bin/grep: `dispatchChannelDelist|outboundSyncQueue|OutboundSyncQueue|UNPUBLISH_LISTING|DELETE_LISTING` over apps/api/src/services/flat-file/ returns only pending-sync-stamp.ts:13 and :31 (an unrelated read). Positive control: 14 files in the same tree match "prisma". I also checked the two indirect routes out — there is no Prisma `$use`/`$extends` middleware anywhere in apps/api/src or packages/database/src, and the only FLAT_FILE_IMPORTED consumer is product-event.service.ts:113, which maps it to `product.updated` and enqueues nothing. applyDeletes emits no event at all (the emitMany is in applyChanges, apply.ts:500-512, and returns before applyDeletes). So the ENDED write is genuinely terminal: Amazon/eBay are never told.
4. Set claim (b) re-established with /usr/bin/grep: `flat-file/import` over apps/web/src returns 7 hits, all of them either vitest headers or `@/components/flat-file/import-accept` (a MIME-accept constant) — zero URL callers. Positive control: 40+ apps/web files match "flat-file", and 8 of them do call other flat-file endpoints (`/api/flat-file/pull-history`, `/api/flat-file/unified-rows`, `/api/flat-file/pull-job/active`). The route is nonetheless live: registered at index.ts:700 with prefix '/api', permission-gated at permissions-manifest.ts:351, paths `/flat-file/import/preview` (:63-64) and `/flat-file/import/:id/apply` (:124-126), and :175 is the sole applyDeletes call site (/usr/bin/grep for applyDeletes over apps+packages returns only that route, the definition, and its own vitest file).
5. Worker short-circuit is real: bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158 routes UNPUBLISH_LISTING/DELETE_LISTING straight to `dispatchChannelDelist` (channel-delist.service.ts:91), so the fix's mechanism exists.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED:
- Studio: the channel sheet's action registry has exactly three verbs — channelActions.ts:163 'offer-toggle', :309 'broadcast-to-listings', :381 'open-record'. The pause verb's own preflight copy states the boundary: "Buyers stop seeing this offer on this channel and market. The listing itself is not ended and its reviews and identifiers are untouched." (channelActions.ts:230-232). No end, no relist, anywhere under _studio/ (grep for delist|unpublish|relist|'ENDED' returns only types, images-restore copy, and a listingStatus display in drawer/panes/ListingsPane.tsx:103).
- The studio's own Import drawer is a different route entirely — transport.ts:88 `${getBackendUrl()}/api/products/${productId}/import` (product-studio.routes.ts), which has no delete/END path at all (grep for delete|ENDED|listingStatus in that 1004-line route file returns only an overrides-key delete at :833 and an alias ARCHIVE at :990).

WHAT IS MIS-STATED (why severity drops to high, not critical):
The finding reads as though nothing anywhere can end one market on the channel. Two sibling paths do, and both ARE UI-reachable — just not from the studio, and not from an import file:
- POST /api/amazon/flat-file/remove (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1804-1820) → removeAmazonListing (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:32), which is explicitly market-scoped, `deleteMany` on the AMAZON ChannelListing rows for that one marketplace (:59-64) and then `dispatchChannelDelist(... syncType:'DELETE_LISTING')` per external id (:66-83). Called from AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1886.
- POST /api/ebay/flat-file/delete (ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:3806-3824) → runEbayFlatFileDelete → dispatchChannelDelist (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:212). Called from EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:2024.
These are hard deletes of the local row with no inverse capture, so they serve "remove from this market" but not "and relist it next season" — the Owner's second half. The defect therefore stands, but as: the studio has no end/relist verb, and the one engine that models end-with-inverse correctly is both unreachable from the web app and channel-blind, while the two channel-aware paths are destructive and live on pages outside the studio.
The first half of the fix is sound and mechanically verified: enqueue one OutboundSyncQueue row per ended coordinate with syncType 'UNPUBLISH_LISTING' and bullmq-sync.worker.ts:141-158 already short-circuits it to dispatchChannelDelist, skipping the publishing-control and pricing checks that a deleted row would fail. Note the worker reads externalListingId off the QUEUE ROW (:147), so applyDeletes must copy it from the `before` it already fetches at apply.ts:602/:632 — the current code selects only `marketplace` in the 'ALL' arm's findMany (:609-612) and would otherwise have nothing to send.

Two over-promises in the second half:
1. "its inverse 'Relist on this market' driven by the inverse capture the import already produces" — the capture is `captureInverse(endData, before)` over three booleans (apply.ts:584-590). Restoring `{listingStatus, isPublished, offerActive}` puts the Nexus row back; it does not recreate an offer that was ended on Amazon or eBay. A relist is a publish/feed submission, not the inverse of three flags. Whatever verb is built must state that boundary or it becomes exactly the dishonest-UI failure this codebase already annotates elsewhere.
2. Reusing this service as the studio verb inherits deleteConfirmationPhrase, which by its own comment at apply.ts:553-560 counts channel-ends inside a "DELETE N PRODUCTS" phrase. A studio verb that makes an operator type "DELETE 3 PRODUCTS" to end three market rows on one product is a worse gate than no gate.

Also, the fix leaves the Amazon/eBay legacy paths (amazon-flat-file-remove.service.ts:59, ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:212) as a third and fourth semantics for the same operator intent — hard delete, no inverse. Any real resolution has to say which of end-with-inverse and hard-delete the studio verb is, and whether the legacy pages converge on it.

[critical]verifiedAMAZONdata integrity risk

#### Typing record_action=delete and pressing Save ends the listing in Nexus only — and Nexus then stops pushing stock to an offer that is still live on Amazon

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator wants the jacket off Amazon IT. In the Amazon flat-file grid they set record_action = delete on the IT rows (the Amazon-native way to express it) and press Save, intending to submit the feed later — or they submit and the feed is rejected.

##### What happens today
Save posts to /api/amazon/flat-file/sync-rows (AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:2517) which runs syncRowsToPlatform. That function mirrors the delete locally before doing anything else: for every record_action='delete' SKU it writes {listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false} plus the row snapshot to the market's ChannelListing (flat-file.service.ts:3175-3205), with the comment describing this as optimistic w.r.t. an async feed. Save itself submits no feed — the feed is a separate button (/api/amazon/flat-file/submit, AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:2360). The consequences compound: the same Save's auto-enqueue of quantity/price pushes filters on isPublished:true, offerActive:true (amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1513-1518), and the sync worker skips every queued row for an unpublished listing (bullmq-sync.worker.ts:163-186), while the stock cascade still enqueues rows it will never send (stock-movement.service.ts:766-846 checks offerClosedAt and syncPaused, never listingStatus/isPublished). Net effect: Nexus shows the IT listing ENDED and silently stops maintaining its quantity, while Amazon keeps selling it — the classic oversell shape.

##### Proposed fix
Do not let a Save change lifecycle state. Move the local ENDED mirror out of syncRowsToPlatform and into the feed-submit path, applied only when the DELETE feed is accepted (or optimistically with an explicit pending flag that the reconcile job clears). Until the feed lands, a record_action='delete' row should render as an armed intent — DS Pill tone="warning">Delete on next submit</Pill> in the row's identity cell plus a DS Banner above the grid stating that N rows will be withdrawn from Amazon IT only when Submit runs — and the Save summary must not report them as ended. If an operator-visible "end it now" is wanted, route it through the same delist dispatch as IE-03 rather than through a status write.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3154-3212
- apps/web/src/app/products/amazon-flat-file/AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:2506-2527
- apps/web/src/app/products/amazon-flat-file/AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:2355-2365
- apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1505-1520
- apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:163-186
- apps/api/src/services/stock-movement.service.ts:766-846

##### Verifier
Every cited line checks out within ±3 lines, and my attempts to refute the mechanism failed — the "backstop" the code comment invokes does not exist.

CONFIRMED, code I opened myself:
1. The local mirror is real and unconditional. apps/api/src/services/amazon/flat-file.service.ts:3142 `async syncRowsToPlatform(...)`; :3155-3157 filters delete rows OUT of `validRows`; :3159-3166 the "Delete-sync" comment explicitly calls the write "Optimistic w.r.t. the async feed" and says it "Runs before the empty-validRows early-return"; :3196-3206 `channelListing.updateMany({ where: {productId, channel:'AMAZON', marketplace: mp}, data: { listingStatus:'ENDED', isPublished:false, flatFileSnapshot } })`; :3208-3211 refreshes ProductReadCache so the /products grid also shows ENDED. No feature flag, no publish-mode gate, no `opts.isPublished` guard on this branch.
2. Save reaches it. apps/api/src/routes/amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1490-1502 — POST /amazon/flat-file/sync-rows → `syncRowsToPlatform(rows, mp, expandedFields, { isPublished })`, and the route's own header comment says it is "Called on Save and after a feed is DONE". Client side: AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:2513-2521 posts to `/api/amazon/flat-file/sync-rows`, called from `onGridSave` at :2747 with `isPublished=false`. Delete rows are not stripped client-side before Save (the only client-side delete filters are in `withParents` at :2252 and completeness at :5014).
3. Save submits no feed. The only `/api/amazon/flat-file/submit` fetch is in the submit handler at AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:2360-2364, a separate action; its pre-submit "auto-save" at :2344-2346 is localStorage + version snapshot only.
4. Pushes then stop. amazon-flat-file.routes.ts:1512-1519 the post-save auto-enqueue queries `isPublished:true, offerActive:true` — the row it just flipped is excluded. apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:162 "PHASE 15: Publishing Control Checks", :177-190 `if (!channelListing.isPublished)` → marks the queue row SKIPPED and returns. apps/api/src/services/stock-movement.service.ts:695-713 the cascade's listing query selects `syncPaused` and `offerClosedAt` but never `isPublished`/`listingStatus`, and :785-793 `resolveIntendedQuantity` is fed only `offerClosed`/`syncPaused`, so :806-846 still writes the new quantity and creates the OutboundSyncQueue row that the worker will then skip. Exactly as stated.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED (this is what makes it critical rather than merely wrong):
- The comment at flat-file.service.ts:3162-3164 claims "the Nexus↔channel reconciliation is the backstop". /usr/bin/grep for `isPublished` across apps/api/src/services/listing-reconciliation.service.ts (961 lines), channel-reconciliation.service.ts (393), amazon-sync.service.ts (417) returns zero hits (positive control: the same grep for other tokens in those files hits). listing-reconciliation.service.ts:270-400 only upserts rows into the separate `ListingReconciliation` discovery table — it never touches ChannelListing.isPublished/listingStatus. No code path restores publication.
- The one job that could catch "Amazon still selling, Nexus says ended" is apps/api/src/jobs/amazon-qty-readback.job.ts:114-131 — and its own `where` excludes exactly this state: `isPublished: true` (:119) and `listingStatus: { notIn: ['ENDED','REMOVED'] }` (:130). The drift detector is structurally blind to the listing the mirror just created.
- flat-file.service.ts:3458 shows the only re-publish write is `...(opts.isPublished ? { isPublished:true, listingStatus:'ACTIVE' } : {})`, i.e. only on the post-feed-DONE sync. A later ordinary Save that changes record_action back to partial_update does NOT restore isPublished — the listing stays mute.
- Alternative existing capability, checked and NOT a refutation: there IS a market-scoped removal path — AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1880-1899 `removeFromAmazon` → POST /api/amazon/flat-file/remove, reachable from the context menu "Delete rows" (:4225-4233) and `deleteSelected` (:4243-4249, wait: :1903-1912), both behind a confirm(). That is a different verb (prunes ChannelListings) and does not make the record_action=delete Save path safe; it does not overlap the scenario as stated.

SCOPE CAVEAT (not a refutation, but the finding should say it): this defect is in the legacy Amazon flat-file editor, not in the PES studio tree. /usr/bin/grep for `record_action` across apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/, apps/api/src/services/pim/studio-sheet.service.ts and sheet-rows.service.ts returns nothing, and the studio has no link to /products/amazon-flat-file (only ebay-flat-file Presentation imports). So the studio inherits the risk only via the state the flat-file editor writes into ChannelListing, which the studio then reads.
The direction is right (a Save must not change lifecycle state; the mirror belongs on the accepted-feed path), but the fix as written is incomplete and partly misplaced:

1. It leaves the real hole open. Even if the mirror moves to the submit path, a DELETE feed that Amazon later rejects, or a submit that Amazon partially applies, produces the same ENDED-in-Nexus / live-on-Amazon divergence — and amazon-qty-readback.job.ts:119,130 will still never look at that listing (`isPublished: true`, `listingStatus notIn ['ENDED','REMOVED']`). The fix must include an explicit "ended in Nexus but present in Amazon's active catalog" arm (the readback already pulls fetchActiveCatalog at :101; the SKUs it needs are the excluded ones), otherwise the silent-divergence class survives the fix.
2. It says nothing about the rows already in this state. The mirror has been live; there are likely existing AMAZON ChannelListings at ENDED/isPublished=false whose offers are still live. The fix needs a read-only detection query before any behaviour change lands, or the change simply freezes the existing damage.
3. The "pending flag that the reconcile job clears" hands work to a job that does not do this today — listing-reconciliation.service.ts only upserts into the ListingReconciliation table (:359-400) and writes nothing back to ChannelListing. That is a new capability, not a wiring change, and should be costed as such.
4. The DS Pill/Banner remedy is aimed at the wrong surface. The defect is in /products/amazon-flat-file (AmazonFlatFileClient), which is on the owner's untouchable flat-file-editor list and is not a Nexus-DS studio surface; proposing DS components there is both out of the studio's scope and a change to a protected file. The operator-visible half should be raised as a proposal against that page, and the server-side half (stop writing lifecycle on Save) treated as the actual fix.
5. Missing an alternative already in the codebase: removeFromAmazon → POST /api/amazon/flat-file/remove (AmazonFlatFileClient.tsx:1880-1899), already confirm()-gated and already the "market-scoped removal, product and stock kept" verb. The fix should say whether the armed-intent path converges on that endpoint rather than inventing a third delete verb.

#### The editing workbook round trip is blind to listing state: an ENDED listing is offered as an editing destination exactly like a live one

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The jacket's Amazon IT listing was ended last month. A merchandiser opens the studio on the Amazon·IT scope, presses Export, chooses "All existing listing destinations", spends an afternoon rewriting bullets and aspects in the workbook, and imports it back.

##### What happens today
Everything succeeds and nothing goes to Amazon. productTransferOptions selects every ChannelListing for the family with no status filter at all (catalog-product-transfer.ts:31) and filters only on ALIAS status (:42), so an ENDED row is a first-class destination; the drawer labels it `SKU · Amazon IT · Account · Primary listing` with no state anywhere (ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:145, 188, 191). The workbook itself carries no lifecycle field — the exported column set is attributes minus MANAGED_FIELDS/managedChannelField (catalog-transfer-export.ts:99,150,157; catalog-transfer-plan.ts:16-22), and the Instructions sheet states that publication "retain[s] its dedicated workflow … cannot be changed by a catalog import" (catalog-workbook.ts:55). So the export is lossless for attributes (version CAS at catalog-transfer-plan.ts:178-179 correctly refuses a stale file) and completely silent about lifecycle. The import then writes the values onto the dead row (catalog-transfer.service.ts:170-176) and reports success. The studio sheet's own readiness never mentions it either — sheet-rows.service.ts:264-272 derives live/ready/missing/unlisted from externalListingId+isPublished and never reads listingStatus.

##### Proposed fix
Carry the state in both directions. (1) Add `listingState` to ProductTransferOptions.listings and render it in destinationLabel and in the Listings <Select> options as a DS Pill (tone neutral for Ended, warning for Offer closed, success for Live); when the current-scope destination is not live, show a DS Banner tone="warning" in the drawer before the Download button: "This listing is ended on Amazon IT. Edits save in Nexus; relist it before they can reach the channel." (2) Add a read-only reference column `listing_state` to each Listings sheet of the workbook (the same grey reference styling as version/sku, catalog-workbook.ts:171) so the file itself answers the question. (3) Make readiness honest: sheet-rows.service.ts should return a distinct 'ended' state when listingStatus is ENDED, so the channel sheet's existing chips can surface it.

##### Evidence
- apps/api/src/services/pim/catalog-product-transfer.ts:30-43
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/import/ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:145
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/import/ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:173-179
- apps/api/src/services/pim/catalog-workbook.ts:55
- apps/api/src/services/pim/catalog-transfer-export.ts:99
- apps/api/src/services/pim/catalog-transfer.service.ts:165-178
- apps/api/src/services/pim/sheet-rows.service.ts:264-272

##### Verifier
Every cited line checks out. catalog-product-transfer.ts:30-32 selects ChannelListing rows for the family with `where: { productId: { in: ... }, channel: { in: TRANSFER_CHANNELS } }` and a `listingIdentity` projection (line 11) that does not include `listingStatus` at all; the only status filter is on the ALIAS (line 42, `aliasById.get(l.aliasKey)?.status === 'ACTIVE'`). So an ENDED listing is a first-class destination and the wire payload cannot express its state even if the UI wanted to. ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:145 confirms destinationLabel = sku · channel marketplace · account · aliasLabel, with no lifecycle token, and it is the only per-destination rendering (used at :188 and :191); I read the drawer's full render (lines 148-210) and the only Banners are for unsaved edits, empty-destination scope and shared-value inheritance — nothing about a non-live destination. catalog-workbook.ts:55 does say publication "retain[s] its dedicated workflows … cannot be changed by a catalog import", and catalog-transfer.service.ts:170-172 writes the patch onto the matched existing row with no state check. sheet-rows.service.ts:264-272 does derive live/unlisted/missing/ready from `listing.externalListingId && listing.isPublished` and never reads listingStatus.

I tried three refutations and none killed it. (a) Does the state exist elsewhere in the studio? Partly: the drawer pane shows it (ListingsPane.tsx:103 renders `listing?.listingStatus`), sheet-rows.service.ts:392/467 does select and return `listingStatus` on each row, and AliasBandCell.tsx:132 reads `alias?.listingStatus`. So this is a surfacing gap in ONE surface (the transfer picker), not a missing datum — that is why I cut the severity to medium rather than high. (b) Is the harm overstated? Yes, somewhat: no catalog import ever reaches a channel (catalog-workbook.ts:55 states this), so "nothing goes to Amazon" is true of live destinations too; the real residue is that edits parked on an ENDED row cannot reach the channel at all without a relist, which is exactly the Owner's delist/relist class. (c) Any standing ruling? Nothing in the top of docs/pes-claims.md (rulings #1-10, read from line 1) settles listing lifecycle in the transfer picker.

One warning on the proposed fix, part (3): listingRisk.ts:11-17 records a MEASURED PES.3 result that `listingStatus` is not a liveness test — a family where all 20 non-ACTIVE eBay rows still carried a real ItemID — and isLiveOnChannel (listingRisk.ts:47) deliberately keys on externalListingId only. A new 'ended' readiness state keyed on listingStatus must be stated as "the channel says ended", never as "nothing is live there". Parts (1) and (2) are unobjectionable, but (1) requires adding listingStatus to `listingIdentity` (catalog-product-transfer.ts:11) and to the shared ProductTransferOptions type first — the drawer literally cannot render what the endpoint does not send.
(1) is blocked until listingStatus is added to catalog-product-transfer.ts:11's listingIdentity and to the shared ProductTransferOptions.listings type — the drawer cannot render a field the endpoint never selects. (3) conflicts with a measured decision: listingRisk.ts:11-17 found 20 non-ACTIVE eBay rows carrying live ItemIDs, so any 'ended' state must be phrased as a channel-reported status, not as a liveness verdict.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
On the Amazon·IT channel sheet an operator opens Import/Export, expands "Download the displayed table for reference", downloads the CSV of what they are looking at, edits three cells in Excel, and drags it back into the same drawer's file box.

##### What happens today
It is refused with "Unknown columns: brand, colour, …" and "The file needs sku, field and action columns. Download a catalog template first." (catalog-transfer-file.ts:56-61) — a template the studio never offers. The refusal is correct, but the surrounding contract is not: sheetExport.ts still stamps channel coordinates into every key (`brand@AMAZON:IT:it`, exportKeyFor at :53-58) and its module doc still asserts "the import routes a column to the coordinate its header names (D15.3)" and "Both produce importable files" (:6-8, :23-25), while the endpoint that was built to that contract now refuses channel scope outright — POST /products/:id/import/diff returns 409 account_identity_required both for scope=channel (product-studio.routes.ts:513) and for any channel-coordinate header (:535), and apply/revert 409 legacy channel jobs (:783, :809), all pointing at /products/catalog-transfer. Close the loop in one direction and say so. Either (a) restore the round trip by extending the export key with account identity (`brand@AMAZON:IT:it#<accountId>/<aliasKey>`) and lifting the 409s once import-diff can resolve a coordinate rather than infer one — which is what the refusal text is actually asking for; or (b) retire it: delete liveTransport and the channel branch of exportKeyFor, correct sheetExport.ts's doc (a doc asserting a shipped contract the route refuses is the stale-comment class), and relabel the Disclosure in ProductTransferDrawer as "Download a read-only CSV of this view (cannot be imported)" with the reason inline. In both cases the file the drawer hands out and the file the drawer accepts must be the same file, and the refusal — if it stays — belongs in the FileDropzone hint at rest (DS FileDropzone `hint`), not after the operator has already uploaded.

#### The green "Live" verdict ignores listingStatus entirely — a SUPPRESSED, REMOVED or ERROR listing renders as "Already published on this channel"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the GALE jacket live on Amazon DE. Amazon suppresses the ASIN (missing GPSR responsible-person data), so a colleague opens the suppression in the syndication console; `ChannelListing.listingStatus` becomes 'SUPPRESSED' and the buy box is gone. The operator then opens /products/<id>/edit/studio?scope=amazon&market=DE to find out why the DE numbers dropped.

##### What happens today
The studio says the listing is Live, in green. The sheet read's only liveness test is `listing.externalListingId && listing.isPublished` (studio-sheet.service.ts:1449-1450) — `listingStatus` is selected (LISTING_SELECT, :457) and then never consulted by the verdict. The suppression write touches only `listingStatus` (listings-syndication.routes.ts:2335-2338), so both halves of the test are still true and readiness stays 'live'. `readiness.ts:53` renders that as a success-tone pill labelled "Live" with the hover sentence "Already published on this channel". On the channel sheet the alias band's CompletenessPill takes its colour from `readyPillTone(state)` (IdentityBand.tsx:142) and the real status only survives inside the `title` string built by `bandTitle` (AliasBandCell.tsx:132,147). In the record drawer the contradiction is visible in one card: `ListingsPane.tsx:89-97` prints the green "Live" Pill and `ListingsPane.tsx:103` prints `Status: SUPPRESSED` eight lines below it. The same holds for 'ERROR', 'INACTIVE' and 'REMOVED' — every value schema.prisma:1615 declares as terminal. Two shipped writers reach this state without clearing isPublished/externalListingId: the suppression route above, and ebay-status-reconcile.job.ts:222-227, which writes `listingStatus: 'REMOVED'` after eBay returns HTTP 404 for the SKU and leaves both liveness fields untouched.

##### Proposed fix
Make the liveness verdict read every field that can contradict it, and split 'live' into two row states. In `sheet-rows.service.ts`/`studio-sheet.service.ts`, gate 'live' on `externalListingId && isPublished && !TERMINAL.has(listingStatus)` where TERMINAL = {ENDED, REMOVED, CANCELLED, INACTIVE}; add a fifth ROW state `impaired` to `grid/renderers/readiness.ts` (tone `warning`, label "Listed · not selling", hint templated with the actual status string) and a sixth `ended` (tone `neutral`, label "Ended on channel"). Because the DS Pill is the one tone source, both the alias band's CompletenessPill and the drawer's Pill pick it up with no further edits. Separately, never let a status this important live only in a `title` attribute: put `listingStatus` back on the band as a second DS `Pill` (size xs) beside the completeness pill, per the Owner's visibility-over-minimalism rule — the band already reserves 130px of trail for exactly this (ChannelSheet.tsx:1640-1643).

#### A market whose Amazon offer was deliberately closed (SCT.6) is invisible to the studio — `offerClosedAt` is never read and the drawer prints "Offer: selling"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator takes the GALE jacket off sale on Amazon IT for the season using Sync control → CLOSE_OFFER, keeping the ASIN, the reviews and the DE listing. Weeks later they open the studio on scope=amazon&market=IT to check why IT has no orders, and to decide whether to reopen.

##### What happens today
The studio shows the IT listing as Live and selling. `closeMarketOffers` deletes the purchasable offer on SP-API and records the closure in `offerClosedAt` / `offerCloseSnapshot` only — it writes neither `offerActive` nor `listingStatus` (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:178-195). The studio sheet's `LISTING_SELECT` does not select `offerClosedAt` (studio-sheet.service.ts:457-464), and a /usr/bin/grep for `offerClosedAt|offerCloseSnapshot` over the whole `_studio/` tree returns rc=1 — zero references, against a positive control of 5 files matching `offerActive`. So readiness is still 'live' (studio-sheet.service.ts:1449) and the drawer's Offer row falls into its truthy branch and prints the word "selling" (ListingsPane.tsx:122-135), because `offerActive` is still its schema default `true` (schema.prisma:1634). The one fact the studio needs — this market is deliberately closed and a one-click verbatim reopen exists — is held in the database and shown nowhere. The pane's own comment at :105-107 states the rule this violates: a paused offer and a live listing are different things an operator acts on differently.

##### Proposed fix
Add `offerClosedAt`, `offerClosedBy`, `offerCloseReason` to `LISTING_SELECT` and to `SheetListing` on the wire, mirrored into both `drawer/types.ts` and `sheet/channel/types.ts` (the channel mirror currently omits it, so the sheet could not render it even if sent). Render it as a third state on the drawer's existing Offer row — `closed — market offer withdrawn <ago>, by <actor>` — and fold it into the row verdict as the `impaired` state proposed in SH-1 so the pill is amber, not green. Then hang the remediation off the state the way the DS intends: a `GridAction` `reopen-market-offer` in the channel registry (`danger: false`, `preflight` naming the snapshot date and the exact price/quantity that will be replayed, rendered by `useActionConfirm`), posting the existing `POST /api/stock/sync-control/actions {action:'REOPEN_OFFER'}` — no new endpoint required.

- apps/api/src/services/pim/studio-sheet.service.ts:457-464
- apps/api/src/services/pim/studio-sheet.service.ts:1449

##### Verifier

1. Close writes only the close columns. apps/api/src/services/amazon-market-offer.service.ts:178-195 sets offerClosedAt/offerClosedBy/offerCloseReason/offerCloseSnapshot and nothing else; `/usr/bin/grep -n 'offerActive|listingStatus|isPublished' apps/api/src/services/amazon-market-offer.service.ts` returns rc=1 — the close path never touches either flag. The fix is directionally right and cheap, but three corrections. (1) The wire addition must carry `offerCloseSnapshot`'s price/quantity too, or the proposed preflight text ("the exact price/quantity that will be replayed") cannot be rendered — the snapshot is where those live (amazon-market-offer.service.ts:184-193), and it is Json, so type it at the parse boundary rather than mirroring Prisma's JsonValue into the client. #### "Not listed" is an affirmative claim about the marketplace derived from the absence of a local row — and a shipped path deletes that row while the channel listing survives

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator removes the GALE jacket from eBay IT via the eBay flat file (Delete → Remove channel listing). The jacket's IT ItemID is a shared Trading-API item that another market's row still references, so the guard refuses to end it — the eBay listing stays live and selling. The operator then opens the studio on scope=ebay&market=IT to confirm the takedown.

##### What happens today
The studio reports "Not listed", in the neutral tone that means nothing is wrong, with the hover sentence "This row has no listing on this channel". `handleRemoveChannelListing` hard-deletes the ChannelListing rows inside its transaction (ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:645-648) and only afterwards attempts the delist, which pushes the ItemID onto `delistSkippedShared` and never calls eBay when the ItemID is still referenced (:687, :719-721). With the local row gone, the studio read takes the `!listing && coordinate → 'unlisted'` branch (studio-sheet.service.ts:1451-1452) and `readiness.ts:56` renders it as "Not listed". The alias band prints the same claim as `status = alias?.listingStatus ?? 'NOT LISTED'` (AliasBandCell.tsx:132). The contradiction is written into one file: `readiness.ts:13` documents `unlisted` as meaning "the question has never been asked", while `readiness.ts:56` ships it as "This row has no listing on this channel". Those are opposite claims, and the studio has no way to tell them apart because a deleted row and a never-created row are byte-identical to the read.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, both small. (a) Retire the false hint: `unlisted` must read label "No listing here" / hint "We hold no listing record for this coordinate. The studio then distinguishes three cases the operator acts on differently: never listed, removed and confirmed, removed but the channel call was skipped or failed. Surface the third as a DS `Banner` (tone `warning`) above the sheet — "eBay IT: the local record was removed on <date> but the ItemID <id> was not ended (shared listing). It may still be selling." — with a link out to the item. That banner is the only honest thing that can be said today.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens the studio on scope=ebay&market=IT for a jacket whose last real sync ran eight months ago, next to a colleague's screen showing the same page for a jacket synced ten minutes ago. Both want to know which numbers they can trust before repricing.

##### What happens today
The two pages are pixel-identical. The channel sheet's own `SheetListing` mirror (sheet/channel/types.ts:370-389) omits the field entirely, so the alias band, the CompletenessPill, the view chips and the scope-bar readiness chips could not render it even if asked. The drawer's handling is exemplary — three states, `undefined` = not reported, `null` = never synced, a timestamp = when — and it is reachable only by opening a record. Every summary surface in the studio therefore presents a state derived from a possibly year-old row with the same confidence as one confirmed a minute ago, and the sheet is the surface the operator spends the whole session on.

##### Proposed fix
Add `lastSyncedAt` (and `lastSyncStatus`) to the channel sheet's `SheetListing` mirror and to `AliasGroup`, then put one freshness statement where it cannot be missed: the `trailing` status slot of `SheetToolbar` is already defined as transient STATUS only (CH.1, SheetToolbar.tsx:15-30), which is exactly the right home for "Amazon · IT — our record last synced 8 months ago" with a DS `InfoTip` carrying the full sentence ("nothing polls the channel; this is when our own sync last ran"). At the row level, reuse the existing `ProvenanceMark` convention on the alias band rather than inventing a control: a staleness mark on any listing whose `lastSyncedAt` is null or older than a threshold, with the same never-invented-value discipline `clampPct` already applies (rows.ts:281-284). Do not label anything "verified" until something actually polls the channel.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator ended the GALE jacket's IT variation on eBay last season through the flat file, and now wants to delete that dead variation from the family in the studio's master sheet.

##### What happens today
The confirmation asserts the variation was never on eBay at all. `isLiveOnChannel` correctly uses `externalListingId` rather than status (listingRisk.ts:47-49), but `classifyListings` turns the same nullable field into a claim about the past: a row with no external id gets the label `"<channel> · <market> — <status>, never published to the channel"` (listingRisk.ts:61-63). Both sentences are historical claims the data cannot support, inside the studio's only hard-delete confirmation.

##### Proposed fix
Say what is known, not what is inferred. In `listingRisk.ts`, replace "never published to the channel" with "no channel reference on our record" — a statement about our own row, which is all `externalListingId == null` supports. In `familyActions.ts`, replace the empty-verdict consequence "It is not listed on any channel" with "We hold no listing records for this product. We have not checked the channels." Both keep the existing `ActionImpact` shape and are rendered unchanged by `useActionConfirm` (ActionConfirm.tsx), which already itemises consequences rather than counting them. Durably, this finding disappears if SH-3's tombstone lands: with `externalListingId` preserved and a `removedAt` beside it, `classifyListings` can return a real third verdict — `ended` — and say "eBay · IT — ended <date>, ItemID <id> retired", which is both true and the sentence the operator actually needs.

#### When readiness cannot be measured the alias band renders nothing at all — the carefully written "not measured" sentence is unreachable

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens the studio on a channel × market whose category schema declares no required fields, so the server honestly sends `readiness.percent: null` — "there is nothing to be ready against". They scan the alias bands to decide which listing to work on next.

##### What happens today
That band shows no readiness indicator and no tooltip, and reads exactly like a band whose pill simply has not loaded. `clampPct` deliberately preserves the null rather than coercing it to 0 or 100 (rows.ts:275-284, documented as a shipped defect that was caught), and `bandTitle` writes two distinct sentences for it — "…this channel declares no required fields, so there is nothing to measure" and "Readiness has not been measured for this listing" (AliasBandCell.tsx:73-79). But `CompletenessPill` returns `null` on `pct == null` before it can render anything (IdentityBand.tsx:137), and that pill is the only element carrying `tip` (AliasBandCell.tsx:181). The fallback route is closed too: the band's other `title` carrier is `secondaryTitle`, passed only when `multi` is true (AliasBandCell.tsx:147,174). So on the common single-alias product, the whole sentence is dropped — three files' worth of deliberate honesty about an unknown, rendering as a blank space that is indistinguishable from a loading failure. This is the exact inverse of SH-1: there the studio shows a state it cannot vouch for; here it shows nothing where it should show "unknown".

##### Proposed fix
Do in the band what `readiness.ts:38-41` already does for the scope chips, which get this right: an unparseable or absent verdict becomes an explicit `absent` state with a note, never a blank. Change `CompletenessPill` so `pct == null` renders a neutral-tone pill with an em-dash glyph and the `tip` string as its `title`/`aria-label` instead of returning null — it already takes `state` and `tip` independently of `pct`, so no signature change is needed, and no other caller regresses because a blank is never the intended output. Then pass `title` as `secondaryTitle` unconditionally in `AliasBandCell` rather than only when `multi`. Nothing new is designed: the sentences exist, the tone table exists, the control exists — only the early return stands between them and the screen.

An operator has the GALE-JACKET live on Amazon IT and Amazon DE under the seller account "XAVIA Europe". Amazon revokes the SP-API grant (or an admin disconnects it in Settings → Channels). There is no chip, no banner, no count — the live ASIN is unreachable from every studio surface. With the bookmark, `scope` silently falls back to master (contracts.tsx:652-654) and the operator is shown a neutral Banner reading "This channel is unavailable in the selected market. (1) In `deriveScopeOptions`, keep a marketplace row whose channel has Marketplace coverage but no usable connection, and mark it `connected: false` instead of `continue`-ing (scopes.ts:116). (2) In `StudioBar`, render that channel as a DS `ScopeBarItem` with `disabled: true` and `disabledReason: 'The <label> account is disconnected — reconnect it in Settings → Channels to edit this listing.'` (ScopeBar.tsx:45-51 already carries it into the chip tooltip and `aria-description`). (3) Replace the scopeError sentence with the true one: distinguish "this channel does not serve this market" from "no usable account for this channel" in `contracts.tsx:676` and render the second as a DS `Banner tone="warning"` whose action is a `Button asChild` link to `/settings/channels/<type>`. (4) Give `StudioBar` the ScopeBar `onAdd` handler (`addLabel: 'Connect a channel'`) so the empty case has a route out. ▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator moves the jacket to the bin from /products, then reopens a still-open studio tab (or a teammate follows a Slack link to /products/<id>/edit/studio). They want to know whether the Amazon IT listing came down with it.

##### What happens today
`GET /api/products/:id` is a bare `findUnique({ where: { id } })` with NO `deletedAt` filter (products.routes.ts:385), and `toStudioProduct` never reads `deletedAt` (studio-data.ts:40-54), so the frame loads fully: the DetailHeader shows the name, the SKU, the ASIN and a green `Pill tone="success"` reading "Active" derived from `Product.status`, which a soft delete does not change (StudioHeader.tsx:27-35,65-67). On MASTER the sheet read `getStudioSheet` refuses the binned row (`deletedAt: null`, studio-sheet.service.ts:864-867 → `UnknownProductError`) and the route answers **404** (product-studio.routes.ts:59, 387-413). `useMasterSheet` interprets any 404 as "the studio route is not deployed yet" and silently falls back to the legacy catalogue read (useMasterSheet.ts:186-196), which itself filters `deletedAt: null` (sheet-rows.service.ts:320) and returns zero families — `adaptLegacySheet` happily produces a sheet with `rows: []`, `family.sku: ''` and `meta.source: 'legacy'` (adaptLegacy.ts:94-96,140-157). Rendered result: an empty grid whose overlay says "No products to show — This product group has no rows available in this scope." with a Reload button that can never help (sheetGridStates.ts:15-19, wired at MasterSheet.tsx:1709,1857), plus an "adapted read" Pill whose tooltip asserts "The studio sheet route is not deployed yet" (MasterSheet.tsx:1830-1833) — a false statement about the deployment. Switch to Amazon and the same product produces a contradicting `Banner tone="danger"` "This destination is unavailable — This product is unavailable." (workspace-destination.ts:26-27 → StudioTabHost.tsx:70). Nowhere on the page does the word bin, deleted or restore appear. The stakes: `POST /products/bulk-hard-delete` acts only on products already in the bin and cascades a channel delist, so this is exactly the product whose state the operator most needs stated.

##### Proposed fix
Three surgical changes. (1) Add `deletedAt: string | null` to `StudioProduct` and read it in `toStudioProduct` (studio-data.ts:44-53) — the field is already in the response body. (2) In `StudioLoader`, when `deletedAt` is set, render the DS `EmptyState` it already uses (StudioLoader.tsx:69-78) with title "This product is in the bin", the deletion date, and a `Button` action "Restore from the bin" (or a link to /products?view=bin) instead of mounting an editable studio; if the Owner wants a read-only look, mount the frame with a persistent `Banner tone="warning"` and a `Pill tone="danger"` "In the bin" beside the status pill in `StudioHeader` — the tone table for that already exists. (3) Stop the 404 conflation in `useMasterSheet.ts:188-191`: fall back to the legacy read only when the body's `error` is absent or the response is a route-level 404, and treat `error === 'unknown_product'` as a real failure routed to `SheetLoadError` with the server's own sentence. #### `marketplacesFailed` is computed, threaded through three components and then thrown away — a connections-API blip renders as "this product sells on no channel"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The API is cold-starting (or `/api/connections` 500s for ten seconds). An operator opens the jacket. They see one chip, "Shared product", no Amazon, no eBay, no Shopify, no market switcher — and conclude the product has been de-listed everywhere, or that someone removed the channel connections.

##### What happens today
`loadStudioData` sets `marketplacesFailed = true` on a marketplaces failure AND on a connections failure (studio-data.ts:100,115), and on the connections failure path every marketplace row is still mapped with `connected: connected.has(m.channel)` against an EMPTY set (studio-data.ts:107,116) — so `deriveScopeOptions` drops every channel (scopes.ts:116) and the bar shows only the master chip. The flag survives all the way to `StudioFrame`, where it is destructured into a discard: `export function StudioFrame({ marketplacesFailed: _marketplacesFailed }: StudioFrameProps)` (StudioFrame.tsx:35). The doc comment above it claims "the empty-marketplaces case is now stated by the scope bar itself" (StudioFrame.tsx:28-32) — the ScopeBar states nothing of the kind: it renders the `items` it is given and has no empty or failure branch anywhere in its body (ScopeBar.tsx:188-230). That comment asserts a property the code does not have. The two failures are also merged: "the marketplace table is unreadable" and "connection discovery failed" produce the same silent result, and the operator cannot tell either from "this catalogue genuinely sells nowhere".

##### Proposed fix
Split the flag and spend it. (1) Replace the boolean with `discovery: { marketplaces: 'ok' | 'failed'; connections: 'ok' | 'failed' }` in `StudioData` (studio-data.ts:21-33) so the two causes stay distinguishable. (2) Thread it into `StudioStateProvider` rather than into `StudioFrame`, and in `StudioBar` render, for each channel the marketplace table knows about, a DS `ScopeBarItem` with `disabled: true` and `disabledReason: 'Channel availability could not be read. Reload to try again.'` — this keeps the layout rule intact (nothing new above the grid, v2 §6.6) while making the absence legible, and it uses the ScopeBar affordance that already exists (ScopeBar.tsx:45-51). (3) Put the retry where the studio already puts transient status: the `SheetFooterNote` slot, as a `Button variant="link"` "Reload channels". (4) Delete the false comment at StudioFrame.tsx:28-32 along with the prop.

#### A listing imported from a channel but never published is simultaneously "Ready" and "a marketplace listing you must resolve" — and the refusal drops the findings that would name the ItemID

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A jacket variant was imported from eBay IT during onboarding: the ChannelListing carries a real ItemID but `isPublished` is false (nothing here ever published it). The operator sees the channel scope reporting the variant as ready, decides the variant is a local mistake, selects it on the master sheet and chooses "Delete child…".

##### What happens today
The two halves of the studio disagree about the same row by design. The server's readiness only calls a row `live` when `externalListingId && isPublished` are BOTH set (sheet-rows.service.ts:266-268), so the imported row reports `ready`/`missing` and the scope chip and toolbar show it as publishable. The deletion guard deliberately uses the opposite test — `isLiveOnChannel` is `externalListingId` alone, with a comment recording that PES.3 found 20 non-ACTIVE eBay rows carrying real ItemIDs (listingRisk.ts:41-48) — so `delete-variant`'s preflight refuses with `unavailable: 'This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record.'` (familyActions.ts:452-454). Both readings are defensible; what is not is that the operator is shown one on the chip and the other in the refusal, with no way to reconcile them and no verb to "resolve" anything (the studio has no delist/end/unpublish path at all). Worse, the carefully built evidence never reaches the screen: the preflight attaches `findings` naming each listing as "EBAY · IT — DRAFT, ItemID 256789012345" (familyActions.ts:455-457, labels from listingRisk.ts:59-63), but `runAction` returns `{ kind: 'refused', problem: impact.unavailable }` at level `'none'` and never opens the confirm dialog (runAction.ts:74-75), and `useActionPress` renders only that one string (useActionPress.tsx:58-60) as a bare inline `<span role="alert">` in the family bar (FamilyBar.tsx:105 / FamilySelectionBar.tsx:47). The operator is told to resolve a listing that is never named, on a channel and market never stated. The same path even produces a self-contradiction for wizard-created rows (`isPublished` true, no external id): the headline says "still has a marketplace listing" while the finding for that row reads "never published to the channel" (listingRisk.ts:63) — and the finding is the half that is discarded.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, one DS and one studio. (1) DS: let a refusal carry its evidence. `runAction` should return `{ kind: 'refused', problem, impact }` (runAction.ts:74-75) and `useActionPress` should hand the impact to `useActionConfirm` to render a NON-destructive informational dialog — the `ActionConfirm` surface already itemises `findings` under its own heading and already separates consequences from side effects; a refusal that names "eBay · IT — ItemID 256789012345" is the whole point of ruling #110's "consequences itemised, not counted". (2) Studio: make the two liveness readings one. Surface `externalListingId` in the row readiness vocabulary so a row with an external id but `isPublished: false` renders as its own state (e.g. `live` with a warning tone rather than `ready`), and give the channel sheet's one `⋯` a real `GridAction` — `id: 'remove-from-channel'`, `danger: true`, `scope: 'selection'`, `preflight` naming the channel, market, account and external id, `ConfirmLevel: 'type-to-confirm'` with the real SKU as the phrase — backed by a new `POST /api/products/:id/listings/:listingId/delist` taking `{ mode: 'end' | 'delete', expectedVersion }` and enqueueing `UNPUBLISH_LISTING`/`DELETE_LISTING` on `OutboundSyncQueue` for the existing `dispatchChannelDelist` worker branch. That is the verb the refusal sentence currently tells the operator to use and the studio does not have.
