Confirmed on every load-bearing line. The server calls a row live only when `listing && listing.externalListingId && listing.isPublished` (sheet-rows.service.ts:270; the same test again in studio-sheet.service.ts:1484-1486), while the deletion guard uses the external id alone — `isLiveOnChannel` returns `trimmed(row.externalListingId) !== ''` with the comment 'Not status, not isPublished' (listingRisk.ts:42-48). familyActions refuses with exactly 'This product still has a marketplace listing. Add a `GridAction` `id: 'list-on-this-channel'` to the channel sheet's one `⋯` (CH.1 requires scope verbs to be ITEMS of that overflow, never buttons — SheetToolbar.tsx:15-30), whose `preflight` reports the row's blocking readiness issues and whose `run` opens the wizard BOUND to `{channel, market, accountId}`. #### The cross-channel write acknowledgement is rendered inside a 40px no-wrap bar with flex-basis:100% — the one warning that an eBay edit rewrites Amazon lands off-screen, and the held edit never saves

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket listed on eBay IT and on Amazon DE/IT. On the eBay·IT channel scope they retype the Item title in the sheet. 33 of 35 columns on that scope carry `affectsAllChannels`, so this edit routes to the master record and will change the title Amazon and Shopify show too. Ruling #58 exists exactly to stop that being silent: the sheet must hold the write and say so before it leaves the browser.

##### What happens today
The write IS held — `channelWriteGate` returns `acknowledge`, the edit is parked in `pendingMasterWrite` and nothing is sent (ChannelSheet.tsx:715-726, and the docblock at :660-671 states the contract). But the acknowledgement UI is passed through `SheetToolbar`'s `trailing` slot (ChannelSheet.tsx:2122,2139-2172), i.e. it becomes a direct child of `.nds-grid-sheet .nds-toolbar`. That bar is `height: 40px; flex: 0 0 40px; flex-wrap: nowrap; overflow-x: auto` with `> * { max-width: 100%; flex-shrink: 0 }` (grid.css:1179-1190). `.nds-channel-ack` still carries `flex: 1 1 100%` plus `flex-wrap: wrap` and 8px/12px padding (channel-sheet.css:212-227) — geometry written for the WRAPPING `.nds-channel-toolbar` container that no longer exists (channel-sheet.css:193-204; the class now appears only inside comments, ChannelSheet.tsx:2062, SheetToolbar.tsx:7). Specificity is determinate: grid.css's `flex-shrink: 0` (0,2,0) beats the component's `1` (0,1,0), so the ack becomes an element one full bar-width wide that cannot shrink, placed AFTER the count, search, views trigger, the Required chip and up to four state chips — all themselves unshrinkable. Estimated: those siblings occupy ~1300-1500px before the ack begins, so on a ~1660px sheet the ack starts at or past the right edge and is reachable only by shift-scrolling the bar (macOS overlay scrollbars leave no affordance that anything is there). Vertically its content box is 28px button + 16px padding + 2px border = 46px inside a 40px band whose overflow-y computes to auto, so it is clipped. Net operator experience: the cell shows the new title, the sheet reports nothing, and the value is never sent; or the operator scrolls, finds a clipped button row and presses 'Save to all channels' without the sentence that explains what it does having been visible. The control-census guard has a check for exactly this (`toolbarLayoutInPage`, 'Clipped toolbar control', check-control-census.mjs:391-405, swept at 320..2048px at :608-613) but it never arms the ack, because arming it requires a real cell edit the census does not perform.

##### Proposed fix
Take the acknowledgement out of the toolbar entirely and raise it through the confirm surface this file ALREADY mounts: `useActionConfirm` (imported at ChannelSheet.tsx:105, in use at :608 and :629). ▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator working a jacket's eBay·IT channel scope on a 1440px laptop has a mapping run finished and readiness computed, so the bar carries the Required chip plus Missing required, Invalid values, Warnings and Mapping errors. They want to add a second listing for the same market — the studio's only working '+ Add listing alias' is an item in that bar's ⋯ menu.

`.nds-grid-sheet .nds-toolbar` is `flex-wrap: nowrap; overflow-x: auto` with every direct child `flex-shrink: 0` except the search slot, which floors at 80px (grid.css:1179-1193). `.nds-sheet-toolbar-actions` (Customise · Export · Import · ⋯) is pushed right by `margin-inline-start: auto` (grid.css:1197-1206) — an auto margin that resolves to 0 the moment the content overflows, so the action group goes from pinned at the right edge to beyond it in one step as soon as one more chip appears. Estimating from the CSS (12.5px labels at 22px button padding, 11.5px chips at 22px padding, 8px gaps): master loaded with four chips ≈ 2030px of content, channel ≈ 2100px; the lane's own measurement corroborates the order of magnitude — ChannelSheet.tsx:2085 records the bar was '503px over at 1728' before one sentence was moved to the footer. There is no affordance: the bar is 40px tall with overlay scrollbars. The only mitigation in the CSS is dead — the compaction container query fires at `max-width: 900px` of the toolbar's OWN inline size (grid.css:1420-1424), which is a fact about the container, never about its content, so it cannot fire at 1440 where the overflow is; and none of the eight sheet chips supplies `compactLabel` anyway (master: MasterSheet.tsx:766,791,806; channel: viewChips.ts:121-172 — the only producers that do are the Variants tab's, ChannelProjection.tsx:98,106, which never mount this toolbar), so `.nds-fchip-compact` is never emitted (FilterChip.tsx:48, primitives.css:1611-1612). The `⋯` is the sole studio path to '+ Add listing alias' (only working instance: ChannelSheet.tsx:2019; the ChannelProjection copy at :410 is deliberately held) and to 'Check Information'/preflight, Formula history and Apply formula.

Three changes, all inside the DS. (1) Stop the bar hiding controls behind a scroll: change `overflow-x: auto` to `overflow: hidden` on `.nds-grid-sheet .nds-toolbar` so any overflow becomes a guard failure rather than a silent clip, and keep `.nds-sheet-toolbar-actions { flex-shrink: 0 }` so the action group is the one thing that can never be displaced. (2) Give the chips their own bounded group: wrap the preset chips + view chips in `<div class="nds-sheet-toolbar-chips">` with `flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0; display: flex; overflow: hidden`, and add a `+N` `FilterChip` at its end that opens a DS `Menu` of the chips that did not fit — measured with one `ResizeObserver` hook in `design-system/grid/toolbars/` (`useOverflowIndex(containerRef)`), which is the same collapse the ⋯ already models for verbs. A chip that is currently ACTIVE is never collapsed. (3) Retire the dead container query and require `compactLabel` on every `ViewChip` by making it non-optional in `types.ts:279`, so the eight existing producers must each supply one ('Missing', 'Invalid', 'Warnings', 'Mapping', 'AI', 'Required') — the compact form then has somewhere to be used by the `+N` logic rather than depending on a query that cannot see content.

#### Three adjacent chips print “N columns” for three different quantities, and the number shown is never the number the chip computed or the number it filters to

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens the jacket on master·DE. The bar reads `Required 12 columns` · `Missing required 7 columns` · `AI drafts 1 column`. They read that as three comparable facts and click Missing required expecting 7 things to fix; the sheet filters to 20 rows, the tooltip says 42 cells, and the AI chip's '1 column' is actually 3 pending drafts sitting in one column.

##### What happens today
The Required chip is a PRESET and prints the size of the column set it applies: `count={`${x.columns.length} columns`}` (SheetToolbar.tsx:164) — pressing it NARROWS the sheet to 12 columns. The state chips print `viewChipColumnCountLabel(chip)` (SheetToolbar.tsx:193), which returns `${distinct affected columns} columns` (viewChips.ts:19-24) — pressing one FILTERS ROWS (`rowsForChip`, channel/viewChips.ts:186-200) and tints cells. Same words, opposite meaning, adjacent in the bar. Worse, the producers compute CELLS, not columns: master's `missing-required` sets `count: cells` (MasterSheet.tsx:766) and the channel accumulator increments `acc.cells` per cell (channel/viewChips.ts:56-62,128,140,152), while the rendered number is the column count and the tooltip is a third number again ('42 affected cells across 7 columns and 20 rows', viewChips.ts:26-32). `ai-drafts` leaves `noun` unset (useAiDraftLayer.ts:63-84), so its count of PENDING DRAFTS is re-expressed as a column count by the same branch — approving two of three drafts in one column leaves the chip reading '1 column' throughout. The honesty machinery around these counts is meticulous (`count: null` never renders as 0, viewChips.ts:52-59) which makes the unit slippage harder to spot, not easier.

##### Proposed fix
Make the unit part of the contract instead of a rendering guess. Change `ViewChip.count` in `_studio/types.ts` from `number | null` to `{ n: number; unit: 'cells' | 'rows' | 'columns' | 'variants' | 'axes' } | null` and have `viewChipColumnCountLabel` render `n` with the producer's own unit — dropping the `noun` special-case that silently reinterprets a draft count as a column count. Render the number the chip's own click produces (rows filtered / cells tinted), and keep the full breakdown in the existing `title`/`aria-label`. Separately, stop the Required PRESET wearing a count at all: it is a view, not a measurement, so per §14.4 ('chip leads with STATE, number second') it should render as a pressed/unpressed `FilterChip` with no `count`, or `12 of 137` to mark it unambiguously as a column-set size. That one change removes the collision without touching any producer.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/SheetToolbar.tsx:156-174
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/SheetToolbar.tsx:191-219
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/viewChips.ts:19-32
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/MasterSheet.tsx:766
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/viewChips.ts:56-62
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/viewChips.ts:121-172
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/ai/useAiDraftLayer.ts:63-84

##### Verifier
Confirmed from the code. The Required PRESET renders `count={`${x.columns.length} columns`}` (SheetToolbar.tsx:158-172) and its onClick calls onApplyPreset, i.e. it NARROWS the sheet's columns. The state chips two pixels away render viewChipColumnCountLabel(chip) (SheetToolbar.tsx:193/205), which returns `${viewChipColumns(cells).length} columns` (viewChips.ts:19-24), while clicking one filters ROWS (channel/viewChips.ts:186-200 rowsForChip) and tints cells. Identical trailing noun, opposite consequence, adjacent in one bar — that is the design-inconsistency, and it is real. The producers do compute a different quantity from the one rendered (MasterSheet.tsx:766 `count: cells`; channel/viewChips.ts:56-62,128,140,152 acc.cells), and for ai-drafts the divergence reaches the screen: useAiDraftLayer.ts:63-84 sets count to the number of PENDING DRAFTS with no `noun`, so viewChips.ts:20-23 discards it and prints the affected-column count instead — approving 2 of 3 drafts in one column leaves the chip unchanged. Two corrections to the finding: (1) for the ordinary state chips the number on screen IS the column count and is labelled "columns", so it is not a false number — the defect is the unit/consequence collision, not a lie; the tooltip (viewChips.ts:26-32) and aria-label carry the full cells/columns/rows breakdown. (2) The fix section cites "§14.4 (chip leads with STATE, number second)"; /usr/bin/grep finds no §14.4 in docs/2026-09-01-product-edit-studio-layout.md, so that authority is uncited. Nothing at the top of docs/pes-claims.md settles chip count units. Severity is medium, not high: the ambiguity misleads, it does not lose data or capability.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator notices the jacket's Amazon DE requirements are stale. On the channel scope there is a `Requirements` button next to the chips that opens a modal with a real `Refresh requirements` action. They switch to master to do the same thing and find a warning Pill reading `Cached requirements` that lists the stale schemas on hover and cannot refresh anything.

##### What happens today
`SheetToolbarProps.trailing` is typed `ReactNode` and documented 'Transient STATUS only — a staleness pill, an export note, an in-flight acknowledgement. Never a control.' (SheetToolbar.tsx:105-106), and the file's own header restates the CH.1 ruling that scope verbs are ITEMS of the one ⋯, 'they never add a button of their own' (SheetToolbar.tsx:15-18,99-103). Master passes `ClassificationDialog` into it — a `Button size="sm" variant="ghost"` that opens a modal which PATCHes `/studio/classification` (MasterSheet.tsx:1779, ClassificationDialog.tsx:52). Channel passes `SchemaStatus` — a `Button size="sm" variant="secondary"` opening a modal that force-refetches category schemas (ChannelSheet.tsx:2124, SchemaStatus.tsx:31). The schema-staleness fact itself is rendered twice, two ways: an `InfoTip` + `Pill tone="warning" size="md"` on master (MasterSheet.tsx:1782-1790) and an actionable Button on channel, from the same `meta.schemaAge`/`meta.schemaMissing` payload — so the scope that can fix it looks like a status, and the scope that shows a status has the fix.

Move both verbs into the ⋯ as `MenuItemDef`s under a separator — master gets `Classification…` and channel gets `Requirements…`, joining the family verbs / preflight / Formula history already there — and give MASTER a `Requirements…` item too, fed by the same `meta.schemaAge`/`schemaMissing` it already receives, which closes the parity hole rather than papering over it. Keep the staleness FACT in the bar as the DS `Pill` on both scopes (identical component, identical tone rule), and let the overflow item carry the action. Then narrow the prop as in ST-01 (`status?: { tone; label; tip }`) so the 'never a control' rule is enforced by the type rather than by a comment. This is the same restructure CH.1 already ordered; it is only the two scope-exclusive buttons that were never moved.

#### One bar is doing three jobs, and the guard that would have caught it can only ever measure the bar in its empty state

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Anyone opening the jacket on any scope: the same 40px strip is simultaneously telling them what they are looking at (21 rows · Parent · 12 variations · unlisted · 2 listings), what subset they are seeing (search, All attributes ▾, Required, four state chips), and what they can do (Classification/Requirements, Customise, Export, Import, ⋯ with ten verbs behind it) — plus, on channel, a mid-write confirmation. Fourteen to sixteen interactive elements of six different control kinds in one line.

##### What happens today
In DOM order the bar renders: `.cnt` (count + descriptor, no-wrap, est. 286-403px) → search `Input size="xs"` (flex 1 1 180, floor 80, cap 340) → `GridViewsMenu` trigger (a `Menu` disguised as `.nds-btn sm`, est. 169px) → the Required preset `FilterChip` (est. 137px) → up to four state `FilterChip`s (est. 131-195px each) → `trailing` (master: ghost Button 113px + warning Pill 151px + a 'no children' Pill; channel: secondary Button up to 172px + export note + the ack) → `.nds-sheet-toolbar-actions` (Customise 87 · Export 61 · Import 61 · ⋯ 36). That is a Button, a FilterChip, a Menu-as-button, a static Pill, a bare status `<span>` (the 'Views unavailable' fallback, SheetToolbar.tsx:176-183) and an icon-only Menu sitting in one row with a single 8px gap between every pair — nothing in the markup separates 'what I see' from 'what I can do' except the `.nds-sheet-toolbar-actions` div, and its `margin-inline-start: auto` separation evaporates the moment the bar overflows. The layout gate checks the bar's HEIGHT (40 exactly, check-layout-v2.mjs:653-656) and that the DOCUMENT does not scroll horizontally (:766-769) — which stays true precisely because the toolbar absorbs the overflow into its own `overflow-x: auto`. The control census does have the right check (`bar.scrollWidth > bar.clientWidth`, check-control-census.mjs:399) swept across 320-2048px (:608-613), but it measures whatever bar is on screen: with no session the sheet is `blocked`, so the chips, the Required preset and `trailing` are all absent (SheetToolbar.tsx:112,137-138) and the bar it measures is the one that trivially fits.

##### Proposed fix
Keep ONE bar and one 40px band — CH.1 is right — but make the three jobs structurally separate inside it, in this fixed order on every scope: `[count + descriptor] | [search] [All attributes ▾] [chip group, collapsing to +N] | [Customise] [Transfer ▾] [⋯]`. Concretely: the chip group becomes its own `flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden` div (ST-02) so it is the ONLY thing that yields under pressure; the actions group keeps `flex-shrink: 0` so it can never be displaced; `trailing` becomes a typed status prop (ST-01/ST-04) so no verb can re-enter the middle; Classification/Requirements join the ⋯; Export+Import become `Transfer ▾`. That is five controls plus one chip group plus one overflow, buildable from `GridToolbar`, `FilterChip`, `Menu`, `Button` and `GridViewsMenu` as they exist. Then fix the gate so it can convict: in `check-control-census.mjs` make the sheet sweep ABSTAIN loudly (non-zero, 'NOT MEASURED') unless it observed at least one `FilterChip` and one enabled action in the bar, so a vacuous fit on an unloaded sheet can never read as a pass — and add one arm that seeds the `pendingMasterWrite` state so the acknowledgement from ST-01 is measured at all nine widths.

The finding's own hinge — "the guard that would have caught it can only ever measure the bar in its empty state" — is false. scripts/check-control-census.mjs:443 gets its page from `authenticatedStudioPage`, which throws "A signed-in studio session is required" when /api/auth/me returns no user (scripts/studio-browser-auth.mjs:37-45), so the `blocked` bar the finding describes (SheetToolbar.tsx:112,137) is never what the gate sees; the runner then waits for `.ag-row[row-id]` (:489, ROWS_MS 60s), reports a surface that never rendered as NOT MEASURED (:539), refuses a 0-control census as "vacuous, NOT MEASURED" with exit 1 (:604), and only then runs the 320–2048 sweep of `bar.scrollWidth > bar.clientWidth + 1` plus per-control clipping (:399-406, :608-613). NNN px each" census is estimated from CSS, with no measurement anywhere in the finding. What is left is a restatement of ST-02/ST-04/ST-05 plus a taste argument about grouping, which the layout doc's own CH.1 one-bar ruling already settles in the other direction. Refuted.

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens GALE-JACKET — a jacket with four size variants — at /products/[id]/edit/studio on a 1440x900 MacBook (innerHeight ~750px). They want to scan the family's attributes. Five stacked chrome bands occupy the top third of the window before a single row of the jacket appears, and scrolling the grid does not give any of it back.

##### What happens today
Derived from CSS (global `box-sizing: border-box`, app/globals.css:8), the bands above the grid's first row are: AppTopBar 56px (`--nds-topbar-h: 56px`, design-system/styles/tokens.css:358; rendered on this route because NO_RAIL_PATTERNS matches `/products/[^/]+/edit/studio`, AppShell.tsx:59,112) + WorkspaceSubheader 49px (DetailHeader `dense` height 48, patterns.css:1226-1233, whose own border is zeroed at patterns.css:1556, plus the subheader's 1px border, patterns.css:1553) + StudioBar ScopeBar 40px (`min-height: var(--nds-toolbar-h)`, patterns.css:1595; token 40px, tokens/css-vars.ts:431) + SheetToolbar 40px (grid.css:1178-1182) + grid header 28px (gridDensity.compact.header, tokens/grid.ts:72; GridSheet defaults `density = 'compact'`, GridSheet.tsx:55) = **213px**. Below the rows sit a 36px footstrip (grid.css:1011) and an 8px gutter (GridSheet.tsx:55), so ~257px of a ~750px viewport is not rows — about 34%, against the 74.8%-in-rows budget the host's own comment cites (GridSheet.tsx:38-41). The only reclaim mechanism is `useHeaderCollapse`, which frees C = 16px (useHeaderCollapse.ts:36) and arms only when the expanded scroll range satisfies `expandedRange - 16 >= 32`, i.e. >= 48px (useHeaderCollapse.ts:237-239). At 750px innerHeight the row viewport is 750 - 145 - 8 - 40 - 36 - 28 = 493px, so at the 36px `rowMediaLine` height (tokens/grid.ts:72) a family needs >= 16 rows before the header collapses at all; on a 1080p monitor it needs ~21 — which the hook's own comment confirms ("a 21-row family at 906px has R = 22 and never collapses", useHeaderCollapse.ts:13-14). A four-variant jacket is five rows. So for the overwhelming majority of products the studio's entire vertical-space strategy is inert, and when it does fire it returns 16px of 213. Separately, the responsive tier system built for this row is dead: `useContainerTier`/`tierFor`/`RowTier` have zero consumers (`/usr/bin/grep -rn "useContainerTier|tierFor(" apps/web/src packages` returns only useContainerTier.ts:19,25,35 — self-references; positive control: the same scan for `useHeaderCollapse` returns StudioFrame.tsx:24,38 plus the test), and the CSS it drove — `.mergedRow`, `.tabsCompact`, `.tierC`, `.tabRow`, `.tabStrip` (studio.module.css:69,235,243,250,256,261,264) — has no `styles.*` consumer anywhere in apps/web/src.

##### Proposed fix
Reclaim 49px by moving the DetailHeader `dense` band into the topbar's already-reserved page-context slot, and delete the dead tier machinery.

1. `.nds-topbar-context` (app-topbar.css:91-98) is `flex: 1 1 auto` and renders an empty `<div>` on every route (AppTopBar.tsx:86). Its comment promises "pages opt in via usePageChrome()" — that hook does not exist (`/usr/bin/grep -rn "usePageChrome|PageChrome" apps/web/src` returns only that comment line, AppTopBar.tsx:84). Build it as the DS pattern it is: `usePageChrome({ back, title, meta, status, actions })` publishing into a `PageChromeProvider` mounted by `AppTopBar`, with `DetailHeader dense`'s existing slot names so nothing is re-invented. StudioHeader then calls `usePageChrome(...)` and renders nothing, and the studio's top stack becomes topbar 56 (now carrying `< Products · GALE-JACKET · SKU · Active · Autosave on · Publish ▾`) + ScopeBar 40 + toolbar 40 + header 28 = **164px**, one extra row on a laptop and ~2 on a 1080p monitor, with no information lost.
2. Delete `useContainerTier.ts` and the `.mergedRow` / `.tabsCompact` / `.tierC` / `.tabRow` / `.tabStrip` rules from `studio.module.css`; they encode a layout (merged chips + tab strip) that the WorkspaceSubheader nav drawer replaced, and leaving them reads as live responsive behaviour to the next reader.
3. With the header folded up, `useHeaderCollapse` has nothing left to collapse — retire it rather than keeping a 16px mechanism that fires only on >=16-row families. Its arming-invariant doc comment is worth preserving in `docs/` as the record of why range must be measured against expanded geometry.

#### Row count, selection count and autosave state are each rendered twice — once at the top of the sheet card and once at the bottom, 213px apart, from two independent sources and two aria-live regions

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator editing a 21-variant jacket family on the shared-product sheet ticks three rows and pastes a price column down. The toolbar above the grid says "21 rows · 3 selected" and "Saving 4…" appears in the page header at the very top of the window; at the same moment the strip under the grid says "21 rows · 3 selected" and "Saving…". A screen-reader user hears the same save event announced twice. When the writes land, "Saved 14:32" appears in both places, and the Amazon scope chip simultaneously swaps to a loading state for the same event.

##### What happens today
Three separate duplications, all rendered at once:

**Row + selection count.** `SheetToolbar`'s count slot renders `<b>{p.visible}</b> rows … {p.selected} selected` (SheetToolbar.tsx:119-121) from `visible={visibleRows.length} selected={selected}` (MasterSheet.tsx:1743-1745). `GridSheetStatus` renders `<b>{rows}</b> rows … <b>{selected}</b> selected` (GridSheet.tsx:133-141) from `rows={visibleRows.length} selected={selected}` (MasterSheet.tsx:1811). Same two numbers, same two sources, two bands apart. The two have already drifted once in production — ChannelSheet.tsx:2073 carries the fix comment "the toolbar said 20 while the footer beneath it said 21".

**Autosave state.** The header's `SaveIndicator` renders `Saving {n}…` / `Saved 14:32` / `N changes not saved` (saveState.ts:192-205, SaveIndicator.tsx:52-79). The footer strip renders `Saving…` / `N unsaved cells` / `N refused` / `Saved 14:32` (GridSheet.tsx:142-165). Both are `role="status" aria-live="polite"` (SaveIndicator.tsx:54,63 and GridSheet.tsx:131), so every save is announced twice.

**A third copy on the scope chip.** `StudioBar` feeds the same save state into the active channel's readiness: `if (id === scope && save.kind === 'error') return { state: 'blocked', note: save.message }` and `if (id === scope && save.kind === 'saving') return 'loading'` (StudioBar.tsx:17-18). So a refused cell turns the Amazon chip red — overwriting the chip's real meaning (listing completeness) with a transient write outcome, in a bar whose DS contract defines readiness as "how complete a scope is, as far as the SERVER has said" (ScopeBar.tsx:19-25).

The cost is not only pixels: the toolbar count slot and the header status are the two slots the CH.1 contract reserves for things the operator cannot get elsewhere, and both are spent restating the footer.

##### Proposed fix
One fact, one slot — the DS already has the right homes, they are just both occupied.

1. **Counts live in the footer only.** `GridSheetStatus` is the DS component specified as "the strip under a sheet: what is on it" (GridSheet.tsx:128). Change `SheetToolbarProps.count`/`visible`/`total`/`selected` so the toolbar's count slot carries only the `descriptor` — what this sheet *is* ("Family · 1 parent, 4 variations" on master; "Amazon · IT · 2 listings, 4 variations" on a channel) — and drop the tallies. That also removes the class of defect ChannelSheet.tsx:2073 documents, because there is then only one counter.
2. **Save state lives in the header only.** The header's `SaveIndicator` is the studio's single autosave authority by design (SaveIndicator.tsx:6-13). Give `GridSheetStatus` a `reportSaveState?: boolean` (default `true`, so no other grid host changes) and pass `false` from both studio sheets; keep `refused` in the footer, because its `GridSheetNote` slot is the only place that can narrow the sheet to the affected rows. That also leaves exactly one `aria-live` region for saves.
3. **Take the save state off the scope chips.** Delete StudioBar.tsx:17-18. If a refusal must be visible on the bar, it belongs in the DS `Banner` the tab host already mounts (StudioTabHost.tsx:68), not in a completeness vocabulary that means something else.

No ruling settles this: the spec assigns the descriptor to the toolbar's count slot (docs/2026-09-01-layout-v2-spec.md:149,185) and the refusal count to the footer (:660,:1191) but nowhere ratifies rendering the tallies in both, and the 09-04 review lists the toolbar/footer disagreement as an inconsistency to fix (:85,:118), not as an accepted shape.
Directionally right and DS-shaped, with two cautions. (a) Stripping the tallies from SheetToolbarProps touches the SHARED toolbar both sheets mount (ChannelSheet.tsx:2065-2081 comments call the standard controls 'not props here, they ARE the component') — the `absent` mechanism at SheetToolbar.tsx:113 exists precisely so a control cannot be silently dropped, so the count slot's contract change needs the same treatment rather than a quiet prop removal. #### On Amazon and eBay scopes the content language is invisible and uncontrollable, and a round trip through a channel chip silently discards the operator's chosen master language — the next master edit then writes into a different language record

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is writing the French copy for GALE-JACKET on the shared product. They pick "French" in the language select, type a new description, then click the Amazon chip to check how it reads on Amazon IT, then click "Shared product" to come back and finish the French bullet points. The language select now reads Italian (the IT market's default) — nothing said so, nothing moved on screen except the values in the cells. They keep typing French copy, and it is saved into the Italian record.

##### What happens today
Three linked facts.

**(a) There is no language control on Amazon or eBay.** `StudioBar` renders the language `Listbox` only when `scope === MASTER_SCOPE` (StudioBar.tsx:29-31) or when the scope is SHOPIFY/ETSY (StudioBar.tsx:36). On AMAZON/EBAY the right slot holds account (only if `accounts.length > 1`), market, and a Clear button — no language, and no read-only statement of it either.

**(b) Language is nonetheless a live read dimension on those scopes.** `ChannelScopeTab` passes `locale` into `ChannelSheet` and into its remount key (ChannelScopeTab.tsx:58,64), and `useChannelSheet` puts it on the wire (`if (o.locale) params.set('locale', o.locale)`, useChannelSheet.ts:74) and on every write coordinate (useChannelSheet.ts:309). `contracts.tsx:672-673` narrows the option list to `Marketplace.languages` for AMAZON/EBAY, and `localeError` (contracts.tsx:674-675) can replace the entire tab with a Banner (StudioTabHost.tsx:68) telling the operator to "Choose a supported content language" — for a control that is not rendered on that scope.

**(c) The master language choice is destroyed by the channel hop.** `setScope` writes `[URL_KEYS.locale]: ['AMAZON','EBAY'].includes(next) ? undefined : localeParam ?? undefined` (contracts.tsx:904). Going master(fr) → AMAZON strips `locale` from the URL; coming back, `localeParam` is gone, so `locale` falls back to `defaultLocaleFor(market, …)` (contracts.tsx:681-685, scopes.ts:190-194) — the market's language, not the operator's. Nothing announces the change.

**Why that is a data risk, not just a legibility one.** Master writes are keyed on the resolved locale: `masterWrite.ts:211` builds `const patch = { [ctx.locale]: {} }` and `:217` assigns `patch[ctx.locale][field] = c.value`, with resets at `:216` also per-locale. So text typed after the silent revert lands on the default-locale record and overwrites whatever was there. The FR value is not lost, but the IT/default one is — and the sheet gives no signal that the coordinate moved.

I searched the whole studio tree for any other language affordance: `StudioBar.tsx` is the only site rendering a `Content language` control; the nav drawer groups (StudioSubheader.tsx:29-51) carry no language item; `navigationHref.ts` preserves `locale` on tab and channel navigation (studioViewHref:23-29 keeps every param; studioChannelViewPatch:4-9 does not touch `locale`) — so the drawer path is safe and only the scope chip drops it, which is exactly what makes the loss hard to attribute.

##### Proposed fix
Make language a permanent member of the coordinate line, and stop discarding it.

1. **Render the language control on every scope.** Delete the `scope === MASTER_SCOPE ? … : …` branch in StudioBar.tsx:29-36 and render the DS `Listbox` unconditionally, with `options.locales` already narrowed per channel by contracts.tsx:672-673. Where a marketplace declares exactly one language, render it as a DS `Pill` rather than a select — visible, not interactive — so the answer to "which language am I editing" is never blank.
2. **Stop stripping `locale` on scope change.** Change contracts.tsx:904 to carry `localeParam` across and let the existing `localeError` validation (contracts.tsx:674-675) do the refusing, which is what it is for. When the carried language genuinely is not supported by the destination, the honest behaviour is the one the codebase already uses elsewhere (navigationHref.ts:8's `channel.markets[0]` fallback): substitute the nearest supported language **and** surface it — a DS `Banner tone="info"` in the tab host reading "Amazon IT does not publish French. Showing Italian." A silent substitution and a silent strip are the same defect.
3. **Make the coordinate one statement, not three controls.** The ScopeBar's `right` slot now holds up to four independent selects. Replace them with a single DS `Menu`-triggered coordinate control whose trigger reads `Amazon · IT · Seller-EU · Italian` and whose panel holds the four lists — one thing to read at a glance, one place to change it, and `patchSearch` already coalesces multi-key changes into one history entry (contracts.tsx:119-126), so market+account+language can move together without three URL writes.

- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/StudioBar.tsx:36
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:904
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:672
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:674

[high]verifiedALLux defect

#### On the shared-product scope the market is not rendered anywhere, yet the channel chips report readiness computed for that hidden market

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens GALE-JACKET on the shared product. Their last session was on Amazon DE, so `lastMarket` restores DE. The scope bar shows "Editing: Shared product | Amazon · Blocked 62% | eBay · Ready 94% | Shopify". They read that as "Amazon is blocked", tell a colleague the Amazon listing is broken, and click Amazon — landing on DE, a market they never chose in this session and whose name appeared nowhere on the page. The Amazon IT listing they actually care about is fine.

##### What happens today
`StudioBar` renders the market `Listbox` only on a channel scope; the master branch renders the language select and nothing else (StudioBar.tsx:29-36). But the chips it builds in that same render are market-scoped: `readiness: market && c.markets.includes(market) ? scored(c.id) : undefined` (StudioBar.tsx:25), and `scored` reads `readiness.byScope[id]` (StudioBar.tsx:20) from `useReadinessQuery`, whose coordinate is `JSON.stringify([productId, market, channel, accountId, listingId, locale])` (contracts.tsx:349). So each chip states a per-market verdict under a bar whose only visible label is "Editing".

The market that produced those numbers is chosen without the operator: `market` falls back to `defaultMarket(baseOptions)` (contracts.tsx:647-650), which is `lastMarket.ts` localStorage first and otherwise "the market served by the most channels, alphabetical tiebreak, GLOBAL excluded" (scopes.ts:143-184). Neither value is displayed on master.

The lane has already diagnosed this exact failure in a neighbouring form — contracts.tsx:365-370 records "switching IT → DE left `Amazon 71%` on screen for the whole of the new read, and 71% was IT's number sitting under a bar that said DE. Showing a value under the wrong coordinate is worse than showing no value, **because nothing on screen says it is the wrong one**." The staleness was fixed; the labelling half was not, and on the master scope the bar does not say *any* market.

Relatedly, `scopes.ts:199` states the intended contract as "A chip outside its markets is disabled, not hidden" — but `StudioBar` never sets `disabled` or `disabledReason` on a `ScopeBarItem`, so a channel that does not serve the hidden market renders as an ordinary chip with no readiness and no explanation. `ScopeBar.tsx:46-51` requires `disabledReason` precisely because "a disabled control that cannot explain itself is a dead end"; here the control is not even disabled, so there is nothing to explain with. (Clicking it is safe — `setScope` re-points the market at `channel.markets[0]`, contracts.tsx:905-906 — but that is a fourth silent coordinate change.)

##### Proposed fix
The market select must be rendered on every scope, including master — it is the coordinate the chips are scored against, so hiding it makes the chips unreadable rather than making the bar simpler.

1. Move the market `Listbox` out of the channel-only branch in StudioBar.tsx:32-38 into the shared part of the `right` slot (or into the single coordinate control proposed in CS-3), so "Editing: Shared product · IT" is always on screen. It costs no vertical space — the ScopeBar `right` slot is already occupied on master by the language select.
2. Give the DS `ScopeBar` a `readinessScope?: string` prop rendered as the bar's eyebrow suffix (`label="Editing"` → `Editing · Italy`), so the coordinate a readiness number belongs to is stated by the same component that draws the number. That closes contracts.tsx:365-370's rule structurally instead of by convention.
3. Honour `scopes.ts:199`: pass `disabled: !market || !c.markets.includes(market)` and `disabledReason: \`${c.label} does not sell in ${marketLabel(market)}.\`` on each `ScopeBarItem` (StudioBar.tsx:25). The DS already renders both (ScopeBar.tsx:46-51); today neither is supplied, so a documented affordance is absent from every chip.

#### The route skeleton draws three bands totalling 129px against the real frame's two bands totalling 89px, so the sheet jumps 40px upward on every studio load — in a file whose comment promises it does not

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator clicks GALE-JACKET from the products list. The studio paints a skeleton: a header strip, a scope strip with three pill placeholders, and a third strip of four short tab placeholders. A moment later the data arrives, the third strip vanishes and the second shrinks, and the whole sheet — toolbar, headers and rows — jumps up by about 40px under the cursor they were already moving toward a chip.

##### What happens today
`ProductStudioLoading` renders three bands from `studio.module.css`: `.skelHeader` 48px, `.skelScope` 44px, `.skelTabs` 34px (loading.tsx:19,24,30; studio.module.css:193-203), each with a 1px bottom border — 129px total.

The real frame renders two: `StudioSubheader` mounts `WorkspaceSubheader` with a `header` and **no `tabs` prop** (StudioSubheader.tsx:63-75; `tabs` is optional and only rendered when non-null, WorkspaceSubheader.tsx:119), giving DetailHeader `dense` 48px (patterns.css:1226-1233) inside a 1px-bordered subheader = 49px; then `StudioBar` as a sibling (StudioSubheader.tsx:76) at `min-height: var(--nds-toolbar-h)` = 40px (patterns.css:1595, tokens/css-vars.ts:431). Total 89px.

Two concrete mismatches: the tab strip the skeleton draws no longer exists at all (tabs moved into the nav drawer, StudioSubheader.tsx:29-51), and the scope band is drawn at the pre-v2 44px (`.nds-scopebar` base, patterns.css:1273-1281) rather than the 40px the `.nds-workspace-scope` override actually applies.

The stylesheet comment directly above those rules claims the opposite: "The frame's own shape — three bands at the exact heights the real ones use, so the first paint does not move when the data lands" (studio.module.css:181-182). It is a comment asserting a property the code does not have, and it is the reason nobody has looked: the skeleton is the one surface whose correctness is invisible in every screenshot taken after load.

##### Proposed fix
Stop restating the band heights in a second place, and delete the band that no longer exists.

1. In `studio.module.css`, drop `.skelTabs` entirely and make `.skelHeader` / `.skelScope` *consume the same declarations as the real bands* instead of copying their numbers: `.skelHeader { height: 48px }` → `composes` nothing, but set both from the shared tokens the real bands use — `.skelHeader { height: var(--nds-detailhdr-dense-h) }` (add that token to `tokens/css-vars.ts` beside `--nds-toolbar-h` and have `patterns.css:1228` consume it too) and `.skelScope { min-height: var(--nds-toolbar-h) }`. One definition, no drift — the same rule `reference_token_scale_defined_twice` exists for.
2. Update `loading.tsx` to two bands, and change the `.skelScope` placeholders from three 28px pills to the real shape (pills + right-hand 28px selects) so the horizontal layout settles too.
3. Correct the comment at studio.module.css:181-182 to say what it is: two bands, heights derived from the band tokens. Then add the height pair to `scripts/check-layout-v2.mjs`, which already keys a band budget on the `.nds-scopebar`/page-band geometry (patterns.css:1282-1293) — a skeleton that silently diverges from the frame is exactly the class that gate exists to catch.

[medium]verifiedALLdesign inconsistency

#### The collapsed header hides the product's status pill and keeps the SKU — the exact inverse of what its own rule says it does, and of what an operator needs while scrolling

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is working down a 21-variant jacket family on a 1080p monitor. They scroll past the top of the grid, the header snaps from 48px to 32px, and the "Active" status pill, the ASIN, the "Parent" pill and the "Child of GALE-PARENT" link all fade out — while the SKU, which is already the first column of every row beneath them, stays. Fifty rows down they want to check whether this product is still Active before pushing a price change; nothing on screen says, and there is no control to expand the header — only scrolling back to the top.

##### What happens today
Two rules drive the collapsed state. `studio.module.css:286-287` hides `.nds-detailhdr-meta > *:not(:first-child)` and, redundantly, every `.nds-pill` inside the meta group. `StudioHeader`'s meta children are, in order: the SKU span (StudioHeader.tsx:57-59), the ASIN span (:60-64), the status `Pill` (:65-67), the `Parent` pill (:68), and the family link or `Child` pill (:69-82), all rendered into `.nds-detailhdr-meta` by DetailHeader.tsx:98/119. So the **first** child — the SKU — always survives, and everything after it, including the status, is hidden.

The comment immediately above those rules states the intent as the reverse on both counts: "What the collapsed strip drops: the SKU/ASIN pair and the pills. The name, status, autosave and Publish ▾ stay — see spec §4.1" (studio.module.css:284-285). The code drops the status and keeps the SKU.

The consequence is not cosmetic. The SKU is already in the grid's identity band on every row (the band is structurally pinned on both scopes, ChannelSheet.tsx:1488-1492), so the collapse keeps the one fact that is redundant and hides the four that are not — product status, ASIN, parent/child role, and the way up to the family. The hidden elements are `opacity: 0; pointer-events: none` (studio.module.css:288-290), so they are not merely small, they are unreachable, and there is no expand control: the state is driven only by `scroller.scrollTop > 32` / `<= 16` (useHeaderCollapse.ts:90-91).

##### Proposed fix
If CS-1's fold into the topbar lands, this rule disappears with the collapse. Until then, invert it to match its own stated contract, and make the choice explicit rather than positional.

1. Replace the positional selector with an intent attribute. Have `StudioHeader` mark the meta children it is willing to lose — `<span data-collapse="drop">` on the SKU and ASIN spans, nothing on the status pill, the Parent pill or the family link — and change studio.module.css:286 to `.shell.collapsed :global(.nds-detailhdr-meta) [data-collapse='drop'] { … }`, deleting the blanket `.nds-pill` rule. A collapse rule that selects on DOM order silently changes meaning the next time someone reorders the meta slot; one that selects on a declared intent cannot.
2. Correct the comment at studio.module.css:284-285 to describe what ships, and record the SKU-is-already-in-the-grid reasoning there — that is the fact that makes the decision obvious to the next reader.
3. Either way, keep the status visible: `Pill tone="success" dot` at 20px fits a 32px band with room to spare, so nothing about the collapsed geometry forced this.

##### Verifier
Confirmed against both the code and the approved spec, and the spec makes it worse than the finding claims. studio.module.css:284-285 states the intent — 'What the collapsed strip drops: the SKU/ASIN pair and the pills. The name, status, autosave and Publish ▾ stay — see spec §4.1' — and :286-290 implements `.shell.collapsed .nds-detailhdr-meta > *:not(:first-child)` plus `.shell.collapsed .nds-detailhdr-meta .nds-pill` at `opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-2px); pointer-events: none`. StudioHeader.tsx:54-83 renders the meta children in order: SKU span (:56-58), ASIN span (:59-63), status Pill (:64-66), Parent Pill (:67), family link or Child Pill (:68-81), and DetailHeader.tsx:98 puts exactly that fragment into `.nds-detailhdr-meta`. So the first child — the SKU — survives and the status pill is hidden, the inverse of the comment. The spec agrees with the comment and not the code: docs/2026-09-01-layout-v2-spec.md:478-481 §4.1 says the collapsed strip 'keeps, in one line: back link, product name (truncated), status dot, autosave state, Publish ▾' and 'drops: the SKU/ASIN monospace pair, the Parent pill' — so this is a divergence from a ratified decision, not just from a comment. The redundancy argument checks out too: the SKU is structurally pinned in the identity band on the channel sheet (ChannelSheet.tsx:1488-1492 region). And there is no expand affordance — useHeaderCollapse.ts:89-91 drives the state purely from `scroller.scrollTop > 32` / `<= 16`.
Step 1 (declare intent with a `data-collapse="drop"` attribute instead of selecting on DOM order) is the right shape and fixes the class of bug, not just this instance — a positional selector silently changes meaning when the meta slot is reordered, which is what happened here. Two corrections to the framing: the fix should cite spec §4.1 (docs/2026-09-01-layout-v2-spec.md:478-481) as the binding contract rather than the stylesheet comment, since the spec also says the `⋯` menu moves into Publish ▾ while collapsed and that menu no longer exists (Owner D9, StudioHeader.tsx:86-92) — so §4.1 needs a note either way. And step 1's deference to CS-1 ('if the fold into the topbar lands, this rule disappears') should be dropped: CS-1's fold is not approved and this two-line correction should not wait on it.

[high]verifiedALLux defect

#### Jumping to a channel via the navigation drawer carries the content language across; on Amazon/eBay that replaces the whole surface with a banner the operator has no control to satisfy

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is editing the shared record of a winter jacket on the Shared product scope and switches the content language to French to check the FR copy (?locale=fr). The remembered market is DE. They open the navigation drawer and click 'eBay › Listing information' to go check what eBay Germany is missing.

##### What happens today
The navigation path and the scope-bar path are two different scope changes with two different rules. The scope-bar chip goes through setScope, which deliberately drops the locale key for Amazon and eBay: `[URL_KEYS.locale]: ['AMAZON','EBAY'].includes(next) ? undefined : localeParam ?? undefined` (contracts.tsx:904). The navigation drawer goes through setTab(tab, channel) → studioChannelViewPatch (contracts.tsx:946, navigationHref.ts:4-10), whose patch names tab/scope/market/account/listing/rec/cell/chip and NOT locale — so `?locale=fr` survives verbatim. On eBay×DE, supportedLanguages resolves to the Marketplace row's languages (contracts.tsx:670), 'fr' is not among them, and localeError fires: 'Choose a supported content language for this destination: de.' (contracts.tsx:674-675). scopeError falls through to localeError (contracts.tsx:676-678) and StudioTabHost replaces the ENTIRE tab body with `<Banner tone="neutral" title="Choose an available scope">` that carries NO action prop (StudioTabHost.tsx:68) — while the sibling account banner four lines down does carry one (StudioTabHost.tsx:72). There is then no language control on screen: StudioBar renders a Content language Listbox only on master (StudioBar.tsx:29-32) and on SHOPIFY/ETSY (StudioBar.tsx:36), and `setLocale` has exactly two call sites, both in StudioBar (verified with /usr/bin/grep over the whole studio tree, positive control: 7 hits in contracts.tsx). The banner instructs the operator to choose a language and simultaneously removes every means of choosing one. The only escapes are the browser Back button, hand-editing the URL, or re-clicking the eBay chip they are already on (ScopeBar fires onChange even for the active chip, ScopeBar.tsx:224) — none of which is discoverable from the banner.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, both small. (1) Make studioChannelViewPatch the single definition of 'change scope', so the navigation drawer and the scope chip cannot disagree: add the locale rule to the patch in navigationHref.ts (clear it when the destination channel is AMAZON or EBAY) and have setScope call studioChannelViewPatch rather than hand-build its own object — one function, two callers, no drift (the DS README's 'one concept defined once'). (2) Make the refusal recoverable rather than terminal: give the scopeError Banner an `action` slot exactly as the account branch already does — `action={<Button onClick={() => setLocale(supportedLanguages[0])}>Use {localeLabel(supportedLanguages[0])}</Button>}` — and, for the general case, render the DS Listbox for Content language on every scope, narrowed to `options.locales` (which contracts.tsx:672-673 already narrows per channel) instead of hiding it on Amazon/eBay. DS Banner + DS Listbox; no new component needed.

[high]verifiedALLdesign inconsistency

#### The market governs where every channel task lands but is invisible on the Shared product scope, and a navigation jump changes it silently and does not remember it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator's home market is Italy. They open a jacket on the Shared product scope to fix the shared description. The scope bar shows 'Shared product · Amazon · eBay · Shopify' and one Language dropdown — no market anywhere. They open the navigation drawer and click 'eBay › Listing information' to check the eBay listing. eBay does not sell in IT for this workspace, so they land on eBay Germany and start editing German offer data believing they are in Italy.

##### What happens today
On master, StudioBar's right slot renders ONLY the Content language Listbox (StudioBar.tsx:29-32); the Market Listbox exists exclusively in the channel branch (StudioBar.tsx:34-35). Yet `market` is fully live on master: it is resolved from `?market=` or defaultMarket (contracts.tsx:646-651), it decides which channel chips carry readiness at all (StudioBar.tsx:26), and it is the market every channel-group link will open in — studioChannelViewPatch computes `market && channel.markets.includes(market) ? market : channel.markets[0]` (navigationHref.ts:8). So on a channel the operator does not serve, the destination market is the channel's FIRST market alphabetically (deriveScopeOptions sorts, scopes.ts:127-130), chosen by the code, announced nowhere: WorkspaceNavItem has no description field and no disabled state (WorkspaceSubheader.tsx:11-18), and the landing surface shows no 'market changed' notice. Worse, the two market writers diverge on memory: writeLastMarket is called ONLY inside setMarket (contracts.tsx:924 — the sole call site, verified with /usr/bin/grep over apps/web/src). A market arrived at through a navigation jump or through setScope's fallback (contracts.tsx:905-906) is therefore never remembered, so the next session silently reverts to a market the operator has not worked in since.

##### Proposed fix
Render the Market Listbox in ScopeBar's `right` slot on EVERY scope including master — the market is part of the coordinate the chips are read at, which is exactly what that slot's own doc comment says it is for (ScopeBar.tsx:74-82). On master populate it from `options.markets` unfiltered; on a channel keep the existing `m.channels.includes(scope)` filter. Then make a code-chosen market audible: have studioChannelViewPatch return the resolved market and, when it differs from the incoming one, emit a DS toast via `useToast()` ('Opened eBay in DE — eBay does not sell in IT'). Finally call writeLastMarket from one place — inside `enqueue` whenever the patch carries a market key — so every writer of the market remembers it, not just the dropdown.

Market is nonetheless live on master — resolved at contracts.tsx:646-651, used to decide whether a channel chip carries readiness at all (StudioBar.tsx:26), and it is the market every channel-group link opens in (navigationHref.ts:8, `market && channel.markets.includes(market) ? market : channel.markets[0]`, with markets sorted alphabetically by deriveScopeOptions at scopes.ts:124-134). The toast on a code-chosen market is good; prefer it over a banner since the change is not an error.

[high]verifiedALLcorrectness risk

#### A studio URL is not a durable address of a coordinate: when the operator sits on their remembered market, ?market= never enters the URL and the recipient's own localStorage silently re-resolves it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Two merchandisers share a workspace. One is Italy-facing (their browser remembers IT), the other Poland-facing (remembers PL). The Italy merchandiser opens a jacket, goes to the Media task on the Shared product scope, sees a broken image, copies the URL out of the address bar and pastes it into chat: '/products/abc/edit/studio?tab=images'. The Poland colleague opens it and is looking at a different coordinate.

##### What happens today
The market reaches the URL through only three writers — setMarket (contracts.tsx:917-936), setScope (contracts.tsx:905-906) and studioChannelViewPatch (navigationHref.ts:8) — plus a restore effect that is guarded: `if (marketParam) return; ... if (!remembered || remembered === market) return` (contracts.tsx:888-893). So when the operator's remembered market already equals what defaultMarket computes, or when they simply never touch the scope bar, `?market=` is never written at all. The URL then carries no market, and on the recipient's machine that same effect reads THEIR localStorage key `nexus:studio:market` (lastMarket.ts:19-27) and replaceStates a different market in. Same link, two coordinates — and on master neither operator can see the market to notice (NAV-2). This is a concrete mechanism for the defect scopes.ts:160-167 records as still unexplained ('unpinned deep link resolves to a different market per load', DE and PL reported), and it fits the fact that comment uses to exonerate defaultMarket: PL is served by one channel so defaultMarket can never return it, but readLastMarket can return any market that passes the validity check at contracts.tsx:892. The same class hits the scope: a `?scope=EBAY` link with no `?market=` resolves against the recipient's remembered market, and if eBay does not serve it the scope silently falls back to master (contracts.tsx:659) and the surface is replaced by the 'Choose an available scope' banner (StudioTabHost.tsx:68).

##### Proposed fix
Pin the resolved coordinate into the URL once, on first resolve, instead of only when it differs from a remembered value. Replace the early return at contracts.tsx:891 with an unconditional normalisation effect: when `?market=` is absent, write the RESOLVED market (remembered ?? defaultMarket) through the existing coalesced `push` in replace mode, so the address bar always states the coordinate on screen. Do the same for `?scope=` when master is reached by fallback rather than by choice. One replaceState on load, no history entry, and 'copy the URL' becomes the shareable coordinate the module header at contracts.tsx:11-13 already promises. Additionally, when a shared link's scope is dropped by the market fallback at contracts.tsx:659, the DS Banner should name both halves and carry the recovery — `action={<Button onClick={() => setMarket(firstMarketServing(scopeParam))}>Open eBay in DE</Button>}` — instead of the current generic sentence with no action.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:888-893
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/lastMarket.ts:19-27
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/scopes.ts:160-167
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/scopes.ts:174-182
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:646-651
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:659
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/StudioTabHost.tsx:68
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:11-13

##### Verifier
Mechanism confirmed; the illustrative scenario is internally inconsistent but that does not kill the defect. Confirmed: the restore effect is double-guarded — `if (marketParam) return` then `if (!remembered || remembered === market) return` (contracts.tsx:888-891) — so no `?market=` is written whenever the operator's remembered market already equals the resolved default, or when they have no remembered market at all; and `readLastMarket` reads a per-browser key `nexus:studio:market` (lastMarket.ts:18-29). The recipient's own localStorage therefore re-resolves the coordinate for the same link. This contradicts the module header's own promise that a studio link 'is a coordinate someone can send to a colleague' (contracts.tsx:11-13, read). The scope half is also confirmed: a `?scope=EBAY` link with no market falls back to MASTER_SCOPE when the resolved market is not served (contracts.tsx:659) and the tab body is replaced by the actionless banner (StudioTabHost.tsx:68). The unexplained-defect note the finding leans on is real and at the cited place (scopes.ts:160-167, 'unpinned deep link resolves to a different market per load', DE and PL). Weakness noted, not fatal: the finding's own scenario has the Italy operator remembering IT while defaultMarket computes DE — in that case the effect DOES write `?market=IT` and the copied link is pinned; the mechanism only bites when remembered equals the default or is absent. Severity corrected to medium for that reason.
Sound and cheap: the normalisation write goes through the existing coalesced `push` in replace mode, so it adds no history entry and cannot lose a key to a same-tick write (the reason the effect was moved onto `push` in the first place, per the comment at contracts.tsx:880-887). One caution the fix does not mention: writing the resolved market unconditionally on every cold load means a shared link is pinned by the FIRST viewer's resolution the moment they load it, which is what you want, but it also means the URL changes under the operator on load — acceptable with replaceState, worth stating. The scope-fallback banner with a recovery action is the same Banner `action` slot NAV-1 asks for; land them together.

[medium]verifiedALLa11y defect

#### The same destination appears twice in the navigation drawer under two names and both are marked aria-current='page'; and the 'THIS PRODUCT' group label is false because its items re-project by scope

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator scoped to eBay Italy opens the navigation drawer to move from the sheet to the Media task. They see 'THIS PRODUCT: Information · Variants · Media · Needs attention · Performance · Activity' and below it 'EBAY: Listing information · Description themes · Variation order'. Both 'Information' and 'Listing information' are highlighted as the current page, and nothing says that 'THIS PRODUCT › Media' will open eBay's media workspace rather than the product's shared gallery.

##### What happens today
The THIS PRODUCT items are marked active on `tab === id` alone, ignoring scope (StudioSubheader.tsx:30), while channel items use `scope === channel.id && tab === task.tab` (StudioSubheader.tsx:48). On any channel scope with the sheet open both predicates are true, and WorkspaceSubheader stamps `aria-current="page"` on every active item (WorkspaceSubheader.tsx:161) — two current pages in one nav. They are also literally the same URL: studioViewHref('sheet') deletes the tab key (navigationHref.ts:25) and studioChannelViewPatch returns `{tab: undefined}` when `scope === channel.id` (navigationHref.ts:6), so 'Information' and 'Listing information' resolve to the identical address under two labels (navigation.tsx:16 vs StudioSubheader.tsx:38). The group heading compounds it: the comment at StudioSubheader.tsx:28 asserts 'THIS PRODUCT holds the shared tasks', but every one of those items is re-projected by scope — SheetTab branches on scope (StudioTabHost.tsx:44-47), ImagesTabRoute returns EbayMediaRoute/AmazonMediaRoute/ShopifyContentRoute purely on scope (ImagesTabRoute.tsx:22-25), and `errors` is channel-only in practice. The group asserts a product-level axis it does not have, which is what makes the two-axis model illegible: navigation does not pick the task independently of the owner, it picks the task and inherits the owner from a bar the operator may have forgotten they set.

##### Proposed fix
Make the group label state the owner instead of denying it: rename the first group from the constant 'THIS PRODUCT' to the live scope — 'SHARED PRODUCT' on master, 'EBAY · IT · <account>' on a channel — built from the same strings the ScopeBar chips use, so both axes share one vocabulary. Then drop the duplicate: when `scope === channel.id`, omit that channel's 'Listing information' item so its group keeps only the channel-exclusive tasks (Description themes / Variation order / Product family); the double aria-current disappears by construction. If the Owner wants the channel group to stay complete, the one-line alternative is to scope the first group's predicate to master — `active: tab === id && scope === MASTER_SCOPE` — so the two groups never both claim the page.

Confirmed on every cited line. THIS PRODUCT items are `active: tab === id` with no scope term (StudioSubheader.tsx:30-32); channel items are `active: scope === channel.id && tab === task.tab` (StudioSubheader.tsx:48). On any channel scope with the sheet open both are true, and WorkspaceSubheader stamps `aria-current={item.active ? 'page' : undefined}` on every item (WorkspaceSubheader.tsx:161) — two current pages in one nav. The two items resolve to the same URL: studioViewHref deletes the tab key for 'sheet' (navigationHref.ts:24-25) and studioChannelViewPatch returns `{tab: undefined}` when `scope === channel.id` (navigationHref.ts:5-6), and 'sheet' survives visibleTabs on every scope (scopes.ts:219-222) with the label 'Information' (navigation.tsx:16) against the channel group's hardcoded 'Listing information' (StudioSubheader.tsx:38). The group-label half also holds: the comment at StudioSubheader.tsx:28 asserts the shared-task framing while SheetTab branches on scope (StudioTabHost.tsx:44-47) and ImagesTabRoute re-projects purely on scope. Severity stays medium: it is a labelling/a11y defect, not a data hazard.
The one-line alternative (`active: tab === id && scope === MASTER_SCOPE`) is wrong as stated: on a channel scope it would leave Media/Performance/Activity with NO active item at all even though those items are the live destination there — the duplicate only exists for 'sheet'. Prefer either the stated primary fix (omit the channel's own 'Listing information' when `scope === channel.id`) or scope the predicate for the sheet item only. The group-relabel is a good idea but note the channel group headings already carry the channel label, so 'EBAY · IT · <account>' on the first group and 'EBAY' on the second may read as two eBay groups; the relabel needs the scope chip's exact vocabulary, as the fix says.

[medium]verifiedALLux defect

#### An open record survives a task change into tabs that cannot render it, and the drawer's close button then walks the operator to a different task instead of closing

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator scoped to Amazon DE opens the record drawer on the jacket's 'bullet_point' cell to read the full value, then clicks 'Media' in the navigation drawer to check the images, then clicks 'Information' to come back. The drawer is still open on the same cell. They click its close button to get the sheet back to full width.

##### What happens today
setTab is the only URL writer that does not clear the record keys: setScope clears rec/cell (contracts.tsx:907-908), setMarket clears them (contracts.tsx:932-933), setAccount and setListing clear them (contracts.tsx:940-941), but setTab patches only the tab key (contracts.tsx:948). `?rec=…&cell=…` therefore rides into every task. StudioDock is mounted by exactly two surfaces — MasterSheet.tsx:1916 and ChannelSheet.tsx:2222 (verified with /usr/bin/grep over the whole studio tree; the remaining hits are the module, its barrel and comments) — so on Media, Performance, Activity, Description themes and Variation order the keys are live in the URL with no UI at all: an invisible open record that a reload or a shared link faithfully restores to nothing. Then the close path breaks: openRecord pushes a history entry and increments a counter (contracts.tsx:983-986), and closeRecord decrements it and calls `router.back()` (contracts.tsx:990-993) on the assumption that the entry immediately behind is the open. setTab also pushes (contracts.tsx:948), so after Information → Media → Information the stack is [sheet, sheet+rec, media+rec, sheet+rec] with the counter still at 1. Pressing the drawer's close (StudioDock.tsx:256 → record.close) steps back one entry and lands the operator on the Media task with the record still open in the URL and no drawer rendered — the close button silently became a navigation, and the thing it was asked to close is still there.

##### Proposed fix
Two lines and one invariant. (1) Add `[URL_KEYS.record]: undefined, [URL_KEYS.cell]: undefined` to setTab's patch (contracts.tsx:948) — a record belongs to the surface that opened it, the same reason setScope and setMarket already clear it; the coalescing at contracts.tsx:808-830 means this costs no extra navigation. (2) Stop inferring 'the entry behind me is my open'. flushUrl already passes a fresh state object, so pass `{ studioRec: true }` when the patch opens a record (Next's copyNextJsInternalHistoryState preserves extra keys alongside __NA) and have closeRecord call router.back() only when the CURRENT entry's state carries that marker, otherwise drop the keys in place — the branch the code already has at contracts.tsx:995 for arrivals via a shared link. Close is then correct under any interleaving of task changes and browser Back.

- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/master/MasterSheet.tsx:1916
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/channel/ChannelSheet.tsx:2222

##### Verifier
Confirmed. setTab's plain branch patches only the tab key (contracts.tsx:949; the channel branch at :948 clears rec/cell only when the scope actually changes, via studioChannelViewPatch's `scope !== channel.id` arm, navigationHref.ts:5-8), while every other coordinate writer clears the record keys — setScope :907-908, setMarket :932-933, setAccount :940, setListing :941. So `?rec=&cell=` rides into every task. The mount set is confirmed with /usr/bin/grep over apps/web/src: `<RecordDrawer` appears exactly once, inside StudioDock.tsx:247, and `StudioDock` is mounted by exactly two surfaces — MasterSheet.tsx:1916 and ChannelSheet.tsx:2229 (the finding cites 2222, which is the comment block immediately above the mount — a harmless off-by-seven, the set claim is right). The close path is confirmed: openRecord increments `opened` and pushes (contracts.tsx:983-989), closeRecord decrements and calls `router.back()` (contracts.tsx:990-996) with the in-place drop only in the counter-zero branch (:997); setTab also pushes history (`push(..., true)`), so after Information → Media → Information the entry behind is the Media view and Back lands there with the record keys still in the URL and no drawer mounted. StudioDock passes `onClose={record.close}` (StudioDock.tsx:259).
(1) is correct and consistent with the four writers that already do it. (2) is the sharper half and is stated safely: the codebase's own hard-won rule is that the state object passed to pushState must NOT be `window.history.state` (it must be a fresh object free of `__NA`) — passing `{ studioRec: true }` respects that, and historyStateIsInternal (scopes.ts:230-240) only rejects `__NA`/`_N`, so the guard at contracts.tsx would not fire. Verify empirically that Next's copyNextJsInternalHistoryState preserves the extra key before relying on it; if it does not, the simpler correct fix is to compare the CURRENT URL's rec key rather than a marker.

#### A channel chip for a market that channel does not serve is mute and fully clickable — no dot, no state word, no tooltip, not disabled — contradicting the rule stated in the studio's own source

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the jacket's market set to Poland, where only Amazon sells. The scope bar shows 'Shared product · Amazon · Not set up · eBay · Shopify'. The eBay chip carries nothing at all. They click it expecting to see why eBay is empty in Poland, and land on eBay Germany.

##### What happens today
StudioBar builds each channel chip as `{ id, label, readiness: market && c.markets.includes(market) ? scored(c.id) : undefined }` (StudioBar.tsx:26). ScopeBar's contract already has the fields this case needs — `disabled` and a `disabledReason` whose doc comment says it is 'Required in practice, not by the type: a disabled control that cannot explain itself is a dead end' (ScopeBar.tsx:44-52) — and StudioBar passes neither (no occurrence of 'disabled' in the file; /usr/bin/grep rc=1, with the file's own 'ScopeBar' hit as the positive control). With `readiness` undefined the chip renders no dot, no state word and no title, because chipTitle returns undefined when there is no readiness and no disabledReason (ScopeBar.tsx:94-97) and the dot/state/percent only render when `ready` is truthy (ScopeBar.tsx:230-236). It is still fully clickable (ScopeBar.tsx:224). Clicking it runs setScope, which re-defaults the market to `options.channels.find(c => c.id === next)?.markets[0]` (contracts.tsx:905-906) — the channel's alphabetically first market — with no notice. Meanwhile scopes.ts:198 states the intended rule verbatim: 'Is this channel actually sold in this market? A chip outside its markets is disabled, not hidden.' Nothing implements it: channelServesMarket has only three runtime callers, all in contracts.tsx (:659, :905, :922), none of them a chip's disabled state. The mute chip is also ambiguous against a second case — a scope whose readiness has simply not been fetched — because both render as a bare label.

##### Proposed fix
Honour the rule the source already states, with the DS fields that exist. In StudioBar.tsx:26 build the channel item as `{ id: c.id, label: c.label, ...(market && c.markets.includes(market) ? { readiness: scored(c.id) } : { disabled: true, disabledReason: `${c.label} does not sell in ${marketLabel(market)}. Markets: ${c.markets.map(marketLabel).join(', ')}.` }) }` — ScopeBar already renders disabledReason as both the title and the aria-description, keeps the chip out of the roving tabindex (ScopeBar.tsx:218) and out of the arrow-key ring (ScopeBar.tsx:164). Apply the same rule to the navigation drawer's channel groups, which today list every connected channel unconditionally (StudioSubheader.tsx:33): WorkspaceNavItem has no disabled field, so either add one to the DS type alongside `badge` (WorkspaceSubheader.tsx:11-18) or render that channel's group with a single non-interactive item naming the markets it does serve. A channel the operator cannot reach from here must say so rather than silently relocating them.

The StudioBar half uses only fields ScopeBar already honours (title, aria-disabled, roving-tabindex exclusion at :218, arrow-ring exclusion at :164) — verified in the render. Two cautions. First, it collides with the spirit of ruling #235: make sure `c.markets` is the Marketplace-table derivation (it is — deriveScopeOptions, scopes.ts:124-126), so a channel that genuinely sells in the market is never disabled just because the product is unlisted there. Second, the drawer half needs a DS type change (WorkspaceNavItem has no disabled field, WorkspaceSubheader.tsx:11-18), which is another lane's file — raise it as a DS request rather than editing it inline.

[critical]verifiedALLdata integrity risk

#### The channel delist the operator authorised is destroyed by the same transaction that deletes the product — it never reaches Amazon or eBay

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket (SKU GALE-JACKET-BLACK-L) live on Amazon IT and eBay IT. They bin it, open the recycle bin, select it, press Permanently delete, leave the pre-selected "Unpublish (recommended)" channel action, type DELETE, and confirm. They see success and the rows disappear. The Amazon SKU offer and the eBay ItemID stay live and sellable — and the local record that could have managed them is gone.

##### What happens today
`POST /products/bulk-hard-delete` creates the delist queue rows INSIDE the same Prisma transaction that then deletes the Products. `tx.outboundSyncQueue.createManyAndReturn` (products-catalog.routes.ts:1878-1899) writes each row with `channelListingId: l.id` and `productId: l.productId`; `tx.product.deleteMany` runs at :1972-1973 in that same `tx` callback. `OutboundSyncQueue` declares BOTH FKs `onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:6822-6826), so the Product delete cascades through ChannelListing and destroys every delist row it just created. `fireOutboundJobs` then runs post-commit (:2000-2003) and pushes a BullMQ job whose payload is only `{ queueId: e.id, productId, syncType }` (outbound-enqueue.ts:48-58) — an id with no row behind it. The code comment at products-catalog.routes.ts:1845-1851 asserts the opposite in so many words ("by then the local Product + ChannelListing are gone, but the queue rows still carry productId + externalListingId"); the schema contradicts the comment. No dry-run, no receipt and no post-hoc status: the UI's only feedback is the optimistic toast fired from `hardDeleteBulk`'s `run(...)` wrapper (BulkActionBar.tsx:334-348).

##### Proposed fix
Two parts, and the UX half is the one this audit owns. (a) Backend: the delist rows must not be children of what is being deleted — either enqueue them AFTER the transaction commits, or drop `channelListingId`/`productId` from the delist rows and carry the whole coordinate (channel, marketplace, externalListingId, externalParentId, sellerId) in `payload`, which the adapters already read. (b) UX: stop reporting a channel outcome from a local transaction. Model this as the two-phase operation it is, using the pattern the studio already ships in `FormulaBulkDialog` (apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/FormulaBulkDialog.tsx:12,95-100): DS `Modal` + `DataGrid` showing one row per (SKU × channel × market) with its live identifier, then Apply, then a per-row result table of what the channel actually answered. On completion render a DS `Banner tone="warning"` with `action={<Button>View sync log</Button>}` (Banner.tsx:25-26,49) rather than a success toast, and never mark the operation done until the queue rows report SUCCESS/FAILED. A destructive verb whose remote half is asynchronous must have a visible pending state; today it has none.
