CONFIRMED at the mechanism level, from code I read myself; two secondary UX assertions in the finding are overstated and are corrected below.

CORE DEFECT — every link verified:
1. The route is live and unique. `fastify.post('/products/bulk-hard-delete', ...)` at apps/api/src/routes/products-catalog.routes.ts:1773; the file is registered (apps/api/src/index.ts:144). /usr/bin/grep for "bulk-hard-delete" across apps/api/src returns only orders/fulfillment variants at other paths — no shadowing duplicate for products.
2. The delist rows are created INSIDE the transaction: `tx.outboundSyncQueue.createManyAndReturn` with `productId: l.productId` and `channelListingId: l.id` at products-catalog.routes.ts:1880-1897.
3. The Products are deleted in the SAME `tx` callback: `tx.product.deleteMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })` at :1971-1974 (the transaction closes at :1998).
4. The FK is CASCADE at the DATABASE, not just in the Prisma schema — this is the link the finding asserted only from schema.prisma, and I chased it into the migration SQL: `ALTER TABLE "OutboundSyncQueue" ADD CONSTRAINT "OutboundSyncQueue_productId_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("productId") REFERENCES "Product"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE` (packages/database/prisma/migrations/20260502_phase31b_channellisting_marketplace/migration.sql:232-235) and the same for `channelListingId` (:237-240). I checked for a later override with /usr/bin/grep -rli "outboundsyncqueue" across all migrations: six files touch the table; only the workspace-isolation migration adds a constraint and it is `OutboundSyncQueue_business_owner_fkey` on `workspaceId` (20260908b_workspace_data_isolation/migration.sql:4384). No SET NULL anywhere. The table is created once, in the same migration as the FKs (:146). So both cascade paths are armed, and `relationMode` is unset (default foreignKeys — datasource block, schema.prisma:5-8), so Postgres does the delete.
5. The post-commit fire carries only ids: `fireOutboundJobs(delistFireEntries, …)` at :2000-2003, payload `{ queueId, productId, syncType, source }` at apps/api/src/services/outbound-enqueue.ts:48-58.
6. The consumer proves the row is required: apps/api/src/workers/bullmq-sync.worker.ts:104-110 does `prisma.outboundSyncQueue.findUnique({ where: { id: queueId } })` and, when absent, logs "Queue record not found" and THROWS before ever reaching the delist branch at :141-158. The cron backstop drains PENDING rows and there are none. So no path — instant lane or cron — can reach `channelDelist`.
7. The contradictory comment is real and verbatim at :1844-1851 ("by then the local Product + ChannelListing are gone, but the queue rows still carry productId + externalListingId"). A SECOND file holds the same wrong belief: apps/api/src/services/channel-delist.service.ts:31-32 — "productId (may be null after hard-delete cascade — that's OK)" / "channelListingId (likely null after cascade — that's OK)". Two authors independently assumed SET NULL; the DB says CASCADE. That is corroboration, not a wash.
8. The UI path is the one described: HardDeleteConfirmModal's `onConfirm` calls `hardDeleteBulk(channelAction)` (BulkActionBar.tsx:1053-1057), which POSTs to `/api/products/bulk-hard-delete` (BulkActionBar.tsx:334-348), and the radio defaults to 'unpublish' whenever any listing exists (BulkActionBar.tsx:1116). No test covers the cascade (/usr/bin/grep found no vitest file naming hard-delete).

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED: no duplicate/shadowing route; no earlier or later migration weakening the FK; no tombstone or alias table carrying the coordinate forward (the payload the adapters could work from is written on the row that dies); eBay is NOT a stale no-op that would make the loss moot — `endFixedPriceItem` is really wired at channel-delist.service.ts:284-302, so a working delist is what gets destroyed.

WHERE THE FINDING IS OVERSTATED (corrected, but not fatal):
(a) "No dry-run" is FALSE. `/api/products/hard-delete-preflight` is fetched on modal open (BulkActionBar.tsx:1099-1126) and renders a pre-flight panel with channel·marketplace listing counts, open orders, bundles and FBA stranded inventory (BulkActionBar.tsx:1205-1240). What is missing is per-row identifiers and any AFTER state, not the pre-flight.
(b) "Optimistic toast" is imprecise: `run()` awaits the fetch and toasts on HTTP 200 (BulkActionBar.tsx:228-246). The defect is that a local-transaction 200 is reported as the whole operation. Worth noting the backend does return `channelCascadeEnqueued` (:1993) and /usr/bin/grep -rn "channelCascadeEnqueued" apps/web/src returns ZERO hits — the one number that could have hinted at channel work is never surfaced.
(c) The modal is also hand-rolled (raw `div role="dialog"`, Tailwind slate/rose classes, BulkActionBar.tsx:1147-1160) rather than the DS Modal — which supports the proposed fix's DS direction, though it is a separate finding.
Fix (a) is right and the second variant is the better one: dropping `channelListingId`/`productId` and carrying the full coordinate in `payload` also survives the ChannelListing-side cascade, which enqueue-after-commit does NOT (a concurrent listing delete still orphans the row). But it needs one addition the proposal misses: the worker cannot dispatch a row whose FKs are null unless the dispatcher reads channel/market/externalListingId off the row and payload — channel-delist.service.ts:30-40 claims it already tolerates nulls, so verify that claim against the actual dispatch code at :108 before relying on it. Also, `fireOutboundJobs` uses `jobId: e.id` for dedup (outbound-enqueue.ts:57), so moving the enqueue post-commit needs the row id to still exist at fire time — fine for variant two, and a reason not to mix the two variants.

Fix (b) — the UX half — is sound in direction but mis-scopes the starting point twice. It says "no dry-run"; there IS one (hard-delete-preflight, BulkActionBar.tsx:1099-1126, rendered at :1205-1240). The work is to upgrade that panel from per-channel COUNTS to one row per (SKU x channel x market) with the live identifier — which is exactly the DataGrid the proposal describes, so the proposal is right about the destination and wrong that it is starting from nothing. Second, "success toast" understates: the operation must not report done at all until the queue rows report SUCCESS/FAILED, which means the modal needs a real pending state fed by a poll or the sync-log — the proposal says this but does not name the data source. A cheaper interim that the proposal skips: the route already returns `channelCascadeEnqueued` (:1993) and nothing in apps/web reads it — surfacing "N channel delists queued, not yet confirmed" is a one-line honesty fix that can ship before the two-phase dialog.

One more thing the proposal should own: the modal is hand-rolled (raw div role="dialog", Tailwind slate/rose, BulkActionBar.tsx:1147-1160), so "use DS Modal + DataGrid" is a rewrite of this dialog, not a decoration of it — size it accordingly.

[critical]verifiedAMAZONux defect

#### "Unpublish (recommended)" is the pre-selected default and promises republishability that Amazon cannot deliver — the adapter performs a hard SP-API delete

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
The same operator reads the channel-action radio group and picks the one labelled "(recommended)" because it promises "keeps the listing record so you can republish later". On Amazon that sentence is false: the SKU offer is deleted from the Listings Items API, which is the irreversible option they were steered away from.

##### What happens today
The radio defaults to `'unpublish'` (BulkActionBar.tsx:1097) and is labelled `Unpublish (recommended)` with the body `Pause the offer on each channel — keeps the listing record so you can republish later. Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing; Shopify: status DRAFT.` (en.json products.hardDelete.channelAction.unpublish.label/body). `delistAmazon` does not implement unpublish at all: when `action === 'unpublish'` it logs `'Amazon UNPUBLISH falling back to DELETE (PATCH client TODO)'` and falls straight through to `amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem` (channel-delist.service.ts:150-166). Shopify has the same shape with a runtime `typeof svcAny.updateProduct === 'function'` check and a silent delete fallback (:186-200). The same dialog also contradicts itself on the local half: its own body says "Local rows + every dependent (channel listings, sync history, stock log, FBA shipment lines) are wiped" (en.json products.hardDelete.body) while the radio directly beneath promises the listing record is kept. Nothing in the dialog is derived from what the adapter will actually do — the three bodies are hardcoded strings.

##### Proposed fix
The option text must be generated per channel from the adapter's declared capability, not written once as prose. Introduce a `delistCapability(channel): 'reversible' | 'irreversible' | 'unimplemented'` on the API and return it from the existing `GET /api/products/hard-delete-preflight` the dialog already calls (BulkActionBar.tsx:1103-1122). Render the radio group as DS `RadioCard` (primitives) with one card per action, and where a selected product is on a channel whose capability is not `reversible`, that card is shown in the `disabled(reason)` shape the grid registry already mandates (registry.ts:55-68): "Amazon has no unpublish — the SKU offer is deleted. Use Close offer on the fulfilment page to pause it reversibly." Never default-select an action whose promise does not hold for every channel in the selection; default to the narrowest one (`Local-only`) and make the operator choose the wider blast radius deliberately.

So the operator's "recommended, republishable" choice reaches `deleteListingsItem` with no other branch in between.

Mis-stated sub-claims (do not refute the finding, but should be corrected before it is acted on):
1. Shopify does NOT lie today — `async updateProduct(` exists at apps/api/src/services/marketplaces/shopify.service.ts:383, so the `typeof` guard passes and Shopify really does go to status DRAFT. It is a latent fragility (a runtime duck-type on a method that exists), not a false promise.
2. The "dialog contradicts itself on the local half" is an over-read. en.json:5204's "channel listings … are wiped" means the local `ChannelListing` rows; the radio's "keeps the listing record" means the channel-side record. Ambiguous wording, not a contradiction — the real defect is the Amazon promise alone.
3. Blast-radius context the finding omits: `deleteListingsItem` reads the mode from raw env at amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1142 (`process.env.AMAZON_PUBLISH_MODE ?? 'dry-run'`), unlike the other SP-API writes which call `getAmazonPublishMode()` (client.ts:519, 669, 792). That is a second, separate defect (the master gate cannot dry-run a delist), and it means the live-ness of the Amazon delete depends on an env var I cannot read from a read-only audit.

Scope note for the PES brief: `/usr/bin/grep -rn "hardDelete|hard-delete"` over apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio returns nothing — this dialog lives only in the products-list BulkActionBar (products/_components), so the studio itself exposes no per-channel delist/relist at all. The finding's own evidence therefore supports a broader gap than it claims.
The direction is right (derive the option text from an adapter-declared capability rather than prose) but the proposal has three problems. (1) It treats capability as a per-channel constant; it is per (channel, action, build): Shopify's 'reversible' is currently decided at runtime by `typeof svcAny.updateProduct === 'function'` (channel-delist.service.ts:186-190) and eBay's delist branch is documented as pending in the same file's header (:20-25) — a static `delistCapability(channel)` table would drift from the adapters exactly the way the prose already has. Derive it from the adapter module (one exported `capability` per adapter, asserted by a test that fails when an adapter's branch falls through) so the string cannot outlive the code. (2) Disabling the card is the wrong affordance for a mixed selection: with Amazon + Shopify selected, the operator still needs a way to unpublish Shopify; the card should stay selectable and carry a per-channel breakdown ("Shopify, eBay: reversible · Amazon: SKU offer deleted, ~30-day cooldown"), which the preflight already has the data to render since it returns channelListings grouped by channel (BulkActionBar.tsx:1135-1141). Prefer no pre-selection at all (confirm stays disabled until the operator picks), which is the only option that neither over-promises nor silently orphans. Also missing from the fix: the raw-env dry-run read at amazon-sp-api.client.ts:1142 should move to getAmazonPublishMode(), or the whole dialog's promise is unverifiable from the gate the rest of the system uses.

#### The app's most destructive verb is gated by typing the literal word DELETE, pre-shown in the input's own placeholder — the exact anti-pattern the design system forbids

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator who purges the recycle bin weekly has learned the gesture: click Permanently delete, type the word already printed in the box, press the red button. The one week the selection also contains a live jacket on Amazon DE, nothing about the gesture is different — the friction is muscle memory, not reading.

`armed = typed.trim().toUpperCase() === 'DELETE'` (BulkActionBar.tsx:1129). The phrase is the constant `products.hardDelete.confirmPlaceholder = 'DELETE'` (en.json), it is printed as the instruction label (BulkActionBar.tsx:1337) AND set as the input's `placeholder` attribute (:1345), so the string to type is visible inside the field the operator must fill. Matching is case-insensitive. The design system's own destructive doctrine says the opposite twice: `registry.ts:117` — "For `type-to-confirm`: exactly what must be typed. A SKU, never \"DELETE\"." — and `ActionConfirm.tsx:18-21` — "the phrase is the real SKU — never the word \"DELETE\", which trains an operator to type five letters without reading anything." The studio's own verbs follow the rule (channelActions.ts:337 uses the channel name as `confirmPhrase`; familyActions.ts:510 escalates to `type-to-confirm` only when children exist), so the app has two contradictory standards for the same gesture and the weaker one guards the more dangerous verb.

Replace the hand-rolled block with the DS one: build an `ActionImpact` from the preflight the dialog already fetches and render it through `useActionConfirm` (ActionConfirm.tsx:55). The `confirmPhrase` becomes the real subject — the SKU for a single product, or `"<channel> <marketplace>"` for a channel-scoped delist (the shape channelActions.ts:337 already uses) — and the `placeholder` attribute is removed entirely so the phrase has to be read from the label and reproduced. Keep `validateImpact` (registry.ts:264-273) in the path so a typed confirm can never silently soften into a click.

[high]verifiedALLcorrectness risk

#### A refused channel verb shows the operator a developer diagnostic instead of the reason the lane wrote — and delist will inherit the same shape

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the jacket live on Amazon IT, selects its row on the Amazon · IT channel sheet and picks "Pause 1 offer on Amazon · IT" from the row menu, intending to stop buyers seeing it while they fix the size chart. They get: "Pause 1 offer on Amazon · IT was refused: preflight failed but still asked for a confirmation — a verb must not run on a guess." They never learn that the verb is preview-only on live listings, and nothing tells them what would work instead.

##### What happens today
`offerVerb`'s preflight always returns `level: 'confirm'` (channelActions.ts:225) and, when any selected row sits on a live alias, ALSO sets `unavailable: 'Refused for now: N of these are live listings, and wave-1 verbs do not send to a channel. Preview only.'` (:248-250). `broadcastToListings` does the same with `level: 'type-to-confirm'` (:330, :343-345). But `validateImpact` treats `unavailable` with any level other than `'none'` as a malformed impact and returns the developer string "preflight failed but still asked for a confirmation — a verb must not run on a guess" (registry.ts:270-272); `runAction` applies rule 3 (validation) BEFORE rule 4 (unavailable) and returns `{kind:'refused', problem: <that string>}` (runAction.ts:72-80); `useActionPress` renders it verbatim as `${label} was refused: ${problem}` (useActionPress.tsx:57-59). So the honest sentence the lane wrote is unreachable on exactly the rows it was written for. `delete-child` proves the contract's intent by doing it the other way — `level: 'none'` with `unavailable: 'This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record.'` (familyActions.ts:445-449) — and that message does reach the operator. These two are the studio's only write-capable channel verbs, so today 100% of live-listing refusals on the channel sheet surface the diagnostic.

##### Proposed fix
Separate the two facts the shape is conflating. Add to `ActionImpact` a typed refusal — `refusal?: { reason: string; whatWouldFix?: string; verb?: { label: string; actionId: string } }` — and have `runAction` return `{ kind: 'refused', problem: refusal.reason, refusal }` before it ever validates confirmation level; keep `unavailable` meaning only "the preflight itself could not complete". ▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
Next season the operator wants the jacket off Amazon IT only, keeping DE and keeping the ability to put IT back. The right verb (reversible close, snapshot kept) and the wrong one (permanent delete, ASIN history gone) will be two adjacent items in the same ⋯ menu, and when either opens its confirmation the operator will see the same modal, the same two bullet sections and the same button reading "Confirm".

##### What happens today
`ActionImpact` carries exactly `level, cancelled, title, consequences, sideEffects, findings, payload, confirmPhrase, unavailable` (registry.ts:76-125). There is no field for "this is reversible", "here is how to put it back", or "this cannot be undone". `ActionConfirm` therefore renders three fixed blocks — "What this changes", "What the check found", "This also happens" — plus the typed input, and nothing else (ActionConfirm.tsx:96-152). The only irreversibility statement anywhere in the studio is a hand-typed sentence inside a `consequences` array: `${row.sku} is deleted permanently — there is no undo and no trash` (familyActions.ts:466) — prose in a list, invisible to any guard, and absent from every other verb. The product is not short of the ingredients: the DS `Banner` has an `action` slot (Banner.tsx:25-26,49) and the studio already uses it for a real undo — `AmazonMediaWorkspace.tsx:278-279` renders `<Banner tone="info" action={<Button>Undo bulk changes</Button>}>` after a bulk apply — while `FormulaBulkDialog` ships a full dry-run → apply → server `/undo` loop (FormulaBulkDialog.tsx:12, 95-100). The DS Toast is deliberately NOT that surface: it takes only `(message, tone, {duration})`, renders `role="status"` with no action slot, no dismiss control and no hover-pause, and removes itself on a fixed `setTimeout` (Toast.tsx:12-16, 30-50) — a toast-with-undo would vanish mid-reach and is unreachable by keyboard.

##### Proposed fix
Add one required-by-convention field to `ActionImpact`: `reversal: { kind: 'reversible'; summary: string; verb?: { label: string; actionId: string } } | { kind: 'permanent'; summary: string }`. `ActionConfirm` renders it as a fourth, visually distinct block — "Putting it back" for reversible, a `danger`-toned "This cannot be undone" strip immediately above the footer for permanent — and `validateImpact` refuses any impact with `danger: true` that omits it, the same way it already refuses a typed confirm with no phrase (registry.ts:264-273). This is what makes escalating friction real rather than cosmetic: "End listing on Amazon IT" declares `reversible` with `verb: { label: 'Relist on Amazon IT', actionId: 'relist' }` and gets `level: 'confirm'`; "Permanently delete this offer" declares `permanent` and gets `level: 'type-to-confirm'` with the SKU. After a reversible run the host renders `Banner tone="warning" action={<Button>Relist on Amazon IT</Button>}` — the AmazonMediaWorkspace precedent, persistent and keyboard-reachable — never a toast.

(b) `apps/web/src/design-system/components/index.ts` has 53 export lines and zero matches for confirm/dialog/alert (/usr/bin/grep rc=1, positive control 53); `useActionConfirm` is exported only from `grid/index.ts:54`. #### "Unpublish (recommended)" promises three things the code does not do — it is an irreversible Amazon delete described as a pause

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a winter jacket live on Amazon IT, Amazon DE and eBay IT. They want it off for the season. The studio offers no lifecycle verb at all, so they go to /products, tick the jacket, bin it, then open Permanently delete. The modal's channel-action radio defaults to "Unpublish (recommended)" whose body reads: "Pause the offer on each channel — keeps the listing record so you can republish later. Amazon: discontinued; eBay: end listing; Shopify: status DRAFT." Every word of that sentence tells them this is the reversible seasonal option. They type DELETE and confirm.

##### What happens today
All three claims are false. (a) "Amazon: discontinued" — channel-delist.service.ts:151-155 logs 'Amazon UNPUBLISH falling back to DELETE (PATCH client TODO)' and falls through to amazonSpApiClient.deleteListingsItem at :162; the word DISCONTINUED exists in this repo only inside that comment (/usr/bin/grep -rn DISCONTINUED over apps/api/src returns one hit, the comment at :152). (b) "keeps the listing record" — the route's own comment at products-catalog.routes.ts:1845-1851 says the opposite: "by then the local Product + ChannelListing are gone"; ChannelListing is onDelete: Cascade off Product (schema.prisma:1515). (c) "so you can republish later" — there is no relist implementation; ENDED→anything has no writer, and the studio tree has zero references to any relist, recovery or reopen endpoint. The Italian string carries the same three falsehoods (it.json:5222-5223). Additionally the delist cascade only reads listingStatus in ['ACTIVE','INACTIVE'] (products-catalog.routes.ts:1857), so a wizard-created listing left at DRAFT is silently not unpublished at all while the modal says every channel was handled.

##### Proposed fix
Delete the word "unpublish" from the product vocabulary entirely and replace this radio with the canonical three-verb set, rendered per channel from server truth rather than one hardcoded sentence. Canonical verbs: **Pause offer** (buyers stop seeing it, the listing and its identifier survive, one click puts it back), **End listing** (the listing stops existing on the channel; putting it back creates a new one), **Delete listing** (the channel record and the local row are both destroyed). Until Amazon's patchPurchasableOffer unpublish path is wired, the Amazon row of that table must read "End listing — Amazon has no pause; the SKU offer is deleted and the ASIN survives" and the option must not be labelled "recommended". Implementation: this modal is legacy Tailwind; rebuild it on the DS grid action registry so it goes through ActionImpact — consequences itemised per channel (registry.ts ConfirmLevel 'type-to-confirm', ActionConfirm.tsx renders consequences vs sideEffects separately), with the per-channel native term shown as secondary text ("Amazon · IT — deleteListingsItem, the SKU offer is removed"). The per-channel mapping belongs in ONE exported table beside readinessMeta (e.g. design-system/grid/renderers/lifecycle.ts) so no surface can restate it, exactly as readiness.ts:51-66 already does for state labels.

That column is a free String (schema.prisma:1615) whose comment declares DRAFT/ACTIVE/INACTIVE/ENDED/ERROR while the code writes ten values including SUPPRESSED, REMOVED, FAILED, PENDING and LIVE. So the same pane can show a pill reading "Live" above a Status reading "SUPPRESSED", or a pill reading "Ready" above a Status reading "ACTIVE". Nothing in the studio maps these strings to English; they are uppercase database identifiers, against docs/CONTENT.md's sentence-case, English-console rule.

##### Proposed fix
Split the two questions the word "live" is currently answering and give each its own word, then forbid raw status. (a) Rename the risk vocabulary: listingRisk's 'live' becomes **"exists on the channel"** — it is a question about the identifier, and the confirmation should read "eBay · IT — ItemID 256789012345 exists on eBay and will be destroyed", never the adjective "live". (b) Keep "Live" reserved for the readiness pill's externalListingId && isPublished meaning. (c) Replace ListingsPane.tsx:103 with a labelled render from a new exported table beside readinessMeta — listingStatusMeta(raw) → {label, tone, hint}, with an explicit row for each of the ten values actually written and the readiness.ts:84-86 unknown-state behaviour (render the raw token neutrally with an 'Unrecognised status' hint) as the fallback, so a contract change is visible rather than mislabelled. Use the DS Pill for it, the same primitive the pill above already uses, so both facts read as one vocabulary. Add a vitest that derives the member list from a shared constant rather than hardcoding it, since a hardcoded status list is exactly the set claim that goes stale.

[high]verifiedAMAZONcorrectness risk

#### Three different off-switches are described with two words, and the one the studio cannot see makes it report "Offer — selling" for an offer that is closed

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator closes the jacket's Amazon IT offer for the season from the /fulfillment sync-control page (CLOSE_OFFER). Two weeks later a colleague opens the same jacket in the studio on the Amazon · IT scope to check why IT has no sales. The record drawer tells them the listing is Live, is being pushed to the channel, and its offer is selling.

##### What happens today
ChannelListing carries three independent off-switches — isPublished (schema.prisma:1629), offerActive (:1634), syncPaused (:1649) — plus the SCT.6 reversible pair offerClosedAt/offerCloseSnapshot (:1591-1594). The studio's wire contract carries only offerActive: /usr/bin/grep for offerClosedAt|syncPaused across studio-sheet.service.ts, sheet-rows.service.ts and the studio's channel and drawer types returns zero hits, against a positive control of 2 hits for offerActive in studio-sheet.service.ts. amazon-market-offer.service.ts writes offerClosedAt at :181 and clears it at :278 and touches nothing else — it never writes listingStatus, isPublished or offerActive (grep of that file lists only the offerClosedAt/offerCloseSnapshot/price selections). So after a close, ListingsPane renders Status "ACTIVE" (:103), "Pushed to channel — yes" (:109-113) and "Offer — selling" (:123-128), and the readiness pill reads "Live". Separately, the two words in play collide: sync-control calls its verb "close offer", the studio's channel verb calls the offerActive flip "Pause"/"Activate" (channelActions.ts:178-182), and the Shopify automation panel uses "Paused" for a third thing entirely (AutomationPanel.tsx:14). Two words for one concept, one word for three.

##### Proposed fix
Adopt one word per switch and put every switch on the wire. Vocabulary: **"Offer paused"** = offerActive false (Nexus-side, buy box suppressed); **"Offer closed"** = offerClosedAt set (SCT.6, the offer is withdrawn at Amazon and a verbatim snapshot is held); **"Sync paused"** = syncPaused (Nexus stops pushing, the channel keeps what it has); **"Not being pushed"** = isPublished false. Never reuse "pause" for two of them, and retire "close" as an operator-facing verb for anything else. Concretely: add offerClosedAt and syncPaused to the StudioRow listing projection in studio-sheet.service.ts, and give ListingsPane a fourth and fifth dt/dd pair using the same DS Pill/absent conventions it already uses; when offerClosedAt is set the Offer fact must read "closed — reopen restores the saved offer" and the readiness pill must not read "Live" (add a row state or, cheaper, suppress 'live' in sheet-rows.service.ts:269 when offerClosedAt is set). Rename the Shopify automation Pill's "Paused" to "Automation off" so the word is not spent three ways.

Confirmed from code on every load-bearing point. schema.prisma:1629/1634/1649 declare isPublished, offerActive and syncPaused as three independent flags, and the SCT.6 offerClosedAt/offerCloseSnapshot pair exists on the same model. `/usr/bin/grep -rn 'offerClosedAt|syncPaused'` over apps/api/src/services/pim/studio-sheet.service.ts, sheet-rows.service.ts and the whole `_studio` tree returns ZERO hits against a positive control of 2 hits for `offerActive` in studio-sheet.service.ts — so the studio wire genuinely cannot see a closed offer or a paused sync. amazon-market-offer.service.ts writes offerClosedAt/offerClosedBy/offerCloseReason/offerCloseSnapshot at the close (~:178-193) and clears them at the reopen (~:275-287, setting lastSyncStatus 'PENDING'); `/usr/bin/grep -n 'isPublished|offerActive|listingStatus'` on that file returns nothing, so a close leaves listingStatus, isPublished and offerActive untouched. ListingsPane.tsx:103/:109-118/:123-131 therefore renders Status = the unchanged token, 'Pushed to channel — yes' and 'Offer — selling' for an offer that is withdrawn at Amazon, and sheet-rows.service.ts:269 still returns state 'live'. The trigger is reachable in the product, not hypothetical: SyncControlClient.tsx:603 and SyncProductsGrid.tsx:69 expose 'Close offer' (CLOSE_OFFER) and ProductDetailClient.tsx:41 exposes both close and reopen. The vocabulary collision is also real: channelActions.ts:175-176 words the offerActive flip 'Activate'/'Pause', while AutomationPanel.tsx:14 renders a Pill reading 'Paused' for the Shopify automation mode. This is the one finding in the batch that makes the UI state a false fact about the marketplace; high severity stands.
The wire change (project offerClosedAt and syncPaused into StudioRow's listing) is the necessary half and is correctly identified as the root — the copy fix alone would leave the pill lying. One caution on the cheap variant: suppressing 'live' in sheet-rows.service.ts:269 when offerClosedAt is set changes the ROW STATE that readiness and the delete-risk path both read, so it must not be done without checking what else consumes state 'live' (the pill, the risk copy, any filter/count). #### The Delete-child refusal instructs the operator to "resolve" a listing — a verb no control in the product implements — and the sibling refusal claims demoting "removes" a parent, which it does not

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a discontinued jacket variant, XXS, that was listed on eBay IT. They open the studio on master, select the XXS row and choose Delete child…. The dialog refuses with "This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record." They look for something called Resolve. There is nothing. They then select the parent instead and read "NEXUS-JKT-01 is a parent — a parent is removed by demoting it", so they demote it — and the parent, its eBay listings and its ItemIDs are all still there.

##### What happens today
familyActions.ts:454 returns the unavailable string "This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record." whenever classifyListings finds any row with an externalListingId or isPublished. "Resolve" appears in no label anywhere in the studio: the channel sheet's entire verb set is open-record, offer-toggle and broadcast-to-other-markets (channelActions.ts), its overflow offers only Cell details, Check Information / Review synchronization and + Add listing alias (ChannelSheet.tsx:2002-2023), and the studio tree has no delist, end, remove-from-channel or relist control at all. So the refusal names a remediation that does not exist — the Owner's dead end, stated verbatim by the product. Separately at familyActions.ts:428 the refusal for a parent reads "a parent is removed by demoting it", but demote's own confirmation at :515-520 says the children are NOT deleted and the parent survives as a standalone product — "removed" there means "removed from being a parent", a fourth meaning of remove on the same screen.

##### Proposed fix
A refusal must name a control the operator can reach. Replace the string with the exact next step and, once the lifecycle verb exists, make it the action: "NEXUS-JKT-01-XXS is listed on eBay · IT (ItemID 256789012345). End that listing first — Listing lifecycle → End listing." The DS grid action registry already supports this: ActionImpact.unavailable is a string today, so either (a) extend it to carry an optional {label, actionId} the ActionConfirm footer renders as a secondary Button that runs the named GridAction, or (b) until that lands, name the surface in words that exist on screen. Fix familyActions.ts:428 to say what demote actually does — "NEXUS-JKT-01 is a parent. Demote it first; demoting does not delete it." And ban "resolve" and bare "remove" from the lifecycle vocabulary: the canonical verbs are Pause offer / End listing / Delete listing / Relist / Stop syncing / Delete from Nexus, each with exactly one meaning.

#### One verb carries four names inside the channel sheet, and which name you see depends on the channel and on whether the item is disabled

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator checks the jacket before listing it. On eBay · IT the sheet's ⋯ menu offers "Check Information ▪ (20)"; they click it and a modal opens titled "Information check · eBay · IT · ▪". They switch the scope bar to Shopify and the same menu entry now reads "Review synchronization ▪ (20)", opening "Review synchronization". On a Shopify alias with no applicable rows the same entry reads "Preflight ▪", greyed out. They open the Variants tab on the same channel and the ⋯ there says "Preflight".

##### What happens today
ChannelSheet.tsx:2006 builds the disabled label as `${channel === 'SHOPIFY' ? 'Preflight' : 'Check Information'} ${mark}` while :2011 builds the enabled label as 'Review synchronization' / 'Check Information' — so on Shopify the same menu item renames itself between its enabled and disabled states. The modal title at :2131 uses a third form, 'Information check', reversing the two words of the menu entry. ChannelProjection.tsx:403 labels the same class of action 'Preflight' on the Variants tab. "Check Information" and "Information check" are also Title Case on a capitalised common noun, against docs/CONTENT.md's sentence-case rule, and "Preflight" is aviation jargon that the same file's own description already explains in plain English ("What a send would carry, checked by the server. Nothing is sent.", ChannelProjection.tsx:404). Owner ruling D11 requires the same UI on all scopes and CH.1 requires one identical bar on every scope, so a channel-conditional verb name is a parity defect, not a nicety.

##### Proposed fix
One name on every scope and in every state: **"Check before sending"** for the menu item (with the count suffix unchanged) and the same phrase as the Modal title, subtitle "Nothing is sent from here." — which is what AliasPublishControl.tsx:14 already says. Shopify's genuinely different action (it does send, via /synchronize) must not share the name: call it **"Review and synchronize"** and keep it visibly distinct, because a verb that sends and a verb that does not must never look like the same control with different words. Drop 'Preflight' and 'Information check' entirely. Mechanically: derive both the menu label and the Modal title from one exported constant per channel-kind rather than two ternaries in two JSX expressions, so the disabled branch cannot drift from the enabled one.

'Preflight' : 'Check Information'} ${mark}`, while :2019 builds the ENABLED label as `Review synchronization ${mark} (${n})` / `Check Information ${mark} (${n})` — so on Shopify one menu entry renames itself between states, which no ruling could have intended. [critical]refutedEBAYdata integrity risk

#### The one per-market removal an operator can actually reach calls itself "Remove from eBay IT", reassures that everything stays in Nexus, and silently destroys the ItemID, the overrides and the snapshot with no relist path

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator wants the jacket off eBay IT for the season, keeping eBay DE. The studio offers nothing, so they use the eBay flat file page, select the row and choose the eBay-market removal. The confirmation reads: "Remove \"NEXUS-JKT-01\" and its 4 variants from eBay IT? The product and its stock stay in Nexus, and other channels are untouched." Both sentences are true and both are beside the point. Next season they look for a Relist and there is none — and the ItemID they would have needed is gone.

##### What happens today
handleRemoveChannelListing reads externalListingId into a local variable at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:636-639, ends the listing, then hard-deletes the row: tx.channelListing.deleteMany({ productId: { in: productIds }, channel: 'EBAY', marketplace }) at :645. The filter names only (productId, channel, marketplace) — no channelConnectionId, no aliasKey — so on a multi-account or multi-alias coordinate it removes every account's row, not the one displayed. The cascade takes ChannelListingSnapshot, ChannelListingOverride, Offer, ChannelListingImage and the queue rows with it (all onDelete: Cascade off ChannelListing in schema.prisma). None of that appears in the copy. The same dialog uses a fourth and fifth word for neighbouring intents — "Delete Family", "Delete Variant", "Remove from Listing" — and leaks implementation into the confirmation twice ("This is recoverable (soft-delete)." at :721, "Soft-delete — recoverable." at :738), while its own title alternates between "Remove from eBay IT" and "Confirm delete" for the same dialog (:746). So the operator's word map across the product is: studio = no word at all; eBay flat file = Remove; /products bulk bar = Unpublish / Delete on channel / Local-only; API = delist / DELETE_LISTING / UNPUBLISH_LISTING; schema = ENDED / REMOVED / SUPPRESSED.

##### Proposed fix
Publish ONE lifecycle glossary and make every surface read it — the studio's new verb, this eBay dialog, and the bulk bar. Canonical operator verbs and their native mappings, to live in one exported module (design-system/grid/renderers/lifecycle.ts, sitting beside readiness.ts so the two vocabularies are governed together): **Pause offer** — buyers stop seeing it, identifier kept, one click back (Amazon: close the purchasable offer, snapshot held; eBay: not built; Shopify: not built). **End listing** — the listing stops existing on the channel (Amazon: SKU offer deleted, ASIN survives; eBay: EndFixedPriceItem, the ItemID is retired; Shopify: status DRAFT). **Relist** — puts it back on the same coordinate as a NEW listing. **Stop syncing** — Nexus stops pushing; the channel keeps what it has. **Delete from Nexus** — the local record only. Banned as operator-facing words: delist, unpublish, unlist, withdraw, retire, deactivate, archive (for listings), soft-delete, preflight, resolve. For this dialog specifically: keep the reassuring sentences but add the two consequences the operator is actually agreeing to — "eBay ItemID 256789012345 is retired and is not stored anywhere afterwards" and "This market's saved overrides, images and offer history are deleted with the row" — and, if the row is to be relistable, capture a ChannelListingSnapshot before the deleteMany rather than writing copy that implies one exists. Render it with the DS grid action registry's ActionConfirm (consequences itemised, side effects separated, type-phrase the real SKU per ruling #133) instead of the hand-rolled Modal, and tighten the deleteMany to include channelConnectionId and aliasKey so the sentence "other channels are untouched" can be extended to "other accounts and aliases are untouched" truthfully.

##### Verifier
The cited code lines are accurate, but the three premises that make this finding "critical" are false, and each is refuted on the very page the finding audits.

(1) "The one per-market removal an operator can actually reach" is a set claim, and it is wrong. The same eBay flat-file grid ships an operator-facing per-row lifecycle enum column, Action, defined at apps/web/src/app/products/ebay-flat-file/ebay-columns.ts:154-163 (options '', 'deactivate', 'end', 'skip'), whose own help text reads: "deactivate = set the live offer to quantity 0 (keeps the ItemID — the safe hide) · end = end on this market (child row = that variation, parent row = the whole listing; the ItemID is lost, a later publish creates a new one) · skip = leave this row out of pushes. Deleting rows stays under the Delete toolbar action." That module is imported by the client at EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:61, typed at :115-116, and honoured client-side at :2178-2185. It is implemented server-side, per target market, at apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1841-1900 (deactivateRows → pushOffersOnly with qty 0, result message "deactivated — quantity 0 on the live offer (ItemID kept)") and guarded in feed mode at :1715-1720. So a reversible, ItemID-preserving per-market removal exists and is reachable one column away from the dialog the finding indicts.

(2) "No relist path" is wrong. Full Publish is a per-market panel on the same screen (EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:435-468, publishTargets/onPublish), the Action column's own text says an ended coordinate is re-created by a later publish, and the deleteMany's file-exclusion stamp is auto-cleared when the SKU is saved in the file again — the clear is real code at apps/api/src/routes/ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1437-1462, and the stamp is written at apps/api/src/services/ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:656-672. A separate, generic relist orchestrator also exists at apps/api/src/services/listings/recovery.service.ts:10-38 with a UI at apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/recover/RecoverClient.tsx:31 (DELETE_RELIST_SAME etc.), though its eBay arm is documented as stubbed.

(3) "Silently … with no warning" misquotes the dialog. The finding quotes only the headline sentence at EbayFlatFileClient.tsx:717-718 and omits the radio body in the SAME modal at :725: "Remove from this eBay file — ends its eBay {marketplace} listing if live; the product and other channels are untouched. The row stays gone until you save this SKU in the file again." That sentence states both the destructive consequence (the live listing is ended) and the return path, which is precisely what the finding says is absent.

(4) "The ItemID … is gone" is also wrong on the read I did: the ItemID is not only on ChannelListing. Product.ebayItemId (packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma:95) is selected at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:611-613 and still used after the deleteMany at :691, and the Product row is deliberately never modified by this handler (:601-603). It survives the removal. Separately, EndFixedPriceItem retires the ItemID on eBay's side regardless of what Nexus stores, so retaining it would not have given the relist the scenario asks for.

(5) The terminology charge is overstated. "Delete Family" (:721) and "Delete Variant" (:725 label at :724) are product-level soft-deletes, a genuinely different intent from a channel removal, so they are not "a fourth and fifth word for the neighbouring intent". And the title at :746 is `isAllScopedRemoval ? 'Remove from eBay {marketplace}' : 'Confirm delete'` — it varies with the selection's intent mix, not arbitrarily "for the same dialog".

What survives is real but is a different, narrower finding than the one under test: the deleteMany at ebay-flat-file-delete.service.ts:645 filters on (productId, channel, marketplace) only, while ChannelListing's identity includes channelConnectionId and aliasKey (schema.prisma:1770, 1784-1785), so on a multi-account or aliased coordinate it deletes rows the dialog did not name; and the cascade (208 `onDelete: Cascade` relations in the schema, including ChannelListingSnapshot at schema.prisma:2003 and ChannelListingOverride at :2001) discards this market's saved overrides and history without saying so. Those are scope/disclosure defects, not the "no verb, no relist, silent destruction" story this finding tells, and they do not support critical severity for a terminology finding whose central premises I could not confirm.
The proposed fix is mostly a re-write of copy that already partly exists, and one part of it is actively wrong for this codebase. Its own glossary lists "Pause offer … eBay: not built" — but eBay's pause IS built and shipped: Action=deactivate sets the live offer to quantity 0 and keeps the ItemID (ebay-columns.ts:154-163; ebay-flat-file.routes.ts:1873-1890). A glossary that declares a shipped capability missing would push an operator toward the destructive path the finding is complaining about. Likewise "capture a ChannelListingSnapshot before the deleteMany" cites a table whose own schema comment records that the prior art has never run (schema.prisma:1985-1988), so it is new work, not a copy tweak. The two pieces worth keeping are the two the finding buries: tighten the deleteMany to include channelConnectionId and aliasKey so "other channels are untouched" can honestly be extended to accounts and aliases, and name the cascade (this market's overrides, images and offer history go with the row) in the confirmation. Everything about a banned-word list and a DS ActionConfirm re-render is a separate, non-critical consistency task.

#### Four studio popup cell editors bypass the DS editorBox() sizing contract and hardcode widths up to 620px

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket on Amazon DE. On the master sheet they scroll right to the last visible column — a record-shaped attribute such as the GPSR responsible-person block — and double-click the cell to edit it. The cell sits ~200px from the right edge of the viewport.

##### What happens today
The editor is an AG popup (`cellEditor: StructuredAttributeEditor, cellEditorPopup: true`, sheet/master/columns.tsx:353) whose root is a hand-written `<div className="nds-list-editor" style={{ width: 'min(620px, 85vw)' … }}>` (sheet/StructuredAttributeEditor.tsx:24). The DS owns exactly this geometry: `editorBox()` is documented as 'THE ONE SIZING FUNCTION for every popup cell editor' and caps width at `min(cap, roomToRight)` precisely so AG's hardcoded `keepWithinBounds: true` never has anything to correct (design-system/grid/editors/editorBox.ts:1-35). Its caps top out at 560 (`EDITOR_CAPS`, editorBox.ts:53-66; `list` is 360, `select` 320). 620px exceeds every cap, and with ~200px of room AG slides the popup left off its own cell — the exact −202px/−79px displacement editorBox.ts:14-19 was written from. The same bypass is in sheet/AttributeShapeInput.tsx:49 (520px), sheet/ImpactProtectorsInput.tsx:32 (520px) and sheet/EbayPolicyInput.tsx:35 (480px, and with no maxHeight at all, so a long eBay business-policy list grows unbounded). `/usr/bin/grep -rn editorBox` over the whole `_studio/` tree returns rc=1 — zero hits — against a positive control of 5 `stopEditing` hits in EbayPolicyInput.tsx alone. The three copies also drop the `role="group"` + `aria-label` the DS shell carries (ListPanelEditor.tsx:71).

##### Proposed fix
Extract the DS shell from `ListPanelEditor` into an exported `EditorPanel` in design-system/grid/editors (props `{ kind: EditorKind; label?: string; eGridCell?: HTMLElement; column: { getActualWidth(): number }; contentWidth?: number; children }`), which internally calls `editorBox({ cellWidth, cellHeight, roomToRight, kind, contentWidth })` and renders `<div className="nds-list-editor" style={{ width: box.width, maxHeight: box.height }} role="group" aria-label={…}>`. Replace the four hand-written roots with it — `StructuredAttributeEditor` and `ImpactProtectorsInput` declaring `kind: 'list'`, `AttributeShapeInput` `kind: 'measure'`, `EbayPolicyInput` `kind: 'select'`. If 620px is genuinely needed for record-shaped attributes, mint a `record` entry in `EDITOR_CAPS` rather than an inline literal, so the cap is still bounded by `roomToRight`. Add an assertion to the existing editor gate that every `cellEditorPopup: true` component in the studio resolves its width through `editorBox`.

#### GridAction.danger is dropped by every menu surface — 'Delete child…' renders identically to 'Open record'

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is on the master sheet of GALE-JACKET (a parent with four size children, live on Amazon IT and eBay DE). They right-click the XS child row, or open its ⋯ row menu, intending to open it. The menu lists Open record, Attach existing product, Unlink, Reparent, Promote, Add child, Demote…, Delete child…

##### What happens today
'Delete child…' and 'Demote…' both declare `danger: true` (sheet/master/familyActions.ts:423, :498) and the registry's own contract promises 'Destructive verbs are grouped apart and rendered with danger tone by every adapter' (design-system/grid/actions/registry.ts:183). No menu surface honours it. `MenuItemDef` has no tone/danger field — `/usr/bin/grep -n 'danger\|tone' components/Menu.tsx` returns rc=1 against the full interface at Menu.tsx:8-50. `actionMenuItems` builds `{ id, label, title, disabled, onSelect }` and never reads `action.danger` — `/usr/bin/grep -n danger grid/actions/menuAdapters.tsx` returns rc=1, positive control `disabled` = 5 hits in the same file. There is no `.nds-menu` danger rule in the DS stylesheets. So all four menu-shaped surfaces render it neutral: the master row menu and AG context menu (MasterSheet.tsx:484, :494), the channel row menu (ChannelSheet.tsx:1011, :1058), the variants row menu (variants/useVariantRowMenu.tsx:18) and the family bar's own menu (FamilyBar.tsx:86-95, which hand-rolls the same mapping and also drops `danger`). Exactly one surface in the studio does honour it — the drawer, at drawer/RecordActions.tsx:65: `variant={action.danger ? 'danger-outline' : 'secondary'}`. The same verb is therefore red in the record panel and neutral in the row menu that is the primary way to reach it. This matters more than usual here because the DS deliberately specifies a single plain confirm for an unlisted child delete (design/grid-lab/GdsScenarios.tsx:464-473, 'it asks once and lets go'), so the menu's tone is the only pre-dialog signal that a permanent, cascading, undo-less delete (familyActions.ts:461-466) is one click away.

##### Proposed fix
Add `tone?: Tone` to `MenuItemDef` (design-system/components/Menu.tsx) using the existing `primitives/tone.ts` vocabulary, with a `.nds-menu button[data-tone='danger']` rule in styles/components.css that paints the label `--nds-danger-text` and the hover fill `--nds-danger-soft` (both already tokens, both AA). Then set `tone: action.danger ? 'danger' : undefined` in both DS adapters (menuAdapters.tsx:75-91 and :150-169) so the promise at registry.ts:183 becomes true by construction, and delete FamilyBar.tsx's hand-written mapping in favour of `actionMenuItems`. Pin it with a vitest that asserts every `danger: true` action reaching an adapter emits `tone: 'danger'` — the same shape as the existing recordActions.vitest.test.ts checks.

#### The DS menu adapter puts a disabled verb's reason in a hover-only tooltip, against the DS's own written rule — while the lane's hand-rolled adapter does it correctly

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has a jacket parent on Amazon DE and wants to remove one size child. They keyboard-navigate the master sheet's ⋯ row menu (or are on a touch device). 'Delete child…' is greyed out.

##### What happens today
`actionMenuItems` writes the availability reason into `title` only — `title: reason ?? undefined` (design-system/grid/actions/menuAdapters.tsx:79,86). `MenuItemDef.title` is documented at Menu.tsx:25 as 'Tooltip. #### Five ad-hoc confirmation dialogs in the studio, and the same 'discard unsaved edits' verb gets three different button treatments across the three channel media workspaces

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator edits the gallery for a jacket on Amazon DE, then on eBay DE, then its Shopify content — in one session — and in each workspace clicks Reload or navigates away with unsaved changes. They see the same question three times and must judge three different-looking buttons.

##### What happens today
Three per-file confirmation implementations, each a local `useState` plus a DS `Modal`, with divergent destructive affordance: Amazon renders 'Keep editing' / 'Discard changes' with `variant="danger"` (images/amazon/AmazonMediaWorkspace.tsx:377-378); eBay renders 'Keep editing' / 'Discard changes' with NO variant on either button — Button defaults to `secondary` (primitives/Button.tsx:111), so the destroy button is pixel-identical to the keep button (images/ebay/EbayMediaWorkspace.tsx:307-308); Shopify renders 'Keep editing' / 'Discard edits' with `variant="danger-outline"` (images/shopify/ShopifyContentWorkspace.tsx:240). A fourth, in shopify/ShopifyLinkedWorkspace.tsx:33,358, is a generic `{title, text, run}` modal whose confirm button is `variant="primary"` labelled 'Continue' — and it is the surface used for the genuinely destructive 'Unlink <member>' (:307) as well as for benign verbs like 'Keep shared with family' (:337), so the same button means both. The studio already has two governed confirmation surfaces that do this properly and are used elsewhere in the same tree: the DS `useActionConfirm` (ChannelSheet.tsx:608,629; MasterSheet.tsx:598), which itemises consequences, separates side effects and can require a typed phrase (ActionConfirm.tsx:1-31), and `drawer/DrawerConfirm.tsx`, whose header at :4-24 documents a real z-order reason for existing. The channel workspaces reproduce neither.

##### Proposed fix
Promote one promise-based confirm to the DS as `components/useConfirm()` returning `{ confirm(req): Promise<boolean>, element }`, with `req: { title; body: ReactNode; confirmLabel; cancelLabel?; tone: 'danger'|'warning'|'neutral'; acknowledge?; requireTyped? }` — i.e. the `DrawerConfirmRequest` shape (drawer/DrawerConfirm.tsx:34-53) rendered into a `Modal` instead of a Drawer overlay, with the confirm button's variant DERIVED from `tone` so no caller can pick `primary` for a destroy. Replace the four ad-hoc states with it. Where the verb is already a `GridAction` (Unlink a Shopify family member is one), route it through `useActionConfirm` + `runAction` instead, so the consequence list is itemised rather than a single sentence.

[medium]verifiedALLdesign inconsistency

#### window.confirm() is used as the discard guard inside a DS Modal and as the studio's leave guard

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens Manage shared axes on a jacket family, reorders the Colour and Size axes, then presses Esc or switches market from DE to IT without saving.

##### What happens today
`ManageAxesDialog` is otherwise fully DS — `Modal`, `Banner`, `OrderedList`, `Button`, `Select` (variants/family/ManageAxesDialog.tsx:25-26) — but its close guard is `window.confirm('Discard the unsaved axis changes?')` at :81, raised from inside a DS `Modal` that has already taken a focus trap and inerted the background. A native dialog cannot be themed, sized, tokenised, tested through the DS confirm harness, or localised with the rest of the console, and it blocks the main thread rather than resolving a promise like every other confirm in the tree. The studio's route-level leave guard does the same at contracts.tsx:607. These are the only two `window.confirm` calls in the studio (`/usr/bin/grep -rnE 'window\.(confirm|alert|prompt)'` over `_studio/`, other hits are comments in DrawerConfirm.tsx:21, HtmlField.tsx:180 and a vitest stub) — everything else already uses `Modal`, `useActionConfirm` or `DrawerConfirm`, which is what makes these two the outliers rather than a house style.

##### Proposed fix
Use the `useConfirm()` proposed in DSC-4 for ManageAxesDialog: make `canClose` async and await `confirm({ title: 'Discard the unsaved axis changes?', body: <>…names the axes that would revert…</>, confirmLabel: 'Discard changes', cancelLabel: 'Keep editing', tone: 'warning' })`, rendering its element as a second `Modal` above the axes modal (the DS already layers Modal-over-Modal correctly; only Modal-from-modal-Drawer inverts, per --nds-z-overlay 1400 vs --nds-z-drawer 1410). For contracts.tsx:607 the guard runs on a synchronous scope change, so the same async confirm works — `registerScopeChangeGuard` already accepts a promise-returning callback (ManageAxesDialog.tsx:83-87 proves the signature). Keep `beforeunload` native: that one genuinely cannot be replaced.

- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/variants/family/ManageAxesDialog.tsx:25-26

The set claim survives the real binary: `/usr/bin/grep -rnE 'window\.(confirm|alert|prompt)'` over _studio/ returns only these two plus a comment in HtmlField.tsx:180 and a vitest header in saveState.vitest.test.ts:6 — so they are outliers, not house style. The fix contains a false premise and must not be applied as written. It asserts `registerScopeChangeGuard` already accepts a promise-returning callback, 'ManageAxesDialog.tsx:83-87 proves the signature'. It does not: the interface is `registerScopeChangeGuard(guard: () => boolean)` (contracts.tsx:132) and the provider composes guards with `[...guards].every(guard => guard())` (contracts.tsx:634) — strictly synchronous, and `canClose` returns a boolean. Making the axes guard async means changing that contract and every consumer of `canChangeEditor()`. Worse for the second site: contracts.tsx:607 runs inside a capture-phase click listener whose whole job is `e.preventDefault()` (:608-610); you cannot await a promise and then prevent a navigation that has already proceeded, so replacing that one needs an intercept-then-replay design, not a swapped dialog. #### A grid-theme-private class (.nds-addvar-field) is used as a generic field wrapper in four studio files, beside 88 uses of the DS Field component in the same tree

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens Classification on a jacket master record and, separately, edits a measure-shaped attribute cell (weight + unit) on the same sheet. Both surfaces present label-plus-control fields; neither shows a required marker, and neither can attach a hint.

##### What happens today
`ClassificationDialog.tsx:62-84`, `AddVariationDialog.tsx:75-116`, `AttributeShapeInput.tsx:21-38` and `ImpactProtectorsInput.tsx:18-19` lay out fields with `className="nds-addvar-axes"` / `"nds-addvar-field"`. Those are two anonymous rules in the grid theme — `.nds-addvar-axes { display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px,1fr)); gap:10px; margin-top:6px }` and `.nds-addvar-field { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:4px }` (design-system/grid/theme/grid.css:1043-1044). They are exported by no barrel and wrapped by no component, and `/usr/bin/grep -rn nds-addvar` over apps/web/src returns only those four studio files plus grid.css (positive control: the same grep for `nds-list-editor` correctly returns its DS owner ListPanelEditor.tsx). Two of the four then override the grid template inline because the borrowed rule does not fit — `style={{ gridTemplateColumns: '1fr' }}` (ClassificationDialog.tsx:62) and `style={{ gridTemplateColumns: 'minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1.4fr) minmax(0, .7fr)' }}` (ImpactProtectorsInput.tsx:18). The DS ships `Field` for exactly this role — label + required marker + info slot + control + hint wired with `aria-describedby`, written expressly to replace 'SIX spellings of the same wrapper' and to fix two live AA failures in them (design-system/components/Field.tsx:5-41) — and the studio already uses it 88 times across 23 files, including the neighbouring `drawer/fields/RecordField.tsx`. So the sheet's own dialogs are the one place that does not get the required marker or the hint slot.

##### Proposed fix
Replace every `<label className="nds-addvar-field"><span>Label</span><Control/></label>` with `<Field label="Label" required={…} hint={…}><Control/></Field>` in the four files, and replace `nds-addvar-axes` with an explicit local `.fieldGrid` in the owning module.css (or the DS `SectionLayout` where the shape is a plain stack), so no surface overrides a shared grid template inline. Then delete `.nds-addvar-axes` / `.nds-addvar-field` from grid/theme/grid.css — a class in the grid theme with no component and no barrel export is an invitation for the next lane to borrow it too.

[critical]verifiedALLa11y defect

#### The DS primary Button has no visible keyboard focus — so the Confirm button on the permanent-delete dialog is the one control that never shows focus

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is cleaning up a jacket family: GALE-JACKET-BLK is a child that was never listed anywhere, and they want it gone. They right-click the row, choose "Delete child…", and the confirmation opens saying "GALE-JACKET-BLK is deleted permanently — there is no undo and no trash". They Tab from the phrase area to Cancel (which visibly rings), Tab once more expecting Confirm to ring the same way, see nothing change, assume focus is still on Cancel, and press Enter.

##### What happens today
`.nds-btn:focus-visible` (primitives.css:33-37) sets `outline: none; border-color: var(--nds-primary); box-shadow: var(--nds-focus-ring)`. For `variant="secondary"` (Cancel) the border really does change, from `--nds-border` #d8dde4 to `--nds-primary` #1f6fde — a 3.51:1 same-pixel change. For `variant="primary"` the border is ALREADY `--nds-primary` (primitives.css:59-63), so focus recolours it to the value it already has and the entire remaining indicator is `--nds-focus-ring` = `0 0 0 2px rgb(31 111 222 / 0.12)` (css-vars.ts:136,420 → tokens.css:210), which composites to #e4eefb on a white modal and #192f4f on the dark one — **1.17:1 light, 1.13:1 dark**, against a 3:1 floor. `ActionConfirm.tsx:94` renders Confirm as `variant={needsTyping ? 'danger' : 'primary'}`, and `familyActions.ts:445` returns `level: 'confirm'` (no `confirmPhrase`), so the delete-child dialog's Confirm is exactly the primary variant. `.nds-btn.on` (primitives.css:101-105) has the same defect. I checked for a global fallback: `apps/web/src/app/globals.css` contains **zero** `:focus-visible` rules (positive control: 13 matches for "button" in the same file), and `design-system/styles/a11y.css:19-26` only covers `.nds-navitem`, `.nds-tab`, `.nds-pgbtn`, `.nds-fpanel-toggle`, `.nds-builder-navitem` — none of which is a Button — and it applies the same 1.17:1 shadow anyway.

##### Proposed fix
Mint a real focus token and stop overloading the border. Add `--nds-focus-outline: 2px solid var(--nds-primary)` and `--nds-focus-outline-offset: 2px` in `tokens/css-vars.ts` beside `--nds-focus-ring`, then change `.nds-btn:focus-visible` to `outline: var(--nds-focus-outline); outline-offset: var(--nds-focus-outline-offset); box-shadow: var(--nds-focus-ring)` — keeping the glow as reinforcement, not as the indicator. An outline painted outside the control is independent of the variant's own border, so primary/danger/on all get the same 2px, ≥3:1 ring that `.nds-cell-expand:focus-visible` (grid.css:483) and `.nds-ag-floating-set:focus-visible` (grid.css:318) already use after ruling #296. Rename `--nds-focus-ring` to `--nds-focus-glow` in the same pass: grid.css:304-317 records that a name which does not say which CSS property it belongs to already produced one silently-dead focus rule. Then extend `scripts/ds-conformance-guard.mjs` with a check that every `:focus-visible` rule sets either an `outline` or a `box-shadow` whose colour clears 3:1 — the audit at grid.css:319-323 found 9 of 22 rules relying on the glow alone and only two were fixed.

Every cited line says what the finding claims, and I could not find any path that rescues the indicator.

CONFIRMED VERBATIM:

- primitives.css:59-63 — `.nds-btn.primary { background/border-color: var(--nds-primary) }`. Focus recolours the border to the value it already has. 1. Global fallback: `/usr/bin/grep -n focus apps/web/src/app/globals.css` → rc=1, zero matches; positive control `grep -c button` → 13. globals.css is only `@tailwind base/components/utilities` (lines 1-3); Tailwind preflight ships no `:focus-visible` outline, and a class-specificity rule would beat an element-level one anyway.
2. Any later override: `/usr/bin/grep -rn "nds-btn[a-z.-]*:focus" apps/web/src --include='*.css' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ts'` returns exactly three rules — primitives.css:33, primitives.css:951 (`.nds-btn.inline`), grid.css:1132 (`.nds-btn.xs.nds-grid-sheet-help`). Neither of the latter two matches a modal footer Confirm. Positive control on the same file: 56 `nds-btn` hits.
3. A different confirm surface: no studio-local confirm dialog supersedes ActionConfirm on this verb.
4. Focus never reaching the button: Modal.tsx:93,102-103 implements a real focus trap and Tab cycle, so Confirm is genuinely tabbable and genuinely unringed.

The DS already convicts this rule class: primitives.css:186-187, 528-529, 802-803, 1360 and 1482 all carry "DS1-18: was `box-shadow: var(--nds-focus-ring)` alone — that token is 12% alpha" and were switched to real outlines. `.nds-btn` was left behind.

Severity corrected critical → high: it is a genuine WCAG 2.4.7/2.4.11 failure on a no-undo destructive control with a plausible misfire path, but familyActions.ts:445's preflight already refuses the verb for anything with a live or published listing, so the blast radius is an unlisted local record, and the scenario needs a keyboard operator who does not look at the fill colour of the button they are on.
Direction is right; three corrections.

(a) The finding under-scopes the defect, and the fix should be sized to the real scope. Because `.nds-btn:focus-visible` (primitives.css:33) precedes every variant rule at equal specificity (0,2,0), its `border-color` is overridden by `.nds-btn.primary` (59), `.nds-btn.danger` (77), `.nds-btn.on` (102), `.nds-btn.ghost` (110), `.nds-btn.link` (123) and `.nds-btn.quiet` (904). So `danger` — the variant ActionConfirm.tsx:94 uses for the typed-phrase confirms, i.e. the MOST destructive dialogs — also shows no border change on focus, contrary to the finding's implication that only primary and `.on` are affected. An outline painted outside the box is the correct escape, but state that as the reason: a border-based fix cannot work without raising specificity on six rules.

(b) `outline-offset: 2px` as a blanket token is wrong for this codebase. grid.css:317 and :483 deliberately use NEGATIVE offsets because AG clips every cell with `overflow: hidden`, and grid.css:1132 uses +1px for the in-grid button. A `.nds-btn` inside an AG cell would have a +2px ring clipped away, reintroducing the same invisible-focus bug one layer down. Ship `outline-offset: 1px` as the default (matching `.nds-tbtn` at 856 and `.nds-expand` at 1482, both already 1px) and let grid contexts override to a negative offset.

(c) The `--nds-focus-ring` → `--nds-focus-glow` rename should not ride along. The token is defined in THREE places — css-vars.ts:420, tokens.css:210 and tokens-global.css:211 — plus the `--nds-grid-focus-ring` alias, and about a dozen consuming rules in primitives.css alone. Renaming in css-vars.ts without the two .css copies is a silent no-op on the shipped page. Land the outline first; rename separately with all three files verified.

On the proposed guard: a real 3:1 contrast computation over CSS custom properties composited against an unknown ground is not something a static script can do honestly, and a hardcoded exempt-selector list goes stale (the audit at grid.css:319-323 is already two fixes out of date). The defensible check is structural — every `:focus-visible` rule must declare an `outline` whose style is not `none` — with the number of conforming rules printed so a vacuous 0/0 pass cannot read as green.

[high]verifiedALLa11y defect

#### A refused verb's reason rides `title` on a disabled menu item that the Menu's own keyboard navigation skips — the Owner's dead end has no keyboard-reachable explanation

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has GALE-JACKET-RED live on Amazon IT and wants the local child record gone. They open the row's ⋯ menu on the master sheet. "Delete child…" is greyed out. They arrow down the menu looking for why; the arrow key jumps straight past it to the next item. They never learn that the block is "This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record." — and a screen-reader user is told only "Delete child, dimmed".

##### What happens today
`actionMenuItems` maps a disabled verb's reason into `MenuItemDef.title` (menuAdapters.tsx:88-92), and `actionContextMenu` into AG's `tooltip` (menuAdapters.tsx:169-173). `Menu.tsx:199` then renders that item as `<button disabled>`, and both of the Menu's keyboard paths query `'[role="menuitem"]:not([disabled])'` — the initial-focus effect at Menu.tsx:122 and the arrow/Home/End/typeahead handler at Menu.tsx:140 — so the item can never receive focus and its `title` can never surface by keyboard. Disabled form controls also suppress pointer events in Chromium, so the native tooltip does not fire on hover either. This directly contradicts the DS contract two files away: `MenuItemDef.title` is documented as "Tooltip. Supplementary only — never the sole home of a reason; see `description`" (Menu.tsx:24-26) and `MenuItemDef.description` is documented as existing precisely because "A tooltip is hover-only: invisible to touch, invisible to a keyboard user scanning the menu" (Menu.tsx:33-41), with `.nds-menu button:disabled .nds-menu-item-desc` deliberately kept at full `--nds-text-2` legibility (components.css:781-783). `SheetToolbar.tsx:247` already uses `description` correctly for its `absent` entries. The reasons lost this way include every permission refusal (`needs(PERM_DELETE)`, familyActions.ts:430) and every shape refusal (`"${row.sku} is a parent — a parent is removed by demoting it"`, familyActions.ts:427). Both studio sheets and the variants page mount these adapters: MasterSheet.tsx:484,494, ChannelSheet.tsx:1011,1058, FamilyVariants.tsx:329,333, useVariantRowMenu.tsx:18.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, both inside the DS. (1) In `actionMenuItems` (menuAdapters.tsx:81-95) put the refusal in `description: reason ?? undefined` rather than `title` — the slot the DS minted for it, already wrap-width-owned and already legible on disabled rows. Keep `title` as the duplicate for pointer users if wanted; the header's own width argument ("~900px wide") was about appending to `label`, not about `description`, which wraps at 34ch (components.css:770-779). (2) In `Menu.tsx`, render a disabled item as `<button aria-disabled="true">` with the click handler suppressed instead of the `disabled` attribute, and drop `:not([disabled])` from the two queries at :122 and :140 in favour of `:not([aria-disabled="true"])` for the *initial* focus only — so arrow keys still land on the item and a reader announces "Delete child, dimmed, This product still has a marketplace listing…". `.nds-btn` already ships this exact pattern: primitives.css:71 documents "A HELD button (aria-disabled): still focusable and clickable so it can say WHY". Apply the same to `ScopeBarItem.disabledReason`, whose doc at ScopeBar.tsx:46-50 promises an `aria-description` that the render at ScopeBar.tsx:213-219 never emits.

#### Every provenance mark in the sheet is `aria-hidden`, so "inherited / pinned / AI-drafted / formula refused" reaches assistive tech as nothing — while every neighbouring cell mark in the same file is exposed

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator with a screen reader is reviewing the master sheet for a jacket family before publishing to Amazon DE. Row GALE-JACKET-RED's Bullet 1 cell shows an AI-drafted value (purple tint, ✦ glyph, italic) that nobody has approved, and its Colour cell shows a value inherited from the parent. 'Read-only'}` (cells.tsx:117) — `role="img"` adds **no** tab stop. The same directory also documents the general rule: `CellSaveReason` exists as a `.nds-vh` clipped text node because "The tooltip is a HOVER overlay. role="img" + aria-label on the three branches is the right shape and matches four in-file precedents. Caveat the auditor half-names: a mark on every non-`own` cell of a 100-column sheet is announced on every arrow move, so the fallback (a `.nds-vh` node, or announcing only on non-default provenance) should be decided by listening, not by symmetry. The proposed test assertion ('no aria-hidden without a sibling accessible name') is a source-grep and cannot see the rendered tree — state it as a source guard, not an a11y proof.

#### `--nds-danger` and `--nds-warning` are fill tokens used as body text in all three surfaces that report a refusal — 3.76–4.05:1, under AA in both themes, while the text tiers minted for exactly this sit unused

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator tries to delete the child GALE-JACKET-RED from the family sheet because they think it was never listed. The preflight comes back with a per-listing verdict list naming "Amazon · IT — live, ASIN B0XXXXXX" in red, and when they cancel and retry the sheet's footstrip prints "Delete child… was refused: This product still has a marketplace listing. Resolve that listing before deleting its local record." Both of those lines — the only two places the studio ever names what is blocking them — are the least readable text on the page.

##### What happens today
Three rules bind a FILL token to text. (1) `.nds-grid-confirm-error { color: var(--nds-danger) }` and `.nds-grid-confirm-warn { color: var(--nds-warning) }` (grid.css:1038-1039) style the `findings` list in the destructive-action dialog (ActionConfirm.tsx:107-118), which is where `familyActions.ts:451,461` sends `impact.verdicts`. (2) `.nds-cell-stock-out { color: var(--nds-danger); font-weight: semibold }` (grid.css:506) styles the refusal strip at MasterSheet.tsx:1807 and FamilyVariants.tsx:608. (3) The same class styles "Views unavailable" in the sheet toolbar (SheetToolbar.tsx:178-182). Measured from the shipped values: `--nds-danger` = `--nds-red-500` #e5484d (css-vars.ts:100 → tokens.css:100) gives **3.91:1** on the light surface #ffffff and **3.89:1** on the dark surface #18263b; `--nds-warning` = `--nds-amber-600` #b87503 gives **3.76:1** light and **4.05:1** dark. All four are under AA's 4.5:1 for sub-18.66px text, and far under the 7:1 the Owner asked for. `.dark` does not override `--nds-danger` or `--nds-warning` at all (they are absent from `cssVarsDark`), which is why the dark numbers are no better. The correct tokens already exist and were minted with this exact reasoning recorded in css-vars.ts:203-218 ("anyone using the system as intended today ships inaccessible warning text"): `--nds-danger-text` #9c2f2a = **7.36:1** light (css-vars.ts:277) with a dark override #ef9c93 = 7.14 (css-vars.ts:581), and `--nds-warning-text` #6d3f10 = **8.87:1** light (css-vars.ts:249) aliasing to `--nds-warning-strong` #f0b46a = 8.30 in dark (css-vars.ts:598). Both clear AAA.

##### Proposed fix
Repoint the three rules: `.nds-grid-confirm-error` and `.nds-cell-stock-out` to `var(--nds-danger-text)`, `.nds-grid-confirm-warn` to `var(--nds-warning-text)`. Both tokens already carry dark overrides, so the fix lands in both themes with no new value. This only ever raises contrast (3.91→7.36 light, 3.89→7.14 dark; 3.76→8.87 light, 4.05→8.30 dark), which is the substitution rule this token file already states. Then close the class rather than the instance: add a token-guard check (`scripts/check-token-resolution.mjs` is the existing home) that rejects `color: var(--nds-danger)`, `var(--nds-warning)`, `var(--nds-success)` or `var(--nds-info)` in any DS or studio stylesheet — those four are documented as fills/lines, and the `-text` tier exists for the text role. The guard needs a positive control: seed it with the three rules above before the fix so a green run is not a vacuous one.
