[high]verifiedALLa11y defect

#### "Still waiting — this change is not confirmed" is drawn as an 8% amber wash at 1.10:1 with no ring and no glyph, in a grid whose adjacent rule declares "never colour alone"

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is retyping prices down the Amazon IT channel sheet for twenty variations of a jacket. Three of the writes stop answering; SheetWriter's patience timer flips those cells to `waiting`. The operator, who has a mild red-green deficiency and a bright office monitor, sees twenty cells that all look the same, closes the tab, and never learns which three prices were never confirmed against the live ASINs.

##### What happens today
The write-state vocabulary is five members (roundTrip.ts:32) and the studio reaches all of them — `saving` (MasterSheet.tsx:1275, sheetWriter.ts:249), `saved`/`refused` (MasterSheet.tsx:1282, ChannelSheet.tsx:748,777), `waiting` (sheetWriter.ts:335) and `unknown` (MasterSheet.tsx:1313, ChannelSheet.tsx:803, sheetWriter.ts:495). Three of them carry a non-colour cue: `saved` an inset success ring (grid.css:566), `refused` a danger ring (grid.css:567), `unknown` a warning ring (grid.css:573). Two do not: `saving` (grid.css:565) and `waiting` (grid.css:572) are `background` only. Computed from the shipped mixes — `--nds-grid-saving-bg` = info 10% and `--nds-grid-pending-bg` = warning 14% (tokens/grid.ts:171,174), `waiting` = warning 8% inline — against the light cell #ffffff: saving **1.14:1**, waiting **1.10:1**; against the dark cell #18263b: 1.10 and 1.08. Their mutual separation is ~1.04:1, i.e. hue only, against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for a state indicator and 1.4.1's prohibition on colour as the sole carrier. The file's own rule two lines below says so: grid.css:576 reads "sheet validation — a tint AND a corner triangle (never colour alone)", and `invalid`/`warned` do get a `::after` triangle (grid.css:585,587) — the *write* states were never held to it. `CellSaveReason` does clip the `waiting` sentence into the cell for a screen reader (cells.tsx:361-364 mounted at columns.tsx:206), so this is a sighted-perception defect, not a total one — but `saving` carries no reason at all (roundTrip.ts:169, sheetWriter.ts:249) and so has no second channel either.

##### Proposed fix
Give `waiting` and `saving` the same non-colour cue the other three already have, in the engine where the rest of the vocabulary lives. Cheapest conformant version: add `.nds-ag-wrap .ag-cell.nds-cell-is-waiting { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--nds-warning) }` so it matches `unknown`'s treatment, and give `saving` an inset `--nds-primary` hairline plus the existing spinner idiom. Better, and matching the project's own "a glyph, not a colour" rule: extend `ProvenanceMark`'s vocabulary pattern with a small write-state mark rendered by the cell renderer — `◷` waiting, `⟳` saving — as `role="img" aria-label` spans beside the value, the way `.nds-cell-required` and the long-text cap marks already sit there. Either way, add `nds-cell-is-waiting` and `nds-cell-is-saving` to whatever check enforces grid.css:576's "never colour alone" rule; today nothing does, which is why the two states that were added last are the two that skipped it.

[high]verifiedALLdesign inconsistency

#### `GridAction.danger` is discarded by both menu adapters, so "Delete child…" renders byte-identical to "Open record" in the row ⋯ and the right-click menu

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator right-clicks a variation row on the master sheet meaning to open its record drawer. The menu lists Open record, Attach existing, Unlink, Reparent, Promote, Add variation, Delete child…, Demote — eight verbs in one weight, one colour, one order, with no rule between the reversible ones and the one that hard-deletes a product with "no undo and no trash". They mis-click one row down.

##### What happens today
`GridAction` declares `danger?: boolean` with the comment "Destructive verbs are grouped apart and rendered with danger tone by every adapter" (registry.ts:183-184), and `familyActions.ts:421` sets `danger: true` on `delete-variant`. Neither adapter reads it: `actionMenuItems` returns `{ id, label, title, disabled, onSelect }` (menuAdapters.tsx:84-93) and `actionContextMenu` returns `{ name, tooltip, disabled, action }` (menuAdapters.tsx:165-174) — the flag is dropped in both, and neither groups danger verbs apart. It could not be honoured anyway on the DS side: `MenuItemDef` has ten fields — id, label, icon, disabled, onSelect, href, target, title, description, separator (Menu.tsx:8-50) — and no tone; and `/usr/bin/grep -n "nds-menu.*danger\|danger.*nds-menu" styles/components.css` returns rc=1 against a positive control of 18 "danger" matches in that same file, so there is no danger rule for a menu item to land on. The studio mounts these adapters on every grid surface it has: MasterSheet.tsx:484,494, ChannelSheet.tsx:1011,1058, FamilyVariants.tsx:329,333,336, useVariantRowMenu.tsx:18. This is not "status by colour alone" — it is status by nothing at all, which is worse, and it sits under the same registry that otherwise takes destructive safety seriously (the COLLECT→PREFLIGHT→CONFIRM→RUN order at registry.ts:215 and the type-to-confirm rules at ActionConfirm.tsx:12-31).

##### Proposed fix
Add `tone?: Tone` to `MenuItemDef` (Menu.tsx:8-50), reusing the DS's one tone vocabulary from `primitives/tone.ts`, and render it as `className={['nds-menu-item', it.tone && it.tone !== 'neutral' ? `tone-${it.tone}` : ''].join(' ')}`. Add the matching rule to components.css beside the existing `.nds-menu button:disabled` block: `.nds-menu button.tone-danger { color: var(--nds-danger-text) }` — 7.36:1 light, and `--nds-danger-text` already has a dark override at css-vars.ts:581, so it is AAA in both themes with no new value (note: NOT `--nds-danger`, for the reason in A11Y-4). Then make both adapters emit it: `tone: action.danger ? 'danger' : undefined` in `actionMenuItems`, and for `actionContextMenu` use AG's `cssClasses: ['nds-ag-menu-danger']`. Honour the second half of the registry's promise too — sort `offered()` (menuAdapters.tsx:58-61) so `danger` verbs come last, with a `separator` before them, which is what "grouped apart" means. Colour must not be the only signal: emit the existing `Trash2` lucide icon into `MenuItemDef.icon` for danger verbs at the same time, so shape carries it as well. Finally file the closure of DS-GAPS:330-344, which already named this gap.

[high]verifiedALLcorrectness risk

#### A failed connections/marketplaces read renders as "this product sells nowhere" — marketplacesFailed is computed, threaded through three files, then thrown away

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens the GALE-JACKET studio at 09:00 while the API is cold-starting. `/api/products/:id` answers, but `/api/connections?all=true` times out. The jacket is live on Amazon IT, Amazon DE and eBay DE. The studio renders: the scope bar shows one chip, "Shared product". The Amazon and eBay chips are gone. The nav drawer's channel groups are gone. Nothing on screen says a read failed. The operator's reasonable conclusion is that this jacket is not listed anywhere — and the reasonable next act is to open "Choose listing destinations" and list it again, creating a duplicate ASIN/ItemID beside the live ones.

##### What happens today
`loadStudioData` deliberately computes the failure: `marketplacesFailed` starts `true` (studio-data.ts:100), clears only on a successful marketplace read (:103), and is set back to `true` when the connections read fails (:115). The doc comment at studio-data.ts:26-32 promises "the bar says why it is empty instead of implying the catalogue sells nowhere". It does not. `StudioFrame` receives the prop and discards it with an underscore rename — `export function StudioFrame({ marketplacesFailed: _marketplacesFailed }: StudioFrameProps)` (StudioFrame.tsx:35) — under a comment claiming the scope bar states the case itself (StudioFrame.tsx:28-31). `/usr/bin/grep -rn "marketplacesFailed" apps/web/src` returns only the producer (studio-data.ts), the two callers that pass it (page.tsx:41, StudioLoader.tsx:89), the type declarations, and the discard at StudioFrame.tsx:35 — StudioBar.tsx references it zero times. Meanwhile the failure actively erases the channels: studio-data.ts:116 stamps `connected: connected.has(m.channel)` from an EMPTY set, and `deriveScopeOptions` drops every marketplace whose `connected === false` (`scopes.ts:115`), so `options.channels` is `[]` and `StudioBar.tsx:25` maps nothing. This is exactly "could not measure" rendered as "measured empty".

##### Proposed fix
Carry the flag into `StudioStateProvider` (contracts.tsx) beside `marketplaces`, and make `StudioBar` render it without adding a band above the grid (v2 §6.6). Two DS-native pieces, no new component: (1) append one `ScopeBarItem` `{ id: 'channels-unknown', label: 'Channels unavailable', disabled: true, disabledReason: 'The connected-account list could not be read, so no channel scopes are shown. This does not mean the product has no listings. Reload to try again.' }` — `ScopeBar` already renders `disabledReason` as both `title` and the chip's accessible description (ScopeBar.tsx:46-51, :221-223), and a disabled chip never takes the roving tabindex (:218). (2) Put a `Try again` control in the header's existing status slot rather than inventing a new row. Additionally fix the silent erasure: when the connections read failed, do NOT stamp `connected: false` (studio-data.ts:116) — leave `connected` undefined so `scopes.ts:115` keeps the channel and the chip renders with `readiness: undefined`, which already means "not scored" rather than "not there". No API change needed.

#### Needs attention prints "nothing recorded on this coordinate yet" about three data sources it never reads — on every coordinate, including when its own read failed

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator's GALE-JACKET has been suppressed on Amazon DE — Amazon's SP-API poll has written an open `AmazonSuppression` row against that listing. The operator opens the studio on Amazon · DE, clicks "Needs attention" (the tab whose entire stated purpose is that an empty panel must not read as reassurance), and reads, in the footer: "Not shown here: Channel rejections, Suppressions, Validation failures — nothing recorded on this coordinate yet." They close the tab satisfied. The suppression is real and unmentioned.

##### What happens today
`ErrorsSyncConsole` makes exactly two network reads — `/api/listings/publish-readiness` (ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:124) and `/api/products/:id/sync-queue` (:156). It never queries `ListingIssue`, `AmazonSuppression` or `ChannelListing.validationStatus`. Yet its footer renders, unconditionally and outside every `page`/`loading`/`error` guard: `Not shown here: {DORMANT_SOURCES.map(d => d.label).join(', ')} — nothing recorded on this coordinate yet.` (ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:373-376). `DORMANT_SOURCES` is a hardcoded three-entry literal naming those three tables (syncQueue.ts:296-300) with the comment "Sources this console would show if they ever held data". Both tables are written by live production code: `amazon-suppression-ingest.service.ts:197` creates `AmazonSuppression` rows keyed to a ChannelListing (reached from `amazon.routes.ts:1863`), and `listing-issues.service.ts:65` upserts `ListingIssue` (reached from `amazon-cockpit-publish.routes.ts:45` and `amazon/preflight-report.service.ts:30`). The sentence is a set claim about data never measured, phrased as a measurement, and it is the last line an operator reads on the surface designed to stop false reassurance. It also survives the error path: when the sync-queue read throws, `page` is null, the console shows "Could not read the sync queue" (:243-247) and then still asserts "nothing recorded on this coordinate yet".

##### Proposed fix
Two steps, and the wording is the cheap half. (1) Immediately: change the footer copy from a measurement to a scope statement — "Not shown here: Channel rejections, Suppressions, Validation failures. This console reads the outbound sync queue only; those sources are not checked." No claim about whether they hold rows. (2) Properly: have `GET /api/products/:id/sync-queue` return a `sources: { rejections: number|null, suppressions: number|null, validation: number|null }` block beside the existing `counts` (sync-queue.service.ts:318-328 already assembles `scope`/`counts`/`causes`), with `null` meaning "not counted". Render each as a DS `FilterChip` beside Dead/Retrying/Stuck using the contract the chips already honour — `count={n ?? undefined}`, which prints no number when unknown (ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:216, and the same `null != 0` rule the view chips state at viewChips.ts:61-70).

#### Export and Import blocked by permission report themselves as still loading — or say nothing at all

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A merchandiser with `products.edit` but not `products.export` opens the GALE-JACKET master sheet. The sheet loads, 120 rows render, the row count is live. Export is grey. They hover it and read "Nothing to export until the sheet has loaded" — so they wait, then press Reload, then wait again, then ask a colleague why the sheet never finishes loading. Import beside it is grey with no tooltip at all.

##### What happens today
`SheetToolbar` derives one `blocked` boolean from `loading || unavailable` (SheetToolbar.tsx:112) and writes Export's title as `blocked || p.exportDisabled ? 'Nothing to export until the sheet has loaded' : …` (SheetToolbar.tsx:228-234) — so every reason folded into `exportDisabled` is reported as a loading state. Both sheets fold permissions into that prop: master `exportDisabled={!sheet || loading || !has('products.export')}` and `importDisabled={!sheet || loading || !has('products.import')}` (MasterSheet.tsx:1767, :1772); channel `exportDisabled={!data || loading || destination.status !== 'ready' || !auth.has('products.export')}` and the import equivalent (ChannelSheet.tsx:2114, :2118) — so a not-ready destination is also reported as "still loading". The Import button carries no `title` prop whatsoever (SheetToolbar.tsx:241-243): a disabled control with zero explanation. The same pattern recurs in the channel overflow: `+ Add listing alias` is disabled on `!auth.has('products.edit')` while its `description` is populated only from `addError` (ChannelSheet.tsx:2016-2022), so a view-only operator gets a greyed item with no reason. The studio already owns the correct vocabulary one file away — `ChannelSheet.tsx:839-844` maps auth into a four-state `PermissionState` (`checking | no-session | granted | denied`) precisely so channel verbs can state which it is — and the DS states the rule outright: "a disabled control that cannot explain itself is a dead end" (ScopeBar.tsx:46-51).

##### Proposed fix
Replace the two booleans with a reason, exactly as `AbsentControl` already does for omitted controls (SheetToolbar.tsx:43-48): `exportDisabled?: true | { reason: string }` and the same for `importDisabled`, and render `title={reason}` on both DS `Button`s — Import gaining a title it currently lacks. The callers then pass the true sentence: "You do not have permission to export products (products.export)", "This destination has not loaded yet", "Nothing to export until the sheet has loaded", picking in that order. Same one-line change for the overflow item: give `+ Add listing alias` a `MenuItemDef.description` of "Changing products requires products.edit" when that is the blocker, rather than leaving `description` populated only on `addError`. No API change.

#### Family verbs run with no in-flight feedback on the grid surfaces — the same verbs show a busy state in the drawer

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator on the master sheet of the GALE-JACKET parent right-clicks the GALE-JACKET-XXS row and picks "Delete child". The confirmation dialog asks them to type the SKU; they type it and confirm. The dialog closes. Nothing else changes: the row is still there, the menu is re-openable, no spinner, no toast, no status line. Several seconds pass while the delete runs server-side. The operator, seeing nothing, re-opens the menu and presses Delete child again.

##### What happens today
All of the family verbs are pressed through `useActionPress`, which tracks the running verb in `busy` and returns it (useActionPress.tsx:44, :50, :72, :89-92). The drawer uses it: `RecordActions` disables every verb while `busy != null` and renders the running one as "Delete child…" (RecordActions.tsx:68, :74). The three GRID surfaces destructure only `problem` and never `busy` — `MasterSheet.tsx:470` + `:1807` (problem only, in the footstrip), `FamilyVariants.tsx:312` + `:608` (problem only), `useVariantRowMenu.tsx:16`, `:19` (problem only, and it is what `ChannelProjection.tsx:356` renders). `/usr/bin/grep -rn "\.busy" over those four files returns only `writer.busy` (the cell-autosave flag) at MasterSheet.tsx:1811 and FamilyVariants.tsx:612 — the action-press `busy` has zero consumers in the studio. `useActionPress.press` itself has no re-entrancy guard: it sets `setBusy(action.id)` and proceeds (useActionPress.tsx:47-55), so a second press while the first is out runs the verb a second time. For the parameterised verbs this matters — `add-variation` reads its draft from `pending?.newVariation` at preflight time (familyActions.ts:366) and that draft is still there until the surface clears it, so a second press re-submits the same child.

##### Proposed fix
Two changes, both inside code that already exists. (1) In `useActionPress.press`, return early when `busy != null` — one verb at a time per host, so a second press can never duplicate a write; this is a substrate rule, not a per-surface one, exactly like the nine rules `runAction` centralises (runAction.ts:1-16). (2) Surface the state where the verb was pressed: `GridSheetStatus` is already mounted on all three grids (MasterSheet.tsx:1811, FamilyVariants.tsx:612, and the channel sheet's equivalent) and already takes `saving` — pass `saving={writer.busy || rowPress.busy != null}` and add the verb's own label to the footstrip beside `problem` ("Deleting GALE-JACKET-XXS…"), using the existing `actionLabel(action, rows)` resolver rather than a second wording. That keeps the outcome line and the in-flight line in one slot, and makes the grid surfaces and the drawer report the same four outcomes the same way (ruling #110, one verb list / three surfaces).

The core defect is confirmed, one sub-claim is refuted, hence the severity correction. Confirmed: useActionPress sets `setBusy(action.id)` and proceeds with no re-entrancy guard, and returns `{ press, busy, problem, clearProblem, confirmElement }`; RecordActions destructures `busy` and uses it (`disabled={!isRunnable(availability) || busy != null}`, label `busy === action.id ? \`${actionLabel(...)}…\``). The three grid surfaces render only `rowPress.problem`: MasterSheet.tsx:1807 `{rowPress.problem && <div className="nds-grid-footstrip" …>}` with `saving={writer.busy}` on GridSheetStatus at :1811; FamilyVariants.tsx:608/612 identical; useVariantRowMenu.tsx:19 `{press.problem && <p role="alert">{press.problem}</p>}` only. menuAdapters.tsx:75-91 confirms `actionMenuItems` sets `disabled: !runnable` with no busy input, so a row-menu verb stays pressable while in flight. So the parameterised re-submit at familyActions.ts:366 is not reachable by the described double-press; what remains is a row verb (e.g. delete-child) re-runnable, and that one re-opens its type-the-SKU confirmation first. Real UX defect and a real substrate inconsistency, but not the silent duplicate write claimed.

[high]refutedALLdesign inconsistency

#### The studio sheet renders at the DS default `spacious` density — 60px rows, 46px header, 56px thumbnails — where the approved layout, the code's own comments and the layout-v2 gate all specify 36px rows and a 32px thumbnail

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
A merchandiser opens GALE-JACKET on master scope to fix the 42 attributes flagged 'Missing required' before the autumn drop. The family has 20 variations. On a 1080px-tall laptop she expects to see the whole family at once — the sheet is sold as 'the flat file', and layout-v2 §2.2 budgets 74.8% of the viewport to rows. She sees about 12 rows, scrolls, loses her place, and scrolls back. The same sheet on Amazon IT behaves identically.

##### What happens today
`MasterSheet.tsx:1853-1859` and `ChannelSheet.tsx:2266-2277` mount `<NexusGrid … rows="media-line">` with no `density` prop and no `rowHeight`/`headerHeight` override (verified: `/usr/bin/grep -n "density|rowHeight|headerHeight"` over both files returns only comments; positive control `rows=` matched 4 and 5 times in the same files). `NexusGrid.tsx:170-175` resolves `density = densityProp ?? contextDensity`, and `lib/density.tsx:34` sets `DEFAULT_GRID_DENSITY = 'spacious'`. A repo-wide `/usr/bin/grep -rn GridDensityProvider` finds nine mount sites — grid-lab, products/next, InventoryGrid, MappingClient, and the studio's own `images/amazon/AmazonMediaWorkspace.tsx:252` and `images/ebay/EbayMediaWorkspace.tsx:242` (both `value="compact"`) — and none of them wraps MasterSheet or ChannelSheet. So `tier = gridDensity.spacious` (`tokens/grid.ts:74`): `rowMediaLine: 60`, `header: 46`, `thumb: 56`. The code asserts the opposite in three places: `ChannelSheet.tsx:2272-2276` states '36px = a 32px thumbnail + 2 above + 2 below in compact'; `scripts/check-layout-v2.mjs:467` declares `row: 36, // rows="media-line" — 🔴 never 28`; and `check-layout-v2.mjs:442` budgets `agHeader: 28`. The gate's failure hints only anticipate 28 (`:545`, `:694-695`), so a 60px row is off its radar entirely, and per the shared brief the layout browser gates currently exit 2 (refused, unauthenticated) — the assertion has never actually run against the page. Net effect: every row is 24px (67%) taller than the approved geometry and the header 18px taller, so the sheet shows roughly 60% of the rows the layout budget was drawn for. This is also why the studio's own media grids look denser than its main sheet — they are the only two surfaces in the tree that set a density.

##### Proposed fix
Wrap the studio frame body in the DS `GridDensityProvider` (`@/design-system/lib/density`) at `StudioTabHost.tsx:78`, so every grid the studio mounts — sheet, variants, media, mapping dock — inherits one density and the two media workspaces can drop their local `value="compact"` wrappers: `<GridDensityProvider value={density}><section className={styles.tabPanel}>…</section></GridDensityProvider>`. Density then becomes an operator preference surfaced where the DS already puts it — the `PreferencesModal` pattern (the ONE Customize dialog), keyed on the existing `compact|cozy|spacious` vocabulary from `tokens/grid.ts:78` — with `compact` as the studio's default so `rowMediaLine` resolves to the 36px the layout-v2 gate asserts. No new DS API is needed. [high]verifiedALLux defect

#### Performance, Activity and Needs attention render inside an `overflow: hidden` panel with no scroll container of their own — content below the fold is clipped, with no scrollbar

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has GALE-JACKET live on eBay DE and Amazon DE. eBay DE has refused eleven pushes overnight. She opens the product, picks eBay · DE in the scope bar, and clicks 'Needs attention' to read the refusals before she edits anything. The console groups them by cause; the fourth cause and everything under it sit below the bottom of the frame. There is no scrollbar on the panel and the page itself cannot scroll, so the refusals she came for are simply not reachable.

##### What happens today
`StudioTabHost.tsx:78` renders every tab inside `<section className={styles.tabPanel}>`, and `studio.module.css:207-214` declares `.tabPanel { flex: 1; min-height: 0; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden; }`. Its ancestors are equally closed: `.tabBody` (`studio.module.css:46-53`) is `overflow: hidden` and `.shell` (`:22-30`) is `overflow: hidden` — deliberately, because `GridSheet` measures the viewport below its own top edge (`studio.module.css:9-17`). So a tab is only scrollable if the tab itself opens a scroll container. The images tab does, and documents why: `images.module.css:17-19` ('The tab scrolls INSIDE itself… the studio frame is a fixed flex column on purpose') and `.tab { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; … }` at `images.module.css:22-30`. Three tabs do not. `AnalyticsAdsTab.tsx:230` and `ActivityTab.tsx:43` both render `<div className={styles.page}>` from `analytics.module.css:9-16`, which declares `min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 16px 24px 24px` — no `flex`, no `overflow-y`. `ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:195` renders `<div className={styles.console}>` from `errors-sync.module.css:4`, which is `display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 16px 24px 24px; min-width: 0` — same omission. A column flex item resolves `min-height: auto` to its content height, so none of the three can shrink; it overflows `.tabPanel`, which clips it. `/usr/bin/grep -n overflow` over `analytics.module.css` returns only `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (:11), a decorative `overflow: visible` on the sparkline (:84) and one `overflow-x: auto` on a table wrap (:105); over `errors-sync.module.css` only four `overflow: hidden` ellipsis rules (:21,:39,:63,:78). Neither file opens a vertical scroll container anywhere.

##### Proposed fix
Stop making every tab re-derive the frame's contract. Give `.tabPanel` the scroll role once — `studio.module.css:207-214` becomes `overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain` — and give the sheet tab (the only one that must NOT scroll, because `GridSheet` measures its own top) an opt-out class `.tabPanelFixed { overflow: hidden }` applied from `StudioTabHost.tsx:78` when `tab === 'sheet'`. That inverts the default so the failure mode is a redundant scrollbar rather than unreachable content. If the frame must stay closed, then the DS `SectionLayout` pattern (`@/design-system/patterns`) is the right wrapper for a scrolling tab body and all three files should mount it instead of hand-rolling `.page`/`.console`. Either way add an assertion to `scripts/check-layout-v2.mjs` that every registered tab surface's root is either `overflow-y: auto` or explicitly opted out — this class of defect is invisible on short fixture data and only appears on a real product with a long event log.

Confirmed from the files. StudioTabHost.tsx:78 renders `<section className={styles.tabPanel}>` around whichever tab component is selected, with no per-tab wrapper. studio.module.css:207-214 gives `.tabPanel` `flex:1; min-height:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; overflow:hidden`, and its ancestors are equally closed — `.tabBody` (studio.module.css:46-53) and `.shell` (:22-30) are both `overflow:hidden`, deliberately, per the file header at :9-16 (GridSheet measures the document, so nothing above the tab may scroll) and StudioFrame.tsx:43-52's 'Nothing here scrolls'. So each tab must open its own scroll container. The images tab does (images.module.css:22-30, `.tab { flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto }`, documented at :17-19). The three cited tabs do not: AnalyticsAdsTab.tsx:230 and ActivityTab.tsx:43 both render `.page` from analytics.module.css:9-16 (`min-width:0; overflow-wrap:anywhere; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px; padding:16px 24px 24px` — no `flex`, no `overflow-y`), and ErrorsSyncConsole.tsx:195 renders `.console` from errors-sync.module.css:4 with the same omission. My own `/usr/bin/grep -n 'overflow|flex:'` over analytics.module.css returns only `overflow-wrap` (:11), `.spacer{flex:1}` (:30), a decorative `overflow:visible` on the sparkline (:84) and one `overflow-x:auto` (:105); over errors-sync.module.css only ellipsis-scoped `overflow:hidden` (:21,:39,:63,:78). A non-shrinking column child inside an `overflow:hidden` parent is clipped with no scrollbar — long event logs and multi-cause refusal lists are unreachable.

The gate assertion suggestion is sound but should key on 'this tab's root scrolls OR hosts a GridSheet'.

#### Four content-left edges across one product — frame bands 16px, tab panels 24px, Shopify workspaces 16px via a different mechanism, sheet toolbar 6px — and `--nds-gutter-content`, the token minted to prevent exactly this, has zero consumers

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator works GALE-JACKET across a single session: master sheet → Media → Performance → eBay DE Needs attention → Shopify Product family. The product name in the header, the scope chips and the nav toggle all start at the same x. The body content underneath jumps left-right on every tab change — 24px on Performance and Needs attention, 16px on the Shopify workspace, and flush against the card border on the sheet — so the page reads as four pages stapled together rather than one workspace.

##### What happens today
The frame's bands hardcode `padding: 0 16px` three times (`studio.module.css:73`, `:189`, `:268`) and the DS bands do the same (`patterns.css:1228` for `.nds-detailhdr.dense`, `:1278` for `.nds-scopebar`, `:1299` for `.nds-pageband`). The tab panels then pick a different number: `analytics.module.css:15` is `padding: 16px 24px 24px` (used by both Performance and Activity — `ActivityTab.tsx:14` imports the same stylesheet), `errors-sync.module.css:4` is `padding: 16px 24px 24px`, `images.module.css:29` is `padding: 16px 24px 40px`, while `shopify/linked.module.css:1` is `padding: var(--nds-space-16)` and `ErrorsSyncTab.tsx:51` uses a raw inline `style={{ padding: '24px' }}`. The bottom padding disagrees too: 24 / 24 / 40. Both panel stylesheets assert in their own headers that they follow 'the studio's rhythm (16/24 page padding)' (`analytics.module.css:4`, `images.module.css:14` — the latter claiming that is 'what `studio.module.css` … use[s]') — but `studio.module.css` contains no 24px gutter at all; `/usr/bin/grep` for `24px` in it finds only `padding: 40px 24px` on the centred/placeholder states (:143, :175). The root cause is that `--nds-gutter-content: 16px`, minted at `css-vars.ts:447` with a comment saying it exists so 'the next band does not pick 14 the way `.nds-grid-footstrip` did', is never read: `/usr/bin/grep -rn nds-gutter-content` over `apps/web/src` and `scripts` returns exactly three hits, all three of them the declaration itself (`css-vars.ts:447`, `styles/tokens.css:226`, `styles/tokens-global.css:227`) and zero `var(--nds-gutter-content)` consumers. The studio is also split on spacing dialect: `/usr/bin/grep -rc nds-space-` across the 22 studio stylesheets shows 0 uses in `studio.module.css` and 0 real uses in `drawer.module.css` (its single hit is a comment at :861 saying so), against 31 in `images/amazon/media.module.css`, 31 in `images/ebay/media.module.css` and 23 in `shopify/linked.module.css`.

##### Proposed fix
Make the token load-bearing instead of decorative. (1) Replace every literal band gutter with `padding-inline: var(--nds-gutter-content)` in `patterns.css:1228,1278,1299`, `grid/theme/grid.css:983` and `studio.module.css:73,189,268`. (2) Give the tab panels one shared inset by having them mount the DS `SectionLayout` pattern rather than each declaring its own `.page`/`.console`/`.tab`/`.workspace` root; `SectionLayout` takes the gutter from the token and the vertical rhythm from one place, so the 24/24/40 bottom-padding spread collapses. (3) Add `--nds-gutter-content` to `scripts/check-token-resolution.mjs`'s consumed-token set so a token with zero `var()` readers fails the push — a declared-but-unread token is the exact failure mode GOVERNANCE.md:23-47 records as having left 285 declarations silently dead. (4) Delete the inline `style={{ padding: '24px' }}` at `ErrorsSyncTab.tsx:51` in favour of the shared empty-state — the DS `EmptyState` component already renders that message shape.

The factual core checks out, though it is a documented-open DS gap rather than a new discovery. Verified myself: `/usr/bin/grep -rn nds-gutter-content apps/web/src scripts packages` returns exactly three hits, all declarations — tokens/css-vars.ts:447, styles/tokens.css:226, styles/tokens-global.css:227 — and zero `var(--nds-gutter-content)` readers; the comment at css-vars.ts:441-446 states the token exists to stop the next band picking its own number. The bands do hardcode the literal: patterns.css:1228 (`.nds-detailhdr.dense { padding: 0 16px }`), :1278 (`.nds-scopebar { padding: 0 16px }`), :1299 (`.nds-pageband { padding: 0 16px }`), and studio.module.css:189 (`.skelHeader/.skelScope/.skelTabs { padding: 0 16px }`), :73 (`.tabStrip`), :268 (`.tabRow`). Tab bodies pick 24: analytics.module.css:15 and errors-sync.module.css:4 are `padding: 16px 24px 24px`, images.module.css:29 is `16px 24px 40px`, while shopify/linked.module.css:1 is `padding: var(--nds-space-16)` (= 16px, tokens.css:415) and ErrorsSyncTab.tsx:51 is a raw inline `style={{ padding: '24px' }}`. `/usr/bin/grep -n 24px studio.module.css` returns only :143 and :175 (`padding: 40px 24px` on the placeholder/centred states), so the analytics header's claim at :4-6 that 24px is what studio.module.css uses is indeed false. .claude/DS-GAPS.md:983-1000 records this class as '🔴 OPEN — four different content-left edges'. Not settled by any ruling I found. Two softening facts: three of the four tab surfaces agree on 24px inline, and their own headers state 16/24 as an intended rhythm — so the live inconsistency is narrower than 'four edges' (band 16 vs body 24 as a possibly deliberate two-tier rhythm, plus the shopify 16 outlier and the inline literal), and the DS-GAPS table it leans on is stale (it lists `.tabStrip`, a class with zero consumers today, and a 14px footstrip that grid.css:983 has since moved to 16).

Step (2) (route every tab body through `SectionLayout`) is a large rewrite of five surfaces to settle a 16-vs-24 question that no ruling has answered; propose the gutter decision to the Owner first, since band-16/body-24 may be intentional.

#### The route skeleton draws 129px of chrome where the live frame draws 90px — the page jumps 39px the moment data lands, which is precisely what the skeleton's own comment says it exists to prevent

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator clicks GALE-JACKET from the Products list. The studio's skeleton paints three grey bands — a title line, a row of chips, a row of tab labels. Data arrives; the third band vanishes, the second shrinks, and the whole sheet snaps 39px upward under the cursor. On a slow channel-destination resolve this is the first thing the operator sees on every product they open.

##### What happens today
`studio/loading.tsx:17-36` renders `.skelHeader` + `.skelScope` + `.skelTabs`. `studio.module.css:193-203` sizes them 48px, 44px and 34px, each with a 1px `border-bottom` from the shared rule at `:183-192`, so the skeleton's band stack is 49 + 45 + 35 = 129px. The live frame renders a different shape: `StudioFrame.tsx:43-45` puts only `<StudioSubheader/>` in `.bands`, and `StudioSubheader.tsx:62-77` renders `WorkspaceSubheader` (no `tabs` prop is passed, so `WorkspaceSubheader.tsx:119`'s tabs row never mounts) wrapping `StudioHeader` — a `.nds-detailhdr.dense` at `height: 48px` (`patterns.css:1226-1233`) whose own border is cancelled at `patterns.css:1556`, plus the subheader's own 1px border (`patterns.css:1553`) = 49px — followed by `StudioBar`, a `ScopeBar className="nds-workspace-scope"` (`StudioBar.tsx:28`) which `patterns.css:1595` re-sizes to `height: auto; min-height: var(--nds-toolbar-h)` = 40px + its 1px border = 41px. Live total 90px. The skeleton's `.skelScope` at 44px is the DS `.nds-scopebar` default (`patterns.css:1277`), a value the studio overrides to 40 and the skeleton restates rather than reads; and `.skelTabs` draws a standalone tab strip that no longer exists, the tabs having moved into the `WorkspaceSubheader` navigation drawer. The comment at `studio.module.css:181-182` claims 'three bands at the exact heights the real ones use, so the first paint does not move when the data lands.' The same drift left a large block of orphaned CSS: a per-class census (`/usr/bin/grep -rho "styles.<name>\b"` over `_studio` and `studio`) returns **0** consumers for `.tabStrip` (:69-86), `.mergedRow` (:235-252), `.tabsCompact` (:256-258), `.tierC` (:261-263), `.tabRow` (:264-275) and all four `.placeholder*` rules (:135-166) — about 90 of the file's 309 lines, including the entire 'v2: the merged chips + tabs row (spec §3)' block whose comment asserts it is where '#182's mint' is applied. Controls in the same census returned non-zero (`shell` 4, `saveState` 7, `error` 10).

##### Proposed fix
Derive the skeleton from the same numbers the live frame uses instead of restating them. Mint `--nds-studio-band-header: 48px` and reuse the existing `--nds-toolbar-h` for the scope band; have `.skelHeader` read the first and `.skelScope` read `var(--nds-toolbar-h)`, and delete `.skelTabs` together with its `<div>` at `loading.tsx:30-35` — the live frame has no third band. Better still, build `loading.tsx` from the DS `Skeleton` primitive inside the real `WorkspaceSubheader` + `ScopeBar` shells with `Skeleton` children, so the skeleton cannot diverge from the chrome by construction. Separately, delete the eight orphaned rule blocks (`.tabStrip`, `.mergedRow`, `.tabsCompact`, `.tierC`, `.tabRow`, `.placeholder*`) — they are not merely dead, they document a band layout that is no longer what the page renders, and a future reader will trust the comment at `studio.module.css:231-233` over the DOM.

#### The sheet toolbar band has two competing padding rules at identical specificity — `0 6px` and `14px 16px` — and which one applies is decided by stylesheet import order, not by a decision

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator on Amazon IT scans down the left edge of the studio: the product name, the 'Editing' scope label, then the sheet's row count, then the family status strip at the bottom of the card. Three of those four align; the row count does not. Whether it sits 10px inboard or 10px outboard of the rest depends on which stylesheet the bundler emitted last.

##### What happens today
`GridSheet.tsx:69` renders the sheet host as `className=['nds-gridcard','nds-grid-sheet', …]`, so the toolbar inside it matches BOTH `.nds-gridcard .nds-toolbar { padding: 14px 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid … }` (`patterns.css:497-500`) and `.nds-grid-sheet .nds-toolbar { padding: 0 6px; height: var(--nds-toolbar-h, 40px); flex: 0 0 var(--nds-toolbar-h, 40px); box-sizing: border-box; overflow-x: auto; }` (`grid/theme/grid.css:1179-1189`). Both selectors are (0,2,0) — identical specificity — so the winner is source order, and the two stylesheets arrive by different routes: `patterns.css` is imported by `app/layout.tsx:28` (whose own comment at `:15-16` states 'ORDER IS THE CASCADE… resolves conflicts by source order, not specificity'), while `grid/theme/grid.css` arrives via a component import at `grid/NexusGrid.tsx:39`. The last recorded measurement of this band reports the gridcard rule winning: `.claude/DS-GAPS.md:993` tabulates 'sheet toolbar (`.nds-gridcard .nds-toolbar`) | box left 67 | padding-left 16px | content starts at 83'. Either outcome is a defect. If `grid.css` wins, the toolbar's content starts at 6 + 1 (card border) = 7px while every band above it starts at 16px and the footstrip directly below it starts at 16 + 1 = 17px (`grid/theme/grid.css:983`, `padding: 10px 16px`, changed from 14 specifically so it would stop being 'the lone outlier' — see the rule's own comment at `:975-982`, which asserts that '`.nds-gridcard .nds-toolbar` … compute[s] `0 16px`' and is contradicted by `:1180` in the same file). If `patterns.css` wins, the author of `:1179` is looking at a rule that has never applied, and the band also carries 14px of vertical padding inside a `box-sizing: border-box` 40px height, leaving a 12px content box for the 28px controls the toolbar mounts.

##### Proposed fix
One band, one rule. Fold the sheet's toolbar geometry into the existing `.nds-gridcard .nds-toolbar` declaration as a modifier the host opts into — `.nds-gridcard.nds-grid-sheet .nds-toolbar` (specificity (0,3,0), so it wins by rule rather than by bundler order) — and give it `padding: 0 var(--nds-gutter-content)` so it lands on the same 16px edge as the header, scope bar and footstrip. The 40px band height is preserved by `height: var(--nds-toolbar-h)` with zero block padding, which is what `grid.css:1181-1183` already intends. Then add a check to `scripts/check-layout-v2.mjs` asserting that the four studio bands report the same `getBoundingClientRect().left + paddingLeft` — the DS-GAPS table at `:983-1000` is that measurement written by hand once; it should be a gate, because the failure is invisible in any single file's diff.

##### Verifier
The cascade tie is real and I reproduced both halves. GridSheet.tsx:69 renders the host div as `['nds-gridcard','nds-grid-sheet', className]`, and the sheet's toolbar is the DS `GridToolbar`, which emits `<div className="nds-toolbar">` (patterns/GridToolbar.tsx:30) — SheetToolbar.tsx:37/116/293 mounts exactly that component, and MasterSheet.tsx:1725-1740 passes it as GridSheet's `toolbar`. One of the two declarations is therefore dead, and which one is a bundler-ordering accident rather than a decision — and grid.css:975-982's own comment asserts `.nds-gridcard .nds-toolbar` computes `0 16px`, which contradicts patterns.css:497 in the same breath. Two caveats that lower, not kill, the finding: the DS-GAPS:993 row cited as the 'last measurement' is a stale table (it lists `.tabStrip`, a class with zero consumers, and a 14px footstrip that grid.css:983 has since moved to 16), so which rule currently wins is NOT established by the evidence offered — the finding survives only because both outcomes are wrong, which is argued from the code and holds.
Raising the sheet rule to `.nds-gridcard.nds-grid-sheet .nds-toolbar` (0,3,0) is the right move — it settles the winner by rule instead of by bundle order. But do not fold in `padding: 0 var(--nds-gutter-content)` as part of the same change: 16px inline is a design decision that has not been ruled (UXLD-3 shows the gutter question is open), and grid.css:1179 was written to 6 deliberately so the search field and views cluster fit the 40px band without wrapping. #### The record drawer cancels the DS drawer's padding with a hardcoded negative margin, then re-insets its own content at 14px — so inside one 520px panel the title sits at 18px and everything beneath it at 14px, and a DS change to `.nds-drawer-b` silently breaks the panel

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator on eBay DE double-clicks the 'Item specifics · Colour' cell for GALE-JACKET-XXS to see why it is inheriting from master. The record panel opens at the right. The SKU line at the top of the panel starts 18px from the panel's left edge; the pane tabs beneath it start at 14px; the field rows start at 14px. A 4px stagger runs down the panel's left edge, in the surface the operator reads most closely.

##### What happens today
`RecordDrawer.tsx:497-536` mounts the DS `Drawer`, which renders `.nds-drawer-h { padding: 16px 18px }` (`components.css:541-548`) around the title/subtitle at `RecordDrawer.tsx:508-535`, and `.nds-drawer-b { padding: 16px 18px }` (`components.css:565-576`) around the body at `:536`. The studio then cancels the body padding by restating it as a literal negative: `drawer.module.css:22-28` declares `.body { margin: -16px -18px; height: calc(100% + 32px); }`. Below it, the panel re-insets everything at a different number — `.tabsRow { height: var(--nds-toolbar-h); padding: 0 14px }` (`drawer.module.css:33-41`) and `.pane { padding: 14px }` (`:45-51`). Two consequences. First, the visible 18px-vs-14px step between the drawer header and everything under it. Second, `margin: -16px -18px` is a hand-synced copy of a DS value with nothing binding them: changing `.nds-drawer-b`'s padding in `components.css:573` is a legal DS change that leaves this file compiling, resolving and wrong — either a residual gutter the panes did not ask for, or content pulled outside the panel and clipped. The height compensation makes the coupling worse: `calc(100% + 32px)` hardcodes 2 × 16px, so a vertical-padding change breaks the pane's scroll height as well. The file knows it is off-scale — `drawer.module.css:861` records 'px, not `--nds-space-*`: this stylesheet uses literal px throughout (0 space tokens today)' — and 18px is not a step the studio uses anywhere else (a spacing census over the 22 studio stylesheets returns 18px only 6 times against 71 × 8px, 65 × 10px, 63 × 12px, 16 × 16px, 15 × 14px).

##### Proposed fix
Give the DS `Drawer` an explicit `bodyPadding?: 'default' | 'none'` prop (default `'default'`, preserving all 22 existing consumers) that emits `.nds-drawer-b.flush { padding: 0 }`. `RecordDrawer.tsx:497` then passes `bodyPadding="none"` and `drawer.module.css:22-28` loses both the `margin: -16px -18px` and the `height: calc(100% + 32px)` — a hosted full-bleed pane stops depending on a number it does not own. Separately, publish the drawer's gutter as a token (`--nds-drawer-gutter`, seeded at the DS's existing 18px) consumed by `.nds-drawer-h`, `.nds-drawer-f`, `.tabsRow` and `.pane`, so the panel's header, tab strip and field rows land on one left edge instead of three files each picking a literal. That also removes 18px as an un-scaled orphan value in the studio census.

- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/drawer/drawer.module.css:23

- apps/web/src/design-system/styles/components.css:541
- apps/web/src/design-system/styles/components.css:565

##### Verifier
Every cited line says what the finding claims. RecordDrawer.tsx:497-536 mounts the DS `Drawer` with `title` (:508) and `subtitle`, and the panel body is `<div className={styles.body}>` at :536, containing `.tabsRow` (:537) and `.pane` (:542). The DS pads both chrome slots at 18px inline: components.css:541-548 `.nds-drawer-h { padding: 16px 18px }` and :565-576 `.nds-drawer-b { padding: 16px 18px }`. drawer.module.css:20-28 then cancels the body padding with the literal `margin: -16px -18px` and compensates the height with `height: calc(100% + 32px)` — a hand-synced mirror of a DS value with nothing binding the two, so a legal change to components.css:573 leaves this file compiling and wrong in both axes. Below it the panel re-insets at a different number: `.tabsRow { height: var(--nds-toolbar-h); padding: 0 14px }` (:33-41) and `.pane { padding: 14px }` (:45-51), against the header's 18px — a visible 4px step down the panel's left edge in the surface an operator reads most closely. The file's own note at :861 confirms it is off the space scale ('px, not `--nds-space-*` … 0 space tokens today'). I found no ruling in docs/pes-claims.md's rulings block or the layout docs sanctioning the negative-margin escape.
The `bodyPadding?: 'default' | 'none'` prop is the correct shape and genuinely additive (components.css:565 says 22 files render this component, so the default must stay). Note the fix must also remove `height: calc(100% + 32px)` — the finding says so, but a partial application that drops only the margin would leave the pane 32px too tall. The second half (mint `--nds-drawer-gutter` at 18 and consume it in `.nds-drawer-h`, `.nds-drawer-f`, `.tabsRow`, `.pane`) changes the visible inset of the tab strip and every field row from 14 to 18 in a panel whose 14px was measured by CT.1 — that is a design change, not a cleanup; it needs the Owner, and it should not ride in the same edit as the padding-escape fix.

[high]verifiedALLdesign inconsistency

#### Channel scope counts a selection it gives no verbs to — master has a selection bar, the channel sheets have none

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is on the jacket's AMAZON · IT sheet, ticks the checkboxes on four of the eight size variations to push those four fields out to Amazon DE and FR, and looks for the verb. The toolbar tells them '4 selected' and the footer agrees — and there is nothing to press. On the master scope of the same product the same four ticks raise a bar with Unlink / Reparent / Delete child.

##### What happens today
The channel sheet turns on row selection (`gridSelection<ChannelSheetRow>()`, ChannelSheet.tsx:1967), renders the checkbox column, reports the count into the shared toolbar (ChannelSheet.tsx:2076 → SheetToolbar.tsx:121) and into the footer (ChannelSheet.tsx:2182) — but it mounts no selection surface. `/usr/bin/grep -rn "BulkActionBar|GridSelectionActions|SelectionLabel"` over the whole `_studio/` tree returns exactly one consumer, master's `FamilySelectionBar` (FamilySelectionBar.tsx:23,46), mounted only in MasterSheet.tsx:1802. The one channel verb declared `scope: SELECTION` — `broadcast-to-listings` (channelActions.ts:311) — therefore has no home: both DS menu adapters resolve verbs against a single row (`offered(o, row)` → `actionsFor(..., SELECTION, [row])`, menuAdapters.tsx:56-58, and the AG context menu at :150-158), so a multi-row selection reaches nothing. The benchmark surface does the opposite: /products/next swaps the toolbar's search slot for `GridSelectionActions` the moment a row is ticked (ProductsNextClient.tsx:1291-1319), which is the pattern the DS documents (GridSelectionActions.tsx:3-24).

##### Proposed fix
Make the selection surface a property of the SHEET, exactly as CH.1 made the toolbar one. Add a `selectionActions?: ReactNode` slot to `SheetToolbar` (beside `trailing`, SheetToolbar.tsx:105-108) governed by the same `absent` discipline, and render the DS pair inside `GridToolbar`'s children — `GridSelectionActions` + `SelectionLabel` when `selected > 0`, `GridSearchSlot` otherwise — so both scopes get the benchmark's swap and neither can omit it by forgetting a prop. Feed it from the registry: `actionsFor(verbs, SELECTION, selectedRows)` with `useActionPress`, i.e. reuse `FamilySelectionBar`'s body generically (rename to `SheetSelectionActions<TRow>`). If the Owner prefers the floating bar, then mount the same component in `GridSheet`'s `footer` on BOTH scopes; the defect is that the two scopes answer differently, not which of the two DS surfaces wins.

Core defect CONFIRMED from code I opened: ChannelSheet.tsx:1975 turns on `gridSelection<ChannelSheetRow>()` (with a comment saying the checkboxes were only just wired), feeds `selected.length` into the toolbar (:2084) and the footer (:2189), and its `footer`/`toolbar` render no BulkActionBar-style surface; MasterSheet.tsx:1802 mounts `FamilySelectionBar` in the footer. `broadcast-to-listings` is `scope: SELECTION` (channelActions.ts:305-312) and menuAdapters.tsx:56-58 resolves SELECTION verbs against `[row]` only, so a 4-row selection never reaches it.

Two parts of the finding are WRONG and I have corrected them rather than let them carry the verdict: (a) the set claim is false — /usr/bin/grep over `_studio/` shows FamilySelectionBar mounted in THREE places, MasterSheet.tsx:1802, variants/family/FamilyVariants.tsx:611 and variants/channel/ChannelProjection.tsx:284, so the channel *tab* in Variants already has a selection bar and only the channel SHEET lacks one; (b) the scenario's 'there is nothing to press' is overstated — ChannelSheet.tsx:2129 puts two selection-dependent items in the ⋯ overflow ('Formula history…', 'Apply formula to selected products…'), both enabled by a multi-row selection, and the single-row broadcast is reachable from the row/context menu. Also, `broadcastToListings.run` is preview-only (returns ok:false, 'Not sent', channelActions.ts:346-357), so the missing surface currently gates a verb that would send nothing. No Owner ruling excludes a channel selection bar (pes-claims.md:27403-27412 discusses which surfaces master mounts and why the ⋯ column is skipped, not the channel scope). Real inconsistency, high severity not earned.
The generic `SheetSelectionActions<TRow>` reuse is right, but the fix must not be written as if the channel scope has no selection affordance at all — it has overflow items keyed on selection, and those should move onto the same surface or be reasoned about, otherwise the sheet ends with two selection idioms. Also note the one SELECTION verb it would surface is preview-only today, so the fix buys shape consistency, not a new capability.

#### 'Delete' means 'recycle bin, restorable' on /products and /products/next, and 'permanent, no bin, no undo' in the studio — and the studio asks for less confirmation than for its reversible verbs

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has been clearing up the catalogue on /products/next all morning: tick a row, Delete, toast says 'Moved 1 to recycle bin', and twice they have fished a row back out of the bin lens. They then open the jacket's studio to remove one bad size variation, pick 'Delete child…' from the same-looking row menu, read a dialog, press Delete — and GALE-JACKET-BLACK-M is gone from the database with its channel listings cascaded away. There is no bin lens to fish it out of.

##### What happens today
The catalogue surfaces implement a two-stage model: `softDeleteBulk` → `POST /api/products/bulk-soft-delete`, toast 'Moved N to recycle bin' (useBulkActions.ts:103-107; ProductsNextClient.tsx:1301-1304), and permanent removal is only reachable from the bin lens where the API enforces `deletedAt != null` (products/_components/BulkActionBar.tsx:262-268 and :328-334). The studio has no soft-delete verb at all: `delete-variant` → `ops.deleteVariant` → `DELETE /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children/:childId` (familyOps.ts:158) → `tx.product.delete` (catalog.routes.ts:1837), with the ChannelListing rows removed by FK cascade. Its own confirm text says so — 'is deleted permanently — there is no undo and no trash' (familyActions.ts:462) — but the confirm LEVEL is the weak one: `level: 'confirm'` (familyActions.ts:457), a single click. In the same file the *reversible* demote is `level: 'type-to-confirm'` while its own copy explains 'The children are NOT deleted — they survive as standalone products, and can be re-attached' (familyActions.ts:510, :519-521), and on the channel scope `broadcast-to-listings` — whose `run` sends nothing at all (channelActions.ts:346-357) — also demands a typed phrase (channelActions.ts:330). So in the studio the only irreversible verb is the only destructive one that does not ask you to type.

##### Proposed fix
Two verbs with the catalogue's vocabulary, not one. (1) 'Move to bin' becomes the studio's default child-removal verb — `POST /api/products/bulk-soft-delete` with the single id, `level: 'confirm'`, consequences worded like the catalogue's toast so the same word means the same thing on both surfaces; it also unblocks the operator, because a soft-deleted child is restorable. (2) 'Delete permanently' keeps the existing `DELETE /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children/:childId` but raises its preflight to `level: 'type-to-confirm'` with `confirmPhrase: row.sku` (the DS reserves exactly this level for it, registry.ts:68-69; `validateImpact` already refuses a typed confirm with no phrase, registry.ts:264-273), and either gates it on `deletedAt != null` like the catalogue's hard delete or itemises the cascade in `sideEffects`. Both stay `GridAction`s so the row menu, context menu and the new selection bar (XP-01) render them from one definition.

Every cited line is exact. familyActions.ts:457 `level: 'confirm'`; :462 '`${row.sku}` is deleted permanently — there is no undo and no trash'; :510 demote is `type-to-confirm` when it has children with :519-521 saying children survive; channelActions.ts:330/342 the preview-only broadcast is type-to-confirm on the channel name. familyOps.ts:157-158 hits DELETE /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children/:childId, and catalog.routes.ts:1837 is `tx.product.delete` (ChannelListings cascade). The catalogue side is as described: useBulkActions.ts:103-105 'Moved N to recycle bin' → /api/products/bulk-soft-delete, and _components/BulkActionBar.tsx:325-334 records that hard delete is bin-only ('API enforces deletedAt != null'). /usr/bin/grep over the whole `_studio/` tree returns ZERO hits for soft-delete/softDelete/recycle — the studio genuinely has no restorable removal.

What I could NOT sustain is the sensational half. The delete preflight refuses outright when the child carries any external listing id or a published listing (familyActions.ts around :450-453 returns `level: 'none'` with `unavailable`), so the plain confirm is only ever reachable on a child with no marketplace record — and that is a DELIBERATE, documented design: pes-claims.md:26806-26812 states the rule 'Delete — severity from fact: nothing listed → plain confirm; a live id → type-to-confirm with the real SKU'. So 'the studio asks for less confirmation than for its reversible verbs' is true only after the fact-based gate has already excluded the dangerous cases; that is a lane design decision, not an Owner ruling, so it does not fully refute — but it drops this from a data-integrity emergency to a cross-surface vocabulary inconsistency plus unrecoverable local data loss.
Raising the existing hard delete to type-to-confirm partly re-litigates a documented decision (pes-claims.md:26806-26812 chose the level from measured fact, and a live id already REFUSES rather than downgrades) — propose that half to the Owner rather than asserting it. The 'Move to bin' verb is the load-bearing half and should be proposed on its own: it needs a check that /api/products/bulk-soft-delete on a CHILD does the right thing with `includeChildren` and with the parent's platformAttributes.variants entry, which the hard-delete route cleans up (catalog.routes.ts:1838-1845) and the bulk soft-delete route may not.

#### Money is rendered four different ways inside the studio and none matches the benchmark; the record drawer stamps '€' on every market, including GBP and USD ones

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator opens a jacket on AMAZON · UK, whose Amazon price is £129.00. In the sheet the price cell reads a bare '129' with no currency at all; they open the record drawer on the same row and it reads '€129.00'; the Performance panel for the same listing reads '129.00 GBP'; and on /products/next the same product's base price is rendered '€129'. They are deciding whether to reprice against a German competitor.

##### What happens today
Four independent implementations, none of them the design system's. (a) Record drawer: `new Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' })` — the host browser's locale and a HARDCODED EUR, applied to `listing.price` whatever market the scope is on (ListingsPane.tsx:30-31, rendered at :138). (b) Sheet cells: every `kind === 'number'` column, price included, renders `String(p.value)` with no formatter (master/columns.tsx:487; the channel sheet takes the same numeric branch, ChannelSheet.tsx:1180). (c) Performance: `revenue.toFixed(2)` and `` `${price.price.toFixed(2)} ${price.currency}` `` (ScopedPerformance.tsx:35, :46). (d) Ads: value + ' ' + code (analytics/readAds.ts:56-58). The benchmark uses the DS grid's `euroColumn` (products/next columns.tsx:335) and `eur0` (ProductsNextClient.tsx:24). CONTENT.md is explicit — 'Use @/design-system/lib/format — never hand-roll Intl … Locales are fixed in the formatters so SSR and client match' (design-system/docs/CONTENT.md:12-19); `/usr/bin/grep -rn "design-system/lib"` over `_studio/` returns only `density` and `cdn-image` imports — zero format imports (positive control: the same grep on `products/next/` returns ProductsNextClient.tsx:24). The EUR hardcode is not merely cosmetic: `Marketplace.currency` is a real column with 'EUR' | 'GBP' | 'USD' (schema.prisma:1947), and the studio's own marketplace projection (`MarketplaceLite`, types.ts:77-79, consumed by `deriveScopeOptions`, scopes.ts:108-141) never carries it, so the drawer has no way to be right and asserts € regardless.

##### Proposed fix
Carry the currency down the scope, then format once. (1) Add `currency: string` to `MarketplaceLite` (types.ts:77-79) from `Marketplace.currency`, project it through `deriveScopeOptions` onto `MarketOption` (scopes.ts:128-134) and expose it from `useStudioScope()`. (2) Add a currency-aware sibling to the DS money helpers — `money(value, currency)` in `design-system/lib/format` with fixed `en-IE`, and `moneyColumn(field, currency)` beside the existing `euroColumn` in `design-system/grid` — then replace ListingsPane.tsx:30-31, ScopedPerformance.tsx:35/46 and readAds.ts:56-58 with it. (3) In the sheet, give a price-shaped contract column (`col.shape === 'money'`, or `writeField` in the CHANNEL_WRITABLE price set, studio-sheet.service.ts:509) the `moneyColumn` formatter instead of `String(p.value)`, so the cell shows '£129.00' on a GBP market while the editor keeps taking a bare number.

#### 'Export' means opposite things on the two rebuilt surfaces — the studio's toolbar Export opens a workbook wizard, and the CSV of what is on screen is three levels down inside it

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has just used /products/next: press Export table, a CSV of the filtered rows lands in Downloads. Ten minutes later, on the jacket's master sheet, they press the identically placed, identically named Export because they want the same CSV to mail to a colleague — and a 900px drawer opens asking them to choose products, listings, content languages and a file type.

##### What happens today
Same word, inverted affordances. /products/next: the toolbar's `Export table` immediately runs the CSV export (ProductsNextClient.tsx:1281, `runExport` → fetchAllRowsForExport, productsExport.ts:1-30) and the workbook engine is a link in the page header, 'Import & export' → /products/catalog-transfer (ProductsNextClient.tsx:1189-1194). The studio: the toolbar's `Export` opens the workbook drawer (`setTransferIntent('export'); setImportOpen(true)`, MasterSheet.tsx:1765; the channel scope is identical, ChannelSheet.tsx:2112) whose primary action is 'Download editing workbook' (ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:202); the studio's own CSV of the sheet exists and is good (`exportGridCsv`, MasterSheet.tsx:1635-1650, with a refusal rather than a silent subset) but the only path to it is `onReference`, i.e. a `Disclosure` at the very bottom of that drawer labelled 'Download the displayed table for reference' (ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:208 → MasterSheet.tsx:1955). The toolbar's own tooltip for the same button reads 'Choose products and destinations for an editing workbook' (SheetToolbar.tsx:232) — honest, but it means the two surfaces label two different artifacts with one word and hide each other's primary artifact behind the other's.

##### Proposed fix
One name per artifact, on every surface. Keep the studio's single toolbar shape (CH.1) but bind `Export` to the CSV the operator can see — call it 'Export table', exactly as the benchmark does (ProductsNextClient.tsx:1281), wire it to the existing `exportGridCsv` path (MasterSheet.tsx:1635) and keep its 'rows × columns → file' note in `trailing`. Move the workbook to a labelled item in the one `⋯` overflow (SheetToolbar.tsx:244-271) reading 'Import & export…' — the same words the catalogue header uses for the same engine — opening the same `ProductTransferDrawer`; drop the drawer's bottom `Disclosure` (ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:208) once the CSV has its own button. `Import` stays where it is, since its meaning already matches.

Confirmed. SheetToolbar.tsx:223-236 renders one 'Export' button whose tooltip switches on `exportPurpose`, reading 'Choose products and destinations for an editing workbook' in the workbook case; MasterSheet.tsx:1765-1768 wires `onExport` to `setTransferIntent('export'); setImportOpen(true)` with `exportPurpose="workbook"`, and ChannelSheet.tsx:2112-2118 is the same. The sheet's own CSV exists and is good (MasterSheet.tsx:1635-1650, `exportGridCsv` with a `GridExportRefused` path and a rows×columns note) but is reached only through `onReference` (MasterSheet.tsx:1955), which ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:208 renders as the bottom `Disclosure` 'Download the displayed table for reference'; the drawer's export primary is 'Download editing workbook' (:202). The benchmark inverts it: ProductsNextClient.tsx:1281-1282 'Export table' runs the CSV immediately, and the workbook engine is the header link 'Import & export' at :1189-1194. No Owner ruling settles this — /usr/bin/grep finds no 'exportPurpose', 'Export table' or 'reference table' in docs/pes-claims.md, and the 09-04 review mentions Export only in a control-inventory line (:82). Medium is the right severity: nothing is destroyed, the tooltip is honest, and both artifacts are reachable.
Rebinding the toolbar's Export changes the meaning of a shipped CH.1 control on both scopes and demotes the workbook — that is an Owner call, not a lane's, so it should be filed as a proposal. Dropping the drawer's reference Disclosure also removes the CSV's only path for anyone who arrives via Import, so keep it until the toolbar button ships.

#### The studio pipes live listing events but refreshes only its readiness chips — the grid beside them keeps showing pre-sync values with no staleness signal, while every peer grid refetches and shows a Live pill

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator has the jacket open on AMAZON · DE while the hourly sync pulls a price and quantity change Amazon made overnight. The readiness chip on the scope bar moves (it re-reads), so the page looks alive — but the price cell under it still shows last night's number, and nothing on screen says the row is behind. They re-key a price from what they can see.

##### What happens today
The studio frame opens one SSE pipe and subscribes to `product.updated`, `listing.updated`, `channel-pricing.updated`, and its own comment states the scope: 'The frame refreshes only what the FRAME owns: readiness' (contracts.tsx:484, hook at :489-521). Neither sheet subscribes: `/usr/bin/grep -rn "useInvalidationChannel|useListingEvents"` over `_studio/` returns contracts.tsx, `shopify/useLiveShopifySchema.ts` and the transfer drawer's *emit* only — no sheet consumer. The sheets' only recovery is the manual Reload item in the `⋯` overflow (SheetToolbar.tsx:258-268), whose own comment records the decision: 'with no live cells in this build (CH.1 row 19), Reload plus the 409 version check on write is the whole "what changed elsewhere" story'. The benchmark does the opposite with the same events: `useListingEvents()` + `useInvalidationChannel([...], () => refetch())` (ProductsNextClient.tsx:414-418) and a permanent status Pill reading Live / Syncing… / Not syncing (ProductsNextClient.tsx:1283-1285). So the studio is the one rebuilt grid that can display stale cells beside freshly-recomputed chips and says nothing — the 409 version check protects the WRITE, not the reading.

##### Proposed fix
Do not force a live refetch under an operator's cursor (CH.1 ruled Reload into the overflow for good reason) — make the staleness VISIBLE, which the toolbar already has a slot for. Subscribe each sheet to the same channel the frame already pipes (`useInvalidationChannel(['product.updated','listing.updated','channel-pricing.updated'], …)`, filtered to this productId as contracts.tsx:515 does) and, instead of refetching, set a `stale` flag that renders in `SheetToolbar`'s `trailing` STATUS slot (SheetToolbar.tsx:105-106, 220) as a DS `Pill tone="warning" dot` reading 'Updated elsewhere' with the existing Reload one press away in `⋯`; clear it on reload. That keeps CH.1's bar shape, adds no control, and closes the gap between the chips and the cells. If the Owner wants the benchmark's steady-state signal too, the same slot can carry the Live / Not syncing Pill when nothing is stale.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:484
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx:489-521
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/sheet/SheetToolbar.tsx:244-268
- apps/web/src/app/products/next/ProductsNextClient.tsx:414-418
- apps/web/src/app/products/next/ProductsNextClient.tsx:1283-1285
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/import/ProductTransferDrawer.tsx:140-141

##### Verifier
Confirmed as stated. contracts.tsx:484 carries the exact sentence 'The frame refreshes only what the FRAME owns: readiness', with `useListingEvents(streamsEnabled())` at :502 and `useInvalidationChannel(['product.updated','listing.updated','channel-pricing.updated'], …)` at :510-521 bumping only a readiness nonce. /usr/bin/grep for `useInvalidationChannel|useListingEvents` over `_studio/` returns only contracts.tsx and shopify/useLiveShopifySchema.ts:40 — no sheet consumer (the finding also credits ProductTransferDrawer as an emit site; that hit did not appear in my grep, which does not affect the claim). SheetToolbar.tsx:244-268 carries the Reload item and the verbatim comment 'with no live cells in this build (CH.1 row 19), Reload plus the 409 version check on write is the whole "what changed elsewhere" story'. The benchmark does refetch and shows the Live/Syncing…/Not syncing Pill (ProductsNextClient.tsx:414-418, 1283-1285). I searched the studio chrome (StudioHeader/StudioSubheader/StudioBar) for a staleness or Live signal and found none. Not refuted, but note the honest framing: CH.1 row 19 is a recorded scope decision that this build has no live cells, so this is an accepted-gap-with-no-signal rather than a regression; medium is right.
Good — it respects CH.1 by adding a status, not a control, and uses the `trailing` slot the toolbar reserves for exactly that ('Transient STATUS only', SheetToolbar.tsx:105-106). One gap: contracts.tsx:502 gates the pipe behind `streamsEnabled()` (off against a local backend by design), so a stale pill that never fires locally must not be verified locally and must not read as 'nothing changed'.

#### The studio→wizard handoff drops the coordinate the operator is standing on, and the bound-destination surface that would carry it lives in the studio tree with no entry point

▸ Scenario, current behaviour, evidence and proposed fix

##### Scenario
An operator is on the jacket at AMAZON · IT, second account, looking at a listing alias, and decides to also list it on eBay IT. They press the one action in the studio header. On a channel scope the button just switches them back to the sheet they are already on; on master it sends them to the legacy wizard, which starts from nothing — the channel, market, account and alias they had selected are not carried, and if anything tried to carry them the route would refuse.

##### What happens today
`PublishMenu` is the header's only action (StudioHeader.tsx:98). On a channel scope with the sheet open it renders nothing (PublishMenu.tsx:13); on a channel scope elsewhere it is a tab switch (PublishMenu.tsx:14-16); on master it is a plain link to `/products/:id/list-wizard` carrying no coordinate (PublishMenu.tsx:17-19), and its own doc comment states why: 'The legacy creation wizard does not accept a bound account/listing and cannot take this handoff' (PublishMenu.tsx:8-9). That is enforced on both sides: `POST /listing-wizard/start` 409s if the body carries `accountId`, `channelConnectionId`, `aliasKey`, `aliasId`, `listingId` or `productContext` (listing-wizard.routes.ts:902-905), and the wizard page refuses the same query params client-side (list-wizard/page.tsx:88-92). The component that CAN create a destination-bound draft — `ProductListingPresets` — physically lives in the studio tree (`_studio/presets/ProductListingPresets.tsx:29`) but `/usr/bin/grep -rn "ProductListingPresets|BoundPresetDestination"` over `apps/web/src` shows its only mount is `BoundPresetDestination` (presets/BoundPresetDestination.tsx:15), whose only mount is `Step1Channels.tsx:114`, taken only when `wizardState.productPresetScope` already exists — a draft only that path can create. A closed loop: the studio owns the surface and has no door to it.

##### Proposed fix
Open the door the studio already built. Replace `PublishMenu`'s master-only link-out with a DS `Drawer` (`components/Drawer`, `mode="modal"`, the same shell `ProductTransferDrawer` uses) that mounts `ProductListingPresets` with the studio's live coordinate — `{ productId, channel: scope, marketplace: market, accountId, aliasKey, locale }` from `useStudioScope()` — so the preset creates the destination-bound draft (`ProductPresetService.apply`) that `/listing-wizard/start` is designed to refuse, and hand off with the draft id only. Make the button render on every scope, not just master (D11: the same UI on all scopes): on a channel scope it should read 'Add a listing here…' and pre-select that channel×market rather than disappearing (PublishMenu.tsx:13). Nothing new is needed server-side — the refusal at listing-wizard.routes.ts:902-905 is already pointing at this path.

##### Evidence
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/PublishMenu.tsx:8-19
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/StudioHeader.tsx:98
- apps/api/src/routes/listing-wizard.routes.ts:902-905
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/list-wizard/page.tsx:88-92
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/presets/ProductListingPresets.tsx:29-30
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/presets/BoundPresetDestination.tsx:15
- apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/list-wizard/steps/Step1Channels.tsx:114

##### Verifier
Every cited fact holds. PublishMenu.tsx:8-19 is the whole component: the doc comment says the legacy wizard 'does not accept a bound account/listing and cannot take this handoff', it returns null on a channel scope with the sheet open (:13), a tab switch otherwise (:14-16), and on master a bare Link to /products/:id/list-wizard with no coordinate (:17-19); StudioHeader.tsx:98 mounts it as the header's only action. Both ends enforce the refusal: listing-wizard.routes.ts:902-905 409s on accountId/channelConnectionId/aliasKey/aliasId/listingId/productContext, and list-wizard/page.tsx:88-92 refuses the same query params client-side. /usr/bin/grep for ProductListingPresets|BoundPresetDestination across apps/web/src returns only presets/ProductListingPresets.tsx:29-32, presets/BoundPresetDestination.tsx:6,15 and list-wizard/steps/Step1Channels.tsx:24,114, where it is gated on `wizardState.productPresetScope` — the closed loop is real. Refutation attempt: the studio DOES have '+ Add listing alias' in the channel toolbar's ⋯ (ChannelSheet.tsx:2026-2031, creating a Nexus draft alias at the current coordinate), but that adds an alias on an ALREADY-connected channel×market, not a listing on a new destination, so it does not close the gap the finding names — it only narrows the scenario's wording.
Mounting ProductListingPresets from the header drawer is the right door, but 'Nothing is needed server-side' is asserted, not shown — the fix never opens ProductListingPresets' own apply path (`ProductPresetService.apply`) to check it accepts a coordinate assembled by the studio rather than one produced by the wizard's `productPresetScope`. Also, making the button render on every scope collides with the existing channel-scope behaviour at PublishMenu.tsx:13-16 ('Review listing information'), which the fix would have to replace or relocate rather than simply relabel.

Method: six agents mapped the studio, the lifecycle backend, the publish path, the data model, the design system and the binding decisions in the design docs. Thirty probes then audited one slice each, capped at six findings, and every finding was handed to an adversarial verifier told to refute it by opening the cited lines.

Two things this audit did not do. It never called an API or edited a file, so every claim rests on reading code. And it stopped early: the critics that would have named what the sweep missed never ran.
